items.desc: At Plumerai, we make it easy and affordable for developers to add highly accurate AI to their camera devices, enabling them to create amazing new products. Major brands deploy our advanced computer vision models on millions of smart home cameras in the field and we're rapidly expanding into other sectors, such as commercial security, elderly care and retail. We combine our on-device Tiny AI software with our cloud-based Vision Language Models, to provide our customers with powerful AI features, including People Detection, Video Search, Familiar Face Identification, AI Captions and more. We prioritize on-device inference, to enable low-power, super-efficient and private AI products. Plumerai leads on accuracy, even when compared to large players, such as Google Nest. We're a small, high-performing team based in London and Amsterdam, with plans to double in size over the next year. Following our recent $8.7M Series A, backed by world-class investors including Tony Fadell, Hermann Hauser, and Zoubin Ghahramani, we have multiple years of runway and rapidly growing recurring revenue. We’re in a period of significant growth and are expanding our engineering team across multiple levels and specialisms. This is one of several hires we’re making as we scale the company. 🎥 Get to know Plumerai Meet the team and see what it's like to work here: ▶️ Life at Plumerai ▶️ What we're building Learn more here: Plumerai 👉 Read more: TechCrunch, Series A funding announcement Role Description We are looking for a Deep Learning Research Engineer that can help us develop state of the art AI products. This can involve anything from improving our training algorithms, training and integrating multimodal LLMs, building our data pipeline, designing new model architectures to using tried and tested ML approaches and coming up with clever algorithms. You will help us build new AI features that will be shipped to millions of camera devices in the field. Together we are building the most advanced AI for embedded devices. What You Will Be Doing We combine our Tiny AI with multimodal LLMs to enable our advanced AI features for our customers. You will use and improve multimodal LLMs to achieve new functionality for our customers and optimize their deployments (cloud and edge). Some of our deep learning models are truly tiny - the memory footprint of our smallest computer vision model is just 1MB. You will train and design more accurate models, while also enabling new and more complex AI applications on low-cost and low-power hardware. You will improve our data pipeline, model architectures and training software. Sometimes there is relevant literature available, but novel approaches and clever hacks are often required for the problems that we are working on. You will use our Kubernetes cluster to deploy PyTorch and TensorFlow training jobs, Snowflake and Dataflow to build datasets, tools like Streamlit to prototype new demos (try one of our live demos here) and lots of GPUs on GCP for training new models and auto-labeling data. What You Need +5 years of professional software engineering experience with proficiency in Python. Comfortable with frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, Keras, or JAX. Strong experience with computer vision and multimodal LLMs. Trained neural networks that moved into production. Nice To Have Industry experience with efficient inference deployments (cloud or edge). Experience with Deep Reinforcement Learning. We only consider applicants who are currently based in, or willing to relocate to, London or Amsterdam. We have flexible working hours and work together from our offices on at least 2 fixed days per week. What We Offer Competitive salary. Generous equity stake in the company. Relocation assistance and visa sponsorship is provided. Choose your own laptop and equipment. 25 days of paid vacation time in addition to bank holidays. Ability to attend top research conferences like NeurIPS, ICML and CVPR. Process Talent Screen Technical Round I Technical Round II Cross Team & Executive Interview

What is your new project?: We’re looking for a highly technical engineer or researcher with deep expertise in GPU computing, CUDA, and LLM inference optimization to work on challenging problems at the intersection of AI systems and high-performance computing. This opportunity is ideal for someone who enjoys understanding how things work under the hood — from GPU architecture and low-level kernels to LLM inference engines and performance bottlenecks. What makes this project exciting?: Investigate and optimize LLM inference performance on modern GPUs. Work with inference and serving frameworks such as vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, or similar systems. Analyze GPU execution, memory access patterns, kernel performance, and inference bottlenecks. Develop, optimize, debug, or reverse-engineer CUDA kernels and low-level GPU operations. Explore optimization techniques for matrix multiplication, attention mechanisms, and neural network layers. Benchmark performance and identify opportunities to improve latency, throughput, and GPU utilization. Work on technically challenging problems requiring strong analytical thinking and hands-on experimentation. What makes you a great fit: Strong hands-on experience with CUDA and GPU programming. Deep understanding of GPU architecture, memory hierarchy, parallel execution, and performance optimization. Experience with LLM inference, AI systems, GPU kernels, or high-performance computing. Familiarity with one or more frameworks such as vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, Triton, or FlashAttention. Experience debugging complex performance issues and investigating low-level system behavior. Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to communicate complex technical concepts in English. Nice to have PhD or research experience in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Computer Architecture, or a related field. Publications, research projects, or meaningful contributions to open-source GPU/LLM infrastructure. Experience with PyTorch internals, distributed inference, quantization, KV cache optimization, or custom GPU kernels. Contributions to projects such as vLLM, SGLang, Triton, FlashAttention, or related repositories. Why work with us?: People-first management with minimal bureaucracy A friendly company culture, proven by employees who choose to return Flexible working hours 29 days of PTO (18 working days per year pluse all national holidays) 10 paid recovery days Full financial and legal support for independent contractors Free English classes, with native speakers or Ukrainian teachers Dedicated HR support

items.desc: About CarbonFarm is a climateTech working on changing the way we grow our food. Our vision? If farming is to become sustainable, it has to make economic sense to the farmer. By using satellites and AI, we quantify emissions from agriculture so that farmers can get rewarded when they adopt low-emission practices. Job Description Apply through our online form! CarbonFarm is looking for a climate-passionate 🌳 Machine Learning Engineer to turn terabytes of satellite data into useful insights about farming practices. Data is at the heart of everything we do, and we have a lot of it! You’ll work with a wide variety of satellite imagery and Internet-of-things data to build a comprehensive understanding of agricultural practices around the world. Our team and partners are spread across dozens of countries, so you’ll need to be a clear technical communicator who’s capable of understanding different points of view. Responsibilities Collaborate with fellow engineers (ML, AI, Data) to develop models and algorithms that identify how farmers are cultivating their land from satellite and IoT data Propose and implement new pre-training and fine-tuning approaches for deep models Work with our chief architect to deploy models in production Research different approaches in remote sensing from the scientific community Test and validate models, with a particular focus on temporal/geospatial cross-validation and the mitigation of bias and leakage Leverage AI tooling to drive rapid iteration, with a strong bias for technical accuracy Requirements Preferred Experience Master’s degree or equivalent in data science, computer science, or remote sensing 3+ years of experience with PyTorch (preferred), TensorFlow, or related frameworks Comfortable with a variety of different database technologies (SQL, OLAP) Strong foundations in statistics and probability Flexible and focussed on solutions Organised and self-sufficient Fluent in English Paris-based or willing to relocate, with the ability to work in person with the team Would be nice Familiarity working in an agile environment Experience using cloud-based computing (GCP or similar) Previous exposure to the remote sensing domain Apply through our online form! items.desc: Company Description Lynqo is an Antwerp-based healthtech startup building computer vision technology that understands what happens in the operating room. Our platform turns surgical activity into reliable information, supporting instrument counting, automating registration and providing insight into procedure progress. Our ambition is to make surgery safer and more efficient, reduce pressure on clinical teams and help hospitals make better use of their ORs. We work closely with Belgian and Dutch hospitals, developing and testing our technology alongside surgical teams under strict reliability and privacy requirements. As our team grows, we’re looking for a Computer Vision Engineer to take ownership of core vision components and help bring robust systems into clinical practice. Role summary Operating rooms are visually complex, dynamic environments. This role sits at the intersection of raw camera data, computer vision models and clinical workflows, turning challenging visual input into robust, deployable perception that works in real surgical settings. Full-time employee role Close collaboration with our CTO, engineering team and hospital partners High ownership from model design to deployment Regular visits to partner hospitals for observation, testing and validation Flexible working setup: Antwerp office and remote Your mission ahead Perception & tracking Develop and optimise detection, segmentation and tracking models for complex OR environments Improve accuracy under challenging conditions, including occlusions, partial visibility and dynamic scenes Build reliable vision pipelines that work consistently across procedures and hospital settings Training & model quality Build reproducible training and evaluation pipelines Develop visual recognition methods for challenging objects Analyse failure modes and improve model accuracy across procedures and hospital environments Edge deployment & robustness Optimise and deploy vision components on edge devices Balance accuracy, latency and robustness under real-world constraints Monitor and validate model performance in deployed systems Clinical validation & integration Observe procedures and test directly in partner hospitals Translate practical observations into improvements to models and pipelines Collaborate with our team to improve overall system accuracy and reliability Integrate vision components cleanly into the broader Lynqo platform This role is a great fit if you have … 2+ years of professional experience in computer vision, applied machine learning or a related field, or equivalent practical experience Strong proficiency in Python and common computer vision frameworks, such as PyTorch and OpenCV Hands-on experience building and evaluating computer vision models and pipelines Experience working with detection, segmentation, tracking or visual recognition systems Familiarity with Linux environments and Docker-based workflows Ability to write clear, structured and maintainable code Experience working with Git and collaborative workflows, including pull requests and issues Clear communication skills and a willingness to work directly with hospital staff Experience deploying and optimising vision models on edge hardware Nice to have Experience with multi-camera vision Experience with the NVIDIA ecosystem Familiarity with production model monitoring and CI/CD pipelines for ML or vision systems Experience working with privacy-sensitive or regulated environments Working at Lynqo We value ownership, curiosity and openness. You’ll join a small but growing team with short feedback loops, where clear communication and reliability matter just as much as technical elegance. You’ll work closely with technical and non-technical colleagues, and your input will shape how the product evolves. What’s in it for you? Full-time employee role in a mission-driven healthtech startup Direct ownership over key parts of our computer vision and AI stack Competitive salary and additional benefits, aligned with your experience Small team, short feedback loops and high autonomy Flexible working setup: Antwerp office, up to two days remote Building software that’s used in real hospitals Interested? items.desc: About Us Every business needs to know who they’re really working with whether it’s suppliers, investors, partners, or third parties. At Xapien, we’re reinventing how organisations do that, combining speed, scale and accuracy with cutting-edge AI. Since 2018, we’ve grown from a deep-tech startup to a global player in AI-driven due diligence and risk intelligence. 2024 was a landmark year as we closed a $10M Series A, earned recognition in the Chartis RiskTech100® and Everest Group’s Leading 50™, and expanded our products, markets and customer base. 2025 was even bigger: With new regulations, rising compliance pressure and growing reputation risks, organisations everywhere are demanding smarter, faster ways to work and they’re turning to us. Customers worldwide from global law firms and private banks to universities and nonprofits rely on Xapien to turn days of manual research into trusted insights, delivered in minutes. Our momentum so far Customers in a diverse range of industries, with particular growth in wealth management, financial services and supply chain onboarding. Demand accelerating beyond our UK headquarters, across multiple continents with new customers in the Middle East, Asia, and Oceania. Why this is an exciting time to join This isn’t just another job role; it’s an opportunity to shape the future of the due diligence industry with a market-leading product trusted by global organisations. Whether you’re in marketing, communications, sales, or finance, you’ll play a critical role in driving growth, building credibility, and defining how we connect our product to a rapidly evolving market. We’re scaling fast with more customers, more releases, and bigger regulatory and market challenges. Expectations are rising, due diligence now means real-time insight, delivered efficiently and with impact. You won’t just be executing campaigns, closing deals, or managing numbers, you’ll be influencing strategy, optimising processes, and helping position a brand that’s setting the new standard for trust and transparency. For people who love learning, innovating, and making an impact that matters now is the moment to be a part of Xapien. The Role We are looking for a detail-focussed Applied Research Engineer to help us develop the next generation of the algorithms at the heart of our system. Our product is experiencing tremendous growth, and we need to ensure that we continue to deliver accurate insights in a rapidly changing landscape. This role requires someone who thrives in a fast-paced environment where continuous innovation and refinement are key. You will be working closely with our product team to ensure our algorithms and models capture their domain knowledge and expertise appropriately. This is an ideal opportunity for someone looking to kick-start a career in AI. Core responsibilities: Designing, building, and testing AI-powered experiments working with leading-edge ML models. Building and deploying AI-powered microservices following standard design patterns. Implementing infrastructure as code using tools like Terraform or CloudFormation to automate deployment and scaling processes. Statistical evaluation of candidate systems against functional and non-functional requirements, optimising for performance and cost-efficiency. Collaborating with our wider engineering team Demonstrating a desire to continuously learn & improve You need to have: Being a small company, candidates need to be able to work autonomously, be comfortable without micro-management, be flexible and have initiative to solve problems. A rigorous and scientific approach to problem solving A demonstrable track record for learning and mastering complex topics Keen attention to detail Strong verbal and written communication Demonstrable experience working with Python and good Python knowledge A good understanding of statistics A strong understanding of algorithm optimisation A strong foundation of working with command-line tooling and knowledge of unix What you will gain out of it: We will provide you with support and training in everything you need. This will include background understanding of the risk and compliance sector, our product, development, AWS infrastructure, log analysis and all other related skills. Here’s our promise to you: We are going to work with you - to build a rewarding and fulfilling career with the opportunities, challenges and resources you need to do you your best work. We succeed together- you will own a meaningful part of the business through our employee shares & equity programme. Private health insurance to keep you in tip-top condition. Life Insurance – let's hope nobody ever needs this! Unlimited holidays – yes, it really is uncapped – take the time you need, when you need it. Everyone is learning, developing and challenging themselves so we have a £1k professional development fund per year if you want to learn new skills, even new things outside of work. Most importantly of all, we will work with you, …

At Deloitte, the world’s number one professional services firm, you will tackle complex challenges in an environment where number one never stops challenging. We are seeking talented AI Engineer(s) to join our AI Scaling and Transformation team, a centre of excellence within Deloitte's Engineering, AI & Data service offering. You will be working alongside world-class technologists and leading organisations across industries to design, build, and deploy cutting-edge AI and Generative AI solutions that solve real-world challenges and unlock measurable business value. This is a hands-on, impact-driven role where you'll combine deep technical expertise with collaborative problem-solving to deliver robust, production-grade AI solutions that drive tangible client outcomes. Key Skills And Prior Experience AI/ML Development Expertise: Proven track record designing, developing, and deploying production-grade AI and machine learning solutions in business or research environments, with hands-on experience in data pipelines, model training, and end-to-end ML workflows. Cloud & MLOps Proficiency: Solid experience deploying AI solutions on cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP), implementing MLOps practices (CI/CD, model versioning, monitoring), and optimising models for scalability and efficiency in production. Generative AI & Advanced Techniques: Demonstrated expertise building and deploying GenAI solutions, including prompt engineering, fine-tuning LLMs (OpenAI, Anthropic, Llama, Gemini), and familiarity with deep learning, NLP, computer vision, or reinforcement learning. Cross-functional Collaboration: Strong ability to work within multidisciplinary teams, communicate complex technical concepts to both technical and non-technical stakeholders, and influence outcomes through clear technical reasoning and client partnership. What type of work will I be doing? Deploy & Operationalise AI Systems: Take ownership of integrating AI models into production systems, ensuring scalability, efficiency, seamless integration with existing applications, and compliance with security and regulatory standards. Research & Apply Emerging Technologies: Stay ahead of the curve by researching, assessing, and applying emerging AI frameworks, tools, and technologies to enhance solution effectiveness and drive continuous improvement. Ensure Responsible AI Practices: Champion ethical and responsible AI implementation, including model interpretability, fairness, bias mitigation, and compliance with relevant regulations and governance frameworks. Contribute to Technical Excellence: Share knowledge and best practices with peers, stay current with emerging AI technologies, and contribute to continuous improvement of delivery approaches and solution quality. Communicate & Influence: Translate complex AI and GenAI concepts into clear, actionable insights for diverse audiences, adapting your communication style to suit technical and business stakeholders. Optimise for Production: Continuously monitor, evaluate, and optimise deployed AI models for performance, cost-efficiency, and alignment with evolving business objectives. Who is the Hiring Manager? The hiring manager is a seasoned technical leader within Deloitte's Engineering, AI & Data practice, recognised for their deep expertise in AI transformation and their collaborative approach to client delivery. items.desc: Kan du forklare attention på en serviet, træne en transformer fra bunden, og bygge de evals, der afslører, om den faktisk virker? Og vil du bruge dine evner på noget, der virkelig betyder noget? Så har vi en mission, adgang til Danmarks nationale AI-supercomputer, og en plads til dig, uanset om du lige har afleveret specialet eller har nogle år på bagen. Om os AI ændrer allerede rammerne for samfund, sikkerhedspolitik, og militær opgaveløsning. Fremtidens kampplads vil i stigende grad være præget af data, autonomi, og hurtigere beslutningsprocesser. Forsvarets AI Center (FAIC) er etableret som ny enhed i Forsvarskommandoen for at sikre, at AI omsættes til reel dansk og allieret forsvarsevne. FAIC sætter retning på Forsvarets brug af AI - fra doktrin til operationel virkelighed. Vi opbygger institutionel kompetence, indgår partnerskaber med NATO, allierede, akademia, og industri, og definerer de operative behov og principper som Forsvarets AI-løsninger udvikles og anskaffes ud fra - i tæt samarbejde med Forsvarets Materiel- og Indkøbsstyrelse (FMI), så anskaffelser og leverancer tager udgangspunkt i soldaternes behov og Forsvarets kerneopgave. Vores samarbejde med Gefion, Danmarks nationale AI-supercomputer, viser arbejdsformen: åbne miljøer giver læring og tempo, mens lukkede rammer sikrer militær anvendelse hvor sikkerhed, klassifikation, og operativ relevans er afgørende. FAIC er stedet hvor Forsvarets AI-fremtid formes. Vi søger erfarne profiler der vil være med fra dag ét. Om stillingen Som AI Engineer i Forsvarets AI Center arbejder du med at udvikle, tilpasse og evaluere AI-modeller til Forsvarets operative behov. Du træner og finetuner modeller på Gefion og arbejder med alt fra transformerarkitekturer, attention-mekanismer og optimering til evaluering af modellers præcision, robusthed og sikkerhed. Du udvikler de værktøjer, evalueringsmetoder og sikkerhedsmekanismer, der gør det muligt at vurdere, om en model er klar til operativ anvendelse. Samtidig bygger du datapipelines, testværktøjer og softwareintegrationer og samarbejder tæt med udviklere, platform engineers og operative brugere om at omsætte forskning til løsninger, der fungerer i praksis. Du bliver en del af et tværfagligt miljø med en stejl læringskurve, hvor både nyuddannede og erfarne kan udvikle sig fagligt og bidrage med deres kompetencer. Rollen er for dig, der er nysgerrig på den nyeste AI-forskning, motiveres af at forstå, hvorfor modeller opfører sig, som de gør, og vil bruge din tekniske viden til at styrke Forsvarets opgaveløsning Dine vigtigste opgaver: Modeludvikling og træning: Du træner, finetuner og tilpasser AI-modeller til Forsvarets opgaver og data, herunder sprogmodeller, multimodale modeller og modeller til sensor- og billeddata. Du eksperimenterer med transformerarkitekturer, attention-mekanismer og andre effektive modelstrukturer samt anvender metoder som supervised fine-tuning, preference-optimering og reinforcement learning til at forme modellernes adfærd. På Gefion og AI Centerets øvrige GPU-ressourcer optimerer du træningsforløb med fokus på effektivitet og stabilitet. Du opbygger og kvalitetssikrer samtidig trænings- og evalueringsdata, herunder syntetiske data, med fokus på kvalitet, sporbarhed og klassifikation. Evals, guardrails, og tillid: Du udvikler evalueringsmetoder og benchmarks, der måler modellernes præcision, robusthed og pålidelighed i relevante operative scenarier. Du implementerer guardrails, der understøtter sikker og forudsigelig modeladfærd, også ved prompt injection og andre adversarielle angreb. Så har vi en mission, adgang til Danmarks nationale AI-supercomputer, og en plads til dig, uanset om du lige har afleveret specialet eller har nogle år på bagen. Om os AI ændrer allerede rammerne for samfund, sikkerhedspolitik, og militær opgaveløsning. Fremtidens kampplads vil i stigende grad være præget af data, autonomi, og hurtigere beslutningsprocesser. Forsvarets AI Center (FAIC) er etableret som ny enhed i Forsvarskommandoen for at sikre, at AI omsættes til reel dansk og allieret forsvarsevne. FAIC sætter retning på Forsvarets brug af AI - fra doktrin til operationel virkelighed. Vi opbygger institutionel kompetence, indgår partnerskaber med NATO, allierede, akademia, og industri, og definerer de operative behov og principper som Forsvarets AI-løsninger udvikles og anskaffes ud fra - i tæt samarbejde med Forsvarets Materiel- og Indkøbsstyrelse (FMI), så anskaffelser og leverancer tager udgangspunkt i soldaternes behov og Forsvarets kerneopgave. Vores samarbejde med Gefion, Danmarks nationale AI-supercomputer, viser arbejdsformen: åbne miljøer giver læring og tempo, mens lukkede rammer sikrer militær anvendelse hvor sikkerhed, klassifikation, og operativ relevans er afgørende. FAIC er stedet hvor Forsvarets AI-fremtid formes. Vi søger erfarne profiler der vil være med fra dag ét. Om stillingen Som AI Engineer i Forsvarets AI Center arbejder du med at udvikle, tilpasse og evaluere AI-modeller til Forsvarets operative behov. Du træner og finetuner modeller på Gefion og arbejder med alt fra transformerarkitekturer, attention-mekanismer og optimering til evaluering af modellers præcision, robusthed og sikkerhed. Du udvikler de værktøjer, evalueringsmetoder og sikkerhedsmekanismer, der gør det muligt at vurdere, om en model er klar til operativ anvendelse. Du bliver en del af et tværfagligt miljø med en stejl læringskurve, hvor både nyuddannede og erfarne kan udvikle sig fagligt og bidrage med deres kompetencer. Rollen er for dig, der er nysgerrig på den nyeste AI-forskning, motiveres af at forstå, hvorfor modeller opfører sig, som de gør, og vil bruge din tekniske viden til at styrke Forsvarets opgaveløsning Dine Vigtigste Opgaver Modeludvikling og træning: Du træner, finetuner og tilpasser AI-modeller til Forsvarets opgaver og data, herunder sprogmodeller, multimodale modeller og modeller til sensor- og billeddata. items.desc: Company Description Get to know the Team The Data Science (Geo Vision) team focuses on improving maps and building map-based intelligence, including localization, routing, and traffic forecasting. We use Computer Vision, Information Retrieval, and Large Language Models (LLMs) to process diverse signals like images, text, and GPS probes. We are looking for an engineer who excels at building the scalable software foundations that power these advanced models. Job Description The Data Science (Geo Vision) team improves Grab's maps and builds map-based intelligence (localization, routing, travel-time, traffic forecasting) using computer vision and deep learning on images, video, and GPS signals. As a Data Scientist, you'll focus on bringing computer vision models to embedded/edge platforms for map creation. You will be working onsite and reporting to the Head of Data Science based in Cluj. What You'll Work On Help adapt and improve CV models (detection, segmentation, tracking) to run on resource-constrained edge devices. Apply model compression — quantization, pruning, knowledge distillation — to shrink models while preserving accuracy. Profile on-device performance (latency, memory, power) and help build efficient inference pipelines. Support training and evaluation, and use AI agents/tooling within the team's quality guidelines. What you'll gain: hands-on experience taking deep learning models to on-device deployment, plus skills in model optimization and real-time edge performance. Qualifications Pursuing or recently completed a degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or a related field. Familiarity with Python and some of: PyTorch/TensorFlow, NumPy, OpenCV, and scikit-learn. Solid ML and deep learning / computer vision fundamentals. Interest in or exposure to embedded systems, edge deployment, or model optimization (quantization, pruning, distillation) — a strong plus. Proficiency in English Additional Information Our Commitment We are committed to building diverse teams and creating an inclusive workplace that enables all Grabbers to perform at their best, regardless of nationality, ethnicity, religion, age, gender identity sexual orientation, and other attributes that make each Grabber unique.

items.desc: The AI Accelerator is a brand-new, London-based hub, within @computationalinnovation, comprising computational biology, human genetics, data and AI expertise. The purpose of the AI Accelerator is to provision production-quality, versatile, foundational biomedical AI capabilities that can be adapted and deployed to improve and accelerate portfolio decision-making, furthering understanding of the biology driving patient outcomes and identifying mechanisms that increase probability of success. To achieve this purpose, the AI Accelerator is organised around three key capabilities - AI Systems, focussing on neural methods, AI Reasoning, focussing on causality and knowing why, and AI Enablement, powering AI Systems and AI Reasoning with big data provisioning, MLOps and AI infrastructure. AI Systems will exploit neural-based methods to integrate data and impute and infer across the biomedical landscape. It could be electronic health records and medical imaging to support patient segmentation. It could be ‘omics data to understand gene regulation and identify novel therapeutic concepts; it could be predicting transcriptional change for a given disease-causing variant AI Reasoning will supplement AI Systems by focussing on developing approaches to identify cause and effect, predict the outcome of an intervention, provide a rationale for a model decision. It could be providing causal structure to multi-omics data; it could be providing orthogonal rationale to a black-box model generated hypothesis; it could be identifying features that are driving model predictions. AI Enablement will support AI Systems and AI Reasoning by provisioning harmonised multimodal data for distributed training, managing the model lifecycle and partnering with the IT organisation to ensure AI Systems, AI Reasoning and downstream beneficiaries have the necessary infrastructure and tooling to prototype, implement, adapt and deploy AI capabilities to advance the portfolio None of the above can be achieved without people. We are looking for AI scientists, machine learning engineers, research engineers, data engineers, MLOps engineers and AI infrastructure engineers from senior up to senior staff level and people leaders in AI science and engineering. If you are passionate about using your talents to build state-of-the-art AI approaches that will advance the portfolio and skilled in the required disciplines, please register your interest. Apply Now to register interest by joining our AI Accelerator talent pool. Please note that this is a talent community, not a particular recruitment process. There will be no follow up communication on this application. By applying you agree to being contacted by us, should there be a new opening in the future, matching your professional profile and/or interest in a particular position stated by you in your application form. Our Company Boehringer Ingelheim is a biopharmaceutical company active in both human and animal health. As one of the industry's top investors in research and development, the company focuses on developing innovative therapies that can improve and extend lives in areas of high unmet medical need. Independent since its foundation in 1885, Boehringer takes a long-term perspective, embedding sustainability along the entire value chain. Our approximately 54,300 employees serve over 130 markets to build a healthier and more sustainable tomorrow. Learn more at www.boehringer-ingelheim.com. Why Boehringer Ingelheim? With us, you can develop your own path in a company with a culture that knows our differences are our strengths - and break new ground in the drive to make millions of lives better. Here, your development is our priority. Supporting you to build a career as part of a workplace that is independent, authentic and bold, while tackling challenging work in a respectful and friendly environment where everyone is valued and welcomed. Alongside, you have access to programs and groups that ensure your health and wellbeing are looked after - as we make major investments to drive global accessibility to healthcare. By being part of a team that is constantly innovating, you'll be helping to transform lives for generations. Want to learn more? Visit https://www.boehringer-ingelheim.com

items.desc: We are excited to offer this opportunity to a highly motivated Research Associate to join an ambitious new team working in the field of Digital Endocrinology. The successful applicant will conduct original research aimed at translating understanding of endocrine function into precision medicine applications. The research will use data from wearable device technologies to characterise variability in circadian hormone profiles in humans, uncovering fundamental insights about endocrine rhythms that can be used to support the diagnosis and management of endocrine conditions. The position is funded through a UKRI Future Leaders Fellowship awarded to Dr Eder Zavala: “Developing a mathematical and computational framework for digital endocrinology”. The work will build on hormonal time series data collected at unprecedented time resolution in healthy humans and in patients, including studies in real life settings. We are seeking to appoint a creative and enthusiastic individual who will lead on computational data analysis projects that interrogate the mechanisms behind hormonal rhythm misalignment. The research will be closely integrated with mathematical models that predict dynamic responses to perturbations (e.g., stressors, sleep disruptions, diagnostic tests), as well as the long-term changes that occur during disease. A key challenge of your work will be accounting for the variability in hormonal rhythms observed across individuals. To characterise this variability, you will take advantage of unique in its kind datasets and advanced mathematical and computational methods and help develop personalised models. The practical element of your project will be based on, but not limited to, time series analysis, network analysis, Bayesian inference, Machine Learning, as well as computational simulation of mathematical models written in terms of differential equations. In addition to leading their own research projects, the appointed candidate will have the opportunity to contribute to the projects of PhD students in the group, as well as with an international team of collaborators including clinicians, computer scientists, and mathematicians. The team is dynamic and ambitious as well as being welcoming and supportive. The applicant should have high proficiency with scientific computer programming in Python, Julia, R and/or MATLAB, parameter estimation methods and HPC simulations. Experience with dynamical systems theory and mathematical modelling using ODEs and/or DDEs is desirable. The vacancy is for a full-time post available from 1st February 2027 until 31st December 2029. What you will get in return: Fantastic market leading Pension scheme Excellent employee health and wellbeing services including an Employee Assistance Programme Exceptional starting annual leave entitlement, plus bank holidays Additional paid closure over the Christmas period Local and national discounts at a range of major retailers As an equal opportunities employer we welcome applicants from all sections of the community regardless of age, sex, gender (or gender identity), ethnicity, disability, sexual orientation and transgender status. items.desc: Data Scientist Help build the AI and data platform changing how financial advice is delivered. Reporting to - Chief AI Officer Employment - Full time Location - Remote within the UK, with travel for team and customer meetings when required Eden Scott is delighted to be the retained search partner to Afternoon. About Afternoon Afternoon is building the operating system for modern financial advice firms. We are replacing fragmented systems and manual processes with one AI- and data-first platform that helps firms work faster, deliver better advice and serve more clients. At the heart of Afternoon is a genuinely difficult technical problem. We connect investment data from 27 platforms with client records, documents, meetings and communications, then use AI to turn that information into dependable, source-attributed outputs. Firms can prepare for meetings, capture and structure conversations, maintain client records, create complex advice reports and communicate with clients in one connected system. Our growth over the past year has been strong. We are working with a rapidly growing number of advice firms, have a live B2B partnership with a UK bank and are increasingly being recognised across the market. Afternoon won the lang cat's Advicetech Catwalk 2026, voted for by more than 150 advisers, and was named Professional Services Start-up of the Year for Scotland at the UK StartUp Awards. We were also selected for J.P. Morgan's Fintech Forward 2026 programme. We are well capitalised, ambitious and entering an important stage of growth. The team is still small enough for every new hire to shape the product, technical direction and company we become, while solving problems that matter to a large and established industry. The opportunity This is an opportunity to join Afternoon at the point where the product is proven, momentum is building and there is still enormous scope to shape our approach to AI. We are looking for a production-focused data scientist to help Afternoon understand and use information held across documents, conversations, client records and investment platforms. You will work on applied NLP and machine-learning problems where accuracy, evaluation, provenance and usability matter as much as model capability. This is not a research-only role and it is not about producing isolated proofs of concept. You will take problems from exploration and experimentation through to production, working closely with software engineers, product colleagues and financial-advice specialists. You will see customers use what you build and help establish the data-science foundations for the next stage of our growth. The role suits someone who enjoys messy real-world data, asks good questions and wants to build systems that users can rely on. What you will do Build and ship NLP and machine-learning systems for extraction, classification, retrieval, summarisation and structured generation, from first experiment to production. Work with LLMs, smaller task-specific models and deterministic methods, choosing the right approach for each problem rather than defaulting to one model or provider. Pull structured, source-attributed information out of complex financial documents and unstructured text, where every output can be traced back to where it came from. Design the evaluation that makes shipping safe: datasets, metrics and frameworks that surface failure modes in development and catch them in production. Own the pipelines behind the models, covering preparation, experimentation, training or fine-tuning, inference and monitoring, along with the reproducibility and experiment tracking that make results trustworthy. Work directly with engineers, product colleagues, advice specialists and customers: turning their problems into testable hypotheses, integrating models into product workflows through reliable APIs, and explaining plainly what works, what does not and why. What we are looking for Strong Python, and production code other people have had to maintain. NLP or machine-learning systems you have taken to production yourself, in some combination of transformers, classifiers, LLMs, named-entity recognition, embeddings and retrieval, built on pre-trained models and open-source tooling rather than from scratch. Evaluation you have designed rather than inherited, and a view on the trade-offs between model quality, latency, cost and maintainability. Work that has moved beyond notebooks into services other people depend on. The ability to explain a technical decision, and its limitations, to someone who is not an engineer. Initiative: comfort making progress through ambiguity, and the confidence to pull people in when you need them. Also useful None of this is required. Any of it would give you a head start: Structured extraction from documents that are as often scans and images as they are text, using OCR, layout-aware models or vision-language models. Fine-tuning with SFT or LoRA, and the judgement to know when it beats a better …

Working across international environments, we combine analytics, artificial intelligence, and business expertise to transform data into strategic value. Our mission is to help organizations evolve through innovation, scalable data platforms, and high-quality analytical solutions, fostering continuous learning, collaboration, and technological excellence. We are looking for a Junior Data Scientist with solid hands-on expertise in machine learning, natural language processing (NLP), business intelligence, data preparation, and MLOps to join our team in digital transformation initiatives supporting large-scale administrative, financial, and digital service domain platforms. The position requires strong proficiency in Python, R, and SQL, along with practical experience in machine learning libraries, ETL orchestration, and cloud/distributed data environments. ⭐ WHAT WE HAVE FOR YOU? 🚩 Remote work model (far-site delivery with occasional presence in Brussels if required). ⏰ Flexible working hours. 📈 Stable position with high-potential professional growth opportunities in international environments. 🚀 Continuous learning and upskilling in cutting-edge MLOps practices, NLP, AI governance, and advanced analytics. 💪 Integration into an experienced, collaborative, and multicultural international team. 💣 Participation in high-impact international digital and ICT projects. 💙 Inclusive and innovation-driven work environment. We combine first-principles thinking with cutting-edge technology to build a radically better energy system. We've raised over $200M from top-tier investors including Balderton, Lakestar, Accel, Creandum, Lowercarbon, Ribbit, 20VC, Hummingbird and Collaborative Fund, alongside strategic angels including Nico Rosberg and GPs behind Meta, Revolut, Spotify and Uber. We're building a fully integrated energy company: developing our own solar, batteries and other generation projects, building our own hardware, improving and developing grid infrastructure, trading power in real time, using AI across the business, and installing distributed energy in homes. items.card: Deine Mission & Herausforderungen Du besitzt das Outcome auf dem Roboter: Du treibst die Entwicklung kognitiver Robotics-Anwendungen durch Physical AI und die NeuraGym-Plattform voran — du besitzt das Outcome auf dem Kundenroboter, nicht nur das Modell im Repo. items.desc: Deine Mission & Herausforderungen Du besitzt das Outcome auf dem Roboter: Du treibst die Entwicklung kognitiver Robotics-Anwendungen durch Physical AI und die NeuraGym-Plattform voran — du besitzt das Outcome auf dem Kundenroboter, nicht nur das Modell im Repo. Führe die gesamte Pipeline aus: Du führst Foundation Models in produktionsreife Robotics-Intelligence über — die komplette NeuraGym-Pipeline mit Teleoperation, Data Annotation, Training, Simulation, Deployment und Validation — tailored auf echte Robotics-Anwendungen. Du definierst die Data Strategy und besitzt den gesamten Post-Training-Loop mit Hyperparameter-Iteration, Data Mixture, LoRA und ehrlicher Evaluation. Deploye zu Real-Time Control: Du bringst Policies vom Checkpoint zu Real-Time Closed-Loop Control — Distillation, Quantization, Action Chunking, Latency Budgets und On-Device/Edge Inference unter den Cycle-Time und Reliability Requirements des Kunden. Beherrsche den vollen Robotics Stack: Du arbeitest über NEURA OS und die Control Layer hinweg — Real-Time Control, Kinematics, Motion Planning, Force/Impedance Control und Safety Architecture — und integrierst gelernte Policies sauber mit dem Low-Level Controller statt ihn als Black Box zu behandeln. Hands-on System Integration: Du arbeitest direkt an MAiRA, MiPA, LARA und humanoiden Plattformen zusammen mit multidisziplinären Engineering-Teams — End-Effektoren und Tool Changer, Sensor-Auswahl und Mounting, Calibration, elektrische und Fieldbus-Schnittstellen und die mechanische Realität der Zelle. Aktiviere und unterstütze Kunden: Du leitest Nutzer in NeuraGym ein, reviewst Training Pipelines und Scripts, identifizierst Data-Quality-Issues, troubleshootst Model-Verhalten und bietest Hands-On-Support, um hartnäckige Blockers zu lösen. Cross-funktionale Zusammenarbeit: Du bist eine Schlüsselschnittstelle zwischen Cloud und AI Teams — du gewährleistest sanfte Zusammenarbeit, technische Alignment und effiziente Problem-Lösungen über Domänen hinweg. Baue Evaluation-Rigor auf: Du erstellst die Eval Harnesses, Success-Rate Benchmarks und Regression Tests, die entscheiden, ob eine Policy ready für Handover ist — und machst Failure Modes sichtbar, bevor der Kunde sie findet. Research in Production: Du prototypisierst Techniken aus aktuellen Papers zusammen mit unserem Research-Team und bringst die ins Produktionsdeployment, die Kontakt mit der Realität überstehen. Schließe den Feedback-Loop: Du übersetzt Field-Erfahrung und Customer Insights in Actionable Feedback für sowohl die NeuraGym Product-Roadmap als auch die NEURA Core AI Roadmap. Was du mitbringst Dein Hintergrund: Master-Abschluss oder PhD in Informatik, Robotik, Elektrotechnik oder verwandtem Bereich. ML in Robotics Tiefe: 5+ Jahre praktische Machine-Learning-Erfahrung in Robotics — stark in mindestens einer von Vision-Based Manipulation, Reinforcement/Imitation Learning oder Multimodalen Modellen, und motiviert, den Rest zu lernen. Fine-Tuning-Expertise: Nachgewiesene Erfahrung beim Fine-Tuning großer vortrainierter Modelle für Robotics oder eine andere Domäne: PEFT/LoRA und vollständige Fine-Tunes, Dataset Curation, Distillation und Evaluation. Vertrautheit mit dem Open-VLA- und Policy-Learning-Ecosystem (z. B. π0/π0.5, OpenVLA, LeRobot, Diffusion Policies) ist ein großer Plus. Programming-Skills: Solide Python-Kenntnisse (C++ ist ein Plus); praktische Erfahrung mit PyTorch oder TensorFlow. Cloud und Simulation: AWS-, Azure- oder GCP-Erfahrung und Vertrautheit mit Robotics-Simulation-Tools (IsaacSim, MuJoCo, etc.) sind Pluses. Robotics Software Stack: Working Command des Robotics Software Stack jenseits der Model Layer — Robot Operating Systems und Middleware (NEURA OS, ROS/ROS2 oder vergleichbar), Real-Time Control, Kinematics und Motion Planning, Force/Impedance Control und wie eine gelernte Policy in den Low-Level Controller und seine Safety Layer integriert wird. Hardware-Literacy: Solides Verständnis von Roboter-Hardware — Drives und Joint Modules, Torque Sensing und Encoder, End-Effektoren, Sensor-Integration, Calibration, elektrische und Fieldbus-Schnittstellen (z. B. EtherCAT) und Functional Safety Concepts — genug, um ein Model-Problem von einem Machine-Problem vor Ort zu unterscheiden. Execution-Mindset: Nachgewiesene Problem-Solving-Fähigkeiten, Fähigkeit, mehrere Projekte parallel zu handhaben, und ein starker Bias zu Execution und persönlichem Commitment. Du nimmst Deployments persönlich, arbeitest dich durch Rückschläge und misst dich daran, was beim Kunden läuft. Kommunikation: Klarer Communicator, der zwischen Forschern, Ingenieuren und End-Usern übersetzt. Du sprichst Englisch und Deutsch auf solidem Niveau (B2–C1). Reisebereitschaft: Bereitschaft, häufig zu Kundenseiten und NeuraGyms zu reisen (ca. 40–60%).

items.desc: We're building the UK's next generation engineering powerhouse, providing critical technology that strengthens national security and resilience. We specialise in turning advances in sensing, AI, and communications into operational capability for the edge, where connectivity may be degraded or denied. Our work focuses on accelerating the deployment of technology, improving decision-making for frontline teams, and protecting people and critical assets in demanding environments. Headquartered in Bristol, Rowden employs over 200 people and operates over 20,000 square feet of engineering and manufacturing facilities. Recognised in the Financial Times FT1000 as one of Europe's fastest-growing engineering businesses, there has never been a better time to join. Engineering Graduates at Rowden This is not a traditional graduate scheme built around a narrow role or a long, segmented programme. The Applied Graduate Programme is designed for engineers who want broad systems and product exposure, with real responsibility early and close engagement with end users and operational constraints. Engineering graduates work on deployable systems supporting defence, emergency services, and national security organisations, alongside engineers from multiple disciplines. You will join a rotational engineering programme designed to build technical breadth fast, supported by experienced mentors, structured feedback, and clear milestones. From the outset, you will be trusted with meaningful work and increasing ownership as your capability develops. Designing and testing system behaviour under degraded communications, including store-and-forward, prioritisation, and security controls. Deploying and evaluating machine learning models for edge use cases such as computer vision or signal processing, with a focus on measurable performance and operational constraints. Building future variants of deployable sensing and communications products, influencing how those systems evolve through hands-on engineering, integration work, and performance data. Shipping software that enables edge devices to be deployed, configured, and sustained at scale. How the Graduate Programme works You will complete several rotations before specialising within one of Rowden’s core engineering disciplines. The exact path isn’t rigid, we’ll shape it around your strengths, interests, and the needs of the business. About The Role Data is playing an increasingly crucial role at the frontier of AI innovation. Many of the most meaningful advances in recent years have come not from new architectures, but from better data. As a member of the Data Team, your mission is to ensure that the data used to train our models meets a high bar for quality, reliability, and downstream impact. You will directly shape how our models perform on critical capabilities. Working with world-class researchers on our pre-training teams, you’ll help turn fuzzy notions of “good data” into concrete, measurable standards that scale across large data campaigns. We’re looking for engineers who combine strong engineering fundamentals with a deep curiosity about data quality and its impact on model performance. Working Closely With Our Pre-training Teams You Will Own upstream data quality for LLM pre-training; as a specialist or generalist across languages and modalities Partner closely with research and pre-training teams to translate requirements into measurable quality signals, and provide actionable feedback to external data vendors In addition to human-in-the-loop processes, you will design, validate, and scale automated QA methods to reliably measure data quality across large campaigns Build reusable QA pipelines that reliably deliver high-quality data to pre-training teams for model training Monitor and report on data quality over time, driving continuous iteration on quality standards, processes, and acceptance criteria About You Strong engineering fundamentals with experience building data pipelines, QA systems, or evaluation workflows for pre-training data Detail-oriented with an analytical mindset, able to identify failure modes, inconsistencies, and subtle issues that affect data quality Solid understanding of how data quality impacts pre-training, with the ability to translate quality concerns into concrete signals, decisions, and feedback Experience designing and validating automated quality checks, including rule-based systems, statistical methods, or model-assisted approaches such as LLM-as-a-Judge Comfortable working autonomously, owning problems end-to-end, and collaborating effectively with researchers, engineers, and operations partners Skills And Qualifications Proficiency in Python and building ML / LLM workflows. items.desc: Physical AI can't be trained on internet data alone. Robots need to learn skills in the real world — by seeing, hearing and feeling real tasks in real environments. in real environments. That's the idea behind NEURA Gym : a global network of physical training centers where robots learn industrial tasks/skills directly from the people who know these processes inside out As Team Lead AI Engineering – NEURAGym , you'll lead the team responsible for turning that expertise into deployable robotic capabilities. Working closely with customers, you'll help capture domain knowledge, guide data collection and teleoperation, and oversee the process from training through to deployment. You'll lead a team of AI Engineers and act as the technical point of contact for partners as they bring new robotic applications to life. Success in this role requires balancing hands-on technical leadership with execution, ensuring that teleoperation, data pipelines, model training, and deployment come together as a reliable and scalable system. This role is well suited to someone who enjoys building real-world AI systems, working closely with customers, and seeing their work deployed on physical robots rather than remaining in research prototypes or demonstrations. Your mission & challenges Grow the team that makes NEURA Gym possible. Hire, coach, and lead a team of AI Engineers responsible for transforming partner expertise into deployable robotic skills. Own the technical relationship with NEURA Gym partners. Evaluate new use cases, determine technical feasibility, select the right algorithms, and define effective data collection strategies. Ensure the training pipeline runs smoothly end-to-end. Oversee the entire process from teleoperation and training through simulation, deployment, and validation, ensuring seamless execution across every stage. Be there when it matters most. Partner closely with on-site Robotics Engineers during live data collection and experiments, ensuring target behaviors are captured successfully while maintaining high safety standards in real-world environments. Provide hands-on technical support. Step in when the team encounters complex challenges, whether that's reviewing training pipelines, investigating data quality issues, or helping reproduce and resolve model-related bugs. Connect teams across NEURA. Serve as the bridge between NEURA Gym, Cloud, and Core AI teams, ensuring knowledge gained from one partner engagement benefits the broader organization. Help shape the product roadmap. Translate learnings from real-world deployments into improvements for both the NEURA Gym platform and NEURA's core AI capabilities. Measure what matters. Define and own key metrics such as skill success rate, time-to-validated skill, and data efficiency, using them to drive continuous improvement and team performance. What We Can Look Forward To A degree in Computer Science, Robotics, Electrical Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Strong hands-on experience developing machine learning solutions for robotics, with expertise in at least two of the following areas: Vision-based manipulation Reinforcement and/or imitation learning Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models, multimodal foundation models, or related embodied AI approaches Experience leading engineers, projects, or technical initiatives, either through people management or formal technical leadership responsibilities. Practical experience with machine learning frameworks such as PyTorch or TensorFlow, solid programming skills in Python. Experience with C++ is a plus. Confidence working with physical robotic systems and relevant robotics software stacks and middleware. Familiarity with cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, or GCP) and/or robotic simulation environments such as Isaac Sim or MuJoCo is advantageous. Track record of delivering complex robotics or AI projects from concept to deployment, with measurable business or technical impact. Strong communication skills and the ability to translate between researchers, engineers, and end-users / customers, and other stakeholders. Professional working proficiency in English; German language skills are beneficial.

items.title: AI/ML Engineer
items.card: What You'll Be Doing Build and ship AI features and systems end to end into live games and internal tools, at production quality and under real deadlines. Do the applied engineering that makes AI work in practice. Own evaluation as a first-class deliverable. Write and maintain the benchmarks, evals, and regression suites that tell you whether something is genuinely good, across the modalities you're working in.
items.desc: Our AI team is looking for an individual who is exceptional at the applied end of the craft: taking modern models and turning them into features and tools that hold up in production, at Supercell scale, under real deadlines. The challenge at the centre of this role is the distance between a demo and a product. A model that works in a notebook is not a feature that works for hundreds of millions of players, or a tool a game team trusts with their daily work. Help us Close that gap: the evaluation that tells you it's actually good, the latency and cost envelope that makes it viable, the failure modes you find before players do, and the plumbing that makes it boring to operate. We're not looking for someone who wants to train a frontier model. We're looking for someone who gets unreasonable results out of the ones that exist. We are looking for someone to build and ship: AI features in live games, and the internal tools that give superpowers to Supercellians. Some of that work will take you inside a game or central team for a while, close enough to their craft to build the right thing with them. In our team, you'll work closely with our AI Platform Engineers, AI/ML engineers, Clients Programmers, Cloud Engineers. You’ll also collaborate with other teams including Data, QA, Engine and game teams. What You'll Be Doing Build and ship AI features and systems end to end into live games and internal tools, at production quality and under real deadlines. Do the applied engineering that makes AI work in practice. Own evaluation as a first-class deliverable. Write and maintain the benchmarks, evals, and regression suites that tell you whether something is genuinely good, across the modalities you're working in. Fine-tune, adapt, and distill models where it pays off, and have the judgment to know when a better prompt, better retrieval, or a smaller model beats training anything. Make sound trade-offs on inference, including on-device where it matters, against real parameter, latency, and battery targets, without losing the feel players expect. Take on the harder applied problems, such as making autonomous agents reliable and accurate enough to trust with real work. Work close to game and central teams, sometimes embedded with them for a stretch, and build things that stay in use after you move on. Mentor our more junior AI/ML engineers through code review, pairing, and design discussion, and raise the technical bar around you. Stay at the frontier by reading the literature and following the major conferences, and bring back what is genuinely useful. What You Have Strong, current command of modern generative methods at the applied level: you know what today's models are actually good at, where they break, and how to build reliably on top of them. A track record of shipping LLM or generative AI applications that real users used, in production, not prototypes. We value this far above a publication record. Real software engineering depth. You write code others can maintain, and you own things in production rather than handing them off. Hands-on experience writing and maintaining benchmarks and evaluation frameworks, ideally across more than one modality. Practical fine-tuning and model adaptation experience, and the judgment to know when not to reach for it. Sound judgment on inference trade-offs under tight compute, latency, and cost constraints, including local or on-device deployment. The ability to work from broadly defined goals, set your own objectives, and drive work forward without waiting to be handed a spec. High EQ and credibility with makers. You can sit inside a protective, high-craft team and earn their trust fast. A generous mentor to less experienced engineers, with high ownership, comfort taking risks and learning from failure, and the humility to do excellent work with kindness. Would Be Nice if You Also Have Experience with agent frameworks, orchestration, or evaluation tooling at production scale. Game industry experience, or a real appreciation for mobile. Experience working alongside a platform or infrastructure team as an internal customer. Where You'll Be The role requires close collaboration with the other central teams and game teams, so ideally, you'd be based in Helsinki. That's it about the role! Below, we've gathered some things we feel are important for you to know. Totally optional, but a highly recommended read. Once you're ready to apply, just send us your application through the form on the bottom of the page. ––– About Supercell Supercell is a games company from Helsinki, Finland, with offices also in San Francisco, Seoul, Shanghai, and London. You might know us as the makers of Hay Day, Clash of Clans, Boom Beach, Clash Royale, and Brawl Stars . Our mission is to create great games that as many people as possible play for years and that are remembered forever. So, how do we make great games? By putting together the best teams and giving them the freedom and independence to succeed. And …

Knowledge of data preprocessing, feature engineering, model evaluation, and model lifecycle management. Experience with Databricks, MLflow, or similar machine learning platforms. Excellent communication skills and the ability to explain technical concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences. Preferred Qualifications Experience within semiconductor manufacturing, advanced manufacturing, or another highly automated industrial environment. Experience with computer vision, image analysis, or defect detection applications. Familiarity with cloud platforms such as AWS or Azure. Experience with big data technologies such as Spark, Hadoop, Apache Delta, Kafka, or Flink. Knowledge of data lakehouse architectures and modern data platforms. The work is aimed at use cases in robotics, AR/VR, gaming, and film. The team is small, and researchers and engineers work closely together on both the models and the systems that take them into products. About the Role This role owns the infrastructure behind the company’s training and evaluation of large diffusion-based generative models. That covers GPU clusters, storage, orchestration, and the path to model serving. It is hands-on and systems-focused. You will work directly with the researchers who use what you build, so priorities come from real training problems rather than a roadmap handed down to you. What You’ll Do Own and evolve the ML and cloud infrastructure used to train and evaluate large models Provision, scale, and maintain multi-node, multi-GPU environments on cloud and/or on-prem, including scheduling, quotas, and capacity planning Support distributed training (PyTorch DDP/FSDP, NCCL) and keep large runs stable, performant, and reproducible Build and optimize storage and networking for petabyte-scale datasets Deploy workloads with Docker and Kubernetes, and manage infrastructure-as-code with Terraform Set up monitoring, logging, and alerting for cluster health, job performance, and cost, and define SLOs and incident response practices Manage secrets, IAM, and network security across research and production Work with researchers to unblock training and support the move from research to served models What We’re Looking For 3+ years in infrastructure, platform, or cloud engineering Hands-on GPU performance debugging (CUDA/NCCL concepts, utilization, network bottlenecks, profiling) Strong experience running AWS, GCP, or Azure, including networking, IAM, and cost management Proficiency with Docker, Kubernetes, and Terraform Strong scripting and automation skills in Python plus Bash or PowerShell Familiarity with distributed training in PyTorch (DDP/FSDP or similar) Experience with observability tooling such as Prometheus/Grafana, OpenTelemetry, or ELK Experience building CI/CD for infrastructure and ML workflows Nice to Have Prior ML infrastructure experience supporting large-scale training Experience running on-prem GPU clusters alongside cloud capacity Experience with model evaluation and serving infrastructure Experience running on-call and incident response Why Join Ownership. You will be responsible for the infrastructure behind a research program, not one corner of a larger platform. Scale. Multi-node GPU training and petabyte-scale datasets are part of the daily work. Proximity to research. You will work alongside the people who depend on your systems. Influence. In a small team, your views on tooling and architecture carry weight. What to Expect This is an on-site role in London. Expect to work across the stack, from cluster operations to developer tooling, and to share responsibility for reliability. If this sounds relevant, get in touch for a confidential conversation.

items.desc:
AI Software Engineer - C++/Python
 Job ID 2026-19000 
 Date posted Sep. 01, 2026 
 Location Lund, Sweden; Manchester, United Kingdom 
 Category Software Engineering 
 Apply 
 About the Role
 We’re looking for experienced software engineers to help develop ExecuTorch, PyTorch’s framework for running AI models efficiently on edge devices.
 You’ll join a team building software across AI model optimisation, compilers, runtimes and hardware acceleration. Our technology spans Python developer tools and ahead-of-time compilation through to portable C++ runtimes and hardware-accelerated backends, giving you the opportunity to contribute at different layers of the software stack.
 A key part of this role is understanding how AI models execute on hardware, identifying bottlenecks and improving cycle count, latency, memory use and power efficiency.
 You’ll move between high-level model transformations and low-level runtime and hardware behaviour to solve complex performance problems.
 ExecuTorch targets Arm technology including Mali GPUs with Neural Graphics, Cortex-A and Cortex-M CPUs, and Ethos-U NPUs. We contribute to ExecuTorch in the open and work with the wider PyTorch community to help developers deploy AI models efficiently across mobile, embedded and other resource-constrained platforms.
 What You’ll Do
 Develop and optimise components of the ExecuTorch compiler, runtime and developer tooling, ranging from Python APIs and model transformations to low-level C and C++ components.
 Analyse and profile AI workloads to identify bottlenecks, improving latency, memory use, cycle count and power efficiency across model transformations, generated code, runtimes and hardware backends.
 Develop optimised backends for Mali GPUs, Cortex-A and Cortex-M CPUs, Ethos-U NPUs and other edge platforms, while investigating software and performance challenges across the stack.
 Identify technical opportunities and take solutions from initial idea through delivery, working with engineers across Arm and contributors in the PyTorch open-source community.
 Share technical knowledge and, depending on your experience, contribute to technical projects and mentor other engineers.
 What We’re Looking For
 We’re looking for professional software engineering experience using C++ and Python, including developing, debugging and maintaining production-quality software.
 You’ll have knowledge of programming, compilers, runtimes or performance optimisation, along with an interest in understanding how software executes on hardware and how its efficiency can be improved. An interest in AI and deploying models on resource-constrained devices will also be valuable.
 You should be able to identify technical problems, determine a practical approach and take work through to completion. The role also requires good communication, technical judgement and the ability to work effectively with engineers across different teams.
 You don’t need to meet every preferred qualification. AI and edge computing are evolving quickly, and relevant experience can come from different technical areas. If you’re keen to develop your knowledge and tackle new technical challenges, we’d like to hear from you!
 Useful Additional Experience
 Experience with PyTorch, ExecuTorch or another machine-learning framework would be useful, as would knowledge of ahead-of-time compilers, graph transformation or model optimisation. We’re also interested in experience with embedded systems, mobile or edge computing, hardware-accelerator programming, performance analysis, Vulkan, open-source development, technical leadership or mentoring.
 Why Join the Team?
 Help develop open-source AI technology used by developers around the world! You’ll have opportunities to build expertise across AI software, compilers, runtimes and edge computing while solving problems that connect software directly with the underlying hardware.
 The breadth of the role allows you to explore both high-level AI frameworks and low-level hardware optimisation, improving performance and power efficiency across a wide range of edge devices. You’ll also work with specialists across Arm and the wider PyTorch ecosystem, with opportunities to develop and share your technical expertise.
 We support different needs and ways of working. If you need reasonable accommodations during the recruitment process, please let us know and we’ll work with you to provide the support you need.
 Please note that no relocation package is available for this role.
 #LI-CM1
 Our 10x Mindset 
 At Arm, we believe progress happens when people are empowered to think bigger and push beyond what seems possible. Our 10x mindset is about curiosity, ambition and creating impact that will be used by millions. We learn fast, prioritise collaboration and turn bold ideas into real technology. We look for people who are inspired by this way of working and want to grow in an environment where bold ideas are welcomed. Discover how the 10x mindset shapes life at …

items.desc: Robot Learning Research Engineer | Paris Our client is a seed stage physical AI company based in Paris, spun out of one of Europe's leading robotics research institutes. Their software lets a humanoid robot learn a new industrial task from a handful of demonstrations and be working on the production line in under an hour, with no code. The software is hardware agnostic and runs across multiple humanoid platforms. It is already deployed with major European manufacturers in automotive, industrial equipment and consumer goods. The team is small and research led. The CTO is a world renowned researcher in robotics and machine learning, and the company combines the rigour of a research lab with the pace of an early stage startup. The role You will design the few shot imitation learning algorithms at the core of the product. The central challenge is data efficiency: learning robust, generalising behaviour from a few demonstrations rather than thousands. Every improvement you make ships directly into real factories. As one of the first 15 hires, you will help shape the company's long term research agenda, culture and hiring. Responsibilities - Design, prototype and evaluate few shot imitation learning algorithms - Advance the state of the art in imitation learning, policy learning and representation learning for control - Run rigorous experiments on real robots, including humanoids, mobile manipulators and industrial arms - Turn research prototypes into algorithms robust enough for production - Work closely with the Vision & Perception and Integration teams to take research from prototype to deployment - Help shape the research roadmap and future hiring Requirements - PhD in robotics, machine learning or a related field from a leading research lab - Research experience at a top academic group or industry lab - Publications at top venues such as CoRL, RSS, ICRA, IROS, NeurIPS or ICML - Deep expertise in imitation learning, learning from demonstration or policy learning for robots - Hands on experience training and debugging learning systems on real robots, not only in simulation - Strong Python and PyTorch - Professional English Nice to have - Few shot learning or meta learning for control - Representation learning for embodied agents - Experience with humanoids or other high DoF platforms - Postdoctoral or industry research lab experience - A track record of taking research into deployed systems - ROS 2 familiarity What's on offer - Open salary for the right candidate - Early and generous founding equity - Full relocation support to Paris - EU and non EU candidates welcome - English speaking team, no French required - Access to a fleet of advanced robots, including humanoids - Research that ships into real factories - Real ownership of the research agenda

items.card: Deine Mission & Herausforderungen Du besitzt das Outcome auf dem Roboter: Du treibst die Entwicklung kognitiver Robotics-Anwendungen durch Physical AI und die NeuraGym-Plattform voran — du besitzt das Outcome auf dem Kundenroboter, nicht nur das Modell im Repo.
