items.desc: Why this role is exciting Rohlik is the leading Central European e-grocer. More than a million customers buy their groceries from us through Rohlik.cz, Knuspr.de, Kifli.hu, Gurkerl.at and Sezamo.ro, choosing from over 17,000 items, delivered within a couple of hours in 15-minute windows. We are building the autonomous grocer. Maia, our AI assistant, already talks to customers and builds their orders; agents are moving into our buying and logistics; vision models are learning to watch quality. The next frontier is physical: robots taking over more and more of the work in our fulfilment centres, until fresh food moves from producers to households at a cost nobody else can match. We are setting out to record how our own people handle groceries and to turn those recordings into a training corpus for manipulation policies. Our warehouses already log what happened on every pick and every quality check, so the recordings can carry labels most datasets never get. Making that hold is part of the job. You decide what makes an hour of footage trainable — before we bank hundreds of them. What You Will Own And Deliver The capture spec. Cameras, mounts, calibration, and what disqualifies an episode. You write it before we buy the fleet and enforce it after. When the spec and the floor disagree, you go to the floor and find out which one is wrong. Ground truth. Hand pose is the signal that transfers from human video to robot policies, and warehouse reality — work gloves, occlusion, cold halls — is exactly where the published models struggle. You own how we measure that and how we close the gap. The evaluation harness. The corpus only counts if a policy can train on it. You build the harness that decides which hours make the bank, and you hold the trainability bar as the volume grows. The first training runs. Once hours bank, you post-train open robot-learning models on our data and run the first task evaluations. Judgment before spend. The field moves monthly. You read what is published, reproduce the claims we depend on, and steer our capture before the money is spent, not after. The scope This is a seat on a small, newly created team: an operations lead who runs capture on the floor, a data engineer who owns the pipeline, and you: the machine-learning voice in the room. This is not a research-scientist role, and no publication record is required. The job is to make a corpus trainable and to train the first policies on it. What We Are Looking For 3+ years of relevant full-time robotics experience. PyTorch, and computer vision with real 3D geometry. Camera calibration, pose estimation, SLAM fundamentals. You have debugged an extrinsic calibration at least once in your life and know why it drifted. You can read a paper and reproduce it. Our pipeline is assembled from published work, and your job is knowing which claims survive contact with a chilled warehouse hall. You know what policies train on. Familiar with the current robot-learning stack and policy classes well enough to know what the training side will demand of the data before the data exists. Dataset instincts. You have trained on data you collected yourself, and you know the failure modes that only show up at training tim.. Comfortable as the only ML voice. You make the call, write it down, and revisit it when the pilot data says otherwise. AI is how work gets done here. Our engineers use Claude Code and Devin daily, and we expect you to direct agents for the unglamorous parts — harness code, data plumbing, reproduction scripts — while keeping the quality bar exactly where it was. Particularly relevant. Hand-pose estimation or egocentric video in production; multi-camera rigs and time sync; experience post-training robot-learning models; ROS 2. What Success Looks Like In 90 Days You have written the capture spec and we set up the first rigs against it. Your pilot gates have numbers, the first hours have passed your harness, and you can tell the people who sign the budget, with data, what the next hundred hours should look like. Are we a good fit? Take this role if you would rather own the spec that decides whether a dataset becomes an asset or a write-off than tune someone else's model on someone else's data, if a fulfilment centre at 6 a.m. sounds like a lab to you, and if you want the shortest possible line between your technical judgment and a capital decision. Read our culture code and are we a good fit?. What We Offer The physical-AI side of the autonomous grocer, with the capture spec and the first training runs yours from day one A data asset few teams in the world get to build, in fresh groceries, a domain as hard as manipulation gets Off-the-shelf hardware, a managed cloud estate, and a mandate that has already started Benefits — see what we offer Are you in? Instead of a cover letter: pick a published human-video-to-robot-policy pipeline you rate, and tell us where it breaks on a warehouse floor where every hand wears a work glove. #Knuspr

Our teams work at the intersection of business and digital, partnering with clients like Polestar, Rijksmuseum, Nike and Hema, to drive measurable results across SEO, paid media, insights & analytics, AI and business consulting. Contribute to Curamando’s internal AI frameworks, playbooks, knowledge sessions and engineering standards. What do you bring? Experience integrating AI services (OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini, Meta and Fal.ai). Strong software engineering skills in TypeScript and/or Python, with experience building real backend systems and data pipelines. Proven experience deploying scalable applications in Azure, GCP or AWS, and running them reliably in production. Experience with Docker, CI/CD and modern DevOps practices, and the ability to move a solution from “it works on my laptop” to “it runs reliably in the cloud”. A pragmatic mindset, and the ability to judge when AI is the right tool and when it is not. The ability to turn vague client questions into concrete technical solutions. Strong communication skills and the ability to collaborate in multidisciplinary teams. Curiosity, creativity and enthusiasm for exploring new AI capabilities and patterns. Bonus points if you have: Experience with machine learning, computer vision, generative images or multimodal models. Experience as a full-stack developer. Experience in consultancy or client-facing environments. Please note: we don't hire applicants living outside the European Union. What do we offer? A flexible workspace in our studio in the center of Amsterdam or Rotterdam. We appreciate it if you are regularly present at the office, but it is also possible to work from home on a regular basis. A delicious daily lunch, chair massages, Friday drinks and company outings. Work with leading brands and ambitious clients in various industries such as automotive, retail, finance, culture and non-profit. An entrepreneurial and inspiring environment with plenty of room for your own ideas, initiative and experimentation. Significant opportunities for personal and professional development, with coaching and mentoring as core elements, supported by training and courses across the Eidra group. The chance to work for global clients and collaborate with colleagues across our offices in the Nordics, US and Germany, including an onboarding week in Stockholm to kickstart your journey. items.desc:
Join a team at the forefront of defending Apple's ecosystem. Our Data and ML Innovation team builds the large-scale machine learning systems that protect millions of users from emerging threats and ensure the integrity of our products.
We are looking for an experienced Applied ML Engineer who has a proven track record of shipping production models. The ideal candidate is passionate about tackling complex safety and security challenges using state-of-the-art techniques. In this role, you will design, build, and deploy the critical machine learning systems that are foundational to the safety of Apple's products, all while upholding our deep commitment to user privacy.
As engineer on this team, you will own the full lifecycle of our abuse detection machine learning models. You will collaborate closely with researchers to understand the threat landscape and partner with software and product teams to deploy robust, scalable defenses. We believe the most effective security systems are built by engineers who can translate adversarial insights into production-ready code. Your work will directly contribute to the architecture of Apple's AI platform and protect users from real-world harm. Here is what you will do:
Proven experience shipping machine learning models to production. You have owned the end-to-end lifecycle of a model, from development to deployment and maintenance.
Strong familiarity with research fundamentals, machine learning principles, and development methodologies around LLMs, foundation models, and diffusion models
Proficient programming skills in Python and deep learning toolkits (e.g. JAX, PyTorch, Tensorflow)
Ability to work with sensitive and offensive content as part of building robust security and abuse detection systems.
BS, MS or PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, or related fields or an equivalent qualification acquired through other avenues
Hands-on experience with fine-tuning or aligning large language models for security or safety applications.
Experience building large-scale data processing pipelines and ML infrastructure.
Experience driving technical projects and collaborating with large, diverse, cross-functional teams.

items.desc: Our Mission Reflection is a research lab making intelligence open and accessible for everyone to use, customize, and build on. We build open models that let anyone control their intelligence and help shape the future of AI. Our mission: make intelligence open and accessible to all. About The Role You will build the evaluation infrastructure that researchers use to understand model capabilities, guide training decisions, and assess readiness for release. The role spans evaluation authoring, distributed execution, and results analysis, with a particular focus on pre-training. You will work directly with researchers to make evaluations faster, more reliable, and easier to use, ensuring that the results accurately reflect the models being evaluated. Design and evolve evaluation abstractions. Build clear APIs and data models for evaluation tasks, datasets, configurations, model outputs, and scores, making it straightforward to add new evaluations and extend existing workflows. Build scalable, reliable execution infrastructure. Develop distributed systems for evaluating model checkpoints throughout training and ahead of release, with robust orchestration, observability, and recovery from failures. Optimize evaluation and inference performance. Profile inference servers and distributed execution to improve throughput, GPU utilization, and time to results. Establish evaluation correctness and reproducibility. Build validation and regression tests, version datasets and configurations, and preserve the provenance needed to reproduce results and investigate discrepancies. Build researcher-facing tools. Create intuitive interfaces and dashboards for inspecting model outputs, comparing checkpoints and experiments, and debugging unexpected behavior. Operate and monitor evaluations as training progresses. Track evaluation workloads and results, triage failures, and develop alerts and diagnostics that help distinguish changes in model quality from inference or evaluation issues. Turn research needs into reusable systems. Partner directly with researchers to identify bottlenecks, prioritize high-impact improvements, and turn bespoke workflows into self-service tools that work across teams. About You Strong proficiency in Python, C++, or Rust, with the ability to reason deeply about concurrency, memory behavior, and performance. Experience designing, building, and operating reliable, maintainable distributed systems, with sound judgment about interfaces, failure modes, and architectural tradeoffs. Working knowledge of model inference and evaluation, including how implementation and configuration choices can affect measured model quality. Ability to investigate complex problems across system boundaries, follow evidence, and identify root causes rather than just address symptoms. Strong product judgment and experience translating the needs of researchers or other technical users into clear APIs and usable tools. Comfort owning ambiguous problems end to end, prioritizing competing research needs, and balancing rapid delivery with long-term reliability and maintainability. Attention to detail and the persistence to investigate subtle discrepancies in model outputs, evaluation results, and system behavior. What We Offer We believe that to make intelligence open and accessible to all, you need to start at the foundation. Joining Reflection means building from the ground up as part of a talent-dense team. You will help define our future as a company, and help define the future of open foundational models. items.desc: Flexible batteries with seamless integration in textiles will revolutionize the healthcare system. Such batteries could power sensors to continuously monitor vital signals (e.g. glucose) and antennas to immediately transmit the information to a medical doctor when urgent action is required. However, such batteries need to be completely safe and non-toxic, as well as energy dense and lightweight; requirements that are often conflicting. The SUSTAIN programme grant (www.sustain-pg.org) will address this challenge using water, lithium and special polymer fabrics to build the batteries. Compared to traditional batteries that use toxic organic solvents and salts, the SUSTAIN batteries will operate using non-toxic lithium-conductive hydrated polymers that enable high deformability and stretchability. Via collaborative work with leading textile designers, experts in printed electronics and wireless communications and sustainability analysts, the SUSTAIN program will build working demonstrations of textile electronics that can act as wearable doctors. This post is suitable for chemists or materials scientists with a PhD (awarded or imminent) in chemistry, materials science or a closely related discipline or equivalent qualification and experience. Although the current funding for this vacancy is for 2 years, we expect to be able to extend the contract further, and there is flexibility about the start date. For informal enquiries about the project, please contact Prof. Nuria Garcia-Araez (N.Garcia-Araez@soton.ac.uk). items.desc:
The Amazon Web Services (AWS) Center for Quantum Computing in Pasadena, CA, is looking to hire a Quantum Research Scientist in the Fabrication group. You will join a multi-disciplinary team of theoretical and experimental physicists, materials scientists, and hardware and software engineers working at the forefront of quantum computing. You should have a deep and broad knowledge of device fabrication techniques. 
Candidates with a track record of original scientific contributions will be preferred. We are looking for candidates with strong engineering principles, resourcefulness and a bias for action, superior problem solving, and excellent communication skills. Working effectively within a team environment is essential. As a research scientist you will be expected to work on new ideas and stay abreast of the field of experimental quantum computation. 
Key job responsibilities
In this role, you will drive improvements in quantum device performance. This will require designing experiments to assess the role of fabrication processes and artifacts on performance metrics, ensuring the collection of statistically significant data through automation, analyzing the results, and preparing clear summaries for the team. Finally, you will work with hardware engineers, material scientists, circuit designers, and measurement scientists to implement changes, collect measurement data, and assess the impact.

If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.
Mentorship & Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

 Job Description 
 Job Description 
 As a Magnetic Resonance Research Scientist, you will:
 Apply deep knowledge in MR physics, mathematics, engineering and chemistry to conceptualize and prototype novel MR systems and applications that address key clinical needs.
 Develop impactful applications that leverage next-generation MRI sub-systems that have enhanced imaging capabilities. Examples are in high-performance gradient coils, RF coils, receiver sub-systems, gradient drivers, etc.
 Develop and deploy investigational MR applications and systems in clinical and preclinical environments for tests and validation.
 Determine the impact of systems hardware performance on image quality and safety.
 Develop algorithmic and/ or systems hardware solutions for MR-guided therapy and interventional applications.
 Grow external collaborations with academic and industry partners through joint publications, grant submissions and advanced technology development.
 Work with clinicians to refine emerging technologies for clinical applications.
 Create intellectual property by generating invention disclosures and filing patents.
 Maintain external visibility through conference presentations and peer-reviewed journal publications.
 Required Qualifications 
 Ph.D. degree in Physics, Electrical Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, Chemistry, Computer Engineering, or other related fields, with at least 3 years of research experience.
 A demonstrated record of research and development outcomes as evidenced by peer-reviewed conference proceedings and journal publications.
 Strong fundamentals in MR imaging physics and sub-systems, signal processing and electromagnetic theory.
 Demonstrated strong problem-solving skills, including the ability to understand and address root causes of MR image quality issues in investigational prototypes.
 Proficiency in programming in C, Python and/ or simulation tools.
 Legal authorization to work in the U.S. is required. You will need to have valid, on-going authorization to work in the U.S.
 Must be willing to work out of an office located in Niskayuna, NY.
 You must submit your application for employment on the careers page at https://careers.gehealthcare.com to be considered.
 Desired Characteristics 
 Demonstrated ability to originate and follow through on ideas.
 High levels of curiosity, independence and adaptability.
 Strong interpersonal skills.
 Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
 Experience in writing and executing grant proposals.
 Experience in developing or modifying components of MR sub-systems leading to measurable changes in image quality and new applications.
 Experience in EM and multi-physics modeling, especially for analysis of RF transmit and gradient field bioeffects.
 Experience in pulse sequence programming on a GE HealthCare MRI scanner and/ or developing new image reconstruction algorithms.

items.desc: About GF GlobalFoundries (GF) is a leading manufacturer of essential semiconductors, enabling AI at scale from the cloud to the physical world. Through deep partnerships with customers, GF delivers differentiated, power-efficient and high-performance solutions for high-growth markets. With global manufacturing operations across the U.S., Europe and Asia, GF is a trusted and holistic technology partner for customers around the world. GF’s talented, global team remains focused every day on security, longevity and sustainability. For more information, visit www.gf.com. Introduction GlobalFoundries is seeking a Principal Member of Technical Staff (MTS) – Software Engineering with a strong AI compiler architecture focus to join the Physical AI SW Engineering team in Eindhoven, Netherlands. This senior, hands-on technical leadership role will define and evolve the architecture for production-ready AI toolchains targeting heterogeneous compute platforms, including neural processing units, vector accelerators, CPUs and related embedded systems. Working across globally distributed compiler, runtime, kernel, verification, infrastructure, hardware, product and customer-facing teams, you will translate product and customer requirements into scalable interfaces, technical direction and executable roadmaps. Your Job Define and maintain the end-to-end architecture for AI compiler and toolchain capabilities across the Physical AI product portfolio. Translate product, model and customer use cases into compiler requirements, architecture specifications, interfaces, and prioritized technical roadmaps. Guide decisions across front-end model import, graph transformations, MLIR/LLVM-based intermediate representations, optimization, partitioning, scheduling, memory planning, code generation and deployment. Align compiler architecture with accelerator runtime, compute-kernel libraries, firmware, verification flows, and hardware architecture. Drive API and ABI consistency, portability and reuse across products while establishing clear extension points for product-specific capabilities. Lead architecture reviews, design reviews, technical risk assessments and proof-of-concept work for critical or novel features. Partner with engineering leads to decompose architectural direction into implementable epics, milestones and acceptance criteria. Analyze performance and quality gaps using representative AI workloads, then guide optimization across the full software and hardware stack. Collaborate with global teams, customers and ecosystem partners on integration, enablement, issue resolution and forward-looking requirements. Mentor compiler engineers and strengthen architecture practices, documentation quality and engineering standards across the organization. Other Responsibilities Perform all activities in a safe and responsible manner and support all Environmental, Health, Safety & Security requirements and programs. Required Qualifications Bachelor’s, master’s or PhD in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Applied Mathematics or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Extensive industry experience in compiler development, including senior technical ownership or architecture responsibility for complex software products. Strong knowledge of compiler design, intermediate representations, optimization, analysis, scheduling, memory management and code generation. Hands-on experience with LLVM and/or MLIR. Experience compiling for heterogeneous targets such as AI accelerators, NPUs, DSPs, GPUs, vector processors or embedded CPUs. Proficiency in modern C++ and Python, with the ability to prototype, review code and diagnose issues across system boundaries. Strong written and verbal communication skills and experience influencing decisions across distributed, cross-functional teams. Preferred Qualifications Experience with AI compiler technologies such as IREE, XLA or TVM. Understanding of AI frameworks and interchange formats such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, TFLite and ONNX, including graph conversion and deployment flows. Experience with performance analysis, benchmarking and optimization of compute-intensive workloads. Working knowledge of low-precision inference, quantization, tensor layouts, operator fusion and hardware-aware optimization. Familiarity with agile development, CI/CD, automated testing, build systems and collaborative engineering tools. Project management skills, including the ability to innovate, execute solutions that matter and navigate ambiguity. Strong planning and organizational skills. Expected Salary Range 94.348,80 € - 141.523,20 € The exact Salary will be determined based on qualifications, experience and location. If you need a reasonable accommodation for any part of the employment process, please contact us by email at usaccommodations@gf.com and let us know the nature of your request and your contact information. items.card: You will work at the intersection of machine learning, dynamical systems, fault diagnosis, and industrial process data , developing algorithms that learn from multivariate sensor data and reason about complex interconnected systems. Your work will span the full research-to-product cycle: formulating problems from real industrial use cases, developing and evaluating new methods, validating them on operational plant
items.desc: KIIO is building AI for AI for process reliability in chemical manufacturing and beyond. Chemical and process manufacturing plants generate enormous amounts of sensor data, yet troubleshooting remains largely reactive. Emerging problems can propagate across interconnected equipment and control loops long before conventional alarms reveal what is happening, while identifying the true root cause can still require hours or days of manual investigation. KIIO develops interpretable diagnostic technology that learns how industrial processes behave from operational data and detects when these relationships begin to change. By modelling the plant as an interconnected dynamical system, our technology identifies emerging faults, traces how disturbances propagate, and helps engineers understand where a problem originates, what may be causing it, and how to respond, without requiring historical examples of every fault. Our goal is to give process engineers and operators the intelligence they need to intervene before deviations become downtime, equipment damage, or quality losses. Role Description We are looking for a Founding Research Engineer to help turn KIIO's research into a robust industrial product. You will work at the intersection of machine learning, dynamical systems, fault diagnosis, and industrial process data , developing algorithms that learn from multivariate sensor data and reason about complex interconnected systems. Your work will span the full research-to-product cycle: formulating problems from real industrial use cases, developing and evaluating new methods, validating them on operational plant data, and translating successful approaches into software that can eventually run continuously in industrial environments. You will work closely with the founder, research collaborators, and industrial partners, and have significant influence over KIIO's technical direction and product architecture. Typical problems include : modelling complex and partially observed industrial dynamical systems; detecting subtle process deviations under changing operating conditions; localising faults and estimating their severity; distinguishing sensor, actuator, and process-related faults; reasoning about fault propagation through interconnected processes and control loops; building reliable evaluation and deployment pipelines for real-world industrial data. Qualifications We are looking for someone with strong technical depth and, equally importantly, the desire to turn research into something that works in the real world. Master's or PhD in Machine Learning, Computer Science, Control, Signal Processing, Applied Mathematics, Physics, Mechanical/Chemical Engineering , or a related quantitative field. Strong background in one or more of: fault detection and diagnosis, dynamical systems, time-series modelling, system identification, graph machine learning, signal processing, or control . Strong mathematical and algorithmic reasoning, with the ability to formulate ambiguous real-world problems rigorously. Experience developing and evaluating machine-learning or data-driven methods on real datasets. Strong programming skills, particularly in Python and modern scientific/ML tooling. Ability to write clean, maintainable software and translate research prototypes into robust implementations. Comfortable working with noisy, incomplete, high-dimensional sensor data rather than curated benchmark datasets. Interested in understanding why a system behaves the way it does , rather than treating models purely as black boxes. Comfortable working closely with process engineers and industrial partners to translate domain knowledge into technical solutions. Able to work independently and take ownership in a small, fast-moving team. Strong written and spoken English. Particularly relevant backgrounds include PhD researchers or engineers working on fault diagnosis, system identification, process monitoring, industrial AI, time-series ML, graph learning, or data-driven control who want to move from research toward building a real product.

items.desc: L'école MIRA est une 'école d'ingénieur·e·s, accréditée par la Commission des Titres d'Ingénieur et reconnue par l'État. Son équipe de recherche MIRA-Recherche, travaille sur la robotique interactive : elle étudie les usages pour intégrer l'IA, l'IoT, la robotique dans des interactions humain-machine utiles aux organisations (cobotique, jumeaux numériques, objets connectés). Le contexte Le poste associe des activités d’enseignement, de recherche, de formation professionnelle, d'animation d'ateliers et de représentation de l'école. Les activités pédagogiques. Les activités pédagogiques portent sur les programmes dispensés au sein de l’école. Les activités de recherche s’inscrivent dans le cadre d’un projet financé consacré à la transition des entreprises corses vers l'industrie 5.0 : une industrie qui associe robotique, objets connectés et intelligence artificielle tout en plaçant l'humain au centre des systèmes. items.desc: Job Details Section Electrochemistry Location: Highfield Campus Salary £37,369 to £45,641 Per annum Full Time Fixed Term for 2 years Closing Date: Monday 16 November 2026 Interview Date To be confirmed Reference 3526226EB Flexible batteries with seamless integration in textiles will revolutionize the healthcare system. Such batteries could power sensors to continuously monitor vital signals (e.g. glucose) and antennas to immediately transmit the information to a medical doctor when urgent action is required. However, such batteries need to be completely safe and non-toxic, as well as energy dense and lightweight; requirements that are often conflicting. The SUSTAIN programme grant (www.sustain-pg.org) will address this challenge using water, lithium and special polymer fabrics to build the batteries. Compared to traditional batteries that use toxic organic solvents and salts, the SUSTAIN batteries will operate using non-toxic lithium-conductive hydrated polymers that enable high deformability and stretchability. Via collaborative work with leading textile designers, experts in printed electronics and wireless communications and sustainability analysts, the SUSTAIN program will build working demonstrations of textile electronics that can act as wearable doctors. This post is suitable for chemists or materials scientists with a PhD (awarded or imminent) in chemistry, materials science or a closely related discipline or equivalent qualification and experience. Although the current funding for this vacancy is for 2 years, we expect to be able to extend the contract further, and there is flexibility about the start date. ABOUT MISTRAL

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.




THE ROLE

As a Research Software Engineer on the Sandboxes team, you will design, build, and operate the platform that runs isolated environments for untrusted code at massive scale. Our work spans distributed systems, low-level virtualization, and product-minded platform design. Engineers on this team move between deep infrastructure work and understanding how researchers actually use the platform.

This is a software engineering role, not an ML research role. You do not need prior ML experience; what matters is writing clean, reliable systems code that scales. You will join a small, senior team where the wrong hire is worse than no hire.




WHAT YOU WILL DO

 - Design, build, and operate the sandboxing platform that runs untrusted code at scale across multiple Kubernetes clusters, from our own bare metal data centers to hyperscalers.

 - Develop the sandbox runtime leveraging Firecracker, enabling fast startup, snapshotting, and efficient scheduling without blocking expensive hardware.

 - Obsess over performance and latency optimisation allowing us to reach millions of concurrent sandboxes.

 - Write robust, well-tested systems code in Rust and Python; review code, CI/CD, and observability across the platform.

 - Own cross-cluster networking, security boundaries, isolation guarantees and monitoring for suspicious activity.

 - Collaborate with researchers and ML engineers who use sandboxes for synthetic data generation and RL training, turning their needs into platform features.




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - A strong background in software engineering and distributed systems, with experience building and operating large-scale infrastructure.

 - Deep expertise in at least one of: Kubernetes and cluster operations, cross-cluster networking, observability, or low-level virtualization.

 - Fluency in Python or Rust; comfortable writing systems code where performance and security matter.

 - Strong software-design instincts: modular code, testing, CI/CD, observability, and a bias for reliability.

 - A self-starter who learns fast. Core skills matter more than specific tools — we value meta-learning ability and motivation highly.

 - Low-ego, collaborative, and comfortable with ambiguity in a small, high-ownership team.


NICE-TO-HAVES

 - Experience with Firecracker, microVMs, or similar virtualization technologies.

 - Product-mindedness: understanding of how sandboxes are used for synthetic data generation or RL training.

 - Experience with GPU clusters, CUDA, or ML workloads.

 - Prior SRE or platform engineering experience at scale.

 - Open-source contributions or widely used internal tools.




WHAT WE OFFER

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page https://app.notion.com/p/mistralai/Benefits-at-Mistral-36e6ba59a7fe836b93dd01737fcc27ef?source=copy_link.




PRIVACY POLICY

ABOUT MISTRAL

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.



As a Research Engineer on the Orchestral team, you will help build the agentic platform we use to train and evaluate our models. Orchestral is the system our researchers rely on to run training and evaluation at scale — from the rollout engine that powers agentic workflows to the infrastructure that keeps their workloads running reliably. What you build becomes the foundation the whole science team works on.

Your work will span the platform's core: the library, tooling, abstractions and rollout engine — including new capabilities like long-running tasks, subagents and RL features — and the machinery that runs data and jobs at scale, with a focus on resiliency, routing and request handling. You will own significant pieces end to end, from design to production.

This is a software engineering role rather than an ML or infrastructure-operations one: RL or PyTorch experience is not required, and you will spend your time building the platform, not operating it. You will be building a distributed RL system, with the scientists as your users.




WHAT YOU WILL DO

 - Design and build the core of the Orchestral platform: the library, abstractions and tooling researchers use to train and evaluate models.

 - Build and evolve the rollout engine, shipping new capabilities such as long-running tasks and subagents.

 - Run Orchestral as a production system: keep training and evaluation workloads reliable at scale.

 - Improve how data and jobs flow through the platform as usage grows — scheduling, routing and request handling.

 - Treat researchers as your users: understand their workflows and turn recurring needs into robust, shared tooling.

 - Raise the bar on engineering quality across the platform: testing, code review, CI/CD, observability and documentation.

 - Contribute to open-source rollout-engine and agent-infrastructure projects where it benefits the platform.




WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - Experience directly building and debugging complex distributed systems at scale, with an emphasis on reliability and scalability.

 - Strong Python skills and solid software-design instincts: testing, code review, CI/CD.

 - A builder mindset: you have constructed systems from the ground up, not just operated polished ones.

 - A track record in small teams running complex systems at scale — for example in finance, crypto or ad tech.

 - Self-starter, low-ego and collaborative, with a product mindset toward your users.

 - Curiosity about ML and RL — this experience is not required, but a desire to learn is.


NICE-TO-HAVES

 - Hands-on experience with Ray or similar distributed-computing frameworks.

 - Open-source contributions, especially to rollout-engine or agent-infrastructure projects such as SLIME, verl or PrimeRL.

 - Experience building or working with agentic workflows and environments.




WHAT WE OFFER

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

AI is one of the biggest opportunities we see for them, and it only works if the people in these companies actually use it. You work closely with us: you bring back what you see in the field, test new capabilities, and help shape the platform for all 55+ companies. You are hands-on. You are their technical backbone: when something needs engineering, you do it, and you make sure the next similar request is faster. What You Will Do Run the AI Hub for 10+ companies: deployments, updates, configuration, SSO with Entra ID, monitoring, backups and incident handling Onboard companies and teams: set up skills, knowledge bases and tools and get each company productive on the Hub Be the technical point of contact: when something breaks or a Champion is stuck, you diagnose and fix it. items.desc: At ZEISS Corporate Research & Technology, we work at the frontier of science and technology to identify emerging computing architectures and translate them into future technology opportunities for ZEISS. We are looking for a Research Scientist who understands accelerator architectures and fundamentally new computing concepts driven by the latest AI developments – from CPUs, GPUs and TPUs to custom accelerators, optical and analog computing, novel memory architectures and new forms of heterogeneous computing. The position combines strategic technology exploration with hands-on technical work. You will build targeted proof-of-concepts to validate promising architecture concepts, while engaging with startups, research groups and technology partners to understand emerging solutions first-hand, assess their maturity and identify the most promising approaches for ZEISS Your role Analyze AI computing systems end-to-end: Understand how training and inference workloads run on modern data-center architectures and identify the fundamental bottlenecks in compute, memory, interconnects and energy efficiency. Explore next-generation computing architectures: Evaluate established, emerging and fundamentally new concepts – custom accelerators, chiplets, in- and near-memory computing, optical and analog computing and heterogeneous systems. Build and benchmark proof-of-concepts: Translate architectural hypotheses into hands-on demonstrators and assess their potential quantitatively against the state of the art. Scout and recommend: Engage with startups, research groups and technology providers, judge maturity and differentiation, and distinguish fundamental technology shifts from incremental improvements. Your profile A university degree in computer science, computer engineering, electrical engineering with a focus on digital systems or computer architecture, or a closely related discipline. A PhD or equivalent research experience is welcome. Expertise in at least two of the following areas: computer architecture and systems; machine-learning systems and AI infrastructure; heterogeneous accelerators and emerging computing architectures. A systems-level understanding of modern AI technology stacks – training and inference workflows, numerical kernels, memory hierarchies, data movement, interconnects, accelerator hardware and system software – and the ability to explain where bottlenecks occur, why, and which architectural approaches can address them. Programming skills in Python and/or C/C++; experience with GPU computing, parallel programming, distributed systems, compilers, runtimes or HPC environments is an advantage. Curiosity and openness toward external technology developments, and the ease to engage directly with startups, research groups and technology providers, understand their approaches in technical depth and assess their relevance. An analytical eye for technology trends, the flexibility to revise your view when the evidence changes, and the ability to present complex topics clearly. Business-fluent English is required. Your ZEISS Recruiting Team: Friederike Kirklar-Harms

items.desc: Founding Robot Learning Engineer | YC-Backed Physical AI & Robotics Startup | London (Remote) | Full-Time | Up to £150K + Equity About the Company Our client is a Y Combinator-backed (S26) physical AI data company building the foundational human video and motion datasets for leading robotics and embodied-AI teams. Focused on egocentric first-person video and UMI demonstration data, the company turns real-world capture operations into high-precision, versioned data products that foundation-model and VLA teams rely on to train physical robots. Backed by a freshly closed seed round, their core constraint is supply, not demand. They are actively scaling deployment engineering, field operations, and capture hardware to keep up with massive customer demand. The founders are building a three-person founding engineering team to set the technical standards, tooling, and evaluation methodology behind the world's reference dataset for robot learning. About the Role Reporting to the Engineering Lead (and working directly with partners and founders), the Founding Robot Learning Engineer bridges human demonstration data and real-world policy performance. You will decide, with empirical evidence, what datasets the company should collect and how that data should be represented. This role balances hands-on data workflow engineering with policy experimentation. You will build task segmentation and assisted-labeling workflows, construct policy data loaders, and execute policy training and evaluation experiments using egocentric and UMI datasets to prove that the company's data directly improves robot task success. Key Responsibilities Turn long recordings into useful task intervals, define annotation schemas for specific customer needs, and ensure every label remains frame-locked to the source video. Deploy AI models to propose task boundaries and labels, route uncertain results for human review, write labeling instructions, and measure reviewer consistency. Build custom data loaders and transformations that format video, labels, and motion trajectories (including human hand motion and UMI gripper paths) into policy-ready inputs. Fine-tune and evaluate robot policies on human demonstration data, running controlled baseline comparisons, held-out split tests, and task performance evaluations under realistic test conditions. Translate policy evaluation insights into precise data recommendations—guiding perception and capture teams on which tasks, viewpoints, and annotations yield the highest policy improvement. Skills & Competencies Demonstrated experience training, fine-tuning, and evaluating robot manipulation or imitation learning policies (e.g., Diffusion Policies, VLAs, ACT). Strong Python and PyTorch capability with comfort building dataset interfaces, loaders, and annotation tooling alongside ML research. Deep understanding of evaluation leakage, dataset confounders, and the gap between offline loss metrics and physical robot task success. Experience working with temporal action segmentation, video annotations, spatial trajectories, and human-to-robot data transfer. Qualifications & Experience Background as a Robot Learning Engineer, Embodied AI Researcher, or Robotics ML Engineer. Proven track record of personally preparing training data, training or fine-tuning robot policies, and evaluating physical or simulated task performance. Hands-on implementation experience connecting dataset decisions directly to policy improvements, identifying confounders, and preventing data leakage. Background in physical robot manipulation, diffusion policies, vision-language-action models, or human-to-robot transfer is highly desirable. Role Details Timing: Immediate Start. Location: London (Remote). Package: Competitive base salary up to £150K + significant founding-engineer equity with absolute ownership over policy evaluation and dataset standards.

items.desc: Do you want to contribute to improving human health? To be a doctoral student means to devote oneself to a research project under supervision of experienced researchers and following an individual study plan. For a doctoral degree, the equivalent of four years of full-time doctoral education is required. The research group The Baranello Lab: Drawing from our expertise in the fields of topoisomerase and cancer biology, we aim to answer fundamental questions about how transcription, replication and DNA topology are functionally coordinated in human cells. We use state-of-the-art approaches to assess transcriptomic, epigenomic and topoisomerase activity profiles, as well as bioinformatics, advanced microscopy and drug screens to understand how topoisomerase regulation affects fundamental nuclear processes (key lab references: Baranello et al. Cell 2016; Wiegard et al. Molecular Cell 2021; Das et al. Molecular Cell 2022, Cameron et al. Nature Communications 2026). The overall aim of our research is to reveal novel cancer dependencies and develop new anti-cancer strategies more specific towards tumor cells and with fewer side-effects. We are a young and dynamic research team with a well-established collaborative network. The group is also associated to the laboratory of Dr. Levens at the National Institutes of Health in the US and Prof. Shirahige at the Institute of Quantitative Biology (IQB), Tokyo University, Japan. The successful applicant will thus be part of multiple networks of recognized scientists. The group is located in the Biomedicum, a top modern research building with a large repertoire of researchers and access to state-of-the-art infrastructure and facilities. Laura Baranello Lab The doctoral student project and the duties of the doctoral student Topoisomerases are essential enzymes that regulate the topology of DNA favoring replication and transcription by cleaving/resealing DNA strands. Because cancer cells have higher rates of proliferation compared to normal cells, they are highly dependent on topoisomerase activity. Therefore, strategies to target topoisomerases could provide a mean to selectively affect cancer cells. The focus of this research project is to understand how topoisomerases are regulated during transcription to develop new ways to target these regulatory mechanisms and affect the viability of cancer cells. Recent evidence show that topoisomerases execute their function through interactions with partner proteins that modulate their activity to affect transcription (Baranello et al. Cell 2016; Das et al. Molecular Cell 2022, Cameron et al. Nature Communications 2026). Using biochemical and molecular biology approaches, DNA and RNA sequencing, and advanced microscopy, this project investigates how the transcription machinery controls topoisomerase activity in physiological and pathological conditions, and how this regulation affects topoisomerase nuclear dynamics. The PhD includes several short research stays (~3 months each) in the lab of Prof. Mazza (Hospital San Raffaele, Italy), where the student will learn and apply key techniques for the project. The findings are expected to open new strategies for targeting topoisomerases in cancer therapy, offering the student broad training across molecular biology, genomics, and advanced microscopy in an international collaborative setting. The PhD program at the Karolinska Institutet corresponds to 4 years full time studies. The project is a combination of practical laboratory work (wet-lab work) and computational analysis (programming in R and/or Python). The program also includes attendance to seminars, courses, and conferences. The PhD student will plan and execute experiments, analyze data, interpret, and present the results as well as write scientific articles, initially under supervision but with greater independence going forward. At Karolinska Institutet, we conduct successful medical research and hold the largest range of medical education in Sweden. As a doctoral student you are offered an individual research project, a well-educated supervisor, a vast range of elective courses and the opportunity to work in a leading research group. Karolinska Institutet collaborates with prominent universities from all around the world, which ensures opportunities for international exchanges. You will be employed on a doctoral studentship which means that you receive a contractual salary. Employees also have access to our modern gym for free and receive reimbursements for medical care. items.desc: Join our Team About The Opportunity We are establishing a new AI-driven Digital ASIC research activity inside Ericsson Research. Our research thesis is that AI-driven design methodology is mandatory from day one — and that we drive the evolution of those tools rather than wait for it. The methodology itself is a research deliverable. This is a single-tier contributor role. Everyone works on the shared research threads, participates in challenge, and contributes to delivery. What differentiates contributors is the expert area(s) each of us brings to the team — the deep technical specialism that anchors our personal contribution. What You Will Do Drive the AI-driven methodology research deliverable: characterized AI-driven design flow, quantified PPA / lead-time / closure-effort deltas vs. a controlled traditional baseline, failure-mode taxonomy of AI-EDA tools, and the methodology playbook. Apply your expert area(s) inside the threads — both as the depth that makes the research credible, and as the lens through which you characterize AI-driven tooling at your part of the chain. Contribute to the controlled traditional baseline in your area(s) — without the baseline anchor, the team's PPA and lead-time claims aren't falsifiable. Co-design across the chain. The boundary between architecture, RTL, verification, physical design, test and packaging is fluid here; contributors are expected to engage beyond their primary area. Engage with Ericsson's product organizations, tool vendors and external research partners as the work and the rotation calls for it. Maintain cross-site presence (Lund / Lindholmen). Contribute openly to the team's culture. Work on shared research threads — typically 2–3 active at any time. Take rotating turns on delivery lead and operations. The Skills You Bring Genuine enthusiasm for AI-driven design and confidence that AI-assisted methods are the right direction for silicon and systems. Demonstrated depth in at least one primary expert area, with working competence in one or two adjacent areas, evidenced through tape-outs, open-source contributions, publications, hands-on projects, joint academic roles, or comparable experience. Typical expert areas include: Software, SW architecture, SW stack and low-level drivers EDA tools and design environment CPU architecture, compute architecture, packet routing, accelerators DSP, signal chains, hardware-efficient algorithms, AI accelerators Verification — model to RTL, RTL to gates, SW emulator RTL implementation — model to RTL, RTL to gates Physical design — P&R, low power ASIC production test Packaging, chiplet, integration, interfaces, DC-DC power Comfort with a peer-led, one-tier research culture: you challenge and accept challenge openly, and align once decisions are made. Ability to work in a cross-site rhythm (regular remote sessions, periodic co-location, strong async collaboration). Strong curiosity and rigour, treating methodology evolution as part of the research, and willingness to work beyond your core discipline when the problem demands it. Why join Ericsson? At Ericsson, you´ll have an outstanding opportunity. The chance to use your skills and imagination to push the boundaries of what´s possible. To build solutions never seen before to some of the world’s toughest problems. You´ll be challenged, but you won’t be alone. You´ll be joining a team of diverse innovators, all driven to go beyond the status quo to craft what comes next. What happens once you apply? We truly believe that by collaborating with people with different experiences we drive innovation, which is essential for our future growth. Build and benchmark proof-of-concepts: Translate architectural hypotheses into hands-on demonstrators and assess their potential quantitatively against the state of the art. Scout and recommend: Engage with startups, research groups and technology providers, judge maturity and differentiation, and distinguish fundamental technology shifts from incremental improvements. Your profile A university degree in computer science, computer engineering, electrical engineering with a focus on digital systems or computer architecture, or a closely related discipline. A PhD or equivalent research experience is welcome. Expertise in at least two of the following areas: computer architecture and systems; machine-learning systems and AI infrastructure; heterogeneous accelerators and emerging computing architectures. A systems-level understanding of modern AI technology stacks – training and inference workflows, numerical kernels, memory hierarchies, data movement, interconnects, accelerator hardware and system software – and the ability to explain where bottlenecks occur, why, and which architectural approaches can address them. Programming skills in Python and/or C/C++; experience with GPU computing, parallel programming, distributed systems, compilers, runtimes or HPC environments is an advantage. Curiosity and openness toward external technology developments, and the ease to engage directly with startups, research groups and technology providers, understand their approaches in technical depth and assess their relevance. An analytical eye for technology trends, the flexibility to revise your view when the evidence changes, and the ability to present complex topics clearly. Business-fluent English is required. items.desc: AI-udvikler søges til Dansk Center for Partikelterapi, AUH, Dansk Center for Partikelterapi (DCPT) søger en fysiker, hospitalsfysiker, datalog, softwareingeniør eller lignende profil til softwareudvikling inden for adaptiv protonterapi. DCPT er et nationalt center, der giver strålebehandling med protonterapi. Vores mission er at levere protonterapi af højest mulig kvalitet til alle relevante danske kræftpatienter. Alle vores udviklingsopgaver er forankret i brede tværfaglige, lokale, nationale og/eller internationale udviklings- og forskningsgrupper. I denne nyoprettede stilling er der fokus på at løse de kliniske behov bl.a. gennem forskning, som bliver en vigtig del af din dagligdag. Du vil blive tilknyttet gruppen af fysikere og dosimetrister, hvis driftsopgave er at planlægge individuelle protonbehandlinger og kvalitetssikre behandlinger og tilhørende udstyr. Gruppen udvikler behandlingsteknikker i tæt samarbejde med læger, sygeplejersker, radiografer, m.fl., samt de ansatte i vores forskningsafdeling. DCPT har udviklet kunstig intelligens til at forbedre billedkvaliteten af de billeder vi anvender til at adaptere patientbehandlingen, samt til segmentering af medicinske billeder. Vi ønsker at styrke denne indsats og målrette den mod udviklingen af adaptiv protonterapi, hvor den individuelle tilpasning af behandlingen sker hurtigere og på daglig basis. Det er afgørende, at du har følgende kompetencer solid erfaring med maskinlæring og deep learning anvendt på billeddata - gerne 3D medicinsk billedbehandling: segmentering, registrering eller billede-til-billede-modeller rutine i PyTorch eller tilsvarende, og erfaring med at træne, evaluere og fejlsøge modeller på virkelige datasæt håndværksmæssig disciplin i kodning: versionsstyring, test, dokumentation og kodegennemgang. Du skal kunne bygge noget, som andre end dig selv kan overtage og videreudvikle evnen til at arbejde tæt sammen med fysikere og klinikere, og til at sætte dig ind i et domæne du ikke selv er uddannet i. Derudover er det en fordel, hvis du har kendskab til medicinsk billedbehandling i praksis: DICOM og DICOM-RT, strålebehandlingsplanlægning, scripting mod et planlægningssystem erfaring med at drifte modeller i produktion: containere, inferensservere, versionering af modeller og data og overvågning serverdrift og databaser kendskab til softwareudvikling under EU's forordning om medicinsk udstyr, herunder undtagelsen for egenudviklet software, samt kvalitetssystemer, risikostyring og validering baggrund som fysiker eller erfaring fra stråleterapi. Med ansættelse ved DCPT skal du være indstillet på at kunne brede dig ud over flere forskelligartede opgaver, der vil veksle mellem udviklingsopgaver og driftsorienterede opgaver. Din opgave- og projektportefølje vil udvikle sig over tid, og afhængigt af dine kompetencer vil den komme til at indeholde forskning, udvikling og drift. Uanset hvor vægten kommer til at ligge, skal du konstruktivt, effektivt og aktivt kunne indgå i samarbejder med forskere og klinikere kunne sætte dig ind i brugeres og domænets behov være ambitiøs og have lyst til at fuldføre dit arbejde med både praktiske og akademiske resultater være indstillet på at løse mangeartede opgaver. Det forventes, at du i samarbejde med DCPT's øvrige akademiske medarbejdere deltager aktivt i forsknings- og udviklingsopgaver. Du kommer til at indgå i et tværfagligt miljø med fysikere, læger, sygeplejersker, radiografer og andre, der ligeledes arbejder for at udvikle teknologi og klinisk udnyttelse af protonterapi. Er du kandidat, der opfylder indgangskrav til uddannelse som hospitalsfysiker, så vil centeret tilbyde dig uddannelsen. Hvis ikke, vil vi tilbyde lignende skræddersyet uddannelse og træning. For yderligere information om stillingerne kontakt hospitalsfysiker, lektor Jesper Kallehauge på mail jespkall@rm.dk eller cheffysiker Ole Nørrevang på tlf. 2117 4193. Bemærk at Jesper Kallehauge ikke er tilgængelig for yderligere information før efter den 27. oktober. Stillingen er som udgangspunkt en fuldtidsstilling. Da Region Midtjylland løbende gennemfører besparelser og omorganiseringer, vil medarbejdere i omplacering, der søger stillingen, have fortrinsret. Region Midtjylland er jf. EU’s løngennemsigtighedsdirektiv, der trådte i kraft 7. juni 2026 forpligtet til at oplyse dig om startløn eller et interval for startløn for en stilling inden du tilbydes ansættelse. Her finder du Region Midtjyllands lønkatalog for de fleste faggrupper og stillinger, som findes i Region Midtjylland: Gennemsigtighed forud for ansættelse - Medarbejder.rm.dk

items.desc: Dans le cadre du laboratoire commun "AI-Native Communications" lancé par Orange et le CEA, dédié à la recherche sur les communications sémantiques pour les réseaux 6G et futurs, nous recherchons un ingénieur en communication sémantique 6G . Ce programme vise à concevoir des réseaux plus intelligents, sobres et efficaces, en intégrant de nouvelles approches où le sens de l’information prime sur la transmission exacte des données. Intégré dans le Service Technologies Sans Fil (STSF) et sous la responsabilité du chef de projet, vous aurez pour principales missions de : Concevoir et valider des algorithmes novateurs destinés aux futurs standards 6G, avec un focus spécifique sur les communications sémantiques. Développer des méthodes et solutions visant à optimiser les performances des systèmes, tout en respectant des contraintes strictes en matière: d’efficacité énergétique, de consommation des ressources réseau, Piloter la mise en œuvre d’une plateforme numérique de validation, intégrant :l’interfaçage de chaînes de traitement (Python/Matlab) avec des plateformes matérielles et logicielles haut de gamme, la validation expérimentale des concepts développés, dans un contexte représentatif des communications 6G. Profil du candidat Vous êtes diplômé d'un Master of Science (ou équivalent) en traitement numérique du signal, communications sans fil, ou domaine connexe. Dans l'idéal vous disposez d'un doctorat dans l'un de ces domaines. items.desc: Job Description Position Details School of Engineering University of Birmingham, Edgbaston, Birmingham UK As this vacancy has limited funding the maximum salary that can be offered is Grade 7, salary £36,636 Grade: 7 Full Time, Fixed Term contract up to October 2027 Closing date: 25th October 2026 Background To create and contribute to the creation of knowledge by undertaking a specified range of activities within an established research programme and/or specific research project. This Research Fellow position is based in the Department of Mechanical Engineering at the University of Birmingham and will support an industry-funded research project focused on engines operating on non-fossil fuels and their integration into hybrid electric vehicle powertrains. The research will involve engine modelling and simulation, intelligent control strategy development, and data-driven calibration, applying AI and optimisation techniques, including machine learning and metaheuristic algorithms, to improve engine performance and efficiency and reduce emissions. Control strategies will be implemented and validated using Pi OpenECU and Cosworth ECU platforms, supported by engine test bench experiments. The project will also address hybrid powertrain development, including engine–electric motor integration, coordinated torque control, and energy management optimisation, in close collaboration with industrial partners. Summary Of Role Develop and apply AI and optimisation techniques, including machine learning and metaheuristic algorithms, to engine modelling, intelligent control strategy development, and data-driven calibration for engines operating on non-fossil fuels. Conduct engine test bench experiments, analyse experimental data, and implement and validate engine control strategies using Pi OpenECU and Cosworth ECU platforms. Contribute to hybrid powertrain development, including engine–electric motor integration, coordinated torque control, and energy management optimisation to improve efficiency and reduce emissions. Develop and validate vehicle-level torque distribution control strategies to optimise traction, vehicle stability, and energy efficiency. Work closely with industrial collaborators, support student supervision, and contribute to research publications, technical reports, and funding applications. Main Duties The responsibilities may include some but not all of the responsibilities outlined below. Develop research objectives and methodologies for engine modelling, intelligent control, and calibration for engines operating on non-fossil fuels. Develop, calibrate, and validate engine, powertrain, and vehicle models using tools such as AVL CRUISE, IPG CarMaker, and MATLAB/Simulink, supported by experimental data and system identification methods. Investigate the effects of non-fossil fuels on combustion characteristics, engine performance, fuel consumption, and emissions through modelling and engine test bench experiments. Develop and apply Artificial Intelligence and optimisation techniques, including machine learning and metaheuristic algorithms, to data-driven engine modelling, intelligent control strategy development, and automated calibration. Implement, test, and calibrate engine control strategies using Pi OpenECU and Cosworth ECU platforms, including sensor and actuator integration, CAN communication, and data acquisition. Plan and conduct engine test bench experiments under steady-state and transient conditions representative of real-world driving cycles, and analyse experimental data to refine models and control strategies. Contribute to hybrid powertrain development, including system integration, coordinated torque control, and energy management optimisation to improve efficiency and reduce emissions. Develop and validate vehicle-level torque distribution control strategies to improve traction, vehicle stability, and energy efficiency using learning-based methods. Support related experimental research in fuel sprays, combustion, and proton exchange membrane (PEM) fuel cells. Contribute to research funding applications, technical reports, and project deliverables. Disseminate research findings through publications, presentations, and seminars. Provide technical support and training to PhD students working on related research topics. Work closely with academic and industrial partners to coordinate research activities, review progress, and deliver project objectives. Participate in public engagement, enterprise, and knowledge transfer activities as required. These indicative responsibilities may also be included in a research role at grade 6. Person Specification A PhD (or thesis submitted) in Mechanical Engineering, Automotive Engineering, or a closely related discipline. Solid experience in engine modelling, simulation, and calibration using IPG CarMaker, AVL tools, or MATLAB/Simulink, with knowledge of non-fossil fuels. items.desc: About Mistral Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms. We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited. As a Research Engineer on the Orchestral team, you will help build the agentic platform we use to train and evaluate our models. Orchestral is the system our researchers rely on to run training and evaluation at scale — from the rollout engine that powers agentic workflows to the infrastructure that keeps their workloads running reliably. What you build becomes the foundation the whole science team works on. Your work will span the platform's core: the library, tooling, abstractions and rollout engine — including new capabilities like long-running tasks, subagents and RL features — and the machinery that runs data and jobs at scale, with a focus on resiliency, routing and request handling. You will own significant pieces end to end, from design to production. This is a software engineering role rather than an ML or infrastructure-operations one: RL or PyTorch experience is not required, and you will spend your time building the platform, not operating it. You will be building a distributed RL system, with the scientists as your users. What You Will Do Design and build the core of the Orchestral platform: the library, abstractions and tooling researchers use to train and evaluate models. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms. We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited. As a Research Engineer on the Orchestral team, you will help build the agentic platform we use to train and evaluate our models. Orchestral is the system our researchers rely on to run training and evaluation at scale — from the rollout engine that powers agentic workflows to the infrastructure that keeps their workloads running reliably. What you build becomes the foundation the whole science team works on. Your work will span the platform's core: the library, tooling, abstractions and rollout engine — including new capabilities like long-running tasks, subagents and RL features — and the machinery that runs data and jobs at scale, with a focus on resiliency, routing and request handling. You will own significant pieces end to end, from design to production. This is a software engineering role rather than an ML or infrastructure-operations one: RL or PyTorch experience is not required, and you will spend your time building the platform, not operating it. You will be building a distributed RL system, with the scientists as your users. What You Will Do Design and build the core of the Orchestral platform: the library, abstractions and tooling researchers use to train and evaluate models. Build and evolve the rollout engine, shipping new capabilities such as long-running tasks and subagents. Treat researchers as your users: understand their workflows and turn recurring needs into robust, shared tooling. items.desc: Description De L'entreprise Ubisoft est une référence mondiale du jeu vidéo, avec des équipes réparties aux quatre coins du monde qui créent des expériences de jeu originales et mémorables, de Assassin’s Creed à Rainbow Six en passant par Just Dance et bien d’autres encore. Nous croyons que la diversité des points de vue fait progresser à la fois les joueurs et les équipes. Si vous êtes passionné·e par l’innovation et que vous souhaitez repousser les limites du divertissement, rejoignez notre aventure et aidez-nous à créer l’inconnu ! Studio pionnier d’Ubisoft, le studio de Paris est à l’origine des premiers succès de l’éditeur suite à sa création en 1992. Il est aujourd’hui à la tête de licences incontournables comme Just Dance, Ghost Recon ou Mario + The Lapins Crétins. Ubisoft Paris s’est également construit une solide réputation comme partenaire de choix dans les collaborations inter-studios comme Watch Dogs, Skull & Bones, Beyond Good & Evil 2 ou encore Star Wars. Fort de cette expérience, le studio continue d’aller plus loin en termes de créativité en travaillant sur des projets très prometteurs encore non-annoncés. Regroupant 750 talents de 35 nationalités, Ubisoft Paris est aujourd’hui le plus grand studio de France et l’un des plus expérimentés de l’industrie. Les jeunes talents peuvent bénéficier de la présence importante de profils seniors, dans les métiers créatifs, techniques ou artistiques. Chacun·e reste animé·e par la même passion : repousser les limites du possible et proposer de nouvelles expériences à nos joueurs et joueuses. Prêt·es à rallier l’aventure ? Rejoignez-nous au Studio de Paris ! Description Du Poste En nous rejoignant sur ce poste, vous intégrerez une équipe multidisciplinaire (data, programmation, game & narrative design, animation, etc.), guidée par une question simple et ambitieuse : parmi toutes les possibilités offertes par l’IA générative, lesquelles sont réellement intéressantes et fun pour le gameplay ? L’équipe a pour mission de tester de nouvelles expériences auprès de joueurs et joueuses, et d’équiper les créateur·rices pour imaginer des interactions plus dynamiques, immersives et surprenantes — jusqu’à faire émerger des features impossibles à réaliser autrement. Son quotidien s’inscrit à la croisée de la R&D, du développement produit, de la création de jeux courts et de la collaboration multi-studios, au service des gameplays de demain. Au sein de l’équipe responsable de l’analyse des données et des projets data science, détachée dans une production de jeu vidéo, vous apportez vos connaissances en Machine Learning et en analyse de données en général aux équipes de développement afin d’exploiter le potentiel de l’Intelligence Artificielle au sein du design de nos jeux. Vos missions seront les suivantes : Contribuer à la faisabilité technique des systèmes gameplay basés sur l’IA. Identifier des algorithmes pertinents (génératifs, information retrieval, classification…) et les adapter pour un usage production (fine-tuning, optimisation, intégration). Mettre en place les processus d’évaluation pertinents Déployer ces algorithmes sur des cloud internes ou externes de manière robuste et scalable, en suivant les meilleurs pratiques en terme de développement et de MLOps, en collaboration avec les ingénieurs du projets Implémenter des techniques à partir de papiers de recherche dans une démarche d'innovation/R&D Qualifications Vous disposez d’une première expérience significative en tant que Machine Learning Engineer et avez mis en production différents algorithmes de Generative AI, Vous avez une connaissance poussée des algorithmes de NLP (comme SentenceBERT, Llama 2, Mistral ou Qwen 3) et vous savez les fine-tuner, Vous avez une bonne maitrise de Python et de Tensorflow ou PyTorch, Vous avez une première expérience avec Docker, Le jeu vidéo est une passion pour vous, Votre très bonne capacité d’écoute et de compréhension vous permet de traduire facilement les besoins des clients en spécifications, Vous êtes en mesure d’adapter vos analyses et votre discours pour atteindre un large public, Vous faites preuve d’autonomie et de curiosité. Enfin, votre aisance en anglais vous permet d’échanger à l’écrit comme à l’oral avec des interlocuteurs variés. Ce sont des + : Vous avez une bonne maitrise du C++, C# ou Rust Vous savez comment utiliser des LLM (du prompt engineering aux approches plus complexes comme Tree of Thoughts) Vous savez comment optimiser la taille et le temps d’inférence des modèles (ex : quantization, LoRA…) Vous avez une affinité avec les jeux de rôle, les jeux narratifs... Informations supplémentaires En tant qu’employeur, Ubisoft offre à tous les mêmes opportunités d’accès à l’emploi, sans distinction notamment de genre, ethnicité, religion, orientation sexuelle, statut social, handicap et d’âge. Ubisoft veille à développer un environnement de travail inclusif qui reflète la diversité de sa communauté de joueurs dans ses équipes.
