items.desc: Applications are invited for a research fellowship focused upon how people and AI can and should work together in a collaborative partnership. The fellowship is jointly hosted by the University of Manchester, Manchester Metropolitan University and the University of Salford, and supported by the UK Government. The fellowship is initially through until March 2028, with the possibility of an extension. Applicants are requested to submit a brief research proposal addressing the topic of human-AI collaboration with their application. If successful they will be required to revise this proposal, in consultation with colleagues from UK Government, both to address government priorities and to improve the fit of the proposal with the demands of the National Security context, where advances in AI capability could give significant efficiency gains but must be balanced against a strong regulatory regime. Some of the research will assume a standard academic form and fellows will be expected to pursue publication in relevant academic journals, subject to approval from the government sponsor. Some may be classified and intended for use by UK Government and their partner organisations only. Fellows will therefore gain experience of two very different research environments and of negotiating the complexities of working between them. The Fellow will have a base within one of the partner universities. They will have mentors both within their University and UK Government, to offer guidance and support. Mentors from the organisations will work together to ensure coherence and consistency in their advice and support. Fellows will be required to be in Manchester several days a week and so are expected either to be located in the North-West or willing to relocate. Applicants should have completed or at least submitted a relevant PhD and have expertise in computer science, AI, machine learning and/or an intersection of those fields. This expertise should be explained in a letter of application and demonstrated in the abovementioned proposal, which short-listed candidates will be expected to present at interview. The fellow must be eligible and willing to apply for national security clearance at a minimum level of Enhanced Security Clearance (eSC) and a preferred level of Enhanced Developed Vetting (eDV), making them subject to the provisions of the Official Secrets Act (which includes restrictions on travel to certain countries). UK nationals currently resident in the UK will normally be eligible, but all applicants should carefully consider their eligibility before applying for the fellowship. Information about vetting and clearance can be found on the UK Government Security Clearance website. The employer reserves the right to terminate a fellowship in the event of a loss of security clearance. Our benefits include: Generous employer contribution pension 29 days annual leave plus bank holidays, along with Christmas closure Ride to work and EV car scheme available For more information, please see University of Manchester Benefits. You can also find information on our Flexible and Hybrid working here. We are an open place of enquiry and challenge. We embrace and celebrate difference, diversity and debate, and we pride ourselves on being a place of education, learning and community where we are able, within the law, to question and test received wisdom, express new ideas and explore controversial or unpopular topics and opinions. Find out more from our Freedom of Speech Policy. Enquiries About The Role, Shortlisting And Interviews Email Address: bsfellowships@manchester.ac.uk. items.desc: COMPUTATIONAL BIOLOGY & AI SOLUTIONS SPECIALIST Driving bioinformatics and AI adoption across R&D and business functions _________________________________________________________________________ Cantanhede, Portugal | Computational role - hybrid ABOUT EXOGENUS THERAPEUTICS Exogenus Therapeutics is a biotechnology company developing multifactorial, disease-modifying biologics for regenerative medicine. Our lead programme, Exo-101, is an extracellular-vesicle-enriched secretome in development for knee osteoarthritis. We are also exploring applications in cisplatin-induced hearing loss and other regenerative medicine indications. We combine scientific rigour, collaboration and responsible innovation to advance new therapies for patients. ABOUT THE ROLE We are looking for a Computational Biology & AI Solutions Specialist to help translate scientific and business needs into practical, responsible and scalable data and AI solutions. Working across R&D and business development, you will combine hands-on bioinformatics with the evaluation, implementation and adoption of AI-enabled tools for data analysis, knowledge management and competitive intelligence. This role is well suited to someone who enjoys working with complex biological datasets, applying emerging technologies to research challenges and collaborating across scientific disciplines. WHAT YOU WILL DO Computational Biology and Bioinformatics: Develop and maintain pipelines for transcriptomic, proteomic and other omics data analyses. Integrate and analyse datasets from multi-omics experiments. Establish appropriate standards for data quality, documentation, version control and reproducibility. Translate analytical results into clear outputs for multidisciplinary R&D teams. AI solutions and cross-functional enablement: Identify and implement AI-based tools and platforms to enhance the company’s’ activities, including research and innovation workflows and business development. Develop guidance, training and reusable workflows to support effective adoption. Implement and maintain platforms for competitive intelligence, including monitoring of scientific publications, patents, clinical trials and market developments. Contribute to the establishment of best practices for data management, reproducibility and analytics. ESSENTIAL EXPERIENCE AND SKILLS MSc or PhD in Bioinformatics, Computational Biology, Data Science, Biotechnology, Life Sciences, Computer Science, Engineering or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant professional experience. Proven background in bioinformatics and computational data analysis. Hands-on experience evaluating, implementing or integrating AI-enabled tools into scientific or business workflows, including the ability to define use cases, test outputs, document limitations and support user adoption. Experience using AI-powered platforms and tools for data analysis, information retrieval or decision support. Experience analysing biological datasets, particularly omics data. Knowledge of data integration methodologies and workflows. Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities, with attention to detail. Strong communication skills and ability to collaborate within multidisciplinary R&D teams. Self-initiative and ability to work both independently and collaboratively. Curiosity and enthusiasm for applying emerging technologies to research challenges. Excellent proficiency in English (mandatory); knowledge of Portuguese (desirable). WHAT WE OFFER Work with a multidisciplinary team developing innovative medicines, with a special focus on extracellular vesicle-enriched secretome technologies. Annual gross salary within the range of €30.000–€40.0000, depending on the candidate’s relevant experience and qualifications, plus meal allowance. Flexible working arrangements, including the possibility of hybrid work. Professional development through internal learning, workshops, conferences and relevant training. An open, respectful working environment where people are encouraged to contribute ideas and different perspectives. Informal team activities and opportunities to connect across the company. INCLUSION AND ACCESSIBILITY At Exogenus Therapeutics, we are not just a team, we are a family that values innovation, collaboration, and the drive to revolutionize healthcare. Our culture thrives on teamwork, mutual respect, and a shared passion for making a significant impact in the EV field. We believe that our employees are our greatest asset, and we are committed to supporting their professional and personal growth. Exogenus Therapeutics is committed to creating equal opportunities and an inclusive recruitment process and workplace. We welcome applications from people with different backgrounds, experiences and perspectives. HOW TO APPLY Please email your CV and motivation letter explaining your interest in the role and the most relevant experience for the role, in a single pdf document titled Computational Biology & AI Solutions …

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited. As a Research Engineer on the Orchestral team, you will help build the agentic platform we use to train and evaluate our models. Orchestral is the system our researchers rely on to run training and evaluation at scale — from the rollout engine that powers agentic workflows to the infrastructure that keeps their workloads running reliably. What you build becomes the foundation the whole science team works on. Your work will span the platform's core: the library, tooling, abstractions and rollout engine — including new capabilities like long-running tasks, subagents and RL features — and the machinery that runs data and jobs at scale, with a focus on resiliency, routing and request handling. You will own significant pieces end to end, from design to production. This is a software engineering role rather than an ML or infrastructure-operations one: RL or PyTorch experience is not required, and you will spend your time building the platform, not operating it. You will be building a distributed RL system, with the scientists as your users. What You Will Do Design and build the core of the Orchestral platform: the library, abstractions and tooling researchers use to train and evaluate models. Build and evolve the rollout engine, shipping new capabilities such as long-running tasks and subagents. Run Orchestral as a production system: keep training and evaluation workloads reliable at scale. Improve how data and jobs flow through the platform as usage grows — scheduling, routing and request handling. Treat researchers as your users: understand their workflows and turn recurring needs into robust, shared tooling. Raise the bar on engineering quality across the platform: testing, code review, CI/CD, observability and documentation. Contribute to open-source rollout-engine and agent-infrastructure projects where it benefits the platform. What We're Looking For Experience directly building and debugging complex distributed systems at scale, with an emphasis on reliability and scalability. Strong Python skills and solid software-design instincts: testing, code review, CI/CD. A builder mindset: you have constructed systems from the ground up, not just operated polished ones. A track record in small teams running complex systems at scale — for example in finance, crypto or ad tech. Self-starter, low-ego and collaborative, with a product mindset toward your users. Curiosity about ML and RL — this experience is not required, but a desire to learn is. Nice-to-haves Hands-on experience with Ray or similar distributed-computing frameworks. Open-source contributions, especially to rollout-engine or agent-infrastructure projects such as SLIME, verl or PrimeRL. Experience building or working with agentic workflows and environments. What we offer We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks. For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page. Privacy Policy Your privacy matters to us. You can learn more about how we handle your personal data in our Applicant Privacy Policy.

items.desc: About SPAICE SPAICE is building the autonomy operating system that empowers satellites and drones to navigate and interact with the world – regardless of the environment. From GPS-denied zones on Earth to the unexplored frontiers of space, our Spatial AI delivers unprecedented levels of autonomy, resilience, and adaptability. At SPAICE, you’ll work on real missions alongside leading aerospace and defense contractors, shaping the future of space and autonomous systems. If you're looking for a place where your work has a real, tangible impact – SPAICE is that place. About The Role Satellites that detect & avoid threats on their own. Drones that collaborate in GPS‑denied fields. Spacecraft that rendezvous with tumbling targets in orbit. All of these feats demand robust scene understanding from multiple sensors. That’s where you come in. As a Computer Vision Engineer (Multimodal Sensing) you’ll implement and refine perception algorithms that fuse cameras, LiDAR, radar, event sensors, and beyond. Working shoulder‑to‑shoulder with a top‑tier team of CV scientists, you’ll translate cutting‑edge research into flight‑ready code for space and defense missions. What you might work on Implement perception pipelines for situational awareness, collision detection & avoidance, formation flying, surveillance and terrain mapping across satellites and drones operating in GPS‑denied, dynamic environments. Build the Perception stack of our Spatial AI architectures, fusing visual, inertial, and depth cues for robust, multi‑sensor scene understanding. Integrate sensor fusion & neural representations to create dense onboard world models that run in real time on resource‑constrained hardware. Deploy semantic scene understanding, visual place recognition, pose estimation, and monocular depth estimation on embedded or edge‑AI processors. Collaborate with a top‑tier team of CV scientists and cross‑disciplinary engineers, delivering well‑tested, high‑performance code into flight processors, Hardware‑in‑the‑Loop (HIL) and Software‑in‑the‑Loop (SIL) setups, and real missions. What we are looking for M.S. in Computer Vision/Robotics, or a related field. Expertise in at least two of the following: multimodal perception & sensor fusion, neural representations, semantic scene understanding, SLAM / camera‑pose estimation, monocular depth estimation, visual place recognition. Strong software engineering skills in C++ and Python, including performance‑critical CV/ML code on Linux or embedded platforms. Familiarity with GPU or edge‑AI acceleration (CUDA, TensorRT, Vulkan, or similar). Demonstrated ability to deliver production‑quality, well‑tested code in collaborative, fast‑moving environments. Preferred Qualifications Industry placements/working experience. Familiarity with GPU or edge‑AI acceleration (CUDA, TensorRT, Vulkan, or similar). Experience deploying perception pipelines on resource‑constrained hardware. Publications in multimodal sensing/neural representations/SLAM for robotics or autonomous navigation in journals and conferences (e.g. CVPR, ICRA, ECCV/ICCV, NeurIPS). Perks & Benefits Competitive salary commensurate with experience and impact. Equity options – you will join us at the ground floor and share in the upside. Well‑being perks – access to premium gyms, climbing centers, and wellness programs. Team retreats & offsites – recent adventures include a half‑marathon in Formentera and a Los Angeles retreat during Oscars weekend.

items.desc: Graham Capital Management, L.P. (collectively with its affiliates, "Graham") is an alternative investment manager founded in 1994 by Kenneth G. Tropin. Specializing in discretionary and quantitative macro strategies, Graham is dedicated to delivering strong, uncorrelated returns across a wide range of market environments. As one of the industry's longest-standing global macro and trend-following managers, Graham remains committed to innovation, evolving its strategies through a robust investment, technology, and operational infrastructure. Graham harnesses the synergies between its discretionary and quantitative trading businesses to offer a broad suite of complementary alpha strategies, each built on the principles of thoughtful portfolio construction, active risk management, and diversification by design. Graham invests significant proprietary capital alongside its clients – including global institutions, endowments, foundations, family offices, sovereign wealth funds, investment management advisors, and qualified individual investors – reinforcing alignment of interests across all strategies. The foundation of Graham's sustainability and success is the experience and contributions of its people. The firm seeks to cultivate talent, encourage the diversity of ideas, and respect the contributions of all. In turn, each employee shares in the responsibility of strengthening those around them. Description Graham is seeking a ML Engineer to join our Data Science team, a future-looking technical arm of Graham. We envision, design, prototype and implement the processes that feed Quantitative Research and Discretionary Trading teams as well as the broader firm. We are passionate about what we do and welcome every opportunity to prove it. The Data Science department straddles traditional Data Science and Engineering roles as well as the application of Machine Learning & AI. We work closely with Quant Researchers, Portfolio Managers, Operations and Execution to continuously improve upon our offering. Every day we work to transform our business through data, technology, and the insights we provide our stakeholders. At Graham, our systems feed live models around the clock, span billions of market data ticks, an ever-increasing corpus of news and other texts as well as a broad spectrum of financial and alternative data. Our objective is to support the research process by providing our stakeholders with all the right pieces to succeed in their jobs. You will work alongside world-class talent to find innovative solutions to some of the most interesting problems on the buy-side. You will work closely with other areas such as Technology, Quantitative Research and Portfolio Manager groups as well as Risk and Operations to learn about problems they face with respect to data and ultimately develop cutting edge solutions. Your focus will be to dive deep into multiple data sets to understand relationships, develop time series, forecasting models, and support quant strategies, and provide new insights and leverage state-of-the-art machine learning and advanced statistical methods to produce the best data sources for the fund. Collaborate with Software Engineers,Data Scientists, and Product Managers to implement features and evaluate their impact. Run experiments, test new ideas, and assist in automating insight generation. Translate complex sensor data into clear insights that can shape our roadmap and product. items.desc: Job Description Position Details Department of Cancer and Genomic Sciences, School of Medical Sciences, College of Medicine and Health Location: University of Birmingham, Edgbaston, Birmingham UK Full time starting salary is normally in the range £36,636 to £46,049 with potential progression once in post to £48,822 Grade: 7 Full Time, Fixed Term contract up to November 2029 Closing date: 25th October 2026 Background This job is part of an Advanced Research + Invention Agency-funded project. "Hephaisteion: Direct Lithium Extraction using inorganic membranes made by proteins" is a highly interdisciplinary 36-month project within ARIA's Universal Fabricators programme. The project will use self-assembling S-layer proteins to programme the manufacture of large-area inorganic membranes with tightly controlled pores, with direct lithium extraction as the first demanding application. It links protein design, high-throughput screening, cell-based expression, biomineralisation, microscopy, process scale-up, membrane manufacture and performance testing. The post will be based in the research group of Professor Steve Smerdon and will work closely with Professor Tim Knowles, project lead Dr Dominik Kubicki and the wider Hephaisteion team. The Research Fellow will take promising proteins emerging from computational and cell-free screening into cellular expression systems; design and construct expression vectors; optimise expression in appropriate bacterial hosts; recover and purify proteins using standard molecular biology and protein-biochemistry techniques; and establish refolding routes where required. Crucially, the Research Fellow will determine whether purified proteins retain the ability to self-assemble into ordered two-dimensional lattices. They will use appropriate biochemical and biophysical assays, work with the microscopy team to validate assembly, and provide well-characterised protein to the biomineralisation, membrane-manufacturing and process-scale-up workstreams. The postholder will analyse sequence-expression-assembly relationships and contribute evidence to the project's design-build-test decisions and major programme milestones. This is an opportunity to engage in a unique interdisciplinary project spanning protein science, materials chemistry, electron microscopy, bioprocessing and membrane engineering. The postholder will collaborate closely with ARIA, participate in frequent programme workshops and meet other ARIA Creators developing ambitious protein-programmed manufacturing technologies. items.desc: Position description Category Thermohydraulics and fluid mechanics Contract Internship Job title Development of Machine Learning Models for Critical Heat Flux predictions H/F Subject Development of Machine Learning Models for Critical Heat Flux predictions Contract duration (months) 6 Job Description The Critical Heat Flux (CHF) is a physical phenomenon that may cause the deterioration of the heat transfer in the core of nuclear reactors, potentially leading to core damage. Its accurate prediction is therefore a crucial issue in nuclear reactor safety. The internship deals with the prediction of the CHF through the development of machine learning techniques and the quantification of the associated uncertainty. It will be realized in the framework of an international OECD/NEA project on the development and application of artificial intelligence methodologies for nuclear engineering. Within this framework, the intern will: Perform a preliminary literature review on the topic and get familiar with the previous works performed at CEA, based on experimental data in tubes with uniform axial heat flux profiles Analyse the new experimental CHF database (e.g., tube with non-uniform heat flux, rod-bundle, rectangular channel, …) to understand the physical phenomenon and to verify the coherence and exploitability of the experimental data. Perform an initial assessment of previously developed machine learning models to the new database. Develop transfer learning to predict as accurately as possible the CHF for the new experiments. If time allows it, investigate the explainability issue and quantify the uncertainty of the models developed during the internship applying different state-of-the-art methodologies such as conformal prediction, hierarchical models and other coverage-driven techniques. Present and discuss the work during technical meetings and write a final report. Applicant Profile The ideal candidate is a MSc. student (in French system: M2 level or Ecole d’ingénieur) who has a good knowledge of artificial intelligence and neural networks with an interest in fluid mechanics. Knowledge of the physics processes underlying the CHF phenomenon will be considered a plus. Good skills in Python coding and code management are required. We welcome previous experience with any major deep learning framework (PyTorch, JAX, Tensorflow) and with uncertainty quantification approaches. Given the international context of the OECD/NEA project, fluency in English is considered necessary (French will be considered a plus). Position location Site Saclay Job location France, Ile-de-France Location Saclay Candidate criteria Prepared diploma Bac+5 - Diplôme École d'ingénieurs PhD opportunity Non Requester Position start date 01/02/2027

items.desc: Type de contrat : CDD Niveau de diplôme exigé : Bac + 5 ou équivalent Fonction : Ingénieur scientifique contractuel A propos du centre ou de la direction fonctionnelle L’Inria est l’Institut national de recherche en sciences du numérique, dont le centre Inria d’Université Côte d’Azur fait partie. Avec une forte expertise en informatique et mathématiques appliquées, les projets de recherche du centre Inria d’Université Côte d’Azur touchent toutes les dimensions des sciences et technologies du numérique, et génèrent de l’innovation. Implanté principalement à Sophia Antipolis, mais également à Nice ou Montpellier, il regroupe 47 équipes de recherche et neuf services d’appui. Il est présent dans les domaines de l’intelligence artificielle, la science des données, la sécurité des systèmes informatiques, la robotique, l’ingénierie de réseaux, la prévention des risques naturels, la transition écologique, la biologie numérique, les neurosciences computationnelles, les données de santé… Le Centre Inria d’Université Côte d’Azur est un acteur majeur en termes d'excellence scientifique par les résultats obtenus et les collaborations tant au niveau européen qu'international. Contexte et atouts du poste Ce poste s’inscrit dans un projet porté par OnTheFly (onthefly3d.com), projet entrepreneurial issu de l’équipe-projet GraphDeco (inventrice du 3D Gaussian Splatting) et accompagné par Inria Startup Studio. Le projet vise à développer des outils de capture 3D sur smartphone à destination des professionnels, associant reconstruction immédiate et analyse automatisée de l’évolution des sites réels dans le temps. Mission confiée Développer des méthodes de comparaison automatique entre des reconstructions 3D issues de captures réelles et des données de référence, comme des maquettes numériques ou des captures antérieures d’un même site. Les travaux porteront sur l’alignement de représentations 3D hétérogènes, ainsi que sur la détection et la segmentation de changements de manière robuste dans des conditions de capture réelles. Principales activités Concevoir et implémenter des méthodes d’alignement 3D combinant correspondances visuelles ou sémantiques et informations géométriques rendues. Développer des approches de décomposition géométrie-matériaux-éclairage pour les représentations par Gaussian Splatting. Mettre en place des méthodes de détection et de segmentation des différences entre captures ou entre reconstruction et maquette numérique, en exploitant images, profondeur, normales et modèles de vision. Entraîner et évaluer les modèles sur des données réelles et synthétiques, puis intégrer les méthodes développées dans des outils de visualisation. Compétences Requises Diplôme d’ingénieur, master ou doctorat en informatique ou dans un domaine connexe Solides compétences en programmation Expérience en entraînement et en évaluation de modèles de deep learning, avec des frameworks de programmation différentiable tels que PyTorch Solides bases en vision par ordinateur, des fondamentaux comme la géométrie multivue aux modèles de vision modernes (par ex. vision transformers, modèles vision-langage) Intérêt pour les projets entrepreneuriaux et les environnements de start-up Appréciées Expérience en programmation de shaders ou en programmation parallèle (par ex. GLSL, CUDA) Expérience en 3D Gaussian Splatting, rendu neuronal ou rendu inverse Une expérience avec les données BIM Avantages Restauration subventionnée Transports publics remboursés partiellement Congés: 7 semaines de congés annuels + 10 jours de RTT (base temps plein) + possibilité d'autorisations d'absence exceptionnelle (ex : enfants malades, déménagement) Possibilité de télétravail et aménagement du temps de travail Équipements professionnels à disposition (visioconférence, prêts de matériels informatiques, etc.) Prestations sociales, culturelles et sportives (Association de gestion des œuvres sociales d'Inria) Accès à la formation professionnelle Participation mutuelle (sous conditions) Rémunération A partir de 2692 € brut mensuel (selon diplôme et expérience) Informations générales Thème/Domaine : Interaction et visualisation Ingénierie logicielle (BAP E) Ville : Sophia Antipolis Centre Inria : Centre Inria d'Université Côte d'Azur Date de prise de fonction souhaitée : 2026-12-01 Durée de contrat : 5 mois Date limite pour postuler : 2026-11-15 Attention : Les candidatures doivent être déposées en ligne sur le site Inria. items.desc: Job Reference 457_26_CS_HAM_RE1 Position Research Engineer - HPC memory systems (RE1) Closing Date Friday, 30 October, 2026 Reference: 457_26_CS_HAM_RE1 Job title: Research Engineer - HPC memory systems (RE1) About BSC The Barcelona Supercomputing Center - Centro Nacional de Supercomputación (BSC-CNS) is the leading supercomputing center in Spain. It houses MareNostrum, one of the most powerful supercomputers in Europe, was a founding and hosting member of the former European HPC infrastructure PRACE (Partnership for Advanced Computing in Europe), and is now hosting entity for EuroHPC JU, the Joint Undertaking that leads large-scale investments and HPC provision in Europe. The mission of BSC is to research, develop and manage information technologies in order to facilitate scientific progress. BSC combines HPC service provision and R&D into both computer and computational science (life, earth and engineering sciences) under one roof, and currently has over 1000 staff from 60 countries. Look at the BSC experience: BSC-CNS YouTube Channel Let's stay connected with BSC Folks! Context And Mission The Memory Systems group in the Computer Science Department at the Barcelona Supercomputing Center is offering a full-time research engineer position for a project that explores advanced memory systems for AI applications. The performance of AI models is typically limited by the memory wall. In this project, we aim to (re)move this wall by designing memory systems tailored to the requirements of AI models. We will explore systems based on HBM, DDR, GDDR devices, and Compute Express Link (CXL) memory expanders. Additionally, we will consider near-data processing architectures that offload part of the CPU/GPU processing to the memory system. The project is conducted in close collaboration with a major memory manufacturer. Most of the development will take place on high-end hardware products and industrial prototypes. We strongly encourage applications from candidates interested in joining a research team with over a decade of experience in industrial projects with major hardware companies from the US, China, and Korea. Your core responsibility is designing, building and operating the system landscape in the NeuraGym so that recording and
items.desc: Your mission & challenges As Compute Infrastructure Engineer – NeuraGym you work at the intersection of server architecture, virtualisation, container orchestration and data processing, with a strong focus on building a scalable compute and storage infrastructure for multimodal robot data. Your core responsibility is designing, building and operating the system landscape in the NeuraGym so that recording and processing on large data volumes run reliably, performantly and reproducibly. You play a decisive role in enabling high-quality embodied AI systems by turning individual servers, workstations and edge devices into a distributed, maintainable and extensible compute system. Server infrastructure planning: You plan and design the NeuraGym server infrastructure, including sizing of compute, GPU, storage and network, rack layout, power and cooling concept, and procurement in coordination with the team. Virtualisation: You build and operate virtualisation environments based on hypervisors such as Proxmox and provide development, test and production environments. Kubernetes & GPU scheduling: You design and operate Kubernetes clusters (or comparable orchestration) for data preprocessing workloads, including GPU scheduling, monitoring and logging. Distributed processing: You intelligently distribute compute- and data-intensive processes across multiple machines, from edge devices on the robot via local servers to central storage systems, and make sure bottlenecks are detected and removed. Network design: You design the NeuraGym network infrastructure: VLANs, switching, bandwidth planning for camera and sensor streams, firewall rules and secure integration with the rest of the company IT. Storage & data pipelines: You build storage and data pipelines for high data volumes (e.g. object storage, distributed file systems, streaming ingest) and ensure that data is reliably captured, stored, versioned and made available for model training. Automation: You automate provisioning, deployment and operations with infrastructure-as-code and CI/CD tooling and document the system landscape in a traceable way. Stability & security: You identify and resolve performance, stability and security issues in the infrastructure and develop backup, recovery and access concepts. What we can look forward to Education: Degree in computer science, systems engineering, engineering or a related field, or comparable vocational training with relevant practical experience. Experience: 4+ years in system administration, infrastructure engineering, DevOps or platform engineering. Server infrastructure: Solid experience planning, designing and operating server infrastructure (sizing, rack build-out, hardware selection, procurement). Virtualisation: Hands-on experience with hypervisors and virtualisation (e.g. Proxmox, KVM, VMware), including storage and network integration. Containers: Strong knowledge of container technologies and orchestration (Docker, Kubernetes or comparable platforms), ideally with GPU workloads. Distributed systems: Understanding of how processes, data and compute load are sensibly distributed, synchronised and monitored across multiple machines. Linux & scripting: Confident with Linux systems, shell scripting and at least one scripting language (e.g. Python, Bash). IaC & CI/CD: Experience with infrastructure as code and automation (e.g. Ansible, Terraform) as well as CI/CD tooling (e.g. GitLab CI). Working style: A structured, self-driven way of working and enjoyment in building infrastructure from the ground up together with an interdisciplinary team. Nice to have: Experience with monitoring and logging stacks (e.g. Prometheus, Grafana).

Look At The BSC Experience BSC-CNS YouTube Channel Let's stay connected with BSC Folks! We are particularly interested for this role in the strengths and lived experiences of women and underrepresented groups to help us avoid perpetuating biases and oversights in science and IT research. In instances of equal merit, the incorporation of the under-represented sex will be favoured. We promote Equity, Diversity and Inclusion, fostering an environment where each and every one of us is appreciated for who we are, regardless of our differences. We value diversity of experiences and skills, and you could bring unique perspectives to our team. Context And Mission The Memory Systems group in the Computer Science Department at the Barcelona Supercomputing Center is offering a full-time research engineer position for a project that explores advanced memory systems for AI applications. The performance of AI models is typically limited by the memory wall. In this project, we aim to (re)move this wall by designing memory systems tailored to the requirements of AI models. We will explore systems based on HBM, DDR, GDDR devices, and Compute Express Link (CXL) memory expanders. Additionally, we will consider near-data processing architectures that offload part of the CPU/GPU processing to the memory system. Poste en CDI basé à Vélizy Votre mission Votre mission consiste principalement à participer au développement d’une nouvelle gamme d’outils utilisant le Machine Learning pour la simulation au sein de notre portefeuille d’applications Virtual Twin Physics Behavior. Optimisation des Performances : Assurer l'efficacité computationnelle (temps d'exécution, gestion mémoire, parallélisation) de nos moteurs ML. Traitement de Données 3D : Développer des pipelines en C++/Python pour l'extraction, le prétraitement et la structuration des données géométriques et physiques CAD/CAE (maillages, champs de scalaires/vecteurs, conditions limites...) Collaboration & Rayonnement : Interagir avec des experts métiers, des équipes R&D pluridisciplinaires et nos partenaires académiques/industriels internationaux (veille technologique, rédaction de documentation technique et valorisation de vos travaux). Vous avez idéalement une expérience supérieure à 3 ans (post-doctorat ou industrie). Solide expertise en Apprentissage Profond appliqué aux EDP / équations physiques et à l'encodage géométrique. Maîtrise d'un framework ML principal (PyTorch, JAX ou TensorFlow) et de Python. Bonnes compétences en C++ moderne et en développement logiciel scientifique dans un environnement Agile. Rigueur scientifique, autonomie et capacité à résoudre des problèmes complexes et non structurés. Anglais courant (écrit et oral), au vu de notre environnement international. Des connaissances pratiques en simulation numérique (FEA, CFD, CAD/CAE) ainsi que des formats et structures de données CAD/CAE (Abaqus odb/inp/sim, CAA, HDF5, ...) seraient un réel plus pour mener à bien votre mission. items.desc: Programista AI / inżynier oprogramowania Projekt:FENG.01.01-IP.02-0224/25 Opracowanie prototypu innowacyjnego systemu wspierającego proces ekoprojektowania oświetlenia miejskiego, który łączy dane przestrzenne, semantykę urbanistyczną oraz metody sztucznej inteligencji w celu optymalizacji decyzji projektowych. STUDIO DL to biuro projektowo-badawcze z blisko 30-letnim doświadczeniem na rynku międzynarodowym w projektowaniu oświetlenia i badaniach na rozwiązaniami IT dedykowanemu oświetleniu. Zespół IT pracuje nad produktem, który łączy oprogramowanie, bazy danych, GIS, integracje oraz rozwiązania dla infrastruktury miejskiej. Tworzymy interdyscyplinarny zespół, w którym programiści współpracują z projektantami oświetlenia, architektami, geoinformatykami i specjalistami zajmującymi się infrastrukturą miejską. Dzięki temu rozwijane przez nas rozwiązania mają bezpośrednie przełożenie na rzeczywiste projekty i funkcjonowanie miast. Do naszego zespołu IT zapraszamy osoby, które chcą mieć wpływ na rozwój własnego produktu technologicznego i pracować przy projektach łączących IT z GIS, danymi przestrzennymi oraz nowoczesnym zarządzaniem infrastrukturą. O projekcie Realizujemy projekt badawczo-rozwojowy dotyczący opracowania prototypu systemu wspierającego ekoprojektowanie oświetlenia miejskiego. System ma łączyć dane przestrzenne, semantykę urbanistyczną, algorytmy obliczeniowe i metody sztucznej inteligencji, wspierając planowanie oraz optymalizację oświetlenia w skali miasta. Rola Osoba na tym stanowisku będzie odpowiadać za rozwój modeli AI/ML, integrację danych GIS i miejskich oraz optymalizację algorytmów wykorzystywanych w kolejnych modułach systemu, a także badanie, projektowanie i testowanie interfejsów użytkownika dla systemu wykorzystującego złożone dane przestrzenne, modele 2D/3D, algorytmy optymalizacyjne oraz moduły wspierające decyzje projektowe. Zakres prac przewidziany dla tego stanowiska: Analiza danych o pokryciu terenu oraz kryteriach decyzyjnych. Modelowanie i trenowanie algorytmów uczenia maszynowego (ML) oraz głębokiego uczenia (DL) wykorzystywanych do mapowania miasta pod kątem masterplanu oświetlenia. Implementacja rozwiązań AI. Optymalizacja modeli. Analiza danych o infrastrukturze oświetleniowej oraz danych o oprawach od producentów. Modelowanie i trenowanie algorytmów integrujących dane z inwentaryzacji z danymi od producentów oraz uzupełniających brakujące dane w oparciu o uczenie maszynowe i statystykę. Analiza danych o oprawach oświetleniowych od producentów i warunkach doboru najbardziej efektywnego rozwiązania dla oświetlenia trójwymiarowej przestrzeni. Opracowanie potoku danych dla algorytmów uczenia się optymalizacji światła. Tworzenie narzędzi opartych na sztucznej inteligencji do oceny różnych konfiguracji przekrojów drogowych i ich wpływu na oświetlenie. Zbudowanie powiązań pomiędzy rozwiązaniami AI dla poszczególnych modułów systemu. Optymalizacja algorytmów pod względem relacji pomiędzy poszczególnymi komponentami. Opracowywanie technik przetwarzania równoległego i rozproszonych rozwiązań obliczeniowych w celu zwiększenia wydajności algorytmów. --------------------------------------------------------- Projektowanie i implementacja algorytmów mapujących miasto. Opracowanie funkcji wspierających implementację algorytmów mapowania miast. Opracowanie szczegółów modelu danych na podstawie diagramu. Opracowanie funkcji umożliwiających zapisywanie i pobieranie danych 3D i semantycznych w dużych zbiorach danych. Analiza danych w celu identyfikacji wzorców i trendów przydatnych w zastosowaniach projektu. Projektowanie i implementacja algorytmów integrujących dane od producentów oraz dane o infrastrukturze w mieście. Opracowanie funkcji oceniających jakość danych, zapewniających dokładność i niezawodność optymalizacji oświetlenia. Uproszczenie geometrii LOD w celu zmniejszenia złożoności modelu przy zachowaniu szczegółów potrzebnych do analizy oświetlenia. Zaprojektowanie wydajnej struktury danych do organizowania i zarządzania różnorodnymi danymi wejściowymi, wspierającej obliczenia oświetlenia oparte na AI. Projektowanie i implementacja algorytmów obliczających oświetlenie dla trójwymiarowej przestrzeni. Zintegrowanie różnych parametrów oświetlenia (np. jasność, kąt i pokrycie) z algorytmem w celu dokładnej optymalizacji. Wdrożenie technik przetwarzania równoległego w celu przyspieszenia optymalizacji 3D na dużą skalę. Opracowanie i udoskonalenie procedur optymalizacyjnych dla optymalizacji częściowych. Badanie metod analiz stanu infrastruktury oświetleniowej pod kątem m.in. obciążenia obwodów, zużycia energii, potencjału oszczędności, benchmarków i priorytetów modernizacyjnych przy zadanym budżecie. Optymalizacja wydajności systemu. Profilowanie algorytmów w celu identyfikacji komponentów wymagających dużych zasobów i optymalizacji. Refaktoryzacja kodu w celu poprawy wydajności i zarządzania czasem wykonania oraz zasobami. Ocena skuteczności istniejących potoków danych. Wymagania …

items.desc: Die Sektion für Klinische Forschungs-IT (SKFIT) wird am UKSH Campus Lübeck eine eigene Plattform für ML-getriebene klinische Entscheidungsunterstützung aufbauen – von der Forschung bis in die Versorgung. Dafür suchen wir eine (Medizin-)Informatikerin/einen (Medizin-)Informatiker im Bereich der KI/ML-getriebenen Datenanalyse für klinische Entscheidungsunterstützungssysteme. Warum diese Stelle besonders ist Als Teil des UKSH dürfen wir Patientendaten inhouse analysieren und eigene klinische Entscheidungsunterstützungssysteme (CDSS) nicht nur erforschen, sondern nach 6 GDNG und Art. 5 Abs. 5 MDR (VO (EU) 2017/745) auch vereinfacht in die Versorgung überführen. Dadurch können innovative Lösungen vergleichsweise schnell von der Idee bis in die klinische Anwendung gebracht werden, ein Umfeld, das in dieser Form bisher nur wenige Forschungsgruppen in Deutschland bieten. Die SKFIT betreibt die langfristig angelegte klinische Forschungs-IT-Infrastruktur für Kliniker:innen und Forschende am UKSH Campus Lübeck und an der Universität zu Lübeck (Schwerpunkt Biobank- und Studienmanagement) und forscht zu KI-/ML-getriebener medizinischer Datenanalyse. Mit dieser Stelle zielen wir darauf ab, eine eigene ML-getriebene CDSS-Plattform aufzubauen. Start in unserem Team Kommen Sie in unser Team und unterstützen Sie uns zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt, zunächst für drei Jahre. Das bieten wir Ihnen: Möglichkeit zur Promotion (Die Stelle ist als Promotionsstelle angelegt, die Betreuung erfolgt direkt im Haus. Prof. Dr. Fudickar ist Zweitmitglied der Sektion MINT der Universität zu Lübeck (inkl. Promotionsrecht), assoziiert mit dem Institut für Medizinische Informatik und PI am Fraunhofer IMTE.) sowie weitere Fort- und Weiterbildungsangebote Zugang zu den Gesundheitsdaten und der Infrastruktur des zweitgrößten Universitätsklinikums Deutschlands Eingruppierung in die Entgeltgruppe E13 TV-L, bei Erfüllung der tariflichen Voraussetzungen Eine Vollzeitbeschäftigung, zzt. 38,5 Stunden/Woche; eine Teilzeittätigkeit kann im Rahmen bestimmter Arbeitszeitmodelle vereinbart sein Anteiliges Mobiles Arbeiten Weitere spannende Benefits des UKSH finden Sie hier: Benefits (uksh.de) Das erwartet Sie: Aufbau einer professionellen Plattform zur klinischen Entscheidungsunterstützung als Eigenentwicklung am UKSH, in Kooperation mit der AMPEL-Plattform des Universitätsklinikums Leipzig Forschungsarbeiten zu ML- und LLM-getriebenen Verfahren im Bereich der CDSS, inklusive eigener Publikationen Integration verfügbarer Patientendaten aus dem Krankenhausinformationssystem/MeDIC (Interoperabilität, ETL, EHR- und Zeitreihendaten) Arbeit in einem engagierten und vielseitigen Team und mit exzellenten Kooperationspartnern an interessanten und abwechslungsreichen Projekten Neben IT-Entwicklungs- und Projektaufgaben wird wissenschaftliches Arbeiten inklusive Reisetätigkeit erwartet, u.a. eine Mitarbeit in entsprechenden nationalen Arbeitsgruppen sowie in Projektmeetings Das bringen Sie mit: Ein mit dem Master abgeschlossenes Hochschulstudium der Medizinischen Informatik bzw. You will support the development and application of quantitative and data-driven approaches to address challenges in maritime transportation, sustainable logistics and decarbonisation, with particular focus on Engineering Net Zero, Artificial Intelligence (AI), digitalisation and data. Key responsibilities include: 1) contributing to scoping, feasibility assessment and proof-of-concept development for maritime and last-mile decarbonisation projects; 2) supporting the development and application of quantitative and data-driven models, including modelling, simulation, optimisation and machine learning; and 3) assisting in the development, testing and evaluation of analytical tools, prototypes and demonstrators, working collaboratively with academic researchers and external partners. You should possess a good honours degree and a PhD (or equivalent professional experience) in transport, logistics, engineering, operations research, data science or a relevant discipline. You must demonstrate strong quantitative research and data-analysis capabilities, proficiency in programming or analytical tools, and the ability to disseminate research findings through high-quality publications in international journals and refereed conferences. Experience with research or innovation projects related to maritime decarbonisation, sustainable logistics, AI, digitalisation or proof-of-concept development is preferred. You will work as part of the EPSRC-funded MaLaMi programme, collaborating with an interdisciplinary team of researchers, investigators and external partners, within the Liverpool Logistics Offshore and Marine Research Institute (LOOM) at Liverpool John Moores University, UK. In return, we offer an excellent benefits package including generous annual leave entitlement, pension scheme, induction, and development support as well as family-friendly policies. This is an exciting time to join the university as we deliver the LJMU Strategy 2030 and its vision of LJMU as an inclusive civic university transforming lives and futures, by placing students at the heart of everything we do. If you feel that this is the role you have been looking for and your skills and experience can make a real difference at LJMU, we look forward to hearing from you. Con sedi a Roma, Milano e Torino ci avvaliamo di professionisti altamente specializzati, utilizziamo tecnologie all’avanguardia e anticipiamo le richieste di mercato. Chi stiamo cercando Siamo alla ricerca di un/una Data Scientist che contribuisca alla progettazione, allo sviluppo e alla validazione di componenti algoritmiche. La figura ideale possiede solide competenze in Python e interesse per l’analisi e la risoluzione di problemi complessi, preferibilmente in ambito di ottimizzazione matematica e Ricerca Operativa. Attività principali Progettazione, implementazione e validazione di componenti algoritmiche. Sviluppo di servizi e API REST per l’integrazione tra applicazioni e algoritmi. Gestione e interrogazione di database relazionali per l’elaborazione dei dati. Sviluppo e sperimentazione di soluzioni basate su modelli di ottimizzazione matematica e algoritmi di Ricerca Operativa. Integrazione e supporto alla distribuzione dei componenti sviluppati tramite tecnologie di containerizzazione. Requisiti Solida conoscenza del linguaggio Python . Esperienza nell’utilizzo di API REST e nello sviluppo di servizi per l’integrazione tra applicativi e algoritmi. Buona conoscenza di SQL e familiarità con database relazionali, in particolare PostgreSQL . Conoscenza di base di Docker e dei principali concetti di containerizzazione. Esperienza nella formulazione e risoluzione di problemi di Ricerca Operativa , ottimizzazione combinatoria e programmazione matematica. Conoscenza di framework e solver per l’ottimizzazione, quali Pyomo, GLPK, IPOPT o equivalenti. Esperienza con Google OR-Tools , in particolare con il solver CP-SAT . Conoscenza di PyTorch e degli Autoencoders . Esperienza nell’utilizzo di servizi AWS . items.desc: En decisiOM.ai desarrollamos software para la orquestación de decisiones. Nuestra plataforma ayuda a las organizaciones a gobernar las decisiones que toman sus sistemas, garantizando que cada acción automatizada sea trazable, consistente y explicable. Nuestra tecnología es independiente de la plataforma y se adapta a distintos sectores, en cualquier contexto donde las decisiones deban automatizarse y, al mismo tiempo, ser auditables y responsables. Buscamos Machine Learning Engineers con sólida experiencia en el desarrollo, despliegue y orquestación de modelos predictivos y de decisión , así como en su integración en procesos de negocio reales. El objetivo es garantizar soluciones escalables, confiables y orientadas a generar valor medible para el negocio. Responsabilidades Diseñar, desarrollar y optimizar modelos de Machine Learning para resolver problemas de negocio. Implementar modelos de decisión para evaluar escenarios, generar recomendaciones y automatizar acciones. Desarrollar y administrar pipelines para la ejecución, integración y orquestación de modelos. Gestionar el entrenamiento, la validación, el despliegue y el monitoreo de modelos en entornos productivos. Integrar soluciones de Machine Learning mediante APIs, microservicios y plataformas en la nube. Aplicar prácticas de MLOps para el control de versiones, monitoreo y gestión del ciclo de vida de los modelos. Evaluar el desempeño de los modelos mediante métricas técnicas y de negocio. Colaborar con los equipos de Data Science, Data Engineering y áreas de negocio para desarrollar soluciones escalables. Requisitos técnicos Lenguajes de programación: Python y SQL. Machine Learning: Scikit-learn, XGBoost, LightGBM, TensorFlow o PyTorch. Modelado de decisiones: Árboles de decisión, analítica predictiva, optimización y análisis de escenarios. Orquestación: Apache Airflow, Prefect, Dagster o herramientas equivalentes. MLOps: MLflow, pipelines de Machine Learning, CI/CD, monitoreo y control de versiones de modelos. Integración: APIs REST, FastAPI y microservicios. Plataformas en la nube: Experiencia con AWS, Azure o Google Cloud Platform. Contenedores: Docker y Kubernetes. Control de versiones: Git, GitHub o GitLab. Experiencia requerida Más de 4 años de experiencia en Machine Learning en modelos de decisión y predictivos. Experiencia comprobable en el desarrollo, despliegue y operación de modelos en entornos productivos. Experiencia en la automatización y orquestación de datos y pipelines de Machine Learning. Conocimientos en optimización de modelos, evaluación del desempeño y mejora continua. Capacidad para traducir requerimientos de negocio en soluciones técnicas escalables. Inglés conversacional avanzado, con capacidad para comunicarse eficazmente en entornos profesionales. Competencias clave Sólido pensamiento analítico y habilidades para la resolución de problemas complejos. Orientación a resultados y toma de decisiones basada en datos. Capacidad para diseñar soluciones técnicas y trabajar colaborativamente en equipo. Comunicación efectiva con equipos multidisciplinarios. Requisitos deseables Experiencia en Inteligencia de Decisiones ( Decision Intelligence ) o automatización de decisiones. Conocimientos de investigación de operaciones y optimización matemática. Experiencia con motores de reglas de negocio y plataformas de toma de decisiones automatizada. Familiaridad con técnicas de explicabilidad y gobernanza de modelos, como SHAP, gestión del riesgo de modelos y trazabilidad de auditoría. Experiencia en industrias reguladas. ¿Te interesa esta oportunidad? Si tienes experiencia en Machine Learning, automatización y despliegue de modelos, y buscas contribuir a proyectos de alto impacto, te invitamos a postularte y compartir tu experiencia con nosotros. Si has llevado modelos de Machine Learning a producción y te interesa desarrollar soluciones que permitan gobernar y explicar las decisiones automatizadas, nos gustaría conocerte . Postúlate y cuéntanos sobre tu experiencia.

items.desc: ATG has a wealth of data, with millions of guests visiting, eating, and drinking in our theatres every year, and there is a growing need to bring machine learning and data-driven decision-making into our core business processes. The focus of this role is to improve revenue, customer satisfaction, retention, and acquisition by delivering production-ready machine learning solutions and actionable insights from our customer data. You will join a small, growing ML team at a pivotal time for ATG, taking ownership of defined parts of our ML estate, and working towards wider ownership as you grow. We have built a Data Platform that collates our rich transactional and behavioural data in a cloud-based environment (Snowflake and AWS), enabling scalable analytics and machine learning across the business. You will contribute to the development, deployment, and continuous improvement of machine learning systems, including a revenue management application used by teams across the UK, USA, and Europe. Working alongside other ML Engineers, you will take ownership of defined workstreams (for example, a regional pipeline, a monitoring layer, or a model component), progressively taking on more of the end-to-end lifecycle: data ingestion, model training and evaluation, deployment, pricing recommendations and production monitoring. You will also have the opportunity to help design and implement AI/LLM-powered solutions, such as internal tools, decision-support systems, or workflow automation, ensuring they are well-evaluated, cost-effective, and integrated with our data platform. You will work closely with Data Science, Technology, Product, and commercial teams, helping to bridge the gap between models, AI systems, and real business decisions. Key Responsibilities You will help us maximise the value we derive from our data, building and iterating machine learning models, propensity models, and audience segmentations. You will collaborate across technical and business teams to create assets that can be used and understood. Take ownership of defined components of the revenue management application (i.e. regional pipelines, seat map and pricing data pulls, or model inference), including their reliability and ongoing improvement. Productionise and automate machine learning models end-to-end, including data ingestion, feature engineering, model training and evaluation, inference, and delivery of pricing recommendations. Build and maintain data pipelines and MLOps workflows (CI/CD, model versioning, reproducibility, runtime handling) in AWS and Snowflake. Support the diagnosis and resolution of production issues, including on-call style triage of failed pipeline runs and data quality problems, escalating to the Lead ML Engineer where needed. Design and implement monitoring for model outputs (data drift, prediction drift, anomaly detection) and build dashboards to track model behaviour and recommendation quality daily. Implement guardrails for pricing recommendations (thresholds, overrides, fallback logic) in line with agreed designs. Write well-tested, documented, maintainable Python and SQL, following team conventions and taking part in peer code review. Work with Data Science to take experimental models and prototypes into production, and with commercial teams to translate business needs into technical requirements. Document systems, runbooks, and model behaviour so that knowledge is shared across the team. Contribute to the design and build of LLM-powered solutions (e.g. internal tools, decision-support systems, automation workflows), including prompt management, versioning, and evaluation. Use our data platform to support and automate decision-making across the business, bringing data together to constantly improve our understanding of our products and customers. Be an active part of our data community as we build new capability across disciplines, sharing learning and contributing to team standards. Your Skills, Qualities, And Experience. If you have most of the essential criteria, we encourage you to apply, and welcome transferable skills from other industries or backgrounds. We can give experience of any desirable criteria but may also use them to decide between candidates for this role. Essential Proven experience as a machine learning engineer, data scientist, or similar role, with a track record of delivering ML work into production. Experience of building and optimising data science workloads in cloud environments (AWS preferred). Strong Python and SQL, including writing complex queries and well-structured, tested code. Experience deploying and maintaining ML models in production, with a working understanding of MLOps (CI/CD, versioning, reproducibility). Experience building monitoring, alerting, and observability for data or ML systems. Bij KickstartAI versnellen we de adoptie van AI in Nederland door te werken aan urgente maatschappelijke vraagstukken. Onze AI-projecten hebben directe impact op gezondheid, duurzaamheid en de kwaliteit van leven in Nederland. Jouw unieke rol in het Nederlandse AI-ecosysteem Als Machine Learning Engineer werk je samen met het team aan het oplossen van complexe problemen en draag je bij aan de adoptie van AI in Nederland door ML-oplossingen te ontwikkelen en implementeren bij onze partners. Je neemt eigenaarschap over je werk en weet hoe je ML-methoden creatief kunt aanpassen en toepassen op real-world uitdagingen. Je werkt nauw samen met Machine Learning Project Managers en engineers, zowel binnen KickstartAI als bij onze partnerbedrijven, om ervoor te zorgen dat je technische oplossingen bijdragen aan duurzame impact. Door je groeiende expertise kun je junior collega's begeleiden en draag je actief bij aan het verbeteren van de best practices binnen het team. Dit ga je doen als Machine Learning Engineer Je bent verantwoordelijk voor het ontwerpen, bouwen en onderhouden van schaalbare machine learning-oplossingen die aansluiten bij de behoeften van onze partners. Dit omvat de volledige levenscyclus van ML-projecten: van data engineering en modelontwikkeling tot experimenten, implementatie en monitoring. Daarnaast richt je je op het implementeren van MLOps-best practices en werk je aan projecten met directe maatschappelijke impact. Als onderdeel van projecten organiseer je of neem je deel aan 3-weken durende Challenges: sessies waarin ideeën snel worden omgezet in werkbare AI-oplossingen met engineers van onze partner bedrijven – geen vrijblijvende hackathon, maar een gestructureerd proces met een duidelijke impact. Door actief kennis te delen, draag je bij aan de adoptie van AI binnen onze partnerbedrijven en de bredere AI-community. Concreet ga je: Beheren van de volledige ML-levenscyclus: van data engineering en modelontwikkeling tot experimenten, implementatie en monitoring in productie. Implementeren van MLOps-best practices om betrouwbare en efficiënte ML-systemen op te zetten. Werken aan projecten met directe maatschappelijke impact binnen sectoren zoals gezondheidszorg, duurzaamheid en logistiek. Actief kennis delen binnen de AI-community en bijdragen aan de adoptie van AI bij partnerbedrijven. Dit zoeken wij Wij geloven dat een sterk team bestaat uit diverse achtergronden. Of je nu uit de econometrie, computer science of software engineering komt: als jij code kunt omzetten in impact, nodigen we je uit om te solliciteren. Je hebt 2+ jaar aantoonbare werkervaring met het ontwikkelen van datagedreven oplossingen. Je hebt uitstekende programmeervaardigheden in Python. Je bent een 'T-shaped' engineer. Je hebt een brede interesse, maar blinkt uit in een specifiek domein (Software engineering/MLOps/Data Science/Computer Vision/GenAI). Je kunt technische concepten helder uitleggen aan niet-technische stakeholders en denkt mee over de business impact. Je bent bekend met ten minste één cloud platform(Azure/AWS/GCP). Ervaring met Tensorflow/Pytorch, Kubernetes, Docker is een pre, maar nieuwsgierigheid en leergierigheid zijn belangrijker. Dit krijg je ervoor terug Bij KickstartAI krijg je een technisch uitdagende rol waarin je werkt aan AI-innovaties die Nederland versterken. Je wordt onderdeel van de grootste AI-community in Nederland (7.500+ professionals) en werkt met de nieuwste technologieën. We bieden een plek waar je op het hoogste niveau aan complexe AI-vraagstukken werkt, samen leert en innoveert. Competitief salarispakket met 15% pensioenbijdrage en 8% vakantiegeld. 26 vakantiedagen. 26 weken volledig doorbetaald ouderschapsverlof vanaf de geboortedatum, op te nemen in één aaneengesloten periode. Hybride werken: 2 dagen thuis, 3 dagen op kantoor/bij de klant. €1.000 jaarlijks opleidingsbudget en toegang tot TechDays en toonaangevende conferenties. 10% van je tijd voor experimenten en eigen projecten. Nieuwe MacBook Pro met alle premium AI-tools. Moderne werkplek bij Tech hub NEXT Delft. €50 maandelijks Alleo-budget voor activiteiten. €20 telefoonvergoeding en €65 onkostenvergoeding per maand. €0,23/km reiskostenvergoeding of een OV Vrij-abonnement met NS-fiets. 12 maanden contract met zicht op vast dienstverband. Klaar om samen met ons AI in Nederland naar een hoger niveau te tillen? We horen graag van je! Stuur je CV en een korte motivatie waarom jij de ideale kandidaat bent voor deze rol.

items.desc: Founding Robot Learning Engineer | YC-Backed Physical AI & Robotics Startup | London (Remote) | Full-Time | Up to £150K + Equity About The Company Our client is a Y Combinator-backed (S26) physical AI data company building the foundational human video and motion datasets for leading robotics and embodied-AI teams. Focused on egocentric first-person video and UMI demonstration data, the company turns real-world capture operations into high-precision, versioned data products that foundation-model and VLA teams rely on to train physical robots. Backed by a freshly closed seed round, their core constraint is supply, not demand. They are actively scaling deployment engineering, field operations, and capture hardware to keep up with massive customer demand. The founders are building a three-person founding engineering team to set the technical standards, tooling, and evaluation methodology behind the world's reference dataset for robot learning. About The Role Reporting to the Engineering Lead (and working directly with partners and founders), the Founding Robot Learning Engineer bridges human demonstration data and real-world policy performance. You will decide, with empirical evidence, what datasets the company should collect and how that data should be represented. This role balances hands-on data workflow engineering with policy experimentation. You will build task segmentation and assisted-labeling workflows, construct policy data loaders, and execute policy training and evaluation experiments using egocentric and UMI datasets to prove that the company's data directly improves robot task success. Key Responsibilities Turn long recordings into useful task intervals, define annotation schemas for specific customer needs, and ensure every label remains frame-locked to the source video. Deploy AI models to propose task boundaries and labels, route uncertain results for human review, write labeling instructions, and measure reviewer consistency. Build custom data loaders and transformations that format video, labels, and motion trajectories (including human hand motion and UMI gripper paths) into policy-ready inputs. Fine-tune and evaluate robot policies on human demonstration data, running controlled baseline comparisons, held-out split tests, and task performance evaluations under realistic test conditions. Translate policy evaluation insights into precise data recommendations—guiding perception and capture teams on which tasks, viewpoints, and annotations yield the highest policy improvement. Skills & Competencies Demonstrated experience training, fine-tuning, and evaluating robot manipulation or imitation learning policies (e.g., Diffusion Policies, VLAs, ACT). Strong Python and PyTorch capability with comfort building dataset interfaces, loaders, and annotation tooling alongside ML research. Deep understanding of evaluation leakage, dataset confounders, and the gap between offline loss metrics and physical robot task success. Experience working with temporal action segmentation, video annotations, spatial trajectories, and human-to-robot data transfer. Qualifications & Experience Background as a Robot Learning Engineer, Embodied AI Researcher, or Robotics ML Engineer. Proven track record of personally preparing training data, training or fine-tuning robot policies, and evaluating physical or simulated task performance. Hands-on implementation experience connecting dataset decisions directly to policy improvements, identifying confounders, and preventing data leakage. Background in physical robot manipulation, diffusion policies, vision-language-action models, or human-to-robot transfer is highly desirable. Role Details Timing: Immediate Start. Location: London (Remote). Package: Competitive base salary up to £150K + significant founding-engineer equity with absolute ownership over policy evaluation and dataset standards.

items.desc:
ABOUT MISTRAL

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.




ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Research Engineer, GPU performance, you will sit at the heart of that spectrum: your low-level work directly determines how fast our frontier models can be trained and served. Working hand-in-hand with Research Scientists, you'll make every GPU count.

Mistral AI is hiring an expert in pushing large language model's GPU utilization and performance to their limits.. In this role, you will own the performance of our models end-to-end: writing the low-level code that extracts the maximum capacity from high-end hardware, and rethinking model architectures so they run efficiently at scale.




WHAT YOU WILL DO

 - Develop low-level code that takes full advantage of high-end GPUs and maxes out their capacity — from custom kernels to memory-layout and communication optimisations.

 - Rethink parts of the generative model architecture to make them more suitable for efficient inference, in collaboration with Research Scientists.

 - Integrate low-level efficient code into a high-level MLOps framework, so that optimisations benefit every training run and deployment rather than a single experiment.

 - Profile, benchmark and squeeze performance out of large-scale training and inference on thousands of GPUs.

 - Model LLM execution on various GPUs with high fidelity to assess hardware usage and build serving performance estimates.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - High technical competence for writing custom low-level kernels and pushing GPUs to their limits.

 - High expertise in the distributed computation infrastructure of current-generation GPU clusters.

 - Overall understanding of the field of generative AI; knowledge of, or interest in, fine-tuning and using language models for applications.

 - Strong software-design instincts: testing, code review, CI/CD.

 - Self-starter, low-ego, collaborative.




WHAT WE OFFER

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

PRIVACY POLICY

Your privacy matters to us. You can learn more about how we handle your personal data in our Applicant Privacy Policy https://legal.mistral.ai/terms/applicant-privacy-policy.

items.desc: 189272 Translational Research Scientist: Experimental Medicine Nuffield Department of Orthopaedics, Rheumatology and Musculoskeletal Sciences (NDORMS) Grade 8: Salary in the range of £49,119-£58,265 per annum. This is inclusive of a pensionable Oxford University Weighting of £1,730 per year. This is a full time, fixed term position for 24 months. The University of Oxford is a stimulating work environment, which enjoys an international reputation as a world-class centre of excellence. Our research plays a key role in tackling many global challenges, from reducing our carbon emissions to developing vaccines during a pandemic. The Nuffield Department of Orthopaedics, Rheumatology and Musculoskeletal Sciences (NDORMS) is part of the Medical Sciences Division and is the largest European academic department in its field, running a globally competitive programme of research and teaching. The Kennedy Institute is a biomedical research centre uniquely bringing together discovery science and early-stage clinical research, to develop transformative new therapies for chronic inflammatory and musculoskeletal conditions. What We Offer As an employer, we genuinely care about our employees’ wellbeing and this is reflected in the range of benefits that we offer including: An excellent contributory pension scheme 38 days annual leave A comprehensive range of childcare services Family leave schemes Cycle loan scheme Discounted bus travel and Season Ticket travel loans Membership to a variety of social and sports clubs About the Role We are offering an exciting and unique opportunity for an experienced researcher to work as a Translational Research Scientist at the interface of academia and industry, joining a large multidisciplinary team working on Experimental Medicine. The team are carrying out histopathological and omics analyses of samples from clinical studies sponsored by industry partners, which aim to understand the molecular basis disease pathways and potential new treatment targets. The Translational Research Scientist will contribute to the set-up, delivery and continuity of the research projects and programmes by providing advanced technical and scientific expertise in support. Unlike a traditional Postdoctoral Research Associate (PDRA) role, this position is not primarily aligned with a standard academic career progression pathway. Instead, the postholder will focus on collaborative research, the application of specialist knowledge, and the development, optimisation, and maintenance of methodologies, facilities, or shared resources. The role emphasises long-term contribution, technical leadership, and support for team-based research objectives, rather than the pursuit of independent academic advancement or principal investigator status. About You You must hold a PhD/DPhil in immunology or related area, together with post-qualification research experience. You will have experience of independently managing a research project and evidence of having collaborated with both wet and dry lab researchers to complete a project. Demonstrated experience in standard laboratory-based immunology techniques, such as human tissue handling and culture, PCR, flow cytometry, is essential. Proficiency in conducting 10X single-cell RNAseq and spatial transcriptomics is desirable. Application Process The University of Oxford is committed to equality and valuing diversity. All applicants will be judged on merit, according to the selection criteria. Applications for this vacancy should be made online and must include a CV and a supporting statement explaining how you meet the selection criteria, using examples of your skills and experience. Interviews will take place during the week commencing 23 November and will be face to face/online. Please quote reference 189272 in all correspondence.

items.desc: Salary : We are committed to equality, diversity and inclusion, creating a community where colleagues feel respected and valued. We aim to reflect the diversity of our students and communities, and to strengthen our university through collaboration and diverse perspectives, across all roles at the University. £38,784 with a dedicated £6,000 training budget for personal development Full Time - 40 hours per week Location: primarily based at the company partner’s premises in Cardiff. Fixed Term – 32 months Frontier Therapeutics Ltd, in partnership with the University of Hull is looking to recruit a dynamic and highly driven graduate with relevant biomedical skills who will lead the implementation of appropriate models to demonstrate efficacy of a prototype radio frequency-based medical device to support the care of hard-to-heal wounds. Chronic wounds, such as diabetic foot ulcers, impose a significant burden on the NHS, costing £8.3 billion annually, and severely impact quality of life. This KTP project is an exciting and rare opportunity to lead an interdisciplinary wound innovation project working at the interface between academia and industry. You will be primarily based at Frontier Therapeutics Ltd, working closely with key Frontier Therapeutics staff, alongside a second KTP associate. You will be supported by academic experts from Hull (Wound biology and translational models) and York (electronics and plasma science). Working in synergy with the second KTP associate (plasma) you will support device development and lead on evaluating pre-clinical efficacy, safety and benefit for patients. The successful applicant for this KTP Associate role will be employed by the University of Hull and primarily based within Frontier Therapeutics at Cardiff Medicentre, Cardiff University Heath Park Campus. Frontier Medical Group is a market-leading provider of a range of specialist medical devices to healthcare professionals in the UK and internationally. The Hull Wound Innovation Centre is at the forefront of UK wound research. It brings together world-leading biologists, engineers and clinical staff to deliver fundamental insight into the mechanisms of wound repair. Supported by £48M investment from Research England and industry, cutting-edge technology, close working with the NHS, and a suite of translational research models, the centre provides a unique environment to develop and evaluate exciting new advanced wound technologies in key areas of unmet clinical need. Role As a KTP Associate, you will lead this high-profile and strategically meaningful project, allowing you to apply your academic achievements in an industrial setting. You are expected to have the confidence and ability to manage your own workloads to ensure outputs. You will receive practical and formal training, gain marketable skills, broaden your knowledge and expertise within an industrially relevant project, and be supported by both industrial and academic mentors. You will work closely with the second associate and have joint responsibility for engaging with and embedding new knowledge within both the business partner and the Universities. Skills, Experience & Qualifications needed PhD in Biomedical science or other relevant discipline. Hands on experience of developing, implementing and/or validating wound models. Relevant experience of working in a commercial and/or industrial environment, Knowledge of the wound regulatory landscape and/or pre-clinical testing pathways. Further information It is essential that you understand how KTP works with business & the University, and the vital role you will play. For information about KTPs please visit https://www.ktp-uk.org/ Restrictions: Previous KTP Associates are ineligible to apply. This is a full-time role for a fixed-term period of 32-months and you will be primarily based at the company partner’s premises in Cardiff. We offer family friendly, flexible working arrangements, with forums and inclusive facilities to support our staff.
