items.desc: Area Engineering Location Jubilee Campus Salary £32,080 to £47,389 per annum, depending on skills and experience (minimum £35608 with relevant PhD). Closing Date Friday 30 October 2026 Reference ENG0484726 This post is part of the EPSRC Programme Grant “Dialling Up Performance for On Demand Manufacturing”. This project aims to develop a TOOLKIT to enable the rapid formulation of 3D printable materials into products. This toolkit will be composed of an integrated suite of software and experimental tools and will be informed by the collection of data en route to the development of advanced 3D printed products. The focus of this specific role is the development of software tools that support the development of TOOLKIT: to develop and use optimisation techniques to determine new geometrical configurations suitable for a range of products. Initially this will be aimed at biocatalytic flow reactors, but it is anticipated that other applications may be considered. This is an interdisciplinary collaboration that will require working with researchers across engineering, catalysis, optimisation and computational modelling. Your role will be to develop and advance the computational framework describing biocatalytic flow reactors to enable design optimisation to be performed, and new, more efficient designs to be proposed and manufactured. You will aid in writing publications, present research at national and international conferences and liaise with collaborators. You will be given support to develop and shape your future career, and hence this position may be particularly attractive to those looking to develop their research independence and leadership skills in a supportive and team-oriented environment. You must have (or about to complete) a PhD in engineering, physics or a related discipline. A demonstrable ability to use scientific languages and packages, such as Python or Matlab, is essential and a knowledge of 3D printing and related techniques is desirable. You will have good interpersonal skills and the ability of working in a team to tight deadlines. The CV and/or cover letter should clearly exemplify how you meet the criteria highlighted herein and in the Role Profile and describe your motivation for applying for this position. items.desc: Department: Centre for Functional Assays & Screening, Therapeutics Discovery Location: Måløv, Denmark Your impact begins here As Research Scientist, you will build the engineered mammalian cell lines and cellular assays that help our project teams identify and select drug candidates. You will turn biological questions into robust, reproducible in vitro data that teams can act on with confidence. Working across multiple projects in Therapeutics Discovery, you will help move research forward today, supporting the search for new treatment options for people living with diabetes, obesity and other serious chronic diseases. What You’ll Bring You combine hands-on expertise in cell line engineering with a strong understanding of what makes a cellular assay reliable and fit for purpose. A PhD in cell biology, molecular biology, biotechnology, pharmacology or a related discipline. Proven expertise in mammalian cell culture, stable cell line generation, clonal isolation and functional cell line characterisation. Experience with engineered cell lines and cellular assays, such as reporter gene, receptor binding, target engagement, flow cytometry and/or high-content imaging assays. Knowledge of assay optimisation and validation. Excellent communication skills and the ability to build and maintain relationships, both internally and externally. Curiosity, a proactive mindset and openness to new ideas, people and challenges – and a habit of sharing knowledge and giving and receiving feedback. Expertise in advanced single-cell cloning, clonal-selection technologies and genetic characterisation of KO/KI cell lines (a strong advantage). Experience with automated liquid handling systems and high-throughput screening. What You’ll Do Your work will give project teams the cell-based models and assay data they need to make clear decisions about which drug candidates to take forward. Design, develop and characterise engineered mammalian cell lines for drug discovery and screening. Apply molecular and cellular biology techniques, including transfection, viral transduction, CRISPR/Cas9 editing, and clonal selection. Establish robust, reproducible and fit-for-purpose cellular assays that support drug candidate identification and selection. Plan, prioritise and coordinate with screening, automation, in vivo pharmacology and project teams to advance cell-based models and screening strategies. Represent the department across a range of projects and help drive research project progression. Who You’ll Work With You will join the Centre for Functional Assays & Screening (CFAS), part of Therapeutics Discovery in Måløv, Denmark. CFAS designs and runs a range of biologically relevant medium- and high-throughput screening assays, with a strong focus on automation and digitalisation. The team delivers high-quality in vitro data to support the identification, optimisation and characterisation of drug candidates across multiple projects. CFAS consists of three sub-departments with 20 scientists at different levels of seniority, 15 laboratory technicians and two PhD students. Day to day, you will work closely with department scientists, laboratory technicians and cross-functional project teams. Because CFAS operates in a matrix organisation, you will also partner with screening, automation and in vivo pharmacology colleagues, and connect with colleagues across our global research sites – combining different expertise to keep projects moving. Your manager will be Assoc. Director Simon Erlendsson. What You Can Expect Here You will be part of a high-performing, multidisciplinary team where knowledge-sharing and feedback are part of how the work gets done. Your expertise will be heard across projects, and you will be trusted to shape the cell-based models and screening strategies teams rely on. The environment is dynamic and evolving, with close links to automation and digitalisation. Working with colleagues across global research sites gives you the opportunity to build a strong scientific network and grow your skills through practical, cross-project experience. Salary: For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from DKK 570,200 to 838,100, corresponding to the level of the position. The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge, and relevant experience. Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks. Learn more about our Reward Philosophy here . Start now Your impact begins today. If you are ready to turn cell line engineering and assay expertise into progress for our research projects, apply for the Research Scientist (in vitro biological assays) role by 1 November 2026 . We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality of opportunity for all our job applicants.

items.desc: Salary: £37,369 to £46,970 per annum Newcastle University is a great place to work, with excellent benefits . We have a generous holiday package; plus the opportunity to buy more, great pension schemes and a number of health and wellbeing initiatives to support you. Closing Date: 28 October 2026 We are excited to offer an opportunity for a Research Associate in Digital Innovation and Transformation to join Newcastle University Business School. Working with Professor Savvas Papagiannidis, you will contribute to research on how artificial intelligence and other emerging technologies are changing organisations, society and higher education. You will join a leading business school in the heart of Newcastle, at the gateway to Newcastle Helix. Newcastle University Business School is part of a Russell Group university and holds triple accreditation from AMBA, AACSB and EQUIS. The School brings together a diverse community of researchers, educators, students and external partners with a shared interest in rigorous, relevant research and teaching. The Opportunity This two-year, full-time fixed term role sits within a portfolio of research and education activity led by Professor Savvas Papagiannidis. The work focuses on digital transformation and information systems, with particular attention to the adoption, governance and consequences of artificial intelligence, including generative AI. The role offers scope to contribute to research examining how digital technologies reshape organisational strategy, innovation, business models and user experience. You will support the development and delivery of research projects, helping to generate evidence that is useful to academic, policy, practitioner and public audiences. You will also contribute to teaching and learning activity concerned with the effective, responsible and evidence informed use of AI in higher education. This may include supporting the design and evaluation of educational interventions, such as TheoryHub, contributing to teaching materials and producing scholarship of teaching and learning outputs. Reporting to Professor Savvas Papagiannidis, you will work across research, education and impact activities. You will undertake literature reviews, support case study research and collect, analyse and interpret qualitative or quantitative data. You will help prepare research outputs, including reports, journal papers, conference presentations and materials for non academic audiences. You may contribute to stakeholder engagement with industry partners, policymakers and academic colleagues, helping to translate findings into practical insights, frameworks and recommendations. The role will also involve contributing ideas on research design and methodology, assessing findings to identify opportunities for further investigation, and supporting funding applications and the development of future research proposals. About You You will hold a doctorate in a relevant discipline, such as information systems management, business, digital innovation or a closely related field. You will have demonstrable knowledge of technology adoption, diffusion and implementation within digital transformation. We are particularly keen to hear from applicants who can critically evaluate theories and concepts to develop original research responses. You will be able to analyse research data accurately, draw well supported conclusions and communicate complex ideas clearly to different audiences. You will bring experience of collaborative research and an ability to manage your own work effectively while contributing to shared project objectives. Experience of presenting at conferences or publishing in high-quality outlets will be valuable, as will an interest in the organisational, societal or educational implications of artificial intelligence. You will be organised, attentive to detail and comfortable managing competing responsibilities to agreed deadlines. We welcome applicants who value inclusive ways of working, ongoing professional development and collaboration across disciplines and sectors. Development and Support Newcastle University is committed to supporting researchers at every career stage through the Researcher Development Concordat . You will have access to mentoring, annual research planning discussions, peer review support for research and innovation funding applications, and pooled funding that supports career development and research activity. The University is committed to a positive research culture that is open, collaborative and sustainable. We support the responsible use of research metrics, guided by expert judgement and inclusive practice. We welcome conversations with prospective applicants and are committed to making the recruitment process accessible. If you require adjustments or additional support during the application process, please let us know. How To Apply We want you to feel confident when applying for a position with Newcastle University. items.desc:
Job Description: 
 Leonardo è un gruppo industriale internazionale che realizza capacità tecnologiche multidominio per la sicurezza globale. Protagonista dei principali programmi strategici dell’Aerospazio, Difesa e Sicurezza, conta oltre 62.000 dipendenti nel mondo. L’azienda ha una significativa presenza industriale in Italia, Regno Unito, Polonia e Stati Uniti e opera in 150 Paesi anche attraverso controllate, joint venture e partecipazioni. Leonardo è partner tecnologico e industriale di Governi, Amministrazioni della Difesa, Istituzioni e imprese
 All’interno della Divisione Spazio , stiamo ricercando un/a Space Navigation Engineer per la nostra sede di Roma - via Faustiniana 
 La persona si occuperà di: 
 Progettare, sviluppare, implementare e validare algoritmi di navigazione avanzata per sistemi autonomi.
 Condurre attività di ricerca su tecniche innovative di Artificial Intelligence applicate a Earth Observation, Space Navigation, Exploration e Surveillance, incluse percezione, mapping e motion planning.
 Studiare e sviluppare tecniche di robust navigation, interference monitoring e mitigazione delle cyber-attacks basate su advanced signal processing e Controlled Radiated Pattern Antenna (CRPA).
 Analizzare e integrare dati provenienti da sensori eterogenei per migliorare la precisione e la resilienza della navigazione.
 Prototipare e testare soluzioni di navigazione in ambienti simulati e reali, definendo metriche di performance, procedure di test e criteri di validazione.
 Collaborare con team di sviluppo software, hardware e AI per integrare algoritmi e moduli di navigazione in piattaforme esistenti.
 Ottimizzare algoritmi per l’esecuzione real‑time su architetture eterogenee.
 Documentare risultati, metodologie e processi attraverso report tecnici, documentazione di progetto, pubblicazioni scientifiche e materiali per conferenze.
 Monitorare lo stato dell’arte tecnico e scientifico, proponendo soluzioni innovative e contribuendo allo sviluppo di nuove metodologie.
 Contribuire alla definizione delle roadmap tecnologiche relative ai sistemi spaziali autonomi e alle attività di ricerca e sviluppo.
 Supportare la preparazione di proposte, la pianificazione di progetti, la definizione dei piani di lavoro e la stima delle risorse.
 Monitorare l’avanzamento tecnico dei progetti rispetto agli obiettivi, fornendo inputs per le review, identificando scostamenti, criticità e rischi.
 Verificare la conformità delle attività e delle spese rispetto alle linee guida interne e ai requisiti progettuali.
 Garantire un flusso informativo costante con partner di progetto e funzioni aziendali coinvolte nei rapporti con l’autorità di gestione/ente erogatore.
 Titolo di studio: 
 Laurea in discipline STEM (Ingegneria Elettronica, delle Telecomunicazioni o affini).
 Livello di esperienza richiesto: 
 Junior/Expert: 1-5 y di esperienzia nel ruolo e/o funzioni analoghe
 Competenze e conoscenze tecniche: 
 Fondamenti di navigazione spaziale e terrestre: meccanica orbitale, dinamiche di volo, sistemi di riferimento e trasformazioni.
 Tecniche di elaborazione del segnale applicate alla navigazione.
 Sensor fusion: Kalman Filter e varianti (EKF, UKF), Particle Filter, metodi bayesiani.
 Tecniche di AI per applicazioni spaziali: deep learning, machine learning, federated learning, probabilistic navigation, SLAM, perception & mapping.
 Architetture e protocolli dei sistemi di posizionamento GNSS (GPS, Galileo, GLONASS, BeiDou).
 Modelli fisici e geometrici per navigazione e percezione (camera models, LiDAR models, error budgeting).
 Principi di integrity e cyber‑resilience per sistemi di navigazione: RAIM, A‑RAIM, interference monitoring, anomaly detection, robust algorithm design, sensor threat mitigation.
 Sviluppo software per sistemi embedded e real‑time, con ottimizzazione su CPU, GPU ed edge computing.
 Conoscenza degli standard e normative del settore spazio (ECSS, ESA, NASA) relativi a sviluppo software, qualifica e documentazione.
 Capacità di redigere documentazione tecnica, report, deliverable e pubblicazioni scientifiche.
 Costituisce un plus l’esperienza maturata in ambito Spazio in aziende, centri di ricerca o consorzi internazionali.
 Competenze comportamentali: 
 Orientamento ai risultati
 Team work
 Negoziazione
 Comunicazione efficace
 Orientamento al cliente
 Problem Solving
 Flessibilità
 Organizzazione e Pianificazione
 Conoscenze linguistiche: 
 Inglese (liv. min. B2)
 Competenze informatiche: 
 Framework e tool di simulazione: MATLAB/Simulink, ANSYS STK.
 Python (NumPy, SciPy, TensorFlow/PyTorch, OpenCV)
 C and C/C++
 Altro: 
 Disponibilità a trasferte in Italia e all’estero.
 Coinvolgimento, valorizzazione delle competenze , cura del benessere e della sicurezza delle persone sono i cardini della nostra cultura aziendale. 
 Ci impegniamo ogni giorno a favorire un ambiente di lavoro inclusivo e stimolante , promuovendo attivamente i principi di inclusione, equità e valorizzazione delle diversità.

items.desc: About Revolut People deserve more from their money. More visibility, more control, and more freedom. Since 2015, Revolut has been on a mission to deliver just that. Our powerhouse of products — including spending, saving, investing, exchanging, travelling, and more — help our 80+ million customers get more from their money every day. As we continue our lightning-fast growth,‌ 2 things are essential to our success: our people and our culture. In recognition of our outstanding employee experience, we've been certified as a Great Place to Work™. So far, we have 13,000+ people working around the world, from our offices and remotely, to help us achieve our mission. And we're looking for more brilliant people. People who love building great products, redefining success, and turning the complexity of a chaotic world into the simplicity of a beautiful solution. About the Graduate Programme Our Graduate Programme is built for ambitious graduates who want to launch their careers in fintech. Over this 12-month programme, you’ll work on real projects, solve complex challenges, and make an impact from day one. With structured training and hands-on experience, you’ll grow your skills while exploring different areas of the business. Top performers can be promoted during or after the programme, giving you the chance to continue your journey at Revolut. About the role The Product team shapes the experiences that power Revolut. They turn complex problems into simple, scalable solutions, collaborating across Design, Engineering, and Data to build features our customers love. We’re looking for Graduate Applied AI Engineers who can combine product ownership with technical execution. You’ll identify how AI can solve high-value problems, guide product strategy, and manage the models, data, architecture, and evaluation needed to deliver measurable business outcomes. Up to shape what's next in finance? Let’s get in touch. Join us from anywhere The Graduate Programme is open to international applicants ready to relocate to one of our tech hubs in Poland, Portugal, Spain, the UAE, or the UK. We’ll support you with visa assistance, travel costs, and accommodation (conditions apply). You’ll be expected to spend around 3 days per week in the office (where role and location allow). Key dates Recruitment process: July–December 2026 Programme start: March or September 2027 Roles are filled on a rolling basis, so apply early. You can specify your preferred intake during the recruitment process. What you'll be doing Owning the design, development, and deployment of AI-powered features, leveraging LLMs and modern machine learning frameworks Collaborating with Data Scientists, Software Engineers, and Product Managers to turn prototype models into scalable features Building and optimising data pipelines, prompt workflows, and model integration components for AI assistants and automation tools Setting goals, metrics, and roadmaps to deliver measurable results in a fast-paced environment What you'll need A predicted or achieved first-class degree (or equivalent grade) A bachelor’s or master’s degree in computer science, artificial intelligence, data science, mathematics, or a related STEM/technical field To have graduated in 2025, 2026, or 2027 Proficiency in Python, SQL, or other programming language skills Knowledge of machine learning fundamentals, deep learning frameworks (PyTorch, TensorFlow, etc.), and modern NLP or LLM techniques (via coursework, research, internships, or personal projects) Hands-on experience building and evaluating ML or AI models (e.g., capstone projects, open-source contributions, or Kaggle competitions) Solid mathematical, statistical, and problem-solving skills Full-time availability from early or late 2027 The ability to travel to a Revolut office in your country of employment A willingness to attend the office at least 3 days per week (this is a hybrid role) Nice to have Experience in product-related work Experience as an entrepreneur or working in a startup Compensation range Krakow: PLN24,600 - PLN24,600 gross monthly* Poland: PLN24,600 - PLN24,600 gross monthly* Other locations: Compensation will be discussed during the interview process Final compensation will be determined based on the candidate's qualifications, skills, and previous experience Building a global financial super app isn’t enough. Our Revoluters are a priority, and that’s why in 2021 we launched our inaugural D&I Framework, designed to help us thrive and grow everyday. We're not just doing this because it's the right thing to do. We’re doing it because we know that seeking out diverse talent and creating an inclusive workplace is the way to create exceptional, innovative products and services for our customers. That’s why we encourage applications from people with diverse backgrounds and experiences to join this multicultural, hard-working team. Important notice for candidates: Job scams are on the rise. items.card: Your Responsibilities: Make an Impact with Us. As a Marketing Data Scientist at Tchibo, you will leverage our advanced data infrastructure on the Google Cloud Platform (GCP) to generate actionable insights. You conduct detailed analyses of customer, marketing, and onsite data using SQL and Python to optimize the operational management of marketing campaigns. You will take end-to-end ownership of your analytical
items.desc: We do things differently. Do you? Tchibo is one of Germany’s ten largest e-commerce companies. We couldn’t have achieved this without the courage to constantly rethink the status quo. In our Tech division at Tchibo, we work to develop sustainable and effective solutions with modern technologies. Want to join us? Bring your fresh perspective to our team! Your Responsibilities: Make an Impact with Us. As a Marketing Data Scientist at Tchibo, you will leverage our advanced data infrastructure on the Google Cloud Platform (GCP) to generate actionable insights. You conduct detailed analyses of customer, marketing, and onsite data using SQL and Python to optimize the operational management of marketing campaigns. You will take end-to-end ownership of your analytical projects—from initial data analysis and preparation to model evaluation and the automated delivery of findings. Expand and optimize Data Science use cases, such as marketing mix modelling or bidding optimizations, using open-source technologies. Develop and provide self-service BI solutions tailored specifically to marketing requirements and customer attributes. Your Profile: You’re Always Reinventing Us. You have several years of professional experience in developing analytical models using machine learning algorithms to derive customer and marketing insights. You possess a broad interest in various modelling approaches, such as time-series analysis, NLP, or deep learning. You have excellent proficiency in at least one programming language, preferably Python, and are skilled in the practical application of statistical methods. Experience with GCP technologies like BigQuery and the Google AI Platform is a strong asset. Experience in onsite tracking, e.g., Google Analytics, as well as in online marketing and an understanding of digital marketing strategies and metrics. Experience with marketing automation tools and CRM systems. You are characterized by an agile and open mindset, a commitment to quality, flexibility, and a proactive, hands-on mentality. You enjoy collaborating with diverse teams and have a strong curiosity for new technologies and analytical methods, completing your profile. Your benefits: Together we stay different. Work-Life Balance: Flexible, hybrid working policy with 26 vacation days + your birthday off. Benefits: Monthly transport allowance (80 RON/month), meal tickets, and health/life insurance. Personal Perks: Free Tchibo coffee for home, and the chance to work on cutting-edge technology in a dynamic environment. Innovative Work Environment: We are a forward-thinking team where creativity and innovation are encouraged. You will collaborate with talented professionals and contribute to building Tchibo Tech, shaping the future of our technology landscape. Inclusive Culture: A diverse and inclusive workplace where your unique perspectives and ideas are valued, fostering a culture of collaboration and mutual respect. Impactful Work: Our meaningful projects make a real difference, driving positive change and contributing to the success of Tchibo.

Elle accompagne ses client·es dans la conception de produits numériques performants, en combinant expertise technique et compréhension des enjeux métiers. Amarflow valorise la collaboration, l’esprit d’initiative et l’amélioration continue des méthodes de travail. Rejoindre Amarflow, c’est évoluer dans un environnement agile, ouvert aux nouvelles idées et aux expérimentations. L’entreprise accorde une importance particulière à la qualité, à l’éthique et à la transparence dans l’usage des technologies d’IA. Description du poste En tant qu’expert·e IA chez Amarflow, vous intervenez en temps partiel sur la conception, l’amélioration et l’évaluation de modèles d’intelligence artificielle pour différents projets. Vous participez à la définition des architectures techniques, au choix des outils et frameworks, ainsi qu’à l’implémentation de solutions IA robustes et sécurisées. Au quotidien, vous collaborez avec les équipes produit et développement pour traduire les besoins métiers en cas d’usage IA concrets, et pour documenter méthodologie, performances et limites des modèles. Vous contribuez également à la veille technologique, à l’optimisation des pipelines de données et à l’intégration continue des modèles dans les applications. Le poste est hybride : vous êtes basé·e dans le Greater Lyon Area, avec une partie du temps de travail réalisable à domicile. Qualifications Maîtrise des concepts fondamentaux de l’intelligence artificielle et du machine learning, incluant la conception, l’entraînement et l’évaluation de modèles. Compétences en programmation (par exemple Python) et utilisation de frameworks IA courants (TensorFlow, PyTorch ou équivalents), ainsi qu’en gestion de versions (Git). Connaissance des bonnes pratiques de gestion et de préparation de données (nettoyage, structuration, pipelines de données) et des enjeux de qualité des données. Capacité à collaborer avec des équipes pluridisciplinaires, à vulgariser des concepts techniques et à documenter clairement les solutions mises en place. Une expérience en déploiement de modèles en production, en éthique de l’IA, en optimisation de performances et en environnement cloud (par exemple AWS, GCP ou Azure) est fortement appréciée.

items.desc: all positions Helsinki – onsite – FullTime AI/ML Engineer Our AI team is looking for an individual who is exceptional at the applied end of the craft: taking modern models and turning them into features and tools that hold up in production, at Supercell scale, under real deadlines. The challenge at the centre of this role is the distance between a demo and a product. A model that works in a notebook is not a feature that works for hundreds of millions of players, or a tool a game team trusts with their daily work. Help us Close that gap: the evaluation that tells you it's actually good, the latency and cost envelope that makes it viable, the failure modes you find before players do, and the plumbing that makes it boring to operate. We're not looking for someone who wants to train a frontier model. We're looking for someone who gets unreasonable results out of the ones that exist. We are looking for someone to build and ship: AI features in live games, and the internal tools that give superpowers to Supercellians. Some of that work will take you inside a game or central team for a while, close enough to their craft to build the right thing with them. In our team, you'll work closely with our AI Platform Engineers, AI/ML engineers, Clients Programmers, Cloud Engineers. You’ll also collaborate with other teams including Data, QA, Engine and game teams. What You'll Be Doing Build and ship AI features and systems end to end into live games and internal tools, at production quality and under real deadlines. Do the applied engineering that makes AI work in practice. Own evaluation as a first-class deliverable. Write and maintain the benchmarks, evals, and regression suites that tell you whether something is genuinely good, across the modalities you're working in. Fine-tune, adapt, and distill models where it pays off, and have the judgment to know when a better prompt, better retrieval, or a smaller model beats training anything. Make sound trade-offs on inference, including on-device where it matters, against real parameter, latency, and battery targets, without losing the feel players expect. Take on the harder applied problems, such as making autonomous agents reliable and accurate enough to trust with real work. Work close to game and central teams, sometimes embedded with them for a stretch, and build things that stay in use after you move on. Mentor our more junior AI/ML engineers through code review, pairing, and design discussion, and raise the technical bar around you. Stay at the frontier by reading the literature and following the major conferences, and bring back what is genuinely useful. What You Have Strong, current command of modern generative methods at the applied level: you know what today's models are actually good at, where they break, and how to build reliably on top of them. A track record of shipping LLM or generative AI applications that real users used, in production, not prototypes. We value this far above a publication record. Real software engineering depth. You write code others can maintain, and you own things in production rather than handing them off. Hands-on experience writing and maintaining benchmarks and evaluation frameworks, ideally across more than one modality. Practical fine-tuning and model adaptation experience, and the judgment to know when not to reach for it. Sound judgment on inference trade-offs under tight compute, latency, and cost constraints, including local or on-device deployment. The ability to work from broadly defined goals, set your own objectives, and drive work forward without waiting to be handed a spec. High EQ and credibility with makers. You can sit inside a protective, high-craft team and earn their trust fast. A generous mentor to less experienced engineers, with high ownership, comfort taking risks and learning from failure, and the humility to do excellent work with kindness. Would Be Nice if You Also Have Experience with agent frameworks, orchestration, or evaluation tooling at production scale. Game industry experience, or a real appreciation for mobile. Experience working alongside a platform or infrastructure team as an internal customer. Where You'll Be The role requires close collaboration with the other central teams and game teams, so ideally, you'd be based in Helsinki. That's it about the role! Below, we've gathered some things we feel are important for you to know. Totally optional, but a highly recommended read. Once you're ready to apply, just send us your application through the form on the bottom of the page. ––– About Supercell Supercell is a games company from Helsinki, Finland, with offices also in San Francisco, Seoul, Shanghai, and London. You might know us as the makers of Hay Day, Clash of Clans, Boom Beach, Clash Royale, and Brawl Stars . Our mission is to create great games that as many people as possible play for years and that are remembered forever. So, how do we make great games? By putting together the best teams and …

The
items.desc: Job number NAT02307 Faculties Faculty of Natural Sciences Departments Department of Life Sciences Salary or Salary range £50,733 - £59,484 per annum Location/campus South Kensington Campus - On site only Contract type work pattern Full time - Fixed term Posting End Date 3 Nov 2026 About the role Do you have expertise in genetic engineering and want to contribute to developing next-generation strategies to control mosquito populations that transmit malaria? We have an exciting opportunity for a Research Associate to join a new research programme funded by the Gates Foundation and focused on developing self-limiting genetic strategies for the population suppression of Anopheles mosquitoes. The successful candidate will play a key role in conducting independent research as part of a small team. The experimental work will focus on improving proof-of-principle technologies that we have already developed, with the aim of advancing them towards potential future deployment, as well as investigating new target genes and developing novel molecular tools to support the next generation of these technologies. What you would be doing As a Research Associate, you will play an active role in planning and delivering research within our programme. You will take initiative in designing and conducting experiments, developing appropriate molecular and experimental approaches, and analysing robust and reproducible data. You will maintain accurate records of your work and contribute to publications, presentations to funders and research meetings. You will work collaboratively with scientists, technicians and students at Imperial and with external collaborators in the UK and internationally. You will also contribute to the supervision and development of undergraduate and postgraduate students and research assistants and, where appropriate, help coordinate the work of small research teams. Alongside your research, you will contribute to the smooth running of the laboratory and to maintaining a safe, collaborative and productive research environment. What we are looking for We are looking for a motivated and proactive researcher with experience in molecular biology and genetic engineering, including DNA cloning, genetic construct design and CRISPR-Cas9 or related genome-editing approaches. You will also have experience with mosquitoes or other model organisms and transcriptomic data analysis. Previous experience with molecular and genetic assays is required as well as basic experience in bioinformatics and data analysis. Experience in embryo microinjection work would be highly advantageous. What we can offer you You will join a collaborative research environment at Imperial College London, with the opportunity to contribute to research addressing major global health challenges. The Group has a long-standing relationship with the Target Malaria research consortium, providing opportunities to engage with researchers and initiatives across the consortium and gain insight into the development, evaluation and potential deployment of genetic strategies for malaria control. You will have access to Imperial’s dedicated career development support for researchers, including 10 development days each year, alongside opportunities for progression, a competitive benefits package and a supportive, inclusive working environment. Sector-leading salary and remuneration package (including 43 days off a year and generous pension schemes). Further information Please note that this is a PhD level role but candidates who have not yet been officially awarded will be appointed as a Research Assistant. This is a full-time post. This role is for a fixed-term contract 31 August 2028, extendable for an additional 12 months subject to funding availability. If you require any further details about the role, please contact: Dr Federica Bernardini (f.bernardini11@imperial.ac.uk) or Ms Clelia Supparo (c.supparo@imperial.ac.uk). Available documents Attached documents are available under links. Clicking a document link will initialize its download. We reserve the right to close the advert before the stated closing date, should we receive a high volume of applications. items.desc: Job number NAT02295 Faculties Faculty of Natural Sciences Departments Department of Life Sciences (Silwood Park) Salary or Salary range £50,733 - £59,484 per annum Location/campus Silwood Park Campus - Hybrid Contract type work pattern Full time - Fixed term Posting End Date 30 Nov 2026 About the role This research associated with this post will be part of a wider team within the new Horizon Europe OceanSOS project https://oceansos.net/. This exciting interdisciplinary project aims to determine the impact of seamounts and the currents they create on stimulating the overlying biological carbon pump (BCP), to then inform marine spatial planning. The knowledge generated will provide a stronger foundation for assessing future ocean risks and developing sustainable management approaches. By improving understanding of the links between biodiversity, food webs, and carbon cycling, this work will support decision-making aimed at protecting ocean ecosystems and the processes that sustain them. This is an exciting opportunity to be part of an international team of biogeochemists, physical ocean modellers, ecologists and policy makers. What you would be doing You will focus on identifying how seafloor topology influences the mesopelagic biological carbon pump, specifically looking at particle type, size and microbial remineralisation across a seamount and abyssal plain. You will be part of a wider team https://oceansos.net/wp3 capturing the contributions of larger organisms, deep-sea communities, and connections between the seafloor and the open ocean in the BCP. Your specific responsibilities will include going to sea in the North Atlantic (Summer 2027) and will use multiple techniques to determine the regional BCP, to then feed into the physical, food-web and statistical models, used by the OceanSOS team. The post-holder will also facilitate fieldwork south of South Africa (early Summer 2027) and the samples collected from this region. The tools you will use at sea include sediment traps, marine snow catchers and optodes to measure microbial remineralisation. You will be responsible for organising your component of the fieldwork so it is essential you have fieldwork experience at sea. You will also process the samples you collect to then lead and co-author peer-reviewed publications, and will work closely with the wider project team. You will have the opportunity to present findings to the research team as well as at national and/or international conferences. As this project is part of a large consortium, the you will have the opportunity, and be expected to, collaborate widely within our smaller sub-team, but also with the rest of the consortia including at annual science meetings. There will also be the opportunity to work with international partners. What we are looking for Experience in fieldwork and sample analysis associated with the biological pump, sediment traps and/or microbial respiration A track record of overseeing successful experiments from design, manipulation and sampling, to data analysis and publishing the results Knowledge of processes involved in organic carbon cycling in the ocean Ideally some experience of leading your own work at sea Knowledge of how to analyse organic carbon samples Enthusiasm for research in ocean carbon science What we can offer you Being part of a large international network of project partners from across Europe, with many travel opportunities Inclusion in a vibrant team at Silwood Park Campus working on many aspects of oceanic and freshwater carbon cycling The opportunity to continue your career at a world-leading institution and be part of our mission to continue science for humanity. Grow your career: Gain access to Imperial’s sector-leading dedicated career support for researchers as well as opportunities for promotion and progression Sector-leading salary and remuneration package (including 43 days off a year and generous pension schemes). Further information The post is funded by UKRI through Horizon Europe. This is a full time, fixed term role until 31 March 2029. items.desc: Job ref: NAT02237 Salary: Competitive Closing date: 31 Oct 2026 About the role You will play a key role in a multidisciplinary programme on computational proteomics in a new physical dimension, supported by UKRI and the NSF, involving Imperial College London (Physics), the University of California San Diego (Computing), as well as industrial and academic partners in Europe and the US. The programme aims to develop conceptually new de novo sequencing tools based on two-dimensional partial covariance mass spectrometry, invented and developed in the Department of Physics at Imperial College London. This role offers a unique opportunity for a physicist interested in developing transformative analytical technologies. What you would be doing This role combines computational and experimental aspects. You will design and implement advanced computational algorithms for reconstructing peptide sequences directly from experimental mass spectral data, without recourse to protein sequence databases. You will also be engaged in mass spectral data acquisition in an analytical mass spectrometry laboratory. You will work collaboratively with the Imperial College team and US project partners on the development and optimisation of de novo sequencing algorithms. You will liaise with project partners and participate in data acquisition campaigns in partner laboratories. What we are looking for You will hold a PhD in Physics (or a closely related quantitative discipline) and have an outstanding record of research achievement. We are particularly interested in candidates with exceptional computational and analytical skills, demonstrated through the development of novel algorithms, advanced data-analysis methodologies, scientific software, machine learning approaches or other computational research tools. The ideal candidate will be intellectually ambitious, highly self-motivated and excited by the prospect of working at the boundary between physics, computation and biomolecular science. Experience in proteomics or mass spectrometry is not required; candidates with strong backgrounds in computational physics, statistical physics, machine learning, signal processing, inverse problems, optimisation, applied mathematics or related fields are particularly encouraged to apply. What we can offer you The opportunity to contribute to a pioneering international research programme aimed at establishing an entirely new physical paradigm for biomolecular sequencing. You will help develop both the underlying physical methodology and the computational frameworks required to unlock information inaccessible to conventional analytical approaches, creating new capabilities with broad scientific and technological impact. Collaboration within a multidisciplinary team involving physicists, computer scientists and analytical mass spectrometrists. Involvement in publications, conference presentations and future grant applications. The opportunity to continue your career at a world-leading institution and contribute to our mission of “Science for Humanity”. Access to Imperial’s sector-leading career support for researchers, as well as opportunities for promotion and progression. A sector-leading salary and remuneration package, including 41 days’ leave per year and generous pension schemes. A diverse, inclusive and collaborative working culture, with staff networks and resources to support your personal and professional wellbeing. Further information The position is available immediately. We would ideally like the successful candidate to start as soon as possible, but the start date is flexible and can be agreed to accommodate notice periods and other commitments. This is a full-time (35 hours per week), fixed-term role based at our South Kensington Campus. If you require further details about the role, please contact: Professor Vitali Averbukh – v.averbukh@imperial.ac.uk

items.desc: Research Associate (m/f/d) in Laser Physics & Femtochemistry (E 13 TV-L, full-time) At HAWK University of Applied Sciences and Arts Hildesheim/Holzminden/Göttingen, Faculty of Engineering and Health, Göttingen campus, the position is to be filled at the earliest possible date, for a fixed term of three years. Within the ERC Advanced Grant project FEMTOMICS, novel photonic and molecular analytical methods are being developed for the high-resolution investigation of dynamic protein-DNA interactions. Femtosecond laser-based crosslinking (fliX) is combined with complementary methods in quantitative and structural proteomics (LC-MS/MS), genomics and sequencing (ChIP-Seq, nanopore sequencing), and bioinformatics for multiomics data integration and analysis to characterise protein–DNA interactions at the structural and functional levels. The aim is to make previously inaccessible dynamic molecular processes experimentally measurable and thereby establish new foundations for investigating regulatory mechanisms in biological and disease-relevant systems. A central focus is the development and physicochemical characterisation of novel irradiation and measurement approaches based on ultrashort laser pulses. Tasks & Responsibilities Designing, constructing, commissioning, and further developing complex experimental laser systems and irradiation platforms using ultrashort laser pulses, particularly pump–probe setups and dual-wavelength irradiation systems Independently planning, conducting, and evaluating time-resolved physical and femtochemical experiments to elucidate the processes leading to protein–DNA crosslinking and DNA damage Systematically investigating and optimising relevant laser and process parameters, such as wavelength, pulse duration, pulse energy, repetition rate, temporal pulse separation, and irradiation dose Characterising, validating, and standardising the optical setups and measurement methods developed, including benchmarking, reproducibility assessments, troubleshooting, and the preparation of SOPs Working closely with experts in physics, molecular biology, proteomics, sequencing, and bioinformatics; items.desc: Descriptif de l'organisation Vous souhaitez donner du sens à votre métier ? Vous avez à cœur de contribuer au développement de l'IA de défense et de participer au renforcement de la souveraineté technologique de la France au service des forces armées ? Vous désirez rejoindre une équipe projet dynamique et agile, animée par un esprit start-up et tournée vers l’excellence opérationnelle ? Rejoignez l’AMIAD. Rattachée au Ministre des armées, l’AMIAD est une entité en en forte croissance qui développe et déploie des solutions d’IA au profit des armées. En lien étroit avec l’ensemble des entités du ministère, elle pilote des projets stratégiques et innovants dans des domaines variés tels que les systèmes d’armes, les opérations, le renseignement, le commandement, le soutien et l’administration. Descriptif du poste Ce stage porte sur la navigation autonome de robots terrestres en milieu tout-terrain. Les politiques de navigation apprises, comme NoMaD ou les modèles de l'AMIAD, génèrent des trajectoires réactives à court terme à partir d'images ou de LiDAR. Leur horizon temporel et sémantique reste toutefois limité : elles décident mal de la marche à suivre, s'adaptent peu au type de terrain et savent difficilement détecter qu'elles sont bloquées ou récupérer d'un échec. Les piles de navigation classiques confient cette supervision à des arbres de comportement (Nav2 sous ROS2), mais ceux-ci reposent sur des règles fixes, difficiles à étendre à des missions ouvertes en langage naturel. Le stage explore le paradigme du « VLA comme orchestrateur », développé en manipulation robotique : un modèle vision-langage de haut niveau supervise une politique bas niveau figée. Le stagiaire devra concevoir l'architecture de cet orchestrateur, développer l'adaptation des paramètres (vitesse, horizon de planification) au terrain perçu, mettre en place la détection d'échecs et des comportements de récupération, puis évaluer l'ensemble en simulation face à un arbre de comportement de type Nav2 et à la politique seule. Des extensions sont envisageables : commandes en langage naturel, distillation pour un usage embarqué, essais sur robots réels (Scout, Barakuda). Profil recherché Actuellement en cours de formation de niveau bac+5 en université ou en école d’ingénieurs, vous recherchez un stage d'une durée de 6 mois à compter d'avril 2027 (flexible). Vous disposez de compétences dans un ou plusieurs des domaines suivants : deep learning, modèles de fondation, modèles Vision-Langage-Action (VLA), ROS, C++ et Python. Vous avez des connaissances en anglais. Informations complémentaires Gratifications Transport Repas

 You implement, adopt, and evaluate new AI/ML algorithms and analytical techniques. 
 You own features end to end from initial model evaluation through to production deployment, within a team that prizes technical rigor and mentorship. 
 You shape how we build contributing to architectural decisions, code reviews, and the evolution of our development processes. 
 You span the stack and contribute where needed, staying curious about emerging technologies and industry best practices. 
 Who you are: 
 You bring technical rigor with a Bachelor's, Master's or PhD in Computer Science or a related technical field, and proven experience in machine learning engineering. You treat testing, clean code, and documentation as the foundation for scalable, high-impact systems. 
 You span the stack working across the ML lifecycle — from GPU optimization and model performance to backend systems and cloud-native architecture (e.g. Kubernetes, AWS) — with a solid grounding in statistics, ML theory, and modern AI/ML frameworks and tools. 
 You value collaborative engineering , seeing code reviews and architectural decisions as spaces for shared growth, and translating complex technical challenges into shared goals with partners from research scientists to DevOps engineers. 
 You are a continuous learner approaching new frameworks and languages with curiosity, as comfortable mentoring others as learning from them. 
 You are an excellent communicator translating technical complexity into clear, actionable insights with empathy and precision, so every stakeholder feels aligned and heard. 
 Preferred: 
 Experience with biological data (ideally multimodal) and scientific processes. 
 Experience working with scientists or in a research environment. 
 Experience with workflow automation, GenAI, and/or agents. 
 If you want to build the tools that make AI an everyday utility for scientists — and help bring life-changing medicines to patients faster — apply now and join us. 
 Who we are
 A healthier future drives us to innovate. Together, more than 100’000 employees across the globe are dedicated to advance science, ensuring everyone has access to healthcare today and for generations to come. Our efforts result in more than 26 million people treated with our medicines and over 30 billion tests conducted using our Diagnostics products. We empower each other to explore new possibilities, foster creativity, and keep our ambitions high, so we can deliver life-changing healthcare solutions that make a global impact.
Let’s build a healthier future, together.

items.title: Ingénieur Data/IA - l’Acoustique Sous-Marine F/H
items.card: vos missions seront les suivantes : Etudier et modéliser un problème et ses exigences, investiguer des nouvelles solutions fondées sur de nouvelles exploitations de capteurs existants ou sur de nouveaux capteurs Développer en Matlab ou Python les chaînes de références des algorithmes et les simulateurs associés Assurer les performances et la validation des algorithmes sur signaux simulés et/ou sur des signaux réels
items.desc:
Lieu : Brest, France 
 Construisons ensemble un avenir de confiance 
 Thales est un leader mondial des hautes technologies spécialisé dans trois secteurs d’activité : Défense & Sécurité, Aéronautique & Spatial, et Cyber & Digital. Il développe des produits et solutions qui contribuent à un monde plus sûr, plus respectueux de l’environnement et plus inclusif. Le Groupe investit près de 4,5 milliards d’euros par an en Recherche & Développement, notamment dans des domaines clés de l’innovation tels que l’IA, la cybersécurité, le quantique, les technologies du cloud et la 6G. Thales compte près de 85 000 collaborateurs dans 65 pays. ​
 Nos engagements, vos avantages 
 Une réussite portée par notre excellence technologique, votre expérience et notre ambition partagée
 Un package de rémunération attractif
 Un développement des compétences en continu : parcours de formation, académies et communautés internes
 Un environnement inclusif, bienveillant et respectant l’équilibre des collaborateurs
 Un engagement sociétal et environnemental reconnu
 Votre quotidien 
Le site de Brest abrite nos activités de services numériques ainsi que l'expertise de Thales en matière de développement, d'intégration et de maintenance pour des systèmes de patrouille et de surveillance maritimes, de guerre électronique, de systèmes sonars et de lutte sous-marine aéroportée ainsi que nos activités de services numériques. 
 Le service Etudes Générales Sonar de Brest est une partie de la Direction Technique DT2 en charge des algorithmes et la modélisation de performances dans le domaine UWS (UnderWater Systems) de Brest et de ses activités en Guerre des Mines (sonar d’imagerie et système de drones de chasse au mines) et Aéroporté (système de bouées larguées par les aéronefs comme les avions de la patrouille maritime ou bien les sonars trempés par hélicoptères).
 La partie Algorithmes vise des études de traitement de signal et du traitement d’image au profit des produits futurs, ou dans la phase de conception. La modélisation des performances nous amène à travailler dès la phase commerciale afin de préciser les performances accessibles de nos produits et tout au cours de la vie du programme pour vérifier la performance des produits livrés et jusqu’aux essais en mer ou en vol.
 Dans ce cadre, vos missions seront les suivantes : 
 Etudier et modéliser un problème et ses exigences, investiguer des nouvelles solutions fondées sur de nouvelles exploitations de capteurs existants ou sur de nouveaux capteurs
 Développer en Matlab ou Python les chaînes de références des algorithmes et les simulateurs associés
 Assurer les performances et la validation des algorithmes sur signaux simulés et/ou sur des signaux réels acquis à la mer
 Rédiger les descriptifs détaillés des algorithmes retenus et validés
 Modéliser les performances des systèmes, notamment par la modélisation des sonars et du milieu
 Collaborer étroitement avec le responsable du laboratoire et le chef de service pour garantir coût, délais et qualité technique des travaux
 Votre profil :
 Votre priorité est de maîtriser les technologies avancées en traitement du signal, de l’image et des données ? 
 Vous avez l’ambition de développer des solutions innovantes et performantes dans ces domaines ? 
 Vous avez envie de découvrir de nouvelles applications en acoustique sous-marine, positionnement inertiel et programmation GPU ?
 Vous disposez d’un diplôme d’ingénieur Grandes Écoles et/ou d’une thèse spécialisée en traitement du signal, de l’image ou de la donnée, et avez de l’expérience en : 
 Traitement du signal, de l’image ou de la vidéo 
 Data Science avec connaissance d’un framework de Machine Learning (TensorFlow, PyTorch) 
 Développement logiciel avec Matlab ou Python pour simulation et test d’algorithmes 
 La connaissance d'un environnement sonar, acoustique sous-marine, positionnement et navigation inertielle, et programmation GPU/CUDA est un plus
 Autonomie, innovation, goût pour l’expertise technique et esprit d'équipe sont des qualités que l’on vous reconnaît ? 
 Alors ce poste est fait pour vous !
Thales, entreprise Handi-Engagée, reconnait tous les talents. La diversité est notre meilleur atout. Postulez et rejoignez nous !

Location: Templecombe, United Kingdom 
 Thales is a global technology leader with more than 83,000 employees on five continents. With over 7,500 people in the UK, operating across defence, space, aerospace, and digital security, we help build a future we can all trust. Thales supports the security and stability of our nation by providing extraordinary technology to our customers, as well as delivering social value to the UK with our products and services.
 2027 Systems Engineering Graduate
 Start Date: 06 September 2027
 Salary: £34,000 per annum
 Employee type: Permanent
 Location: Templecombe
 Working Schedule: 37 hours per week (8 hours Monday - Thursday, 5 hours on a Friday)
 Are you passionate about engineering? Do you have an inquisitive mind? Do you want to be part of a Graduate Programme that will develop and challenge you? If so, then look no further… 
 What is the Engineering Development Programme? 
 This is a 3-year programme with the option to rotate, in Year 3, around the country across different business units experiencing different parts of an engineering lifecycle. You will be assigned to a succession of new or existing programmes where you will work with and be supported by other engineers to design and develop engineering solutions to meet the needs of our customers.
 During your time on the programme, you will be under the sponsorship and guidance of the Engineering Leadership team and will follow a structured and detailed learning pathway to fast track your development within your role.
 During the programme, you will: 
 · Complete a 3-year Graduate Development Programme which is accredited by the IET, IMechE and RAeS
 · An opportunity to rotate in Year 3 or explore an external secondment with one of our Thales partners
 · Participate in discipline specific learning pathways and core training pathway focusing on transversal skills
 · Develop key engineering skills, knowledge and competencies
 · Work in a set location and domain for the entirety of the scheme, enabling you to fully understand how the Engineering Function operates
 · Work on exciting new and existing products
 · Build a professional network across the organisation
 Requirements: 
 This is an entry-level graduate opportunity designed for individuals at the start of their professional career. We welcome applications from candidates who have completed a degree and have limited relevant professional experience. You will have gained or be on track to achieve a bachelor’s degree in a STEM Subject in one of the following subject areas:
 • Aeronautical or Aerospace Engineering
 • Electrical and/or Electronic Engineering
 • Information Technology
 • Mathematics
 • Physics
 • Systems Engineering
 • AI, Machine Learning and Cybernetics
 • Computing or Computer Science
 • All applicable technical or related degrees will be considered
 Benefits 
 · Competitive salary of £34,000 per annum
 · Performance-related pay uplifts
 · Holiday entitlement of 201 hours a year (plus a company day and bank holidays)
 · Contributory Company Pension
 · Health Care Cash Plan
 · Hybrid/flexible working options
 · Employee assistance programme
 · Learning and development support
 · Employee discounts and wellbeing initiatives
 · Life cover
 · 80 Hours Volunteering per year (first two years)
 Thales Graduate Recruitment Process 
 1. Apply Online - submit your application online to register your interest. You only need to register for one role as you will have the opportunity to apply for additional roles at the full application stage.
 2. Upload Your CV 
 3. Check your emails for the invitation to apply – this will come from recruiting@jobalerts.thalesgroup.com
 4. Complete Your Application – follow the link provided in the email to complete your application. You can apply for one primary role and up to 3 additional roles.
 5. Complete Online Tests - undertake the online assessments designed to evaluate your suitability for the role.
 6. Video Interview - if successful in the online testing stage, you will be invited to complete a video interview.
 7. Virtual Assessment Centre - candidates who progress from the video interview stage will attend a virtual assessment centre, which may include presentations, group exercises, and competency-based interviews.
 8. Job Offer – successful candidates who perform well throughout the recruitment process will receive a job offer from Thales.
 For further information about our Future Talent recruitment process, including hints and tips, or to connect with a member of the Future Talent Team, a Graduate, or an Apprentice, please visit Thales Future Talent - Connectr .

items.desc:
Lieu : Limours, France 
 Construisons ensemble un avenir de confiance 
 Thales est un leader mondial des hautes technologies spécialisé dans trois secteurs d’activité : Défense & Sécurité, Aéronautique & Spatial, et Cyber & Digital. Il développe des produits et solutions qui contribuent à un monde plus sûr, plus respectueux de l’environnement et plus inclusif. Le Groupe investit près de 4,5 milliards d’euros par an en Recherche & Développement, notamment dans des domaines clés de l’innovation tels que l’IA, la cybersécurité, le quantique, les technologies du cloud et la 6G. Thales compte près de 85 000 collaborateurs dans 65 pays. ​
 Nos engagements, vos avantages 
 Une réussite portée par notre excellence technologique, votre expérience et notre ambition partagée
 Un package de rémunération attractif
 Un développement des compétences en continu : parcours de formation, académies et communautés internes
 Un environnement inclusif, bienveillant et respectant l’équilibre des collaborateurs
 Un engagement sociétal et environnemental reconnu
 Votre quotidien 
Situé à 20mn du Pôle technologique de Paris-Saclay, le site est l’un des plus grands centres d’excellence radars de surface. Nous contribuons à développer, concevoir, intégrer et tester des radars de surveillance aériennes dédiés à la détection et l’identification de cibles. 
 En tant qu' Ingénieur Systèmes - Algorithmie et IA Radar chez Thales, vous serez impliqué(e) dans un environnement très dynamique dans le cadre du développement des radars Ground Maste r, des projets complexes à haute valeur technique au sein d'une équipe motivée et accueillante.
 Techniquement, vous devrez contribuer à l'analyse fonctionnelle détaillée du système Radar notamment en tenant compte des besoins client et des autres parties prenantes. De plus, vous devrez démontrer votre capacité à communiquer dans ce type de contexte (diplomatie, capacité à convaincre, management sans lien hiérarchique, etc.).
 Mais dans un premier temps, vous participerez à la cellule innovation de nos radars, au sein d'une équipe dédiée et dynamique, vous partagerez les idées d'innovations avec l'appui de nos experts. Au titre de l'innovation vous serez co-localisé(e) pour permettre le développement de solution permettant d'améliorer les performances de nos radars. 
 Puis au titre de votre rôle d'ingénieur système dans le cadre d'un développement plus classique vous serez en charge, en phase de spécification, des aspects suivants :
 Définir les caractéristiques fonctionnelles du radar (bilan énergétique, séquencements, définition algorithmique de traitement en particulier à base d'IA) répondant aux exigences de performances opérationnelles souhaitées,
 Réaliser des analyses et des évaluations en support de la justification de la conception, au moyen de calculs analytiques ou de simulations au moyen de modèles du comportement fonctionnel,
 Proposer des évolutions du système en prototypant les traitements algorithmiques notamment à base d'intelligence artificielle qui font leur apparition dans les chaînes de traitement radar,
 Produire la malle documentaire idoine de spécifications système et sous-systèmes permettant l'implémentation par les métiers.
 En phase de validation du système vous devrez :
 Apporter votre expertise aux équipes d'intégration en identifiant et résolvant les problèmes remontés par celles-ci,

items.desc:
Location: Crawley, United Kingdom 
 Thales is a global technology leader with more than 83,000 employees on five continents. With over 7,500 people in the UK, operating across defence, space, aerospace, and digital security, we help build a future we can all trust. Thales supports the security and stability of our nation by providing extraordinary technology to our customers, as well as delivering social value to the UK with our products and services.
 2027 Software Engineering Graduate
 Start Date: 06 September 2027
 Salary: £34,000 per annum
 Employee type: Permanent
 Location: Crawley
 Working Schedule: 37 hours per week (8 hours Monday - Thursday, 5 hours on a Friday)
 Are you passionate about engineering? Do you have an inquisitive mind? Do you want to be part of a Graduate Programme that will develop and challenge you? If so, then look no further… 
 What is the Engineering Development Programme? 
 This is a 3-year programme with the option to rotate, in Year 3, around the country across different business units experiencing different parts of an engineering lifecycle. You will be assigned to a succession of new or existing programmes where you will work with and be supported by other engineers to design and develop engineering solutions to meet the needs of our customers.
 During your time on the programme, you will be under the sponsorship and guidance of the Engineering Leadership team and will follow a structured and detailed learning pathway to fast track your development within your role.
 During the programme, you will: 
 · Complete a 3-year Graduate Development Programme which is accredited by the IET, IMechE and RAeS
 · An opportunity to rotate in Year 3 or explore an external secondment with one of our Thales partners
 · Participate in discipline specific learning pathways and core training pathway focusing on transversal skills
 · Develop key engineering skills, knowledge and competencies
 · Work in a set location and domain for the entirety of the scheme, enabling you to fully understand how the Engineering Function operates
 · Work on exciting new and existing products
 · Build a professional network across the organisation
 Requirements: 
 This is an entry-level graduate opportunity designed for individuals at the start of their professional career. We welcome applications from candidates who have completed a degree and have limited relevant professional experience. You will have gained or be on track to achieve a bachelor’s degree in a STEM Subject in one of the following subject areas:
 • AI Software Engineering (BSc or MSc)
 • Computer Science (BSc or MSc)
 • Computing (BEng or MEng)
 • Computing and Data Science (BSc or MSc)
 • Software Engineering (BSc or MSc)
 • All applicable technical or related degrees will be considered
 Benefits 
 · Competitive salary of £34,000 per annum
 · Performance-related pay uplifts
 · Holiday entitlement of 201 hours a year (plus a company day and bank holidays)
 · Contributory Company Pension
 · Health Care Cash Plan
 · Hybrid/flexible working options
 · Employee assistance programme
 · Learning and development support
 · Employee discounts and wellbeing initiatives
 · Life cover
 · 80 Hours Volunteering per year (first two years)
 Thales Graduate Recruitment Process 
 1. Apply Online - submit your application online to register your interest. You only need to register for one role as you will have the opportunity to apply for additional roles at the full application stage.
 2. Upload Your CV 
 3. Check your emails for the invitation to apply – this will come from recruiting@jobalerts.thalesgroup.com
 4. Complete Your Application – follow the link provided in the email to complete your application. You can apply for one primary role and up to 3 additional roles.
 5. Complete Online Tests - undertake the online assessments designed to evaluate your suitability for the role.
 6. Video Interview - if successful in the online testing stage, you will be invited to complete a video interview.
 7. Virtual Assessment Centre - candidates who progress from the video interview stage will attend a virtual assessment centre, which may include presentations, group exercises, and competency-based interviews.
 8. Job Offer – successful candidates who perform well throughout the recruitment process will receive a job offer from Thales.
 For further information about our Future Talent recruitment process, including hints and tips, or to connect with a member of the Future Talent Team, a Graduate, or an Apprentice, please visit Thales Future Talent - Connectr .
 Please note, assessment centres for shortlisted candidates will be held between February - May 2027. Induction week for all Graduate and Apprentices will take place from Monday 6 September - Friday 10 September 2027. 
 Closing date: Our applications will close at 11.59pm on Wednesday 6 January 2027 , this is the only time we will be accepting applications this year. Please note, we will be in contact by the end …

items.desc:
Job Description: 
 Zur Verstärkung der Abteilung "Operationelle Analyse und Studien" suchen wir bei Airbus Defence and Space in Friedrichshafen in den nächsten Monaten eine/n
 Software Entwickler:in Simulation: Gen AI (d/f/m) 
 Diese Stelle ist auch mit reduzierter Wochenarbeitszeit und angepasstem Aufgabenbereich möglich. 
 Wir entwickeln militärische Simulationsumgebungen für Studien und Forschungsprojekte, welche für Analysen und zum KI-Training verwendet werden. Mittels Machine Learning/Deep Learning Ansätzen entwickeln wir KI-Verfahren zur autonomen Planung und Entscheidungsfindung unter unsicheren Bedingungen und in komplexen operationellen, militärischen Situationen.
 Wir implementieren und erproben modernste Deep Reinforcement-Learning Ansätze für die Nutzung im militärischen Umfeld, mit denen sich unsere KI-Anwendungen sicher, datensparsam und zuverlässig optimieren lassen. Die wegweisenden Ergebnisse publizieren wir auf internationalen Konferenzen (z.B. Using DeepMind's AlphaStar techniques to support military decision-makers ).
 Wir suchen einen Software Entwickler (d/f/m), der uns bei der Übertragung der Ergebnisse der akademischen Forschung auf reale Systeme unterstützt. Du arbeitest in unserer agilen Studienabteilung an interessanten Studien- und Forschungsprojekten der Bundeswehr, NATO, sowie Europäischen Union im Bereich Sicherheit und Verteidigung.
 Respekt, Teamwork und Kreativität sind die Schlüsselwerte unserer Abteilung. Als Studienabteilung sind wir auch in Innovationsaktivitäten im Bereich Künstliche Intelligenz involviert. Zusammen mit der Airbus Innovation Factory in Friedrichshafen findest du bei uns das richtige Umfeld, um deine innovativen Ideen voranzutreiben und in die Realität umzusetzen. 
 Dein Standort 
 Am Airbus-Standort in Immenstaad am Bodensee arbeitest du dort, wo die Zukunft von Connected Intelligence, Space und Air Power entsteht. In einer Umgebung, die Weitblick bietet, gestaltest du technologische Innovationen über Domänen hinweg. 
 Unser Standort lebt vom Dialog: Auf dem Campus triffst du auf ein einzigartiges Netzwerk aus Experten für Satellitentechnik, militärische Luftfahrt, Cyber-Security, Künstliche Intelligenz sowie Combat Cloud und Ground Support von morgen. Auch unsere Zusammenarbeit ist geprägt von Dynamik – in agilen Teams widmen wir uns den komplexesten Fragestellungen, von KI-gestützter Erdbeobachtung bis zur sicheren Cloud-Architektur. Wer technologische Exzellenz und interdisziplinäre Zusammenarbeit sucht, findet hier das ideale Umfeld. 
 Unsere Benefits für dich 
 Faire Vergütung & Extras: Attraktive Vergütung und individuelle Zusatzleistungen, z. B. betriebliche Vorsorgemodelle, Mobilitätsangebote (bspw. Fahrradleasing) oder Mitarbeitervorteile bei kooperierenden Unternehmen gemäß unseren jeweils gültigen Richtlinien. 
 Zeit für dich (und deine Angehörigen): 30 Tage Jahresurlaub gem. Tarifvertrag (35h/Woche); Vereinbarkeit von Familie & Beruf (Gleitzeit, mobiles Arbeiten, Teilzeit, Jobsharing, Sabbatical) 
 Weiterkommen leicht gemacht: Ausgezeichnete Weiterbildungsmöglichkeiten und internationale, konzernweite Entwicklungsperspektiven 
 Wohlfühlen am Arbeitsplatz: Betriebsarzt; umfassendes Gesundheitsangebot (Sportkurse, Präventionsangebote, uvm.), Kantine und Cafeteria, Kindertagesstätte am Standort 
 Vielfalt verbindet: Arbeiten in einem diversen Umfeld, mit mehr als 140 Nationalitäten, in dem Austausch, Unterstützung und Vielfalt gelebt wird 
 Deine Aufgaben und Verantwortlichkeiten 
 Mitarbeit in der Entwicklung und Erprobung von KI-Ansätzen zur autonomen Planung und Entscheidungsfindung im militärischen Umfeld 
 Verantwortung für die Umsetzung von Arbeitsaufträgen in Zeit, Kosten und Qualität 
 Unterstützung des Projektleiters bei Kundenpräsentationen und Besprechungen
 Unterstützung beim technischen Austausch mit anderen Fachabteilungen und Projektpartnern (Industrie, wissenschaftliche Institute)
 Implementieren und Optimieren verschiedener Deep Reinforcement Learning Verfahren im Zusammenspiel mit militärischen Simulationen (C++ oder Python)
 Implementierung und Erweiterung der militärischen Simulationen (C++ oder Python) in allen militärischen Domänen (Land, Luft, See, Weltraum und Cyber)
 Durchführung von MLOps getriebenen KI Trainings auf modernen Container/Kubernetes Umgebungen und Verteilsystemen (z.B. Ray)
 Implementierung von Schnittstellen zur Einbindung externer Systeme (HW und SW) in die Simulation
 Unterstützung bei der Angebotserstellung
 Praxisnahe Umsetzung und Erprobung in Kooperation mit anderen Fachabteilungen sowie industriellen und wissenschaftlichen Partnern (Universitäten, Fraunhofer Gesellschaft)
 Erforderliche Qualifikationen 
 Erfolgreich abgeschlossenes Studium (Diplom/Master) der Informatik mit Vertiefung in Künstlicher Intelligenz (KI) und/oder Simulation
 praktische Erfahrung in der Softwareentwicklung (z.B. über Nebentätigkeit) ist von Vorteil.
 Du verfügst über erste praktische Programmiererfahrung in C++, …

items.desc:
Job Description: 
 Zur Verstärkung der Abteilung "Operationelle Analyse und Studien" suchen wir bei Airbus Defence and Space in Friedrichshafen in den nächsten Monaten für zukünftige Projekte eine/n
 Study Engineer / Data Scientist (d/f/m) – AI & Operations Research 
 Wir untersuchen innovative zukünftige Technologien (darunter auch eigene aus dem Hause Airbus) und deren Einsatz im operationellen Umfeld mit Hilfe unseres hauseigenen Simulationsframeworks.
 Unsere Hauptaufgabe ist dabei die Konzeption und Durchführung theorie- und datengetriebener Studien. Wir bilden komplexe Systemarchitekturen („Systems of Systems“) mathematisch und algorithmisch ab, optimieren und evaluieren diese. Damit beeinflussen wir frühzeitige Entwurfsentscheidungen und geben richtungsweisende Empfehlungen im Bereich zukünftiger Entwicklungen und Einsätze ab.
 Wir suchen einen Study Engineer / Data Scientist (d/f/m), der uns bei der Erforschung und Anwendung von Methoden der Künstlichen Intelligenz, komplexer Modellbildung bis hin zur tiefgehenden Datenauswertung unterstützt. Du arbeitest in unserer agilen Studienabteilung an interessanten Studien- und Forschungsprojekten der Bundeswehr, NATO sowie Europäischen Union im Bereich Sicherheit und Verteidigung.
 Respekt, Teamwork und Kreativität sind die Schlüsselwerte unserer Abteilung. Als Studienabteilung sind wir aktiv in Innovationsaktivitäten im Bereich Künstliche Intelligenz, Machine Learning, Block Chain oder Quantencomputing involviert. Zusammen mit der Airbus Innovation Factory in Friedrichshafen findest du bei uns das richtige Umfeld, um deine innovativen, theoretischen und algorithmischen Ideen voranzutreiben und in die Realität umzusetzen.
