items.desc:
ABOUT BLACK FOREST LABS

We're the team behind Latent Diffusion, Stable Diffusion, and FLUX — foundational technologies that changed how the world creates images and videos. Our FLUX models are among the most advanced in the world, and we're just getting started.

Headquartered in Freiburg, Germany with a growing presence in San Francisco, we're scaling fast while staying true to what makes us different: research excellence, open science, and building technology that expands human creativity.




WHY THIS ROLE

Frontier image and video models are now good enough that the hard question is no longer whether they work, but whether a new one is actually better, and how you'd know. Aesthetics, prompt following, editing fidelity, text rendering, character consistency: none of these collapse into a single number, and public benchmarks have fallen well behind the models they're meant to measure.

You'll work on the system BFL uses to answer that question. Every FLUX checkpoint, every finetuning and RL run, and every competitor release goes through our evaluation stack, and you'll help build and sharpen it. Product Research relies on what it shows to decide what to fix next, and to confirm the fix worked.

It gets harder from here. FLUX 3 is our first multimodal model, spanning image, video, audio and action, and each new modality needs its own way of being measured.




WHAT YOU'LL WORK ON

What you focus on will depend on where you're strongest and what the team needs most when you join.

In scope:

 - Building and maintaining the evaluation stack that every model checkpoint has to pass through and prove itself on, from automated benchmarking and LLM-as-judge pipelines, to human evaluation through panels (Prolific and otherwise).

 - Designing the breadth of evaluation across the taxonomy, from prompt adherence, editing fidelity, aesthetics, text rendering, subject and character consistency, to safety.

 - Evaluating the evaluation stack itself: checking that human and automated evals agree, that results stay stable over time, and improving them when they don't.

 - Benchmarking FLUX against the frontier models continuously, while obtaining a meaningful perspective on where we are better or worse than competitors and what such differences really mean.

 - Finding the ways in which the quality of the model's output falls short that are not captured by aggregate numbers.

 - Closing the loop, ideally, with the RL and finetuning researchers, by defining target metrics for them to aim for, and verifying that a new checkpoint improved the weakness without introducing new ones.

 - Designing how best to exploit the signals we already capture through the API and MCP, and what new signals we should capture, with help from research, data engineering and legal.

 - Maintaining the usefulness of existing metrics as their natural lifecycle brings up concerns of gaming and overfitting, and anticipating this for new metrics.
   
   


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

You have made meaningful contributions to the evaluation of generative models already. You understand that a benchmark figure without careful consideration of sample size and judge agreement with humans is at best uninformed optimism and at worst dangerously misleading, and you have been the person that found that inconvenient regression that nobody wanted to talk about.

You likely have:

 - Advanced degree (MS/PhD) in a relevant field or demonstrated equivalent practical experience

 - Practical experience with evaluating generative models, in a hands-on way. You may have worked with diffusion or flow-matching based image or video models already, but the capability to evaluate them in earnest transfers to other modalities too

 - Very strong Python and software engineering skills, with pipelines that run reliably and that other people can read if needed

 - Working knowledge of PyTorch and modern ML infrastructure and practices; you are not a pure Python developer, you know what the modern ML code looks like

 - Strong grasp of statistics and its shortcomings in practice, and how to work with those; sample sizes, inter-annotator agreement, confidence levels, etc., and a healthy skepticism about what those numbers say about the world

 - Practical experience with building and operating LLM-as-judge systems, and understanding their limitations

 - Working knowledge of modern benchmarking practices and of standard datasets and benchmarks in the field already; you have an idea of which to trust and which to disregard

 - The inclination to look at the actual outputs your system is judging, and to care about what is there beyond an aggregate score



We'd be especially excited if you:

 - Have practical experience with human evaluation, including study design and execution via panels, and analysis of disagreements and annotator performance

 - Have worked where evaluation meets training (reward models, preference data, RLHF, DPO or similar) and know that whatever you optimize …

items.desc: Type de contrat : CDD Niveau de diplôme exigé : Bac + 5 ou équivalent Fonction : Doctorant A propos du centre ou de la direction fonctionnelle L’Inria est l’Institut national de recherche en sciences du numérique, dont le centre Inria d’Université Côte d’Azur fait partie. Avec une forte expertise en informatique et mathématiques appliquées, les projets de recherche du centre Inria d’Université Côte d’Azur touchent toutes les dimensions des sciences et technologies du numérique, et génèrent de l’innovation. Implanté principalement à Sophia Antipolis, mais également à Nice ou Montpellier, il regroupe 47 équipes de recherche et neuf services d’appui. Il est présent dans les domaines de l’intelligence artificielle, la science des données, la sécurité des systèmes informatiques, la robotique, l’ingénierie de réseaux, la prévention des risques naturels, la transition écologique, la biologie numérique, les neurosciences computationnelles, les données de santé… Le Centre Inria d’Université Côte d’Azur est un acteur majeur en termes d'excellence scientifique par les résultats obtenus et les collaborations tant au niveau européen qu'international. Contexte et atouts du poste Cette thèse s'inscrit dans le cadre du PEPR DynaBiod, qui vise à faire progresser la compréhension et la modélisation des dynamiques de la biodiversité, notamment en mobilisant les avancées récentes de l'intelligence artificielle et de la modélisation mathématique. Le projet sera mené à Montpellier, dans un environnement de recherche interdisciplinaire associant Inria et des équipes spécialisées en intelligence artificielle, écologie quantitative et modélisation des systèmes dynamiques. Il bénéficiera de la complémentarité des compétences des encadrants, ainsi que de l'écosystème scientifique développé autour de Pl@ntNet et de l'IA pour la biodiversité. Le doctorant ou la doctorante contribuera à un programme de recherche ambitieux, à l'interface entre apprentissage profond, modélisation mécaniste et écologie. Le poste offre l'opportunité de développer des méthodes originales, notamment autour des Process-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs), et de les confronter à des données écologiques réelles, dans un contexte de collaborations interdisciplinaires. Mission confiée L'objectif de cette thèse est de développer de nouvelles approches d'intelligence artificielle permettant de mieux comprendre et prédire la dynamique spatio-temporelle des communautés végétales. Les travaux exploreront notamment le potentiel des Process-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) pour combiner apprentissage à partir de données et connaissances issues de l'écologie théorique. L'ambition est de dépasser les limites des approches purement corrélatives en intégrant des contraintes et des processus écologiques dans les modèles d'apprentissage. Un enjeu central sera d'identifier les formulations mathématiques et les architectures d'apprentissage les plus adaptées à la dynamique des communautés végétales, puis d'étudier leur capacité à inférer des processus et paramètres écologiques à partir d'observations spatiales et temporelles incomplètes, hétérogènes et bruitées. Principales activités Étudier l'état de l'art en modélisation dynamique des systèmes écologiques, en Scientific Machine Learning et en PINNs. Explorer différentes formulations mathématiques des dynamiques écologiques et leur intégration dans des architectures d'apprentissage profond. Concevoir et développer des approches fondées sur les PINNs et, si pertinent, d'autres méthodes hybrides combinant modèles mécanistes et apprentissage automatique. Étudier l'inférence de paramètres écologiques et la reconstruction de dynamiques spatio-temporelles à partir d'observations partielles. Développer des outils de simulation et d'évaluation sur des données synthétiques et réelles (inventaires de végétation, données environnementales, télédétection). Évaluer la robustesse, la généralisation et la pertinence écologique des modèles proposés. Publier les résultats dans des conférences et revues scientifiques internationales et contribuer à leur diffusion en logiciel libre. Compétences Formation : Master 2 ou diplôme d'ingénieur en informatique, intelligence artificielle, mathématiques appliquées ou discipline équivalente. items.desc: 13.10.2026 Data Scientist (m/f/d, E13 TV-L, 100%) Cluster of Excellence HUMAN ORIGINS Bewerbungsfrist : 15.11.2026 The Cluster of Excellence HUMAN ORIGINS invites applications for a Data Scientist (m/f/d, E13 TV-L, 100%) to join the Cluster’s Research Data Management Unit. The position is expected to start on January 1st, 2027, and is limited until the end of the current Cluster funding period (December 31st, 2032). In the HUMAN ORIGINS Cluster of Excellence more than two dozen PIs and their teams engage in interdisciplinary research into the last five million years of human history, combining scientific, archaeological and humanities approaches. The Cluster’s Research Data Management Unit is responsible for research data and research software management, as well as research infrastructure and instrumentation. The unit is jointly led by the Quantitative Biology Center (QBiC) and the Digital Humanties Center (DHC), two of the University’s Core Facilities for research data management. The position is expected to complement the unit’s data stewards with a strong data science expertise and experience and will be jointly supervised by QBiC and DHC. Duties and responsibilities will include: Building, testing, and deploying custom research software, web applications, and interactive dashboards/portals to facilitate cluster-wide data exploration, integration, and visualization. Developing and applying state-of-the-art artificial intelligence, machine learning, or NLP solutions to extract patterns, classify artifacts/data, and support hypotheses in and across human origins research projects. Designing, implementing, and maintaining scalable analytical pipelines and workflows for heterogeneous, multimodal datasets (e.g., 3D scans, ancient genomics, archaeological spatial data, and text corpora). Developing interfaces between the research infrastructure of QBiC and DHC to ensure interoperability of computational environments and tools. Partnering closely with the Cluster’s PIs and research teams to translate complex research questions into robust computational methods and contribute to scientific publications. Establishing and applying best practices for Research Software Engineering, including version control, containerization, automated testing, and open-science compliance in close coordination with the unit’s data stewards. Expected applicant profile: Completed university degree (Master’s or equivalent), preferably with a doctorate, in computer science, data science, or a related field. A background or experience in the humanities is a plus. Experience in applying data science methods and tools in research projects, preferably in one or more of the disciplines relevant to the Cluster. Strong software development and web engineering skills. Experience in developing and applying artificial intelligence solutions in data science and software engineering. Openness to interdisciplinary data science and management covering a broad range of research domains, data modalities, methodologies, software and tools. Strong organizational and communication skills, with the ability to work autonomously in an international and interdisciplinary environment. Very good English language skills, written and spoken. The Cluster and the University of Tübingen offer excellent opportunities for cutting-edge collaborative, interdisciplinary research, state-of-the-art laboratories, and access to a wide range of facilities. The position can be split. The University aims to increase the proportion of women in research and teaching and therefore particularly encourages qualified women scientists to apply. The University of Tübingen is committed to equal opportunities and diversity and actively promotes gender equality. Female candidates are expressly invited to submit their application. Disabled candidates will be given preference over other equally qualified applicants. Applications should be submitted electronically no later than November 15, 2026. They should include: (1) cover letter; (2) curriculum vitae; (3) certificates / diplomas / references. Please submit your application as a single PDF file (max. 10 MB) to admin.human-originsspam prevention@ifu.uni-tuebingen.de For any further questions regarding this job posting please contact human-originsspam prevention@dh-center.uni-tuebingen.de The appointment will be made by the Central Administration (Zentrale Verwaltung).

items.desc: Location: Dublin, Ireland, primarily remote with occasional in-person collaboration Team: Product Reporting to: Head of Product, US-based Must have Irish/EU Citizenship Cpl are partnering with an innovative international technology organisation to recruit a Data Scientist for its growing Product team in Ireland. This is a hands-on position for a Data Scientist who enjoys solving complex, loosely defined problems and taking ownership from initial investigation through to production delivery. The successful candidate will work across statistical modelling, machine learning, data engineering and analytical problem-solving. You will contribute to the development of predictive models, classification solutions and scalable data pipelines. The role offers the opportunity to work closely with product, engineering and customer-facing teams while helping turn large and complex datasets into practical insights and reliable technical solutions. Key Responsibilities Investigate open-ended data problems, define an appropriate approach and independently develop solutions through testing and iteration. Design, develop and maintain machine learning models and production-grade data pipelines. Prepare, clean and structure large, complex and sometimes unstructured datasets for analysis and modelling. Develop and improve predictive, classification and entity-resolution models. Measure model performance against real-world outcomes and refine solutions using data-led feedback. Determine when traditional machine learning, automated data integration or LLM-based techniques are most appropriate. Work with product, engineering and business stakeholders to translate commercial or methodological questions into clear technical solutions. Provide understandable explanations of areas such as model performance, bias, data confidence and coverage limitations. Use Python, machine learning libraries, databases and querying tools across the full development lifecycle. Explore new technologies and AI-assisted workflows that can improve delivery speed and quality. Maintain clear documentation covering methodologies, code, models and data structures. Experience and skills Approximately three to five years of experience in applied data science, machine learning or a closely related technical role. Strong Python development skills, with experience using libraries such as pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn, TensorFlow or PyTorch. Good understanding of database design, data schemas, efficient querying and reliable pipeline development. Practical experience deploying machine learning models into production and monitoring their ongoing performance. Ability to work across data preparation, modelling, engineering and production implementation. Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain technical decisions and trade-offs to non-technical audiences. Demonstrated ability to manage work independently, maintain momentum and follow tasks through to completion. Degree in Computer Science, Statistics, Applied Mathematics or another relevant discipline. Equivalent practical experience will also be considered. Experience with REST API development, Django REST Framework or a comparable framework would be advantageous. The person The ideal candidate will be comfortable working in an environment where every problem does not arrive with a predefined solution. You will be proactive, commercially aware and confident making informed technical decisions. You should enjoy delivering an effective first version, evaluating it against real data and improving it through iteration. Curiosity around emerging tools, machine learning techniques and AI-enabled development approaches will be particularly valuable. What The Role Offers A high-ownership position within a growing product and data function. The opportunity to work across machine learning, data science and data engineering. Exposure to complex datasets and meaningful production use cases. Collaboration with international product, engineering and business stakeholders. A primarily remote working arrangement, with occasional in-person sessions in Dublin.

items.desc: Junior Data Scientists, Quantitative Analysts & Machine Learning Researchers. Remote AI Project We are seeking experienced Data Scientists, Quantitative Analysts, Machine Learning Researchers, and Statistical Modeling Professionals to contribute to a remote AI project focused on statistics, machine learning, experimentation, and quantitative reasoning. What You’ll Do Evaluate AI-generated responses across data science, statistics, machine learning, experimentation, and quantitative analysis. Identify incorrect assumptions, statistical errors, flawed methodology, weak experimental design, and unsupported conclusions. Create challenging expert-level prompts based on realistic analytical and quantitative problems. Build or review datasets used to evaluate model performance. Develop reference solutions that demonstrate correct methodology and reasoning. Assess whether analytical approaches are statistically sound, reproducible, and appropriate for the problem. Review model reasoning related to experimentation, causal inference, forecasting, predictive modeling, and data interpretation. Evaluate code and analytical workflows when relevant. Provide structured technical feedback explaining why an approach is correct or incorrect. Help refine evaluation criteria and improve the difficulty and quality of quantitative tasks. Who Can Apply Relevant backgrounds include Data Scientists, Senior Data Analysts, Junior Data Scientists, Associate Data Scientists, Quantitative Analysts, Quantitative Researchers, and Applied Scientists. We also welcome Machine Learning Scientists, Machine Learning Engineers, Research Scientists, and Applied Machine Learning Researchers with strong quantitative foundations. Statistics backgrounds may include Statisticians, Applied Statisticians, Biostatisticians, Statistical Analysts, and Statistical Modeling Specialists. Experimentation backgrounds may include Experimentation Scientists, Product Data Scientists, Decision Scientists, Causal Inference Specialists, and A/B Testing Experts. Finance backgrounds may include Quantitative Researchers, Quantitative Strategists, Financial Data Scientists, Risk Modelers, and Quantitative Finance Professionals. Additional relevant backgrounds include Econometricians, Operations Research Scientists, Analytics Scientists, Research Analysts, and Computational Researchers with strong statistical expertise. Requirements At least one year of professional experience in data science, quantitative analysis, statistics, machine learning, finance, research, or a closely related field. At least part of that experience must have occurred within the past three years. Strong foundation in statistics, probability, and quantitative reasoning. Experience analyzing real-world datasets and interpreting results. Ability to identify flawed methodology and statistical errors. Strong understanding of experimentation or model evaluation principles. Working knowledge of Python, R, SQL, or comparable quantitative tools. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. Ability to communicate technical and statistical concepts clearly in writing. Comfortable working independently in a remote environment. Preferred Background Professional experience at a leading technology company, financial institution, research organization, or quantitatively rigorous company. Experience in product data science, experimentation, quantitative research, applied machine learning, statistics, or analytics. Experience designing or reviewing A/B tests, predictive models, or quantitative research. Experience with causal inference, forecasting, recommendation systems, risk modeling, or optimization is valuable. Experience reviewing technical analyses, research reports, or model outputs for methodological quality. Experience creating technical assessments, analytical case studies, interview problems, or quantitative benchmarks is helpful. This opportunity is ideal for quantitative professionals who can look at a statistical or machine learning problem, identify whether the methodology is genuinely sound, catch subtle errors in assumptions or evaluation, build a rigorous reference solution, and clearly explain why one analytical approach is stronger than another. items.desc: Starting date: 16/10/2026 Job Reference 446_26_ES_AC_RE2 Position Research Engineer on atmospheric composition forecasts and reanalyses (RE2) Closing Date Monday, 19 October, **** Reference: 446_26_ES_AC_RE2 Job title: Research Engineer on atmospheric composition forecasts and reanalyses (RE2) About BSC The Barcelona Supercomputing Center - Centro Nacional de Supercomputación (BSC-CNS) is the leading supercomputing center in Spain. It houses MareNostrum, one of the most powerful supercomputers in Europe, was a founding and hosting member of the former European HPC infrastructure PRACE (Partnership for Advanced Computing in Europe), and is now hosting entity for EuroHPC JU, the Joint Undertaking that leads large-scale investments and HPC provision in Europe. The mission of BSC is to research, develop and manage information technologies in order to facilitate scientific progress. BSC combines HPC service provision and R&D into both computer and computational science (life, earth and engineering sciences) under one roof, and currently has over **** staff from 60 countries. Look At The BSC Experience BSC-CNS YouTube Channel Let's stay connected with BSC Folks! We are particularly interested for this role in the strengths and lived experiences of women and underrepresented groups to help us avoid perpetuating biases and oversights in science and IT research. In instances of equal merit, the incorporation of the under-represented sex will be favoured. We promote Equity, Diversity and Inclusion, fostering an environment where each and every one of us is appreciated for who we are, regardless of our differences. If you consider that you do not meet all the requirements, we encourage you to continue applying for the job offer. We value diversity of experiences and skills, and you could bring unique perspectives to our team. Context And Mission We are looking for an experienced and enthusiastic research engineer to join the Atmospheric Composition (AC) group within the Earth Sciences department at the BSC-CNS. The AC group is currently composed of about 50 people among researchers, engineers and students of different nationalities. It aims at better understanding and predicting the spatio-temporal variations of atmospheric pollutants along with their effects upon air quality, weather and climate. This is addressed through the continuous development and application of numerical models over multiple scales, from weather to climate and from global to urban scales. The AC group develops and maintains its own forecast model MONARCH, which is a coupled meteorological-chemistry model that can be run at global and regional scales to simulate gaseous chemistry and aerosols plus their feedbacks on radiation. MONARCH is also coupled to a data assimilation scheme for gases and aerosols that is used to initialize forecasts or produce reanalyses of the atmospheric composition. The AC group operates several operational forecasting systems in the framework of the World Meteorological Organization Sand and Dust Storm Advisory System (SDS-WAS, the Copernicus atmospheric monitoring services (CAMS, the Spanish air quality forecasting system CALIOPE ( and the International Cooperative for Aerosols Predictions (ICAP). The successful candidate will join the Data Assimilation Forecasting and Application team of the AC group and will play a key coordinating role in the production and continuous improvement of the team's operational forecasting and reanalysis systems. The activities will be carried out mainly in the framework of the Copernicus CAMS2_40bis international project, with contributions to the CAMS2_82bis project and to the activities of the Barcelona Dust Regional Center (BDRC). The candidate will work in a highly collaborative environment, with tight links with researchers and engineers in the AC group. The candidate will have the opportunity to follow multiple training activities, including those aimed at improving coding and data analysis, project writing abilities, or project management. All this will be implemented via the formal courses organized by the Education and Training team and Human Resources, and the participation in the regular seminars organized by the department. Key Duties Manage the team's technical activities within CAMS2_40bis and its contributions to CAMS2_82bis and the BDRC, including planning, follow-up of tasks and milestones, and reporting. Coordinate the preparation and timely delivery of project deliverables, and represent the team in international project meetings. Coordinate the upgrades of the production systems: define and evaluate target model configurations, organize the e-suite experiments, and ensure successful operational deployments. Coordinate the production of atmospheric composition reanalyses, from planning and set-up to monitoring, validation and dissemination. Oversee the overall quality assurance of the forecast and reanalysis products, including routine evaluation against in-situ and …

items.desc: Data Scientist - Broker Flow Team Hybrid in London, United Kingdom We're looking for a Data Scientist to join the Broker Flow team. You'll own the experiments that shape the journey brokers use to apply on their clients' behalf. Brokers are one of iwoca's main routes to new customers. The Company Small businesses move fast. Opportunities often don’t wait, and cash flow pressures can appear overnight. To keep going, and growing, SMEs need finance that’s as flexible and responsive as they are. That's why we built iwoca. Our smart technology, data science and five-star customer service ensures business owners can act with the speed, confidence and control they need, exactly when it's needed. We’ve already cleared the way for 100,000 businesses with more than £4 billion in funding. Our passionate team is driven to help even more SMEs succeed, through access to better finance and other services that make running a business easier. Our ultimate mission is to support one million SMEs in their defining moments, creating lasting impact for the communities and economies they drive. The team Broker Flow, a new team in iwoca's third-party acquisition department, owns the journey for businesses that come to iwoca through a broker – from before they apply to a completed credit assessment. Its aim is to get more of those businesses to an offer. Broker Terms, a separate team, then sets the price, amount, and duration of each offer. The team works on three parts of that journey: Broker engagement. Working with brokers and their clients before an application starts. The application. Making it smooth to complete, and collecting the data a credit decision needs. Operations. Running the CRM tools iwoca's teams work in, and automating operational processes. The team is small and cross-functional – commercial strategy, engineering, design, and data science – and works across the full application stack, from the Broker API to the Introducer Portal brokers use. The role As the Data Scientist in Broker Flow, you'll give the team the evidence behind its product decisions. The core of the work is experiment design and causal inference, with modelling and analysis alongside it. You'll own each project end to end. You'll frame the problem, choose the method, build the model or run the test, and take the answer to the commercial and strategy colleagues who act on it. You'll also meet brokers in person, which gives you the context to ask the right questions. The team is new, so its methods are yours to shape. You'll see the effect of your work in how many businesses reach an offer, and in their lifetime value. You'll work with data scientists in iwoca's other broker and partner teams, and join the analytics guild – iwoca's data science community – to compare methods and build your expertise. Your results reach the wider business through Learnings, short write-ups that iwoca shares at weekly and fortnightly sessions. Live project examples: Refinancing. Modelling which businesses would benefit from refinancing their existing borrowing, and testing a product for them. Stalled applications. Finding where broker applications stall, and testing fixes – from clearer emails and portal updates to an early offer that encourages document upload. Reintroductions. Testing the best moment for brokers to bring existing iwoca customers back to borrow. Approval probability. Measuring how well the estimate brokers see in the Introducer Portal predicts actual credit decisions, and making it more accurate. Measuring impact. Designing early signals – at sign-up and once documents are in – that predict a business's lifetime value, so the team can judge its changes quickly. The Requirements Essential: Statistical foundations. You have a background in probability and statistics from a quantitative field such as mathematics, physics, or statistics. You're comfortable with Bayesian reasoning, and have applied hierarchical models or formal decision-making under uncertainty in real work. Causal inference and experimentation. You've separated signal from noise in observational and experimental data. You know where A/B testing breaks down and what to reach for instead. Analytical ownership. You take loosely defined problems from start to finish – framing the question, choosing the method, and landing the answer with the people who act on it. Data tooling. You're proficient with data manipulation and modelling tools, and with scientific computing libraries. AI leverage. You've used AI to produce work you couldn't have delivered without it – an analysis pipeline, a prototype, or a tool others use. You judge where it helps and where it doesn't, and you check its output before anyone acts on it. Communication. You write and speak clearly, directly, and concisely. You adapt technical detail for non-technical colleagues in commercial and strategy roles. Bonus: Modelling depth. You've built or adapted statistical or ML models and can explain the maths behind them. …

items.desc: Join Jus Mundi – To Power Global Justice 🚀⚖️ Founded in 2019 and recognized as a mission-led company, Jus Mundi is pioneering legal technology to power global justice through artificial intelligence. 🌍 Headquartered in Paris, with additional offices in New York, London, and Singapore, Jus Mundi serves over 150,000 users, including top law firms, multinational corporations, government bodies, and academic institutions in more than 90 countries. By combining legal expertise with cutting-edge AI technology, we provide global legal intelligence, data-driven arbitration professional selection, and business development services. What Makes Jus Mundi the Place to Be 🌟 🧬 Our Values: With core values as Listen (Solve for the Legal Community), Iterate (Start Sharp, Stop Smart), Commit (Step In, Own the Outcome), Belong (Build together through diversity), Uphold (Aim for Justice with Integrity), we cultivate a dynamic environment that encourages collaboration, innovation, and continuous growth. 🚀 Legal Is the Next Frontier for GenAI: Legal is one of the top industries ready to be transformed by GenAI. At Jus Mundi, we’re building transformative AI where it has the power to make the most impact. 🌐 Proven Product Market Fit: Jus Mundi has secured product-market fit in global markets since launch, partnering with top-tier law firms, government bodies, and major corporations, including: Freshfields, Quinn Emanuel, Wong Partnership, Total Energies, Canada, UK, and Japan. 💸 Strategic Investment: In 2024, we raised over $20 million in Series B funding from prominent strategic international investors, including Acton Capital, True Global Ventures, C4 Ventures, and FJ Labs, fueling our growth and innovation. 🤖 Legal Meets Tech: Our engineers and former lawyers collaborate closely with large language models (LLMs) to pioneer the future of generative AI and reshape professional services. 🌟 Exceptional Team: Work with talented professionals from industry leaders, including engineers, legal experts, and AI specialists from companies like Google and Amazon who are pushing the boundaries of legal tech. 📌 About the Role LLMs are confidently wrong. In international law and arbitration, a wrong date, party name or tribunal in front of a lawyer is not an acceptable error. Jus Mundi is building the AI layer for international law. We are now expanding into new areas of law, and each one brings new sources with thousands of documents in different languages. To handle that, we built a Data Platform : a pipeline of AI agents that finds legal documents on court and institution websites, downloads them, reads them and describes them, and has to prove every value it extracts. What it produces feeds our Search and Jus AI products, which lawyers use to prepare international disputes. It Already Runs End To End. Several Design Questions Are Still Open, And The Engineer Who Joins Now Will Help Answer Them Alongside The EM And Senior Engineers How should a workflow recover from a partial failure without repeating expensive model calls? How should evaluation gates balance automation, human review, quality and throughput? How should we version documents, prompts, models and extracted evidence so reprocessing stays safe? 🌟Your mission at Jus Mundi You own the delivery of your area, from design to production. Architecture decisions are made together with the Engineering Manager and senior engineers, and you take part in them. Agents, end to end. Each pipeline step is an agent: crawl a court website, download, read, classify, extract metadata, summarize, index for search. You add capabilities, make them reliable, and onboard new sources. Within your first six months, you take a new source or jurisdiction from first crawl to searchable document, with a senior engineer reviewing the design. Proof, not confidence. Every extracted value is tied to a quote from the source text, so we can always show where it came from. A quote alone does not prove the value was read correctly, so we also measure quality on evaluation sets and route doubtful cases to a human reviewer. You build and improve these checks, with lawyers from our Legal Content team defining what "correct" means. Cost and failure as design inputs. Every document has a processing cost, and every model call is paid for. Jobs fail and get retried. You build and improve retry-safe workflows that never create duplicate documents, keep repeated model calls to a minimum, and make processing cost observable. Lineage for every value. A FastAPI service and a Postgres catalog hold every document, its versions, and where each value came from: which source, which model, which prompt, which reviewer. You add endpoints, write migrations and keep that lineage complete and consistent. What you ship, you run. You deploy, watch logs, metrics and traces, fix what breaks, and know what each document costs to process. Your first 90 days Ship a fix or improvement to an existing agent in your first two weeks. items.desc: Our AI team is looking for an individual who is exceptional at the applied end of the craft: taking modern models and turning them into features and tools that hold up in production, at Supercell scale, under real deadlines. The challenge at the centre of this role is the distance between a demo and a product. A model that works in a notebook is not a feature that works for hundreds of millions of players, or a tool a game team trusts with their daily work. Help us Close that gap: the evaluation that tells you it's actually good, the latency and cost envelope that makes it viable, the failure modes you find before players do, and the plumbing that makes it boring to operate. We're not looking for someone who wants to train a frontier model. We're looking for someone who gets unreasonable results out of the ones that exist. We are looking for someone to build and ship: AI features in live games, and the internal tools that give superpowers to Supercellians. Some of that work will take you inside a game or central team for a while, close enough to their craft to build the right thing with them. In our team, you'll work closely with our AI Platform Engineers, AI/ML engineers, Clients Programmers, Cloud Engineers. You’ll also collaborate with other teams including Data, QA, Engine and game teams. What You'll Be Doing Build and ship AI features and systems end to end into live games and internal tools, at production quality and under real deadlines. Do the applied engineering that makes AI work in practice. Own evaluation as a first-class deliverable. Write and maintain the benchmarks, evals, and regression suites that tell you whether something is genuinely good, across the modalities you're working in. Fine-tune, adapt, and distill models where it pays off, and have the judgment to know when a better prompt, better retrieval, or a smaller model beats training anything. Make sound trade-offs on inference, including on-device where it matters, against real parameter, latency, and battery targets, without losing the feel players expect. Take on the harder applied problems, such as making autonomous agents reliable and accurate enough to trust with real work. Work close to game and central teams, sometimes embedded with them for a stretch, and build things that stay in use after you move on. Mentor our more junior AI/ML engineers through code review, pairing, and design discussion, and raise the technical bar around you. Stay at the frontier by reading the literature and following the major conferences, and bring back what is genuinely useful. What You Have Strong, current command of modern generative methods at the applied level: you know what today's models are actually good at, where they break, and how to build reliably on top of them. A track record of shipping LLM or generative AI applications that real users used, in production, not prototypes. We value this far above a publication record. Real software engineering depth. You write code others can maintain, and you own things in production rather than handing them off. Hands-on experience writing and maintaining benchmarks and evaluation frameworks, ideally across more than one modality. Practical fine-tuning and model adaptation experience, and the judgment to know when not to reach for it. Sound judgment on inference trade-offs under tight compute, latency, and cost constraints, including local or on-device deployment. The ability to work from broadly defined goals, set your own objectives, and drive work forward without waiting to be handed a spec. High EQ and credibility with makers. You can sit inside a protective, high-craft team and earn their trust fast. A generous mentor to less experienced engineers, with high ownership, comfort taking risks and learning from failure, and the humility to do excellent work with kindness. Would Be Nice if You Also Have Experience with agent frameworks, orchestration, or evaluation tooling at production scale. Game industry experience, or a real appreciation for mobile. Experience working alongside a platform or infrastructure team as an internal customer. Where You'll Be The role requires close collaboration with the other central teams and game teams, so ideally, you'd be based in Helsinki. That's it about the role! Below, we've gathered some things we feel are important for you to know. Totally optional, but a highly recommended read. Once you're ready to apply, just send us your application through the form on the bottom of the page. ––– About Supercell Supercell is a games company from Helsinki, Finland, with offices also in San Francisco, Seoul, Shanghai, and London. You might know us as the makers of Hay Day, Clash of Clans, Boom Beach, Clash Royale, and Brawl Stars . Our mission is to create great games that as many people as possible play for years and that are remembered forever. So, how do we make great games? By putting together the best teams and giving them the freedom and independence to succeed. And …

Mission confiée We are seeking a Machine Learning Engineer to design and develop a Python software library for evaluating theoretical generalization bounds in deep learning. The objective is to bridge the gap between theoretical advances in learning theory and practical deep learning by providing a modular, efficient, and user-friendly framework for computing and comparing generalization bounds on modern neural networks. Principales activités Conduct experiments for empirical verification Prepare software libraries Write scientific articles Disseminate the scientific work in appropriate venues. Compétences Strong Python programming skills and experience with PyTorch. Solid understanding of machine learning and deep learning. Experience in scientific software development, testing, and version control. Familiarity with statistical learning theory and generalization bounds is a plus. Ability to work collaboratively with researchers and translate mathematical concepts into reliable software. L’autorisation d’accès à une zone est délivrée par le chef d’établissement, après avis ministériel favorable, tel que défini dans l’arrêté du 03 juillet 2012, relatif à la PPST. items.desc: On-site Bonn, Nordrhein-Westfalen, Germany UNU-EHS / UNU-VIE Job description United Nations University (UNU) The United Nations University (UNU) is a global think tank and postgraduate teaching organization within the United Nations System. UNU engages in policy-relevant research, capacity development, and knowledge dissemination in furtherance of the purposes and principles of the United Nations. The work of UNU contributes to solving pressing global problems that are the concern of the United Nations and its Member States. For the past five decades, UNU has been a source of impartial research on sustainability, human security, and economic development. With hundreds of researchers working at institutes in 12 countries, UNU's expertise spans the full breadth of the 17 Sustainable Development Goals, generating policy-relevant knowledge to effect positive global change. UNU collaborates closely with other UN entities and leading research institutions across the globe. For more information, please visit http://unu.edu UNU-EHS is one of 13 research and training Institutes that comprise the think tanks in the UNU system. UNU-EHS The United Nations University’s Institute for Environment and Human Security (UNU-EHS) was established in 2003 in Bonn, Germany. The institute conducts research work focusing on advancing human security and well-being by addressing present and future risks arising from environmental hazards and climate change. Its main areas of work are risk & adaptation and transformation. In addition to its research activities, UNU-EHS offers educational opportunities at the master’s level and hosts a number of international PhD projects and capacity-development courses on global issues related to environmental risks and sustainable development. More information about UNU-EHS can be found here: https://unu.edu/ehs. Well-being and Equity (WE) Division “Well-being and Equity (WE)” is a pioneering science-to-policy research area of the United Nations University – Institute for Environment and Human Security (UNU-EHS). WE aspires towards a holistic assessment of the preconditions for well-being, sustainability and equity, including leveraging on different knowledge systems that go beyond current predominantly monetary assessments. To transform towards a WE society, this emerging initiative intends to bring together a broad range of interdisciplinary scientific expertise and diverse knowledge necessary to understand the interface between well-being, sustainability and equity. The division aims to develop holistic data and policy models to weigh all dimensions of well-being, sustainability and equity for decision makers; leverage change towards a sustainable and equitable society focusing on well-being and to develop a compelling narrative for a holistic framework. . Responsibilities Under the authority of the Director of UNU-EHS and the direct supervision of the Academic Officer (Head of FAST) , the successful candidate will be entrusted with the following tasks: 1. items.desc: Research Associate (m/f/d) in Laser Physics & Femtochemistry (E 13 TV-L, full-time) Göttingen At HAWK University of Applied Sciences and Arts Hildesheim/Holzminden/Göttingen, Faculty of Engineering and Health, Göttingen campus, the following position in the ERC Advanced Grant project FEMTOMICS is to be filled at the earliest possible date, for a fixed term of three years: Research Associate (m/f/d) in Laser Physics & Femtochemistry (E 13 TV-L, full-time) Within the ERC Advanced Grant project FEMTOMICS, we are developing novel photonic and molecular analytical methods for the high-resolution investigation of dynamic protein-DNA interactions. Femtosecond laser-based crosslinking (fliX) is combined with complementary methods in quantitative and structural proteomics (LC-MS/MS), genomics and sequencing (ChIP-Seq, nanopore sequencing), and bioinformatics for multiomics data integration and analysis to characterise protein–DNA interactions at the structural and functional levels. The aim is to make previously inaccessible dynamic molecular processes experimentally measurable and thereby establish new foundations for investigating regulatory mechanisms in biological and disease-relevant systems. A central focus is the development and physicochemical characterisation of novel irradiation and measurement approaches based on ultrashort laser pulses. For this research area, we are seeking a highly motivated scientist with strong experimental expertise in non-linear optics and ultrashort-pulse laser systems who can independently develop, implement, and characterise complex optical setups and, together with an interdisciplinary team, investigate the underlying femtochemical processes. The work combines fundamental research in ultrafast physics and femtochemistry with applications in molecular bioanalytics and biomedical research. It will open up new opportunities for the structural and functional analysis of protein–DNA interactions and for understanding disease-relevant regulatory processes. Ihre Aufgaben Designing, constructing, commissioning, and further developing complex experimental laser systems and irradiation platforms using ultrashort laser pulses, particularly pump–probe setups and dual-wavelength irradiation systems. Independently planning, conducting, and evaluating time-resolved physical and femtochemical experiments to elucidate the processes leading to protein–DNA crosslinking and DNA damage. Systematically investigating and optimising relevant laser and process parameters, such as wavelength, pulse duration, pulse energy, repetition rate, temporal pulse separation, and irradiation dose. Characterising, validating, and standardising the optical setups and measurement methods developed, including benchmarking, reproducibility assessments, troubleshooting, and the preparation of SOPs. Working closely with experts in physics, molecular biology, proteomics, sequencing, and bioinformatics; jointly interpreting results and integrating them into experimental planning. Contributing to scientific publications, project communication, and, where results are eligible for intellectual property protection, invention disclosures and patent applications. Excellent theoretical and practical knowledge of non-linear optics and ultrashort laser pulses and extensive experience with sophisticated experimental laser setups. Strong analytical and independent scientific thinking, with the ability to critically evaluate experimental results and develop solutions to scientific and methodological challenges. A strong interest in biological and biomedical research questions, together with a willingness to acquire expertise in protein–DNA interactions and molecular analytical methods. Excellent teamwork and communication skills, together with an enthusiasm for close collaboration in an interdisciplinary team. Very good English skills for scientific communication and laboratory work and very good German skills for handling administrative matters are expected. items.desc: Position Details Department of Metabolism and Systems Science Location: University of Birmingham, Edgbaston, Birmingham UK Full time starting salary is normally in the range £36,636 to £46,049 with potential progression once in post to £48,822. As this vacancy has limited funding the maximum salary that can be offered is Grade 7, salary £37,694. Full Time, Fixed Term contract up to October 2030 Closing date: 27th October 2026 UK and International travel may be required for this role. Background Pheochromocytomas and paragangliomas (PPGL) are rare neuroendocrine tumours arising from chromaffin cells in the adrenal medulla and sympathetic/parasympathetic paraganglia. Approximately 35% of patients carry germline mutations in one of over 20 known PPGL predisposition genes, with mutations in SDHx genes ( SDHA, SDHB, SDHC, SDHD, SDHAF2) being most common. Patients with SDHB-associated tumours are more likely to develop metastatic disease than patients with sporadic tumours or tumours associated with other predisposing genes. Once disease is metastatic, there are currently limited therapeutic options creating an urgent unmet clinical need. Despite a sophisticated molecular understanding of SDHB mutation driven tumours, the field lacks validated human cell models - a fundamental barrier to translating insights into new treatments for patients with SDHB-deficient disease. This project will continue our drive to develop much-needed novel cell models of PPGL, with the aim of establishing a comprehensive human PPGL cell resource with a particular focus on SDHx-deficient tumours. The post holder will use these models to investigate aspects of SDH-deficient cell metabolism that has the potential to uncover novel therapeutic targets within the metabolic network. Role Summary The postholder will work within a recently awarded grant from the Paradifference Foundation, a charity set up with the purpose of finding new treatments for SDHB-deficient cancers. The postholder will work alongside others in a dynamic and ambitious research group led by Professor Tennant, and in addition to their own project will have the opportunity to contribute to other research projects within the group. The postholder would be expected to progressively take more responsibility for the direction of their research project as they develop their specific expertise in the project area, will want to explore multiple research strands in parallel. For example, alongside deriving new models of SDB-deficient cancers from clinical material, the postholder will also investigate aspects of the metabolic dysfunction observed in these cancer to identify routes towards better treatments. The postholder should be fluent in the subject matter relevant to the post, including techniques or methods. items.card: The Role Applications are invited from enthusiastic and talented individuals at the post-doctorate research level to work at the Global Centre for Clean Air Research (GCARE; www.surrey.ac.uk/gcare), University of Surrey, UK, under the supervision of Professor Prashant Kumar. items.desc: The University of Surrey is a global community of ideas and people, dedicated to life-changing education and research. We are ambitious and have a bold vision of what we want to achieve - shaping ourselves into one of the best universities in the world, which we are achieving through the talents and endeavour of every employee. Our culture empowers people to achieve this aim and to collectively, and individually, make a real difference. The Role Applications are invited from enthusiastic and talented individuals at the post-doctorate research level to work at the Global Centre for Clean Air Research (GCARE; www.surrey.ac.uk/gcare), University of Surrey, UK, under the supervision of Professor Prashant Kumar. GCARE is a multidisciplinary centre, researching in areas of air pollution, air-climate interactions, built and natural environments in the context of cities, megacities and rural areas, with an aim to develop engineering-driven solutions and regulatory strategies for mitigation of environmental risks by means of advanced measurements and modelling techniques. The GCARE’s research projects are funded by the UKRI, numerous national and international funding bodies and the industry. We are looking for a researcher with a PhD degree (or who will receive a PhD degree soon) in the fields of civil, mechanical, chemical, environmental, data science, computer or transportation engineering, physics, chemistry or mathematical sciences or related disciplines. You will contribute to the GP4Streets project (DIY Greening Prescription for Climate Adaptation in Urban Streets) and support ongoing projects such as the UKRI GREENIN Network Plus, British Council SMARTCOAT, and various air quality consultancy projects. As part of the Guildford Living Lab, you will promote GCARE’s research locally, nationally, and internationally and assist with developing new grant applications. Based at the University of Surrey’s GCARE, you will work closely with GCARE team members and project collaborators and may undertake short visits to partner institutions for collaborative research activities. The postholder must have strong skills in air pollution/urban heating monitoring and computational modelling (ENVIMET, CFD), remote sensing, and big data analysis. Responsibilities include monitoring and modelling the effectiveness of green infrastructure in mitigating air pollution and urban overheating, with advanced statistical data analysis skills (e.g., R, Python, MATLAB) required. The role calls for a self-driven, independent individual who can log, clean, share, assess, interpret, and write data efficiently to publish in top-tier journals. A proven track record of timely report writing is essential. The post is available from 01 December 2026. How to apply Please Submit An Online Application That Includes The Following A maximum one-page cover letter explaining your motivation for joining this post and mapping your skills to the job profile and responsibilities. A maximum two-pages CV detailing your education (including grades) and scientific achievements. A maximum of two-pages list of your journal and conference publications, along with any reports written. Please include a brief description (no more than 150 words) of your two best publications, highlighting the scientific breakthroughs and skills used or developed. Two references, including one from your PhD advisor, if possible. For informal enquiries, please contact Professor Prashant Kumar at p.kumar@surrey.ac.uk.

items.desc:
Do you want to solve real customer problems through innovative technology? At Amazon, we hire the best minds in technology to innovate and build on behalf of our customers. Our Software Development Engineers (SDEs) use modern technology to solve complex problems while seeing their work's impact first-hand. 
As an SDE-I, you'll own the entire lifecycle of your code from design through deployment and ongoing operations. You will design and build scalable, fault-tolerant distributed systems using cloud-native architectures and microservices. You'll work in an agile environment practising CI/CD principles, participate in code reviews, contribute to technical documentation, and take part in on-call operational responsibilities. 
Key job responsibilities
- Design, develop, and deploy scalable microservices using Java and Spring Boot (or equivalent frameworks) in a large distributed computing environment hosted on AWS 
 - Write clean, maintainable, production-quality code with comprehensive unit and integration test coverage 
 - Build and operate resilient distributed systems that are fault-tolerant, horizontally scalable, and cost-effective 
 - Participate in technical design discussions, code reviews, and architectural decision-making with cross-disciplinary teams 
- Implement and maintain CI/CD pipelines for automated build, test, and deployment workflows 
 - Monitor, troubleshoot, and resolve production issues; participate in on-call rotations to ensure 24/7 system availability 
 - Leverage and contribute to the development of GenAI and AI-powered tools to enhance development productivity 
 - Collaborate effectively with international, multilingual teams across multiple time zones
- Education: Currently enrolled in or completed a Bachelor's or Graduate degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Data Science, or a related STEM field (minimum 60 ECTS in programming, algorithms, and systems). 
- Expected graduation between October 2025 – September 2026, or graduated within the last 24 months. 
Technical Requirements: 
- Java: 1+ year hands-on experience developing applications, including object-oriented design patterns and the Java Collections Framework 
- Spring Framework: Experience with Spring Boot or Spring MVC, including dependency injection and RESTful API development 
 - Data Structures & Algorithms: Practical implementation of core structures (arrays, linked lists, hash maps, trees, graphs) and algorithms (sorting, searching, recursion, dynamic programming) — evidenced through coursework, competitive programming, or projects 
- SQL: Experience writing queries (SELECT, JOIN, GROUP BY, subqueries) with at least one RDBMS (PostgreSQL, MySQL, or Oracle), including basic schema design 
 - Git: Collaborative experience including branching, merging, pull requests, and conflict resolution 
 - Cloud Computing: Basic experience with AWS (preferred), Azure, or GCP, including deploying applications 
- Testing: Unit and integration testing experience (JUnit, Mockito, or equivalent) with TDD principles 
- SDLC: Full development cycle exposure via internship (3+ months) or capstone project 
 - CI/CD: Experience with at least one tool (Jenkins, GitHub Actions, or equivalent) 
- Communication: Professional English proficiency (B2+ CEFR)
- Previous technical internship(s) of 6+ months in a software engineering role 
 - Experience with microservices architecture and distributed systems design patterns 
-
 Familiarity with containerization (Docker) and orchestration (Kubernetes, ECS) 
-
 Experience with NoSQL databases (DynamoDB, MongoDB, Redis) 
- Exposure to AI/ML concepts, GenAI tools, or machine learning frameworks (TensorFlow, PyTorch) 
 - Experience with monitoring and observability tools (CloudWatch, Grafana, Datadog) 
-
 Knowledge of cybersecurity fundamentals (OWASP Top 10, secure coding practices, identity management) 
- Additional language proficiency (German, Luxembourgish) is an advantage 
- Contributions to open-source projects or published technical work 
- Experience with agile methodologies (Scrum, Kanban) and tools (Jira, Confluence)

The AI Regulatory Engineer supports the development and release of AI-enabled healthcare software, and will provide guidance and set directions for the engineering operation in the area of AI/ML Product Releases within the healthcare industry. items.desc:
About Anthropic 
 Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
 About Anthropic 
 Anthropic's mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
 About Beneficial Deployments 
 Beneficial Deployments ensures AI reaches and benefits the communities that need it most. We partner with nonprofits, foundations, and mission-driven organizations to deploy Claude in education, global health, economic mobility, and life sciences — focusing on raising the floor for those who need it most.
 About the Role 
 We're looking for an Applied AI Engineer to join our Beneficial Deployments, Life Sciences team. This is a partner-facing role: you'll support nonprofits, research institutes, academic medical centres and public-sector funders as they use Claude to get treatments to patients with rare and neglected diseases, where there is little or no commercial incentive to fund development.
 The role focuses on clinical development, where we think Claude can help these partners today. Trials in these diseases have small patient populations, investigator-led or nonprofit funding and little operational support, and they often stall on protocol quality, operational risk and site start-up. Claude can help teams design better trials and start them sooner. Much of this work is drug repurposing: testing new uses for approved, usually off-patent or generic medicines, whose known safety profiles can let a good hypothesis reach patients years sooner than a new molecule.
 You'll advise and embed in partners' teams, building alongside their engineers, scientists and clinicians.
 Responsibilities 
 Work with partners' trial teams to design, review and prioritise clinical trials with Claude: drafting and reviewing protocols and statistical analysis plans, and flagging enrolment and operational risks.
 Build and validate tools that help partners find new uses for approved, mostly off-patent medicines in rare and neglected diseases, from literature, omics and patient data, and assemble the evidence so the partner can decide the next step.
 Build reusable infrastructure other institutions can adopt (MCP servers for biomedical data sources, agent skills, benchmarks grounded in real clinical questions), and feed what you learn in the field back to product, engineering and research.
 You Might Be a Good Fit If You Have 
 Hands-on clinical development experience: designing, running or analysing clinical trials, or assessing clinical evidence to decide which programmes go forward (for example due diligence or asset evaluation). Drug repurposing work as part of that is a strong plus, as is having contributed to a regulatory submission for a trial.
 Comfort with biomedical data: literature, omics, and real-world patient data (health records, registries, claims), ideally inside secure or trusted research environments.
 Strong engineering skills: you can take an LLM-powered tool from prototype to production code, and write evals to measure it.
 Experience working directly with external partners or customers in a technical role.
 Clear written and verbal communication: docs other institutes can use without you, and results clinicians trust.
 A scrappy mentality: you're comfortable in ambiguity, wear several hats, and do what it takes to get a result for a partner.

 £225,000 — £255,000 GBP

You will work closely with researchers and with the pretraining data, sandbox and data platform teams to make these services reliable, scalable and fast, on infrastructure measured in hundreds of terabytes of NVMe storage
items.desc:
ABOUT MISTRAL

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.



Role Summary

We are seeking a talented and experienced Research Engineer to join our newly forming Search and Services Platform team within Research Platform. You will build and operate the large-scale search and services that our models rely on as tools — from self-hosted, web-scale, search indexes to knowledge graphs and databases served through MCP. You will work closely with researchers and with the pretraining data, sandbox and data platform teams to make these services reliable, scalable and fast, on infrastructure measured in hundreds of terabytes of NVMe storage and thousands of CPU cores to support both data generation and critical training runs.



What you will do

As a Research Engineer on the Search and Services team, your responsibilities will include (but may not be limited to):

 - Designing, building and operating large-scale search infrastructure: self-hosted Vespa clusters indexing web-scale corpora, managed indexes for smaller corpora, and vendor search endpoints.

 - Self-hosting and maintaining a wide range of structured data sources — knowledge graphs (Wikidata, UniProt, Materials Project), scholarly data (OpenAlex, OpenAIRE), statistical databases (Eurostat, World Bank, IMF, OECD), open data portals and more.

 - Designing interfaces and tools to expose to the models and agents to use the services in different ways (direct YQL or SPARQL queries, or more refined and constrained MCPs to mimic external services) to support data generation and agentic training.

 - Building the data pipelines that ingest, index and serve massive datasets, including indexing our own pretraining corpora for exploration, deduplication and eval-leakage checks.

 - Building strong relationships with researchers and adjacent teams (pretraining data,, sandbox, data platform), understanding their workflows and enabling them to achieve more by leveraging your expertise.

 - Communicating and producing documentation or any content that will help teams make the most of the services you'll build.



About you

 - 5+ years of successful experience in search engineering, data infrastructure, or a similar SRE / platform role.

 - Proficiency in software development (Python, Go...) and programming best practices.

 - Hands-on experience with large-scale search or data systems (e.g. Vespa, Elasticsearch / OpenSearch, ClickHouse or similar).

 - Exposure to site reliability engineering: root cause analysis, in-production troubleshooting, on-call rotations...)

 - Exposure to infrastructure management: containerization, orchestration (Kubernetes), infra-as-code, monitoring, logging, alerting, observability...).

 - Experience designing and operating data pipelines that address large amounts of data.

 - Excellent problem-solving and communication skills (ability to contextualizing, gauging risks and getting buy-in for high stakes and impactful solutions).

 - Ownership, high agency and constantly seeking to learn and improving things for others.

 - Autonomous, self-driven and able to work well in a fast-paced startup environment.

 - Low ego and team spirit mindset.

 - Your application will be all the more interesting if you also have:

 - First-hand Vespa (or equivalent large-scale information retrieval) experience.

 - Experience building or operating MCP servers / tool-serving infrastructure for LLMs.

 - Familiarity with knowledge graphs, RDF / SPARQL, or large structured databases (PostgreSQL, ClickHouse, DuckDB...).

 - Experience with large bare-metal infrastructure or HPC environments.




WHAT WE OFFER

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page https://app.notion.com/p/mistralai/Benefits-at-Mistral-36e6ba59a7fe836b93dd01737fcc27ef?source=copy_link.




PRIVACY POLICY

Your privacy matters to us. You can learn more about how we handle your personal data in our Applicant Privacy Policy https://legal.mistral.ai/terms/applicant-privacy-policy.

About Us 
 Teton is redefining the role of healthcare workers through cutting-edge AI technology and a great product experience. As populations gets older and a shortage in staff, healthcare system is under pressure. Our missions is to decrease the cost of healthcare while improving the quality of care.
 Our product enables careteams to intervene, prevent and operator more efficiently. Our ambient sensors in resident rooms captures activity, sleep, respiration, gait and more. These signal used for both react fast to risk events, like falls, and long term health analysis, for care teams to take actions.
 Teton is scaling fast, operating in Nordics, UK, DACH and US. Recently raised 20M $$ series A. Expect travel to the US, to meet users and team members.
 We focus relentless on product excellence and user experience, deploying solutions at speed that make a tangible difference for cares. We are an aspiring meritocracy biased towards action, striving to always raise the bar. If you are driven by impact, speed and leveling up, this might be the place for you.
 If you are looking for a 9-17 job, perform best with structure and struggle dealing with unknowns, this is not for you. We believe close collaboration between a hard working, high agency team enables the fastest and most efficient iteration cycles, helping us build an impactful product that healthcare professionals truly love to use.
 The Job 
 We are looking for a strong backend engineer to help scale the core infrastructure powering Teton’s platform.
 Our systems ingest and process continuous streams of real-time data from thousands of deployed edge devices across care facilities. These systems power critical alerts and operational workflows used by healthcare staff around the clock.
 You will work across:
 Distributed data ingestion systems
 Real-time event pipelines
 APIs and backend services
 Databases and storage systems
 MQTT infrastructure and edge communication
 Reliability, observability, and system performance
 Cloud infrastructure and deployment architecture
 Qualifications: 
 We care more about engineering ability and ownership than specific credentials, but strong candidates will likely have experience with several of the following:
 Building and operating large-scale backend or distributed systems
 Designing reliable real-time data pipelines
 Working with event-driven architectures and asynchronous systems
 Scaling APIs and services handling high-throughput workloads
 Operating production infrastructure with strong reliability requirements
 Database design and performance optimization
 Cloud infrastructure and deployment tooling
 Debugging complex production issues under pressure
 What We Offer 
 Participation in our warrant program (stock options).
 A small team where your decisions directly shape the product.
 A Copenhagen-based office with close collaboration, no async-only culture.
 Work on software that healthcare workers depend on every day, the impact is tangible and immediate.
 Join Our Team 
 We're looking for individuals who share our vision and value ownership and entrepreneurship over a conventional job.
 At Teton, you'll have the chance to make a real impact with your work.
 If you're ready for more than just a job, come aboard and be part of our mission to transform healthcare.

items.desc:
About Us
 At Teton, we are redefining the role of healthcare workers through cutting-edge AI technology. Facing a global nursing shortage, our solutions offer vital support to overburdened health systems. With thousands of patient rooms across 4 countries already benefiting from our technology, we are aiming to expand to much more. We distinguish ourselves by focusing relentlessly on product excellence and user experience, rapidly deploying solutions that make a real difference.
 The Job
 Every patient room we deploy into puts another device on infrastructure we don't control, in a building we can't easily visit, running software that has to keep working. We're looking for an Engineer to own that problem: the systems, tooling, and infrastructure that let us ship to thousands of edge devices confidently and understand what they're doing once they're out there.
 In this role, you will focus on the following areas of interest:
 Fleet Management: Build and run the systems that provision, monitor, and manage our devices in the field, from first boot in a hospital room to end of life.
 OTA & Release Engineering: Own how software gets onto devices: staged rollouts, health checks, automatic rollback, and the confidence that a bad release won't take down a ward.
 Observability: Design the telemetry, logging, and alerting that tell us a device is degrading before a nurse notices. Make remote debugging possible so we don't fly to fix things.
 Device Bring-Up & Debugging: Work with our hardware and firmware teams on new hardware revisions, reproduce field issues on the bench, and get to the bottom of problems that span kernel, driver, network, and application.
 Infrastructure & Tooling: Build the CI/CD, image builds, and internal tools that let the whole engineering team ship to hardware quickly and safely.
 Documentation: Maintain clear and detailed documentation of your work to ensure easy collaboration and knowledge sharing within the team.
 Qualifications:

items.desc: Aanbod Als digital workplace & AI specialist bij Wienerberger maak je deel uit van een internationale en gerenommeerde organisatie met een lokaal en familiaal karakter. Je krijgt de kans om initiatief te nemen, je functie verder te ontwikkelen en je carrière zelf vorm te geven. Als blijk van waardering voor je expertise en toewijding bieden we een aantrekkelijk salarispakket aan, inclusief diverse extralegale voordelen zoals 33 vrij te kiezen verlofdagen, maaltijd- en ecocheques, aandelenplan, hospitalisatie- en groepsverzekering en de mogelijkheid tot verdere opleiding Bedrijfsvoorstelling Wienerberger is niet alleen wereldwijd toonaangevend als producent van dakpannen, snelbouw – en gevelstenen, maar we bieden ook een breed scala aan innovatieve bouwoplossingen. Onze businessunits, Wienerberger Building Solutions (met de gekende merken Porotherm, Terca & Koramic) en Wienerberger Piping Solutions (Pipelife, Preflex & Steinzeug-Keramo), vormen de ruggengraat van ons streven naar duurzame oplossingen. We hechten grote waarde aan milieu, kwaliteit en veiligheid. Met 17 productievestigingen, 2 showrooms en onze bruisende hoofdzetel in Kortrijk, verenigen we meer dan 1500 gepassioneerde medewerkers. Elke dag werken we samen aan het ontwikkelen van hoogwaardige producten en klantgerichte oplossingen die voldoen aan de unieke behoeften van elk bouwproject. Bij Wienerberger België gaan we verder dan bouwen; we creëren toekomstige ruimtes en infrastructuren. We nodigen jou uit om deel uit te maken van ons dynamische team en bij te dragen aan de evolutie van de bouwsector. Functie Om onze digitale werkplek verder uit te bouwen, zijn we voor ons IT & Digital team in Kortrijk op zoek naar een Digital Workplace & AI Specialist. Je bouwt mee aan de verdere ontwikkeling van onze Digital Workplace & AI-roadmap en zet Microsoft-technologie in om processen te optimaliseren, kennisdeling te verbeteren en medewerkers maximaal te ondersteunen in hun dagelijkse werkzaamheden. Dit zal je doen: Je bouwt en beheert oplossingen met Power Automate, Power Apps, Power Pages en Copilot Studio ; Je identificeert opportuniteiten voor automatisatie en AI; Je ondersteunt de uitrol en adoptie van Microsoft Copilot ; Je vertaalt businessnoden naar concrete digitale oplossingen en AI-use cases; Je werkt samen met Corporate IT rond governance, security en architectuur; Je begeleidt medewerkers via workshops, opleidingen en citizen development; Je volgt nieuwe ontwikkelingen binnen Microsoft en AI actief op. Profiel Ervaring binnen Digital Workplace, IT, automatisatie of een gelijkaardige digitale functie. Sterke affiniteit met het Microsoft-ecosysteem en AI Kennis van Microsoft Copilot , Power Automate en/of Power Apps . Hands-on, pragmatisch en sterk in het vertalen van technologie naar businesswaarde. Communicatief, klantgericht en vlot in samenwerking met verschillende stakeholders.
