items.desc: Description de l'entreprise Septeo est un acteur de référence du software en Europe , présent à l’international et reconnu parmi le top 5 des éditeurs de logiciels sectoriels en France . En forte croissance et en transformation permanente, le groupe s’impose comme un acteur clé de l’édition logicielle grâce à la force de son collectif : des équipes déterminées, audacieuses et engagées. Chez Septeo, l’intelligence artificielle est placée au cœur de notre évolution . Nous la concevons comme un levier de performance durable, de collaboration et d’innovation, intégrée de manière responsable dans les pratiques du quotidien et démocratisé sur l’ensemble de nos métiers. L'ambition est claire : “make intelligent software for Europe”. Notre culture repose sur des valeurs fortes : être, faire et transformer ensemble . Elle n’est pas figée; elle se vit chaque jour dans nos actions et nos décisions, à travers un équilibre entre performance, responsabilité et plaisir. Cette ambition s’incarne dans ce que nous faisons au quotidien : concevoir des logiciels qui accompagnent les moments de vie essentiels, au service de millions de citoyens. Être présent derrière ces instants clés est une responsabilité forte. C’est la nôtre. Et peut-être bientôt la votre. Rejoindre Septeo, c’est intégrer une aventure collective à dimension internationale , porter la transformation du groupe dans un environnement en mouvement rapide, et faire de l’IA un levier concret de création de valeur, aujourd’hui comme demain. Prêt(e) à faire partie de l’aventure ? Description du poste Nous recherchons un Développeur Fullstack IA H/F , en CDI, à Montpellier (Lattes), pour rejoindre notre filiale Septeo Solutions Notaires . Intégré(e) aux équipes R&D, vous participez au développement et à l'évolution de nos solutions logicielles dans un environnement produit en pleine transformation. Vous intervenez aussi bien sur la conception que sur le développement de nouvelles fonctionnalités, tout en contribuant à la modernisation des pratiques de développement autour de l'intelligence artificielle. Ce que nous pouvons accomplir ensemble : Au sein d'une équipe organisée par domaine métier, vous contribuez à la construction d'un nouveau produit tout en participant à l'évolution des applications existantes. Vous prenez part aux choix techniques, aux revues de code et à l'amélioration continue des pratiques de développement. Votre quotidien : Développer et faire évoluer des fonctionnalités front et back ; Participer aux choix de conception et d'architecture ; Produire un code maintenable, testé et fiable ; Contribuer aux revues de code et aux pratiques CI/CD ; Explorer et intégrer les usages de l'IA dans les activités de développement. La stack : C# / .NET / Angular, React ou Vue.js / SQL Server / PostgreSQL / Azure DevOps / Git / Kubernetes. La stack IA & pratiques de développement : Claude / Cursor / SDD Qualifications Et si c'était vous ? Vous justifiez d'une expérience significative en développement Fullstack , avec une solide maîtrise de C#/.NET ainsi que d'au moins un framework front moderne ( Angular, React ou Vue.js ). Vous maîtrisez les bonnes pratiques de développement (tests, qualité logicielle, Git, CI/CD) et avez déjà intégré l'IA à votre façon de développer. Que ce soit pour générer du code, accélérer les tests, comprendre un existant ou challenger une architecture, vous savez utiliser ces outils avec discernement et esprit critique. Curieux(se), autonome et pragmatique, vous avez envie d'évoluer dans un environnement où l'IA ne constitue pas un simple outil, mais participe pleinement à la transformation du métier de développeur. N'hésitez pas à postuler ! Informations supplémentaires Rejoindre Septeo, c’est aussi : Participer à l’aventure AI First de Septeo et découvrir de nouvelles façons de travailler grâce à l’intelligence artificielle. Grandir et s’épanouir grâce à un parcours de formation personnalisé et des opportunités de mobilité interne. Vivre une expérience humaine, échanger et partager autour d’événements thématisés : afterworks, sport, RSE, séminaires, etc. Rejoindre un collectif qui prend soin des autres et s’engage en faveur de l’égalité des chances, de la diversité et de l’inclusion. items.desc: Interdisziplinäre KI-Bildung gestalten: Zwei wissenschaftliche Stellen im Digitalisierungskolleg KI-EduLab (Fachdisziplinen: Informatik und Grundschulpädagogik) Ihr Arbeitsplatz Künstliche Intelligenz durchdringt zunehmend den Alltag – auch die Lebenswelt von Grundschulkindern. Damit wächst der Bedarf an Fachkräften, die KI-basierte Bildungstechnologien verantwortungsvoll entwickeln, und an Lehrkräften, die KI nicht nur nutzen, sondern auch verstehen und kindgerecht vermitteln können. Das vom Bayerischen Forschungsinstitut für Digitale Transformation (bidt) geförderte Digitalisierungskolleg „KI-EduLab – Lernlabor für KI und Bildungstechnologien in interdisziplinären Learning Communities“ der Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg (FAU) bringt hierfür Studierende der Informatik und des Lehramts an Grundschulen in gemeinsamen Lehr-Lern-Formaten zusammen. In drei aufeinander aufbauenden Seminaren – von den „Grundfragen der KI“ über eine fachspezifische Vertiefung bis zum interdisziplinären Projektseminar – entwickeln gemischte Teams aus Informatik- und Lehramtsstudierenden Lernangebote mit und über KI für die Grundschule und erproben diese in der Praxis. Dazu suchen wir zum 01.01.2027 vorbehaltlich der endgültigen Bewilligung der Mittel durch das bidt Wir haben einiges zu bieten: unsere Benefits Regelmäßiger Stufenanstieg und steigendes Gehalt nach Tarifvertrag für den öffentlichen Dienst der Länder (TV-L) beziehungsweise Besoldung nach BayBesG sowie zusätzliche Jahressonderzahlung Urlaubsanspruch von 30 Tagen pro Kalenderjahr bei fünf Arbeitstagen pro Woche, mit zusätzlichen freien Tagen am 24. und 31. Dezember Betriebliche Altersversorgung sowie vermögenswirksame Leistungen Intensive Begleitung in der wissenschaftlichen Qualifikationsphase Systematische Karriereentwicklung im Graduiertenzentrum Umfassende Einarbeitung durch engagiertes Team Gemeinsame Aktivitäten im Team Familienfreundliche Umgebung mit Ferien- und Kinderbetreuungsangeboten Flexible Arbeitszeitregelungen Vielfältige Weiterbildungs- und Fortbildungsmöglichkeiten Ihre Aufgaben Die beiden Stellen sind bewusst interdisziplinär angelegt und arbeiten als Tandem eng zusammen. Sie richten sich an zwei Profile, von denen Ihr Profil eines bedienen sollte: 1. Grundschulpädagogisches Profil mit Interesse an Informatik und KI Die Stelle ist am Lehrstuhl für Grundschulpädagogik und -didaktik mit dem Schwerpunkt Lehren und Lernen (Prof. Dr. Bärbel Kopp) angesiedelt und wird von Dr. Saskia Knoth fachlich verantwortet. Sie bringt die grundschulpädagogische und -didaktische Perspektive in das KI-EduLab ein. Im Mittelpunkt stehen die Lern- und Lebenswelten von Grundschulkindern, die Gestaltung kindgerechter Lernangebote sowie die Frage, wie Kinder KI verstehen, kritisch reflektieren und für eigene Lernprozesse nutzen können. Dabei verbinden Sie das Lernen über KI als Unterrichtsgegenstand mit dem Lernen mit KI, beispielsweise durch KI-gestützte Werkzeuge zur Diagnose und Förderung.Die Stelle verantwortet die grundschulpädagogische und -didaktische Perspektive des Kollegs: Lernen und Lehren in der Grundschule, die digitale Lebenswelt von Kindern, KI als Unterrichtsgegenstand (Lernen über KI) sowie der Einsatz KI-gestützter Werkzeuge zur Diagnose und Förderung (Lernen mit KI). Ein besonderer Schwerpunkt liegt auf der kritisch-reflexiven Auseinandersetzung mit KI und ihrer Übersetzung in kindgerechte Lernangebote sowie auf der Erprobung in Lernwerkstatt, Schulnetzwerk und Lehrkräftefortbildung. 2. Informatisches Profil mit Interesse an Bildung und Fachdidaktik Informatik Angesiedelt an der Professur für Didaktik der Informatik (Prof. Dr. Marc-Pascal Berges). Die Stelle verantwortet die informatische Perspektive des Kollegs: technische KI-Kompetenz (z. B. maschinelles Lernen, Deep Learning, NLP, Computer Vision), Human-Centered Design und UX/UI für Bildungsanwendungen sowie Barrierefreiheit. Im Mittelpunkt steht, wie Informatikstudierende entlang realer Bedarfe aus Schule und Unterricht Bildungstechnologien gestalten und entwickeln – etwa adaptive Hilfestellungen oder Werkzeuge zur Unterstützung der Leistungsbeurteilung. Grundsätzlich ist für beide Stellen eine Offenheit für interdisziplinäre Zusammenarbeit sowie ein ausgeprägtes Interesse an Fragen der KI-Bildung und digitalen Souveränität erforderlich. Aufgaben: Konzeption, Durchführung und Weiterentwicklung der drei interdisziplinären Seminare des Kollegs gemeinsam mit den beteiligten Lehrstühlen und Kooperationspartner:innen der FAU Interdisziplinäre Lernbegleitung: Organisation und Moderation gemeinsamer Lernprozesse von Informatik- und Lehramtsstudierenden, insbesondere in interdisziplinären Projektteams, Inputphasen sowie Reflexions- und Feedbackrunden) Material- und Lernangebotsentwicklung: Erstellung multimedialer Lernmodule aus der jeweiligen Fachperspektive sowie Anleitung und Begleitung der Studierenden bei der Erstellung von Lernangeboten mit und über KI Projektbegleitung und …

Die Stelle ist in dem DFG-Projekt SciDocExtreme (A Large-Scale Cross-Domain Dataset for AI-Driven Scientific Document Processing and Scientific Knowledge Extraction) angesiedelt, das vom DFKI (Prof. Dr. Georg Rehm) koordiniert wird. Das Projekt entwickelt das weltweit größte Datenset für die KI-gestützte Verarbeitung wissenschaftlicher Publikationen (insbesondere durch automatische und manuelle Annotation auf verschiedensten Ebenen) sowie entsprechende KI-Modelle (Training, Evaluation). Das Projekt wird gemeinsam mit GESIS (Köln) durchgeführt und kooperiert mit dem Projekt NFDI4DataScience and AI (NFDI4DS). SciDocExtreme startet am 01. Januar 2027. Ihre Aufgaben Forschungs- und Entwicklungsarbeiten im Bereich Natural Language Processing (NLP), Datenannotation und KI-Modelle Aktive Mitwirkung bei der Koordinierung des Projekts und bei der Spezifizierung und Entwicklung des SciDocExtreme-Datensets Leitung eines Teams von AnnotatorInnen (wissenschaftliche Hilfskräfte) Publikation von Forschungsergebnissen (wissenschaftliche Konferenzen und Workshops, Zeitschriften) und Dokumentation der Arbeiten Unsere Anforderungen Master in Computerlinguistik, Cognitive Science, NLP, KI, Informatik, Computer Science (oder vergleichbar) Exzellente Programmierkenntnisse (insbesondere Python) Exzellente NLP-Kenntnisse einschließlich praktischer Erfahrung insbesondere im Bereich maschineller Lernverfahren und neuronaler Methoden Sehr sicherer Umgang mit Korpora und Datensets Idealerweise Erfahrung bzgl. Annotation oder Labelling großer Datensets Idealerweise erste Publikationserfahrung Teamfähigkeit, Ergebnisorientierung, hohe Eigenmotivation Sehr gute Englisch- und idealerweise auch Deutschkenntnisse Was Sie erwarten können Ein innovatives, agiles und professionelles Arbeitsumfeld Ein attraktives Gehalt, flexible Arbeitszeiten und die Option auf Homeoffice Vielseitige und anspruchsvolle Aufgaben Promotion im Rahmen eines im Projekt angesiedelten Themas möglich Bei Fragen wenden Sie sich bitte an Prof. Dr. Georg Rehm <georg.rehm@dfki.de> Das Deutsche Forschungszentrum für Künstliche Intelligenz GmbH (DFKI) wurde 1988 als gemeinnützige Public-Private-Partnership (PPP) gegründet. Das DFKI verbindet wissenschaftliche Spitzenleistung und wirtschaftsnahe Wertschöpfung mit gesellschaftlicher Wertschätzung. Das DFKI forscht seit über 35 Jahren an KI für den Menschen und orientiert sich an gesellschaftlicher Relevanz und wissenschaftlicher Exzellenz in den entscheidenden zukunftsorientierten Forschungs- und Anwendungsgebieten der Künstlichen Intelligenz. In der internationalen Wissenschaftswelt zählt das DFKI zu den wichtigsten „Centers of Excellence“. Schwerbehinderte Bewerberinnen und Bewerber und Gleichgestellte werden bei gleicher Eignung besonders berücksichtigt. Das DFKI beabsichtigt, den Anteil von Frauen im Wissenschaftsbereich zu erhöhen und fordert deshalb Frauen ausdrücklich auf, sich zu bewerben. Bewerbungsfrist 29. Oktober 2026 Fachliche Fragen zu dieser Position beantwortet Ihnen gerne: Prof. Dr. Georg Rehm Deutsches Forschungszentrum für Künstliche Intelligenz GmbH (DFKI) DFKI Labor Berlin, Salzufer 15-16, 10587 Berlin +49 30 23895 1833 georg.rehm@dfki.de

items.desc: Do you get excited about building cutting-edge perception systems that work reliably in the real world? Do you have a strong foundation in computer vision, robotics, or sensor fusion? Are you interested in shaping new technology capabilities within a growing and innovative high-tech company, where people and fun are part of our core values? We’d love to have you! Who is Xsens Xsens is a leading full-stack provider of sensors, software, and analytics that enable the digitization of movement. For more than two decades, our inertial sensor modules and sensor fusion technology have delivered reliable orientation and position data in demanding environments, from autonomous vehicles and drones to industrial machinery and humanoid robots. Xsens serves automation & mobility, humanoid robotics, entertainment, and health & sports markets. By turning complex motion data into actionable insight, we help our partners navigate, control, and learn in the physical world. We collaborate with leading global innovators including Boston Dynamics, Toyota and Siemens, alongside more than 1,000 research institutions, robotics companies and universities worldwide. Your role as a Computer Vision Engineer at Xsens As a Computer Vision Engineer, you will be at the heart of our effort to expand Xsens' positioning and localization capabilities, moving beyond inertial-only solutions toward full visual-inertial systems. You will research, prototype, and deploy algorithms for Visual-Inertial Odometry (VIO), SLAM, and 6-DoF pose estimation, bringing together our IMU technologies with camera-based perception capabilities. You will be part of the Technology team and report to the Technology Manager. You will be based in Enschede, the Netherlands, with the possibility of hybrid/remote working. Key challenges: Design and implement state-of-the-art VIO and SLAM pipelines, combining inertial sensor data with monocular or stereo camera inputs. Develop and maintain camera models, calibration routines, and sensor synchronization pipelines across multiple hardware configurations. Apply optimization techniques and filtering methods to achieve robust and accurate 6-DoF pose estimation. Stay current with the computer vision and research landscape and assess the feasibility of integrating new techniques into Xsens products. Collaborate closely with hardware, firmware, and software teams to deliver end-to-end perception solutions. Xsens is looking for a hands-on Computer Vision Engineer who combines strong theoretical foundations with a proven ability to build and ship working systems. Required MSc in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, or a related field, with 3+ years of relevant industry or research experience; or a PhD with demonstrated hands-on system-building experience. Solid understanding of multi-view geometry and camera and lens models and physics Hands-on experience with VO or SLAM systems, and familiarity with open source frameworks. Proficiency in Python / C++. Strong mathematical background in linear algebra, probability theory, and state estimation. Preferred A few years of experience in automotive and/or robotics industry Experience with IMU signal processing and inertial sensor models. Awareness of GPU-accelerated computing and experience in optimizing algorithms for real-time performance Knowledge of deep learning-based perception methods. Experience with ROS, OpenCV, and standard robotics tooling. Working at Xsens We value ingenious ideas, no matter where they come from. We believe diverse thoughts, voices, and backgrounds make us stronger as a company. We know that it is through collaboration with people from all walks of life that we make the most positive impact as an organization. Join Xsens’ innovative, ambitious, and international team, where your ideas and talents make an impact. Along with a competitive compensation package, we offer a range of benefits designed to support your well-being and help you thrive. 28 paid vacation days with an option to buy, sell, or carry over days, giving you flexibility to manage your time off as appropriate to your situation Tax perks for your sports memberships and bicycle purchase; so staying active is easier than ever. Enjoy company social events as well as fun, informal activities organized by our staff association. items.desc: Our paywall is a model. Come and make it smarter. Schibsted | Oslo, Bergen or Stockholm (hybrid) We built our own dynamic paywall and offer engine. Now we need to make it better, understand what works, and bring it to more brands. We're looking for a Data Scientist who enjoys building models, testing ideas and finding out whether the results actually make a difference. You'll work alongside experienced data scientists, analysts and engineers, with opportunities to take ownership of your work and grow your skills along the way. Why this work matters Our democracies depend on independent journalism, and that is our business. Independent journalism needs readers who choose to pay for it. Our job in Subscription Data Enablement is to understand those readers well enough to offer them the right thing at the right time, and to leave them alone when we shouldn't bother them. Direct relationships with readers and digital profitability are how Schibsted measures success. Your models sit right in the middle of both. Who we are We are the data and analytics team for Schibsted's Subscription business in Norway and Sweden: analysts, data engineers, an ML engineer and data scientists. We work with brands such as VG, Aftenposten, Aftonbladet, Svenska Dagbladet, Bergens Tidende and E24. Our models already cover churn, renewal, segmentation and engagement. The dynamic paywall and offer engine is the newest addition to the family. It is also a good test of how we work. The Dynamic Paywall project has many moving parts and competing priorities, and it needs people from data, product, tech, business and editorial teams in the same room. A consultant who recently worked with us said that, despite technically being a consultant, they "never really felt like one". They described a team where everyone brings different expertise, ideas get challenged, debates are healthy, and we don't always agree, but there is "always mutual respect" and a shared goal of finding the best way forward. We want you to feel the same way about us a year from now. What you will do Make our paywall smarter. Develop and improve the models behind our dynamic paywall and offers: who sees which offer, and when. Propensity, recommender and offer optimisation problems are all in scope. Find out what works. Design, run and analyse experiments with our brands, and report the results as they are, including what they don’t prove. Uplift modelling and causal inference are welcome tools here. Build models that get used. Take models from notebook to production with our data scientists and engineers: feature engineering, training, evaluation, testing, and monitoring once they’re live. We work with tools such as Snowflake, MLflow and Streamlit. Make the results understandable. Explain findings to commercial colleagues with clear analysis and dashboards where they help. Improve how we work. Bring ideas on modelling, tooling and MLOps as more brands come on board, including how AI can make our own work easier. Ask good questions. Including “does this actually make us money?” when someone needs to. What you bring Python or R and SQL, used to analyse data and build models. Hands-on experience developing and evaluating machine learning models, and an understanding of what it takes to run them in production. A solid foundation in statistics and experimentation, including hypothesis testing and A/B tests. The ability to explain your work to people who don’t speak ML, and the curiosity to learn from people who know the business better than you do. items.desc: Job Title AI 3D Designer Shape the future of passenger experiences — bring innovation to life through AI and 3D design. At Amadeus, you’ll play a key role in transforming airport touchpoints and travel products through cutting-edge 3D visualization and artificial intelligence. As a 3D Designe r , you’ll turn complex challenges into tangible, visually compelling solutions that enhance the way millions of travelers interact with our technology. Join a creative, multidisciplinary design team where innovation, collaboration, and impact come together to shape the travel of tomorrow. In this role, you'll Design and develop 3D models, prototypes, and visual assets for airport touchpoints, kiosks, and boarding systems. Use tools such as SolidWorks, AutoCAD, and AI-assisted visualization apps (e.g., Vizcom) to accelerate design and concept exploration. Translate product goals and user needs into engaging and technically feasible designs that align with brand and business objectives. Collaborate closely with UX Designers, Product Managers, R&D Engineers, and AI specialists throughout the design lifecycle. Leverage AI and generative design tools to automate repetitive tasks and streamline the end-to-end creative process. Prototype and validate 3D concepts through storytelling, visual communication, and iterative design techniques. Document workflows, share best practices, and contribute to design knowledge within a global innovation community. Participate in stakeholder workshops, presenting ideas that connect design intent with user journeys and technical feasibility. Stay up to date with emerging trends in AI-driven design, 3D visualization, and product experience innovation. About the ideal candidate Experienced in 3D visualization and physical product design, ideally with exposure to hardware or industrial environments. Proficient in SolidWorks, AutoCAD, or equivalent 3D design tools and prototyping methods for real-world applications. Familiar with AI-assisted tools and automation workflows to enhance design speed and efficiency. Strong visual storytelling and presentation skills, able to convey design intent with clarity and impact. Comfortable working in dynamic, multidisciplinary teams with evolving project requirements. Proactive, collaborative, and curious about integrating artificial intelligence in the design process. Willingness to travel occasionally for research, testing, and collaboration at airport or R&D sites. Fluent in English; other languages are a plus for collaboration in our global environment. What we can offer you A truly global DNA - Everything at Amadeus is global, from our people to our business, which translates into our footprint, processes, and culture. Great opportunities to learn - Learning happens all the time and in many ways at Amadeus, through on-the-job training, formal learning activities, and day-to-day interactions with colleagues. A caring environment - Amadeus fosters a caring environment, nurturing both a fulfilling career and personal and family life. We care about our employees and strive to provide a supportive work environment. A hybrid working model - We want our employees to do their best work, however the hybrid model works best for them. A diverse and inclusive community - We are committed to leveraging our uniquely diverse population to drive innovation, creativity, and collaboration across our organization. A Reliable Company - Trust and reliability are fundamental values that drive our actions and shape long-lasting relationships with our customers, partners, and employees. A critical mission and purpose - At Amadeus, you will be powering the future of travel and pursuing a critical mission and extraordinary purpose. #LI-EMEA Diversity & Inclusion Amadeus aspires to be a leader in Diversity and Inclusion in the tech industry, enabling every employee to reach their full potential by fostering a culture of belonging and fair treatment, attracting the best talent from all backgrounds, and as a role model for an inclusive employee experience. Amadeus is an equal opportunity employer and committed to an accessible recruitment process. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to gender, race, ethnicity, sexual orientation, age, beliefs, disability or any other characteristics protected by law. Be aware of recruitment scams Amadeus Group never charges fees, requests payment, or asks for financial information during recruitment. All legitimate opportunities are communicated solely through official Amadeus channels, including our careers website. Any payment request or outreach via unofficial platforms (e.g., WhatsApp, Telegram) should be treated as fraudulent.

Om bolaget Vår kund är ett internationellt AI-startup/scaleup som utvecklar framtidens digitala relationer. Med en innovativ affärsmodell, starka investerare och höga tillväxtambitioner befinner sig bolaget i en spännande utvecklingsfas. Teamet består idag av cirka 12 personer utspridda över världen. Här möts entreprenörskap, ny teknik och ett modernt arbetssätt i en miljö där idéer snabbt kan bli verklighet. Bolaget har nyligen tagit in nytt kapital och står inför nästa fas av sin internationella tillväxtresa. Rollen som Business Controller – var med och bygg från början Vi söker dig som är i början av din ekonomikarriär och vill vara med och utveckla bolagets ekonomistyrning och ekonomifunktion. Du kommer att arbeta med ekonomisk analys, uppföljning, budget, prognoser och affärsrelaterade nyckeltal. Samtidigt får du möjlighet att utveckla nya arbetssätt och utforska hur AI kan bli en naturlig del av ekonomiarbetet. Du får stort eget ansvar, men också stöd från en extern ekonomibyrå och internt i organisationen. Det här är inte en roll där allt redan är på plats. Tvärtom. Du får vara med och skapa det. Vem är du? Vi tror att du har en ekonomisk utbildning och kanske 1–3 års arbetslivserfarenhet. Du är analytisk, trygg i Excel och gillar att förstå affären bakom siffrorna. Men framför allt söker vi dig som: Är genuint nyfiken på AI och redan använder eller experimenterar med olika AI-verktyg. Är driven, självgående och gillar att ta egna initiativ. Har ett stort intresse för SaaS, BI och digitala affärsmodeller. Tänker nytt, utmanar gamla arbetssätt och gillar att hitta smartare lösningar. Vill arbeta i ett startup och vara med och bygga något från grunden. Trivs med att arbeta självständigt i ett internationellt team och kommunicerar obehindrat på engelska. Du behöver inte ha erfarenhet från AI-bolag, SaaS eller startups. Din nyfikenhet, ditt driv och din vilja att lära dig är viktigare. Varför den här möjligheten? Här får du chansen att kombinera ekonomi, AI och entreprenörskap i ett bolag som befinner sig i början av sin resa. Du får möjlighet att påverka, testa idéer, utveckla nya arbetssätt och växa tillsammans med bolaget. Du arbetar med kollegor över hela världen och får en unik inblick i hur ett internationellt AI-bolag byggs och skalas. Plats: Remote – arbeta på distans. Är du vår nästa Junior Business Controller? Du behöver inte kunna allt från början. Vi söker framför allt rätt person med rätt inställning, analytisk förmåga och ett stort intresse för AI och framtidens affärer. Låter det som du? Vi arbetar nära både kunder och kandidater med fokus på långsiktiga relationer och framgångsrika matchningar. Läs mer om oss på www.evolvefy.com.

items.desc: Vill du leda en europeisk satsning där AI, flyg och drönare möts, och där företag och offentliga verksamheter får hjälp att ta nästa steg? Hos oss får du ansvaret för Aero EDIH(European Digital Innovation Hub) Ai och håller ihop ett konsortium med Linköpings universitet, Lunds universitet, RISE och Linköping Science Park. Vilka är vi? Hos oss på Norrköping Science Park möts innovation, forskning och samhällsutveckling. Här får du utrymme att växa, påverka och samarbeta i en miljö som bryr sig om både resultat och människor. Vi erbjuder en flexibel arbetsmiljö där professionalism möter nyfikenhet och där ditt engagemang formar både din egen och vår gemensamma resa framåt. Ett av våra viktigaste uppdrag är att skapa förutsättningar för fler företag och arbetstillfällen att födas och växa. Vi driver startupmiljöer och ett stort antal utvecklingsprojekt tillsammans med företag, universitet och offentlig sektor, regionalt och i Europa. Projektet Aero EDIH Ai bygger vidare på Aero EDIH, som vi har lett sedan starten och som överträffade sina mål. Nu tar vi nästa steg med ett tydligare fokus på AI. Projektet handlar om att hjälper företag och offentliga verksamheter att testa AI och ny teknik innan de investerar, bygga kompetens inom AI, data och cybersäkerhet och hitta finansiering till nästa steg, med stöd av ett nätverk regionalt och i Europa. Fokus ligger på flyg- och drönarbranschen och det nedre luftrummet. Vi arbetar också med närliggande sektorer som skog, jordbruk, infrastruktur, energi och logistik, där drönare och AI kan göra stor nytta. Dina arbetsuppgifter Som projektledare har du det övergripande ansvaret för Aero EDIH AI och leder arbetspaketet för projektledning och koordinering. Du håller ihop partnerna, ser till att tjänsterna når ut till företagen och att de håller hög kvalitet, och bygger kontakter med nätverk och AI-infrastrukturer i hela Europa. I rollen ingår bland annat att: leda och samordna konsortiet och arbetspaketen, med tydliga mål, roller och uppföljning, och kalla till och driva styrgruppen ansvara för budget, ekonomisk uppföljning och rapportering till EU-kommissionen och medfinansiärerna följa upp projektets mål och risker löpande och ställa om när något inte fungerar följa upp att kundleveranserna håller hög kvalitet och att kunderna är nöjda bygga och underhålla samarbeten med andra nationella och internationella och EDIH:er, bevaka förändringar i regelverk och marknad, bland annat AI Act och cybersäkerhet, och utveckla tjänsteutbudet därefter driva effektiva möten och tydliga rutiner, och se till att arbetet dokumenteras så att det inte hänger på enskilda personer Vem är du? Du har en akademisk utbildning inom teknik, industriell ekonomi, flygteknik, Ai eller annan akademisk utbildning eller erfarenhet som arbetsgivaren bedömer likvärdig. Du har tidigare lett komplexa projekt med internationell koppling, gärna med många olika aktörer och partner i flera länder. Du har lett konsortier eller samarbeten med flera organisationer där du behövt leda utan formellt chefsmandat. Du förstår AI och digitalisering tillräckligt väl för att föra trovärdiga samtal med företag om AI, data och cybersäkerhet. Du behöver inte vara tekniker, men du är beredd att sätta dig in i regelverk som AI Act och NIS2 och hur de påverkar företagen. Det är meriterande om du har erfarenhet av att leda EU-finansierade projekt, till exempel inom Digital Europe, Horizon Europe eller Interreg, och känner EU:s regler för ekonomi och rapportering, som Grant Agreement, Consortium Agreement och Funding & Tenders-portalen. Det är också meriterande om du känner flyg- och drönarbranschen eller innovationssystemet i Östergötland, eller har sålt in och levererat tjänster till små och medelstora företag. Som person är du strukturerad och noggrann med dokumentation. Du kommunicerar tydligt, även med företag som ställer höga krav på vad de får och när. items.desc: The Nuffield Department of Medicine is recruiting a Clinical Research Fellow in Gastroenterology to join a multidisciplinary team investigating the molecular basis of pathogenic autoantibodies in treatment-refractory inflammatory bowel disease and identifying potential new treatment targets. Based at the Centre for Human Genetics in Oxford, you will work under the supervision of Professor Holm Uhlig and Professor Simon Travis, with close collaboration across clinical, laboratory and computational research teams. In this role, you will help deliver interventional gastroenterology studies including identifying and recruiting patients, providing clinical care in accordance with trial protocols, and collecting and processing blood and tissue samples for downstream single-cell and bulk RNA analysis, transcriptomics and proteomics. You will work closely with wet-lab scientists, bioinformaticians, clinical colleagues and the industry partners to generate insights as the trial progresses. You will also contribute to data analysis, research papers, conference abstracts and grant applications, while supporting the accurate documentation and regulatory standards required for clinical research. It is essential that you hold a Bachelor’s degree in Medicine and be a UK GMC-registered medical practitioner with experience working full time as a doctor within the NHS. You will need excellent communication, interpersonal and organisational skills, together with the ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team. A methodical approach to data collection, an understanding of data protection and relevant professional guidelines, and the ability to manage multiple projects are also essential. Experience in gastroenterology, clinical trials or research, MRCP or equivalent, and an understanding of research methodology would be advantageous. The post also offers significant scope for research and professional development. You will be encouraged to develop an area of your own interest and may have the opportunity to work towards a higher degree, such as a DPhil or MSc, with potential funding available through the industry collaboration. Training and research opportunities within the Clinical Trials Unit and wider translational research programme will further support your development during the three-year appointment. Applications for this vacancy should be made online and you will need to upload a supporting statement and CV. Your supporting statement must explain how you meet each of the selection criteria for the post using examples of your skills and experience. Please restrict your documentation to your CV and supporting statement only. Any other documents will be requested at a later date. This position is offered full time on a fixed term contract for 3 years and is funded by Johnson and Johnson. Only applications received before 12 midday on 12 November 2026 will be considered. Please quote 188948 on all correspondence.

items.desc: The Role The Rosalind Franklin Institute (the Franklin) is a technology institute established by the UK Government as a unique centre committed to advancing tools that are needed to transform healthcare in the future. The Institute brings together researchers in life and physical sciences, and engineering, to develop a spectrum of tools which we will use to image, interpret and intervene in biological systems. These insights will speed up the discovery of new medicines, help find new diagnostics and contribute to a deeper understanding of human health and disease. Our Science Strategy seeks to focus the Franklin’s research and unite our researchers around our Technology Innovation Challenges and Life Science Challenges. For more information on the Franklin’s Challenges click here. Every 16 seconds a family suffers from a stillbirth, and the rate of unexplained stillbirth is trending upward. Stillbirth often occurs because of an issue with the amount of oxygen that the developing fetus receives. However, the combination of drivers in each case is unique, and current technologies for predicting stillbirth do not take into account the interactions between the mother, fetus, and placenta when determining risk. As such, prediction of stillbirth falls short. Our team has developed a new way to integrate clinical data to predict how much oxygen is available to a fetus in pregnancy; this tool is called SADIE. Early testing shows the capabilities of SADIE are promising. This research fits within wider product development/design workflows by seeking to understand the care pathways that SADIE will engage with in the NHS through stakeholder engagement and qualitative research approaches. We anticipate future commercialisation of this technology will enable a step-change in a clinician’s ability to take the right steps at the right time to both reduce the occurrence of stillbirth and the short and long term costs associated with preterm birth and neonatal intensive care. This project will be completed in collaboration with the University of Manchester and will entail spending time there. This working pattern is flexible (including part-time hours, minimum 18.75 per week) and will be discussed and agreed with the successful candidate. Key Responsibilities As a Research Associate at the Franklin, you will bring scientific knowledge and skills to deliver a specific research project and/or you will bring independent, creative science, or specific skills to a team delivering a project or program. Through this work, you will build scientific independence, develop new science and leadership skills, and establish a growing reputation externally. In this particular role, you will: Design and conduct interview with stakeholders across the NHS care pathway, including maternal fetal medicine clinicians, midwives, sonographers, digital health experts, information technology experts and patient group representatives. Identify and document current pain points associated across the maternity care pathway. Analyse interview data to Identify opportunities, capacity and staff motivations to embed SADIE in NHS workflows, and technological synergies/parallels that may help enable this. Based on stakeholder engagement, generate user requirement documentation to ensure SADIE is developed to meet the users/use-case. Work to complete these requirements will take place either in person at the Franklin, the University of Manchester or remotely via online meetings. Plan and conduct research, analyse and interpret results and supervise delivery of outputs (e.g. research report, patent application) in a scientific/technology area of interest. Work within a project team, contributing to wider projects around Franklin's key Challenges. Lead major contributions to outputs from research including papers, patents and both internal and external presentations. Support and develop others including day-to-day supervision of students or visitors in areas related to own research. Have supervised, staged progression to first stages of scientific independence with opportunities to further develop science and skills/experience. Enhance your research through collaboration with other researchers and make active contributions to exchanging of ideas through your own network. Be able to understand, interpret, create and communicate appropriately within a research context. Develop search and discovery skills and techniques. Be supervised by a Scientist/Senior Scientist in delivery of research outputs, either in the context of a project or Challenge or as an early career development fellow. Before submitting your application please ensure you read the Job Information Pack for full details of this role. This can be found at the bottom of the page. items.desc: We are seeking to appoint a Project Coordinator (UK Cancer Vaccine AI Scientist & Supercomputing) to join the Nuffield Department of Medicine, University of Oxford, working on an state of the art project funded by Advanced Research & Innovation Agency. Reporting to Dr Lennard Lee, Programme Director, you will serve as UK Cancer Vaccine AI Scientist & Supercomputing Project Coordinator, performing a Chief of Staff function for the programme. The UK Cancer Vaccine AI Scientist & Supercomputing Project is a government-supported national flagship research initiative hosted by the University of Oxford. The project integrates sovereign AI supercomputing, AI Scientists, automated laboratories, advanced immunology and near-patient manufacturing to accelerate the development of safer and better personalised cancer vaccines for NHS patients. The project establishes an end-to-end strategy to connect AI-led target discovery with autonomous experimental validation, vaccine manufacturing and NHS clinical trials. Experimental and clinical results feed back into the AI Scientist, creating a recursive self-improvement cycle of learning and discovery from computational prediction through to patient delivery. You will support the Programme Director and senior leadership team to facilitate project operations and keep this complex multidisciplinary project running smoothly. They will take ownership of defined programme processes and activities across team coordination, budgets, meetings, events, communications, external engagement and executive support, monitoring milestones and expenditure and ensuring actions are progressed. The post holder will also work closely with University, NHS, government, funder, industry and technology partners and support senior-level meetings, government and dignitary visits and project events. With excellent interpersonal and communication skills to build effective relationships with colleagues and stakeholders, alongside experience of project planning/managing project activities and excellent organisational skills, you will work closely with University, NHS, government, funder, industry and technology partners and support senior-level meetings, government and dignitary visits and programme events. They will provide high-quality support to the Programme Director and team, including delivering the strategy, project management, team diary and meeting coordination, briefing documents, minutes and correspondence, and use AI tools to improve administrative efficiency. They will also support recruitment, onboarding, team coordination and HR processes across the wider programme. It is essential that you are educated to degree level or have demonstrable equivalent experience in project coordination. You will have proven ability to take ownership for day-to-day delivery of project activities to enable progress on deliverables and completion of milestones and a detailed-oriented with analysis skill and problem-solving abilities. Demonstrable experience of project planning/managing project activities and excellent organisational skills, working in scaling up small to medium teams or similarly in a fast-moving organisation and experience in taking ownership of defined programme processes and activities across team coordination, budgets, meetings are essential aspects we look for. You will serve as the technical authority on turning raw camera and sensor recordings into accurate, physical 3D trajectories. Your work directly determines whether the motion data is accurate
items.desc: Founding Robotics Perception Engineer | YC-Backed Physical AI & Robotics Startup | London (Remote) | Full-Time | Up to £150K + Equity About the Company Our client is a Y Combinator-backed (S26) physical AI data company building the foundational human video and motion datasets for leading robotics and embodied-AI teams. Focused on egocentric first-person video and UMI demonstration data, the company turns real-world capture operations into high-precision, versioned data products that foundation-model and VLA teams rely on to train physical robots. Backed by a freshly closed seed round, their core constraint is supply, not demand. They are actively scaling deployment engineering, field operations, and capture hardware to keep up with massive customer demand. The founders are building a three-person founding engineering team to set the technical standards, tooling, and evaluation methodology behind the world's reference dataset for robot learning. About the Role Reporting to the Engineering Lead (with direct collaboration with the Founders), the Founding Robotics Perception Engineer owns hand tracking, motion reconstruction, and capture-device software integration. You will serve as the technical authority on turning raw camera and sensor recordings into accurate, physical 3D trajectories. Your work directly determines whether the motion data is accurate enough for its intended use and sets the company's technical standard for motion data. You will build production pipelines for 3D hand tracking and gripper trajectory estimation, integrate camera SDKs and spatial sensors, and establish the physical accuracy benchmarks and quality flags that give robotics teams total confidence in the data. Key Responsibilities Build, refine, and maintain production pipelines for 3D hand tracking from egocentric video and gripper trajectory reconstruction from UMI recordings. Integrate camera streams, IMUs, and device SDKs into the collection software, ensuring flawless handling of spatial calibration, coordinate frames, timestamps, and units. Develop diagnostic tools to detect occluded hands, lost tracks, motion drift, coordinate discrepancies, dropped frames, and timestamp misalignments, applying automated quality flags for data review. Compare motion estimates against physical reference standards, quantify error and coverage, and maintain automated regression tests to confirm that pipeline changes genuinely improve data accuracy. Test and benchmark newly purchased cameras and capture hardware on representative tasks, evaluating baseline signal quality and reliability prior to wider operational deployment. Skills & Competencies Deep spatial understanding of 3D camera geometry, camera-IMU calibration, coordinate transforms, temporal tracking, and multi-view reconstruction. Hands-on experience with 3D hand tracking, visual odometry, SLAM, or pose estimation using real-world camera and sensor recordings. Strong production programming capabilities in Python (along with C++ and GPU inference where required) backed by practical deep learning implementation skills. Exceptional ability to separate model errors from sensor faults, isolating physical discrepancies, dropped frames, and timestamp drift. Qualifications & Experience Background in hand tracking, motion capture, AR/VR, spatial computing, robotics, autonomous systems, or sensor fusion. Proven track record of taking perception or tracking systems beyond controlled lab conditions to real sensor recordings used by actual applications. Direct experience handling raw device SDKs, coordinate frame conventions, and physical accuracy validation against meaningful ground-truth references. Experience with egocentric video, camera-IMU setups, visual odometry, or multi-view reconstruction is highly valuable. Role Details Timing: Immediate Start Location: London (Remote). Package: Competitive base salary up to £150K + significant founding-engineer equity with total technical ownership over the perception domain.

items.desc: The University of Manchester is seeking to appoint a Research Associate to contribute to a short-term translational pilot project focused on the development and evaluation of a novel time-of-flight detector system for in-vivo range verification in proton beam therapy. Based within the Division of Cancer Sciences and working closely with collaborators at The Christie Hospital NHS Foundation Trust, the post offers an excellent opportunity to undertake experimental work in the proton research facility, analyse data to support validation of the technology and contribute to project delivery, dissemination of findings and outputs arising from the pilot study. You should hold, or be close to completing, a PhD in physics, medical physics, engineering or a closely related discipline, with relevant experimental research experience in detectors, instrumentation or radiation physics. You should also be able to demonstrate strong analytical and data handling skills, experience of independent experimental work and the ability to contribute effectively within a multidisciplinary research team. Experience in proton therapy, fast timing techniques, Monte-Carlo methods or clinical research environments would be advantageous. This fixed-term post offers access to specialist proton therapy research infrastructure and close links to one of the UK’s leading cancer centres. The University of Manchester is committed to equality, diversity and inclusion, and welcomes applications from all sections of the community. You will be responsible for: Design, construct and optimise a prototype time-of-flight based range probe integrating ultra-fast silicon detectors and timing electronics. Plan and undertake experimental measurements in the proton therapy research facility to characterise detector performance, timing resolution and calibration against proton range. Carry out validation studies using appropriate phantom models and compare findings with established clinical systems and detectors. Analyse and interpret experimental data to assess system precision, uncertainty and performance against project objectives. Work collaboratively with academic, clinical and technical colleagues across the University of Manchester and The Christie NHS Foundation Trust to support delivery of the project. We welcome candidates who bring diverse perspectives, experiences, and approaches to their work. About You We encourage applications from individuals with a wide range of backgrounds and experiences. You should demonstrate: Essential Criteria PhD (or near completion) in physics, medical physics, engineering or a closely related discipline. Experience in experimental research involving detectors, instrumentation or radiation physics. Experience of designing and conducting experiments independently. Experience of analysing complex data sets and interpreting results. Ability to work independently and collaboratively across disciplines. Desirable Criteria Experience of working with time-of-flight measurement techniques or fast timing electronics. Experience of working with Monte-Carlo simulation tools. Experience of in-vivo range verification research or related translational detector development. We value transferable skills and real-world experience as much as formal qualifications. Our benefits include: Generous employer contribution pension 29 days annual leave plus bank holidays, along with Christmas closure Ride to work and EV car scheme available For more information, please see University of Manchester Benefits. You can also find information on our Flexible and Hybrid working here. We are an open place of enquiry and challenge. We embrace and celebrate difference, diversity and debate, and we pride ourselves on being a place of education, learning and community where we are able, within the law, to question and test received wisdom, express new ideas and explore controversial or unpopular topics and opinions. Find out more from our Freedom of Speech Policy. items.desc: As a public expert in weather and climate, Météo-France is here to help keep you safe every day and assist you in making the best decisions in a changing climate. With dangerous weather events becoming even more intense and frequent due to climate change, our mission to keep you safe is crucial. We mobilize our expertise and scientific and technological excellence to enable you to anticipate and adapt to challenging weather and climate events. Find us online:https://meteofrance.com/carte-didentite-de-meteo-france The Directorate of Higher Education and Research (DESR) brings together the research entities of Météo-France (mainly CNRM, SAFIRE and LACy), the National School of Meteorology and the shared administrative and IT support services. The CNRM is a Joint Research Unit (UMR 3589, https://cnrm.sedoo.fr/) under the joint supervision of Météo-France and CNRS. The CNRM conducts research in the field of meteorology and climate, from the observation, understanding and modelling of processes to the development of weather forecasting and climate projection systems that can be transferred to Météo-France's operational services. The person recruited will join the MOSCA (Modélisation du Système Climat régionaAl, https://cnrm.sedoo.fr/mosca-modelisation-du-systeme-climatique-regional/) team of the CNRM's Groupe de Modélisation Grande Echelle et Climat (GMGEC), whose aim is to improve knowledge of regional climates using a dedicated modelling approach. Why join us? Embark on a stimulating adventure that serves everyone, alongside men and women who are committed every day to tackling the challenges posed to our society by weather and climate. And enjoy the following benefits: flexible working hours, RTT (reduced working time), teleworking, staff restaurant or meal vouchers, 75% contribution to public transport costs, contribution to mutual insurance, sports and cultural associations depending on the site concerned (climbing, gym, pottery, theater, etc.). Other benefits await you, come and discover them! Context: The position offered is part of the FUTURA European project (Future of Climate Change Scenarios of the Earth System, Impacts and Socio-Economic Outcomes for Assessment and Society). Mission: Within the first phase of the FUTURA project, the selected candidate will be responsible for contributing to the publication of CNRM CORDEX data on the ESGF-NG nodes. This work will be carried out in collaboration with other engineers in the research group and under the supervision of CNRM CORDEX manager, Samuel Somot. Activities: The duties of this position will consist of: 1. Checking that the data comply with CORDEX standards (CMOR, etc.) using a dedicated tool and correcting the data where necessary; 2. Uploading the data to the dedicated CNRM servers; 3. Taking the necessary steps to publish the data on the ESGF-NG nodes (indexing, etc.); 4. Organising and backing up CORDEX data at CNRM; 5. Documenting the data and providing support to users of these data; 6. Contributing to the team's work on the management, organisation and processing of climate model data, beyond CORDEX data intended for ESGF. For any further information, please contact Samuel SOMOT (samuel.somot@meteo.fr) General requirements The selected candidate must hold an engineering degree at Master's level (BAC+5), an MSc or a PhD in atmospheric, oceanic or climate sciences, or in data science, obtained before the start date of the contract. Experience in numerical modelling, specifically in climate studies, climate data science or regional climate modelling, would be appreciated but is not mandatory. Experience in data CMORisation or publication on ESGF would be appreciated but is not mandatory. Experience in handling large volumes of data would be appreciated but is not mandatory. Technical skills Good knowledge of the NetCDF format; Familiarity with tools for handling NetCDF files (NCO, CDO, etc.); Proficiency in the Unix environment and Bash scripting; Knowledge of a scientific analysis tool (e.g. Python, NCL, R). Professional skills Autonomy in day-to-day work; Good organisational skills; Spoken and written English at a minimum B2 level. Personal skills Good interpersonal and teamwork skills; Availability and adaptability.

We also operate some infrastructure and services in the cloud, primarily on AWS and Azure. You will work closely with our software engineers and system administrators. Together with our current DevOps Engineer, you will share responsibility for internal tools and services, the CI/CD system, and the infrastructure they run on, both on-premises and in the cloud. This is joint ownership, not a ticket queue. You design, question, and decide together, and you are expected to drive topics end to end. Nice to have Experience building C++ applications using CMake, Bazel, and/or Conan Experience with package and environment managers such as uv, pip and npm Experience with virtualization platforms, ideally Proxmox Experience with managing GPU-Cluster, for example using Slurm Experience with monitoring tools such as Zabbix, OpenTelemetry, Prometheus/Grafana Experience administering Mac systems Why us? items.desc: The AI Teams at Agile Robots are looking for a Robotics Data Engineer (m/f/d) Data Generation & Curation , who will build the pipeline that records, curates, and prepares multimodal robot datasets for foundation-model training. The pipeline has to run across different robot setups and combine real recordings with synthetic data from simulation. Responsibilities Multimodal Capture: Build ROS 2 based capture for RGB and RGB-D cameras, wrist cameras, joint encoders, force-torque sensors, and teleoperation signals. Synchronization: Keep multimodal streams time-aligned through sensor synchronization, calibration, and timestamp integrity checks. Dataset Health: Define and run health checks that detect dropped frames, sync drift, corrupt frames, and missing modalities. Dataset Curation: Filter and deduplicate recorded data, maintain dataset metadata, and define train and evaluation splits. Synthetic Data Integration: Integrate synthetic data generated in simulation into the same datasets and formats as real recordings. Preprocessing: Build preprocessing that aligns, slices, and inspects recorded episodes into a form that foundation-model training can use directly. Formats & Release: Design dataset schemas and storage formats, version datasets so experiments can be reproduced, and package them for external release where approved. Essential Skills Engineering Background: Degree in Computer Science, Robotics, Electrical Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent qualification plus professional experience building comparable data or robotics software systems. ROS 2 Pipelines: Hands-on experience building sensor recording or data pipelines in ROS 2 with Python. Sensor Synchronization: Experience synchronizing multiple cameras and sensors, including calibration and handling timestamp drift. Dataset Schemas: Experience designing schemas and storage layouts for multimodal time-series data, in formats such as Parquet, Zarr, or HDF5. Camera Pipelines: Working knowledge of camera pipelines and video encoding, and how they affect data size and frame integrity. Beneficial Skills Dataset Curation: Experience building curation steps for machine learning datasets, such as filtering, deduplication, and split design. Synthetic Data: Familiarity with combining simulated and real data in one training dataset. C++ Development: Experience writing C++ for performance-critical capture or driver code. Robot Learning Datasets: Familiarity with dataset conventions used in robot learning, such as LeRobot. Teleoperation Data: Experience recording teleoperation data for imitation learning. As a Research Data Scientist, you will bring a rigorous scientific approach to the continuous development and improvement of the services associated with our technology platform. You will work both independently and collaboratively with other researchers, software engineers, and customer-facing biological and operational teams to transform real-world operational data into robust
items.desc: Stingray Marine Solutions AS Stålfjæra 26, 0975 Oslo, Norge, 0975 Oslo Om jobben Lagre favoritt Stillingstittel Research Data Scientist Type ansettelse Fast, heltid 100% Antall stillinger 1 Arbeidsspråk Engelsk eller norsk Søk senest søndag 1. november Did you know that Stingray delivers world-leading Norwegian high-tech? We develop intelligent aquaculture technology for the removal of salmon lice 24/7 using machine vision and laser, as well as monitoring lice levels, measuring fish welfare and growth. Collectively, this is known as The Fish Health Hub ™. Our technology contributes to increased food production on nature's terms, without compromising the environment and animal welfare. With our services, we are proud to help shape the future of aquaculture - Made in Norway. Apply science and data to real-world aquaculture challenges We are now looking for a Research Data Scientist to strengthen our Research team and help turn complex biological and operational information into scientific insight and practical applications. As part of Stingray Aqua, the Research team acts as a bridge between technology and data specialists and customer-facing teams. Aqua Research builds and shares knowledge across Stingray and the wider aquaculture sector. It also supports the development and validation of data-driven solutions that strengthen our day-to-day services and operations, ultimately supporting better fish welfare and customer success in Norway, Iceland, and the Faroe Islands. Key Responsibilities - What will you do? As a Research Data Scientist, you will bring a rigorous scientific approach to the continuous development and improvement of the services associated with our technology platform. You will work both independently and collaboratively with other researchers, software engineers, and customer-facing biological and operational teams to transform real-world operational data into robust analytical workflows and functional capabilities that others can rely on. You will combine rigorous data analysis with iterative technical development, while keeping focus on the biological complexities associated with fish behavior and the constraints of ongoing farming operations. Your work will contribute directly to creating tools and capabilities used by our customers and employees. Your tasks and responsibilities in this role will include: Driving the iterative development of functional capabilities by developing concepts and analytical workflows to test and refine methods and assumptions, ensuring that solutions remain grounded in data and biological understanding. Designing and evaluating validation studies based on data from commercial aquaculture operations, applying appropriate experimental and statistical methods to account for biological variability and operational constraints. Analyzing extensive biological and operational datasets and developing statistical models to identify and evaluate meaningful patterns, relationships, and opportunities for improvement. Defining data requirements and independently retrieving, combining, and quality-assuring large and heterogenous data sets to build reproducible analytical workflows and reusable data pipelines, ensuring traceability and appropriate documentation throughout the process. Interpreting and communicating findings to internal and external audiences, translating complex results into practical insights that support fact-based decision-making and further development. Who we are looking for We are looking for someone with a strong quantitative and computational background who can take ownership of technically complex research problems in the context of day-to-day operations with a focus on fish welfare and behavior. You combine scientific judgement with technical discipline and are comfortable moving between exploratory research questions and the development of hands-on solutions. Most importantly, we are looking for someone who enjoys working across disciplines. You can discuss biological hypotheses with scientists, independently investigate the underlying data, and work with software engineers and customer contacts to determine how a promising research method can become a reliable functional capability. As an ideal candidate, you have: A PhD in aquaculture, biology, environmental science, or another relevant life or quantitative natural science, and preferably 3-5 years of additional relevant research and/or applied analytical experience. A solid understanding of applied research methodology, experimental design, statistical modeling and result validation. The ability to analyze complex longitudinal, time-series, or other observational datasets obtained under real-world operational conditions. Experience with behavioral or sensor data derived from computer vision, sonar, or other monitoring systems is an advantage. Strong programming, data analysis, and statistical modelling skills using tools such as R and/or Python. Experience with Power BI is an advantage. …

items.desc: About IntelliDigest IntelliDigest is a purpose-driven company working with stakeholders across the food system, from farm to fork, supporting the transition towards more sustainable and circular approaches to food production. Through technology innovation, applied research, and capacity building, we enable improved resource efficiency, soil health, and sustainable food systems. Our iDigest technology converts organic waste streams into valuable bio-nutrient outputs intended for use as soil improvers, growing media components, and fertilising products, supporting regenerative and low-input agriculture. Role Overview We are seeking a knowledgeable and motivated Plant Scientist to oversee and optimise the use of IntelliDigest bio-nutrient outputs within agricultural and controlled growing environments. The role will focus on the safe, compliant, and effective application of digestate-derived products as soil improvers, growing media constituents, and nutrient sources for food crops. The successful candidate will lead plant growth trials, evaluate agronomic performance, and generate robust scientific evidence to support product validation, farmer adoption, and regulatory compliance. Working closely with research, engineering, and operational teams, you will help translate nutrient recovery innovation into practical, scalable solutions aligned with UK agricultural and environmental standards. This role is well suited to a plant or soil scientist with a strong interest in sustainable agriculture, circular bioeconomy systems, and applied, field-relevant research. Key Responsibilities Plant Growth Trials and Agronomic Research Design, implement, and manage plant growth trials assessing iDigest bio-nutrient products as soil improvers, growing media inputs, or fertilising materials. Evaluate crop performance metrics including establishment, growth rate, nutrient uptake, yield, and produce quality. Compare bio-nutrient performance against conventional fertilisers, soil conditioners, or substrates in line with recognised agronomic methodologies. Monitor and assess soil and growing media parameters, including nutrient availability, organic matter content, pH, structure, and biological activity. Collect, analyse, and interpret agronomic, soil, and plant physiological data to inform product optimisation and application guidance. Prepare clear, evidence-based technical reports and data summaries for internal use and external stakeholders. Regulatory Alignment and Farm Integration Oversee the practical deployment of bio-nutrient products on IntelliDigest-associated farm and pilot sites. Ensure applications align with UK regulatory frameworks, including relevant requirements under PAS 110, end-of-waste criteria, and good agricultural practice. Support compliance with the Farming Rules for Water, nutrient management planning, and environmental protection standards. Develop and refine application protocols, including rates, timings, and crop-specific guidance, consistent with soil nutrient requirements and environmental safeguards. Work with farm operators to ensure correct handling, storage, and application of digestate-derived materials. Contribute to the development of documentation supporting product classification as a soil improver or fertilising product where applicable. Collaboration and Project Support Work closely with R&D scientists, engineers, and operations teams to align plant performance outcomes with process development and nutrient recovery technologies. Support cross-functional projects involving enzymatic biocatalysis, nutrient management, and sustainable food production systems. Participate in project meetings, providing scientific insight, progress updates, and evidence-based recommendations. Liaise with external partners including farmers, agronomists, research institutions, and regulatory bodies as required. Continuous Improvement and Knowledge Development Maintain awareness of developments in plant science, soil health, digestate utilisation, and sustainable nutrient management. Identify opportunities to improve trial design, data quality, and on-farm implementation practices. Contribute scientific input to grant applications, regulatory submissions, technical guidance, and impact reporting. Engage in continued professional development to strengthen expertise in applied plant and soil science. Essential Requirements Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Plant Science, Agronomy, Soil Science, Horticulture, Environmental Science, or a related discipline. Demonstrable experience designing and conducting plant or agronomic trials in agricultural, horticultural, or controlled-environment settings. Strong understanding of plant nutrition, soil fertility, and soil improver or fertiliser performance. Experience handling, analysing, and interpreting agronomic and soil data. Excellent organisational and record-keeping skills, with attention to regulatory and quality requirements. Effective written and verbal …

items.desc: About Us Teton is redefining the role of healthcare workers through cutting-edge AI technology and a great product experience. As populations get older and staff shortages grow, healthcare systems are under pressure. Our mission is to decrease the cost of healthcare while improving the quality of care. Our product enables care teams to intervene, prevent and operate more efficiently. Our ambient sensors in resident rooms capture activity, sleep, respiration, gait and more. These signals are used both to react fast to risk events, like falls, and for long-term health analysis that care teams can act on. Teton is scaling fast, operating in the Nordics, UK, DACH and US. We raised a $20M Series A. Expect travel to the US to meet users and team members. We focus relentlessly on product excellence and user experience, deploying solutions at speed that make a tangible difference for carers. We are an aspiring meritocracy biased towards action, always striving to raise the bar. If you are driven by impact, speed and leveling up, this might be the place for you. If you are looking for a 9-17 job, perform best with structure and struggle dealing with unknowns, this is not for you. We believe close collaboration between a hard-working, high-agency team enables the fastest and most efficient iteration cycles, helping us build an impactful product that healthcare professionals truly love to use. The Job We're looking for a talented and driven Product Engineer to own customer-facing features from the first conversation with a care team to the feature running in production. Care workers rely on our product during every shift and care managers use it to follow up on their residents, on mobile and on the web. This isn't a ticket-taking role. You'll talk to users, cut scope, build across the whole stack, and check afterwards whether what you shipped actually made a shift easier. Your goal is to shrink the time from a customer request to a deployed solution, without cutting corners on reliability or on the privacy of residents' health data. In this role, you will focus on: Feature Development: Own features end-to-end, from design discussions through implementation to production rollout across multiple markets and languages, on the web app, the mobile app and the APIs behind them. Customer Insight: Talk to care staff and our customer success team every week, visit care facilities, and turn what you hear into clearly scoped product changes. Come with ideas, sketch the solution, and push it forward. Fast Iteration: Break large designs and features into small shippable pieces. Get MVPs in front of users quickly, measure how they're used, and iterate or kill them. Backend & APIs: Design and build the APIs, data models and services your features need. You will not just consume APIs, you will help shape, improve and fix the systems behind them. Quality, Privacy & Safety: Ship with care for health data: sensible access control, auditability and privacy by default. Build test coverage and use staged rollouts so new features never get in the way of the alerts care teams depend on. Qualifications Strong TypeScript skills: this is the language for everything we build. Solid production experience with React on the web and/or React Native. Comfortable working across the stack: you've built backend APIs and worked with relational databases (e.g. Postgres), not just UI. Great product taste and a keen eye for UX. You work well with designers and can make sensible design decisions yourself when needed. Comfortable talking directly with non-technical users and turning messy feedback into concrete decisions. Previous startup experience and/or shipping a product where you owned the outcome, from idea to adoption. Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work both independently and in a team. Nice to Have Experience with React Native and Expo in production. AWS or equivalent cloud platform experience. Familiarity with TanStack, real-time systems or push notifications. Experience with health data or other regulated, privacy-sensitive domains (e.g. GDPR). Experience shipping products across multiple markets and languages. What We Offer Participation in our warrant program (stock options). A small team where your decisions directly shape the product. Work on software that healthcare workers depend on every day, the impact is tangible and immediate. Join Our Team We're looking for individuals who share our vision and value ownership and entrepreneurship over a conventional job. At Teton, you'll have the chance to make a real impact with your work. If you're ready for more than just a job, come aboard and be part of our mission to transform healthcare.

items.desc: About Us At Teton, we are redefining the role of healthcare workers through cutting-edge AI technology. Facing a global nursing shortage, our solutions offer vital support to overburdened health systems. With thousands of patient rooms across 4 countries already benefiting from our technology, we are aiming to expand to much more. We distinguish ourselves by focusing relentlessly on product excellence and user experience, rapidly deploying solutions that make a real difference. The Job Every patient room we deploy into puts another device on infrastructure we don't control, in a building we can't easily visit, running software that has to keep working. We're looking for an Engineer to own that problem: the systems, tooling, and infrastructure that let us ship to thousands of edge devices confidently and understand what they're doing once they're out there. In this role, you will focus on the following areas of interest: Fleet Management: Build and run the systems that provision, monitor, and manage our devices in the field, from first boot in a hospital room to end of life. OTA & Release Engineering: Own how software gets onto devices: staged rollouts, health checks, automatic rollback, and the confidence that a bad release won't take down a ward. Observability: Design the telemetry, logging, and alerting that tell us a device is degrading before a nurse notices. Make remote debugging possible so we don't fly to fix things. Device Bring-Up & Debugging: Work with our hardware and firmware teams on new hardware revisions, reproduce field issues on the bench, and get to the bottom of problems that span kernel, driver, network, and application. Infrastructure & Tooling: Build the CI/CD, image builds, and internal tools that let the whole engineering team ship to hardware quickly and safely. Documentation: Maintain clear and detailed documentation of your work to ensure easy collaboration and knowledge sharing within the team. Qualifications: Solid experience running Linux systems in production: ideally embedded or edge Linux, not just cloud VMs. Proficiency in Rust and/or Javascript/Typescript and/or Python Experience with device fleets at scale: provisioning, OTA update mechanisms (Mender, RAUC, balena, or something you built yourself), and remote access to constrained devices. Familiarity with Linux internals: systemd, kernel modules, device tree, networking stack, containers. Experience with observability tooling (Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, or similar) and designing what to measure, not just wiring up dashboards. Comfortable with hardware debugging: serial consoles, working alongside hardware engineers Understanding of communication protocols and how devices talk to each other and to us: I2C, SPI, UART, Bluetooth, Wi-Fi, MQTT. Pragmatism about networks you don't control: restrictive hospital IT, VLANs, proxies, flaky Wi-Fi, and long offline periods. Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to work independently as well as part of a team. Experience with the NVIDIA Jetson platform and Linux for Tegra is a big plus. Experience with Yocto, Debian packaging, or custom image builds is a plus. Experience in the medical device or healthcare technology field is a plus. A role where you can make a significant impact on healthcare delivery. At Teton, you'll have the chance to make a real impact with your work. If you're ready for more than just a job, come aboard and be part of our mission to transform healthcare.

items.desc: Member of Technical Staff - Pre Seed Start Up Up to £250k + Equity On Site in London Frontier models are great at answering questions. They’re much worse at behaving like real people, systems or environments over time. This team is fixing that. What you’ll do Build post-training pipelines (SFT, preference tuning, RL) that make models behave more realistically in simulation Design reward signals and environments for RL, and figure out what “realistic” actually means in measurable terms Build evals that prove a trained model beats the frontier baseline on the tasks that matter Run experiments fast, read the results honestly and ship what works into production Help set the research and engineering direction as the team grows What they’re looking for Hands-on post-training experience on real models (GRPO, PPO, DPO, LoRA or similar) Someone who’s built RL environments, reward models or evals, not just run training scripts Strong engineering fundamentals: you can scale training and keep it reproducible Comfort with ambiguity and a habit of turning open research questions into shipped results Why it’s worth a look RL for simulation is a genuinely open problem, so your work moves the frontier, not just the product Real ownership of the model layer at an early stage A small, technical team where research goes straight into production
