items.desc: L’entreprise Renault Group Renault Group est un acteur mondial de l’automobile présent dans plus de 130 pays, porté par des marques emblématiques telles que Renault, Dacia, Alpine et Mobilize. Le Groupe est engagé dans une transformation ambitieuse vers une mobilité décarbonée grâce au développement de véhicules électriques, de solutions énergétiques innovantes et de services de mobilité connectée. Qui sommes nous ? L'équipe Système - Stockage d'Énergie de Renault Group développe les fonctionnalités batterie équipant plusieurs millions de véhicules dans le monde. Nous concevons les technologies de stockage qui équipent notamment les Renault 5 E-Tech, Scénic E-Tech et Twingo E-Tech. Aujourd'hui, nous préparons la prochaine génération de plateformes électriques du Groupe à travers des innovations de rupture sur les systèmes de stockage d'énergie. Rejoindre l'équipe, c'est contribuer directement à la définition de technologies qui équiperont les futurs véhicules électriques Renault. Votre Mission Au sein d'une équipe système en charge d'une innovation stratégique pour les futures plateformes électriques du Groupe, vous contribuerez au développement d'un nouveau système de stockage d'énergie à forte valeur ajoutée. Vous évoluerez à l'interface des équipes système, logiciel, simulation et essais véhicule, avec une forte autonomie et une vision globale de la fonction. items.desc: Willkommen bei der Allianz Die strategische Nutzung von Daten und KI beschleunigt sich weiter und birgt gerade in der Finanzdienstleistungsindustrie enorme Potenziale. Immer mehr KI-Fähigkeiten werden dabei konkret als eigenständige, interagierende Agenten umgesetzt, die über offene Standardprotokolle miteinander und mit Fachsystemen kommunizieren. Die technologische Entwicklung – insbesondere von Protokollen wie MCP (Model Context Protocol) und A2A (Agent2Agent) – führt dazu, dass Unternehmen ihre Agenten-Architekturen ständig weiterentwickeln und professionalisieren müssen. Zum nächstmöglichen Zeitpunkt suchen wir einen KI-Architekt (m/w/d), der KI-Agenten mit starkem Blick auf die Geschäftsprozesse der Allianz Kunde und Markt GmbH konzipiert, baut und den produktionsreifen Betrieb von Anfang an mitdenkt. Diese Rolle ist explizit Business-orientiert - technische Kenntnisse sind Erfolgsvoraussetzung für ein wirkungsvolles Ausfüllen dieser Position. Das erwartet Dich bei uns als KI-Architekt (m/w/d) Du entwirfst und implementierst KI-Agenten und Multi-Agenten-Systeme auf Basis gängiger Standardprotokolle (insbesondere MCP und A2A) und stellst deren Interoperabilität mit internen und externen Systemen sicher. Du konzipierst mehrschichtige Agenten-Architekturen (z. B. Orchestrierungs-, Tool- und Serverebenen), inklusive Tool- und Resource-Design, Authentifizierung / Autorisierung (u. a. OAuth 2.1) und Anbindung an LLM-Provider (z. B. AWS Bedrock, Anthropic Claude, OpenAI). Du arbeitest eng mit Business Ownern und Experten (m/w/d) der Allianz in Deutschland zusammen, um Anforderungen in konkrete, produktionsreife Agenten-Lösungen zu übersetzen. Du gestaltest Datenarchitekturen im Einklang mit der übergreifenden Datenarchitektur der Allianz in Deutschland und berätst zum Einsatz von agentenbasierten und generativen KI-Lösungen in den Feldern Kundenschnittstelle, Prozessautomation und Versicherungstechnik. Du stellst Betriebsreife sicher: Observability (z. B. OpenTelemetry), Skalierbarkeit und sicheren Cloud-Betrieb (AWS, containerisiert, Infrastructure-as-Code mit Terraform). Du identifizierst bereichsübergreifend Abhängigkeiten und Synergien für KI-Agenten-Lösungen und arbeitest eng mit dem Chief Data Officer (m/w/d), Enterprise- bzw. Facharchitekten (m/w/d) und den verschiedenen AI Governance Funktionen zusammen. Das bringst Du mit als KI-Architekt (m/w/d) Du hast ein abgeschlossenes Studium der Data Science, (Wirtschafts-)Informatik, Mathematik, Wirtschaftswissenschaften oder eine vergleichbare Qualifikation durch Berufserfahrung. Du bringst nachweisbare praktische Erfahrung im Bau von KI-Agenten auf Basis gängiger Standardprotokolle mit, insbesondere MCP und A2A, sowie ein gutes Verständnis von Tool-/Resource-Design und Agent-Orchestrierung. Du verfügst über sehr gute Kenntnisse in mehreren Programmiersprachen (insb. Python und TypeScript) und deren Einsatz in produktiven KI- und Agenten-Umgebungen sowie fundierte Kenntnisse in Data-Warehouse- und Analytics-Architekturen (u. a. SQL, Snowflake, Databricks). Du hast fundierte Praxis im Umgang mit Cloud-Plattformen und -Services, insbesondere AWS (z. B. ECS, Bedrock, Glue), sowie mit modernen Data- & AI-Plattformen wie Snowflake und Databricks. Ebenfalls verfügst du über Erfahrung im Design, Aufbau und sicheren Betrieb containerisierter, cloud-basierter Agenten- und Data-&-Analytics-Architekturen (inkl. Auth-Lösungen wie Keycloak / OAuth 2.1). Du denkst visionär und in architekturellen Zielbildern. Dabei behältst Du unsere Business-Prozesse immer stark im Blick. Deine langjährige Erfahrung in agiler Softwareentwicklung sowie im Design und Aufbau moderner CI/CD-Pipelines lässt Dich Zielbilder schnell in die Praxis umsetzen. Du bist ein starker Kommunikator, der Menschen mit unterschiedlichem technischen Wissen von Ideen überzeugen kann. Dabei arbeitest Du transparent, kollaborativ und mit hohem Fokus auf nachhaltig tragfähige Lösungen. Du verfügst über verhandlungssichere Deutschkenntnisse und kommunizierst ebenso souverän auf Englisch. items.desc: Data Scientist – Econometrics / Statistics (Amsterdam) You could work as a quantitative analyst at an investment bank. Or you could help model one of Europe’s largest real-world consumer markets. At JP.cars we analyze the dynamics of the European automotive market using one of the most comprehensive vehicle datasets in existence. Every day millions of vehicle listings across Europe generate a continuously evolving system of supply, demand and pricing signals. If you enjoy digging deep into data, uncovering patterns others miss and pushing through datasets until things truly make sense, read further. About JP.cars JP.cars is a fast-growing automotive data company operating across almost all European markets. In 2027 we will further expand internationally with our entry into the United States. At the core of our business are very large automotive datasets containing billions of vehicle records across multiple countries. These datasets provide a unique statistical view on how vehicle markets behave, enabling analysis of pricing dynamics, supply patterns and market inefficiencies at a scale rarely available in this industry. To unlock the full value of this data, we are looking for someone with a strong statistical and quantitative background who enjoys working deeply with large datasets and complex market behavior. What you will do You will build models and work with large-scale automotive data to translate complex datasets into insights and models that support hundreds of customers (automotive dealerships, b2b trading companies, leasing companies, banks, insurance companies and auditors), who rely heavily on our accurate vehicle data to run their daily operations. Your work may include: Building statistical models to better understand vehicle pricing and market dynamics Identifying patterns in supply, demand and pricing behavior Investigating anomalies and trends in large datasets Analyzing datasets with billions of vehicle records Turning complex quantitative analysis into clear insights A large part of this role is deep data exploration and statistical investigation: asking the right questions and pushing through the data until the numbers actually make sense. Your analyses and models directly influence vehicle valuations used daily by hundreds of automotive companies across Europe. Examples of questions we explore How do vehicle prices evolve across different European markets? Can statistical models detect anomalies or inefficiencies in vehicle pricing? How can we forecast vehicle residual values using large-scale market data? How can price elasticities in the automotive market be quantified? What we are looking for We are looking for someone who really enjoys working with numbers and data. Strong candidates typically have: A PhD or MSc in Mathematics, Econometrics, Statistics, Physics, or another quantitative field Strong knowledge of statistics and quantitative modeling Experience working with large datasets Programming experience with Python, SQL and more Most importantly, we are looking for someone who: Has a strong drive to understand data in detail Enjoys digging deep into datasets Keeps investigating when something does not make sense Does not stop until the numbers and patterns are fully understood We value people who enjoy exploring data, questioning assumptions, and developing a deep understanding of how underlying systems and markets behave. At the same time, you enjoy working closely with others and contributing to a team that builds something meaningful together. What we offer Access to one of the largest automotive datasets in Europe with billions of records Real-world problems involving pricing and market dynamics A role where your analysis directly influences real decisions in the automotive market A rapidly growing international company An ambitious and energetic team that pushes each other to reach the highest level. We collaborate closely, share knowledge, and work together to build something exceptional. Location This role is based in Amsterdam. We believe working closely together is important, so you are also expected to be present at our Amsterdam office. Interested? Apply via LinkedIn. Questions? Contact pieter@jp.cars

items.desc: Accelerated Knowledge Transfer (AKT) Associate in Reinforcement Learning The University of Bath is seeking an ambitious and highly motivated graduate to join an exciting Accelerated Knowledge Transfer (AKT) project in partnership with Synoptix Ltd. About The Role Pan--Tilt--Zoom (PTZ) cameras capture detailed imagery of selected contacts, but this reduces awareness of the wider environment. This innovative project will assess the feasibility of a reinforcement learning system that decides where the camera should point and when to zoom. It will balance searching for new contacts, tracking known contacts and maintaining situational awareness under uncertainty. The capability will extend Synoptix's Synx-Lookout product beyond detection and tracking by adding autonomous attention allocation, contact prioritisation and camera control while continuing to run on edge compute. Development will use Synoptix's synthetic environment capability, followed by testing with PTZ cameras and edge hardware. Whilst working on this unique project as an AKT Associate, applying your academic skills to an industrially focused project, you will broaden your knowledge and expertise, and be supported by both industrial and academic supervisors. The project will be supervised by Professor Özgür Simsek (Professor of Artificial Intelligence, Director of Bath's Reinforcement Learning Laboratory, Director of Bath’s Centre for Artificial Intelligence) and by George Leete (Senior AI Engineer at Synoptix Limited). Synoptix Ltd Synoptix is an award-winning engineering consultancy delivering advanced solutions across defence, aerospace, healthcare, energy and cyber security sectors. The company develops innovative AI-powered products including Synx-Lookout, an edge-computing maritime awareness platform that uses computer vision and autonomy technologies. We Welcome Applications From Candidates Who Have A BSc, MComp, MSc, or PhD degree in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Data Science or a closely related discipline Practical experience with modern reinforcement learning algorithms using function approximation. Ability to manage workload independently and effectively. Strong written and verbal communication skills. Technical report writing experience. Intellectual curiosity and enthusiasm for research-driven innovation. Resilience and problem-solving mindset. The Associate will investigate how reinforcement learning can be used to control PTZ cameras operating in complex maritime environments The Post Will Offer The Following Benefits Valuable experience and highly transferable skills. Mentoring from the company and academic team. Access to University resources to complete the project. Experience working directly with a technology-focused industrial partner. This AKT project is funded by UKRI through Innovate UK. This programme has been designed to create short-term collaborations between a university and business to deliver a rapid and targeted intervention to accelerate the development of an innovation project, with potential for significant impact on the business. AKT projects are delivered by graduates who benefit from the opportunity to work on a strategically relevant project within industry, whilst receiving support and guidance from university academics. More information about the Accelerated Knowledge Transfer programme can be found at: https://www.ktp-uk.org/accelerated-knowledge-transfer/ Further information This is a fixed-term role for a period of 3 months, to start no later than 13 November 2026. In addition to your application, please submit an up-to-date full CV, academic transcripts, at least one writing sample, and at last one presentation sample (e.g. slides or a link to a recording). items.desc:
Help shape the scientific software that powers bioinformatics research worldwide. 
 At EMBL-EBI, our bioinformatics services help researchers access and work with biological data at scale. As our Bioinformatics Software Engineer & Scientific Lead, you’ll combine hands-on software development with scientific and technical leadership, helping guide the evolution of Job Dispatcher and other core software products. 
 You’ll work closely with scientists, engineers and infrastructure specialists to shape product strategy, prioritise development and deliver reliable, sustainable services that meet the changing needs of the global research community. 
 About the team 
 The Software Team within EMBL-EBI’s ITS Service and Operations department develops and maintains centrally provided scientific software, including Job Dispatcher, which provides structured access to run bioinformatical analysis tools on our high performance compute clusters and FiRE, which manages the storage and archiving of over 120Pb of scientific data . Working at the intersection of software engineering, scientific computing and bioinformatics, the team delivers services that support researchers in working with biological data and running computational analyses. 
 The Role 
 You’ll combine hands-on software development with scientific and technical leadership, helping shape the strategy, development and long-term sustainability of Job Dispatcher and other software products owned by the team. 
 Primary Tasks & Responsibilities: 
 Lead software development: Develop, maintain and improve production bioinformatics services and scientific software as an active member of the team. 
 Shape product strategy: Work with the team project lead and Head of Services and Operations to define and deliver product roadmaps, technology direction and longer-term development priorities. 
 Guide scientific direction: Provide specialist bioinformatics expertise to ensure services remain scientifically relevant, useful and aligned with the needs of the global user community. 
 Manage priorities and delivery: Help curate and prioritise the development backlog, coordinating projects, dependencies, risks and technical deliverables. 
 Coordinate service updates: Work with EBI service teams to plan and coordinate data updates, particularly for Job Dispatcher. 
 Collaborate across teams: Work with scientists, software engineers, infrastructure teams and other stakeholders to deliver and improve reliable scientific services. 
 Provide technical leadership: Represent the services in regular tools committee meetings, contribute to the wider ITS leadership community (TMC Plus) and support the evolution and modernisation of bioinformatics services. 
 Share knowledge and impact: Promote services through training, conference presentations, scientific publications and service updates, helping users understand and make effective use of the tools. 
 You Will Have: 
 A degree in Bioinformatics, Computational Biology, Computer Science or a related discipline, or equivalent relevant professional experience. 
 Professional experience in bioinformatics, scientific computing or software engineering, with the ability to apply software development expertise to scientific applications and services. 
 Strong programming experience developing and maintaining production software and RESTful APIs, using languages such as Java, TypeScript/JavaScript and Python. 
 Experience developing modern web applications using Angular or an equivalent framework. 
 Experience with scientific workflow technologies and high-performance computing environments, including Nextflow and job schedulers such as SLURM. 
 Experience packaging and deploying bioinformatics tools using containers such as Docker and Singularity/Apptainer. 
 Strong experience with Git-based version control, GitLab and CI/CD automation, alongside Linux, scripting, job scheduling, monitoring and production software operations. 
 You May Also Have: 
 Experience developing or maintaining large-scale, widely used bioinformatics services. 
 Experience communicating scientific work through peer-reviewed publications, presentations or other technical and scientific outputs. 
 Experience working with biological sequence data, including format conversion, processing and database indexing. 
 Familiarity with ServiceNow or similar IT service-management systems and processes, including incident and change management. 
 Contract Length: 3-Year fixed-term Staff Member contract, renewable to 9 years. 
 Working Pattern: This role offers a hybrid working arrangement, with 1-2 days per week on site, including one designated team day to support collaboration and connection. 
 Salary: Grade 6 or Grade 7, depending on experience. Monthly salary from £3,861.91 (grade 6) or £4,395.66 (grade 7) after tax, plus generous benefits and financial allowances based on individual circumstances. Excluding 12.99% personal pension and insurance contributions.

OUR STORY 
 At STMicroelectronics, we believe in the power of technology to drive innovation and make a positive impact on people, businesses, and society. As a global semiconductor company, our advanced technologies and chips form the hidden foundation of the world we live in today. 
 When you join ST, you will be part of a global business with more than 115 nationalities, present in 40 countries, and comprising over 50,000 diverse and dedicated creators and makers of technology around the world. 
 Developing technologies takes more than talent: it takes amazing people who understand collaboration and respect. People with passion and the desire to disrupt the status quo, drive innovation, and unlock their own potential. 
 Embark on a journey with us, where you can innovate for a future that we want to make smarter and greener, in a responsible and sustainable way. Our technology starts with you. 
 YOUR ROLE 
 We are seeking a highly motivated Metal Process Engineer to join our Power Front-End Technology R&D team. The successful candidate will contribute to the development of advanced metal processing technologies and materials solutions for next-generation products. This position is ideal for recent Master's graduates interested in applying their knowledge of materials science, metallurgy, and process engineering in an innovative research environment.
 The engineer will work closely with senior researchers and cross-functional teams to support process development, experimentation, characterization, and technology transfer activities.
 Process Research & Development 
 Support the development and optimization of metal processing technologies.
 Conduct laboratory experiments and evaluate process performance.
 Assist in designing and executing Design of Experiments (DOE).
 Collect, analyze, and interpret experimental data.
 Materials Characterization 
 Perform materials characterization using analytical and microscopy techniques.
 Investigate relationships between process conditions, microstructure, and material properties.
 Support root cause analysis of material and process-related issues.
 Innovation Projects 
 Participate in R&D projects focused on new materials, advanced manufacturing processes, and technology development.
 Review technical literature, scientific publications, and emerging technologies.
 Contribute to technical reports, presentations, and project reviews.
 Cross-Functional Collaboration 
 Collaborate with process engineers, product developers, manufacturing, and quality teams.
 Support prototype builds and technology demonstration activities
 partecipate in knowledge sharing and continuous improvement initiative 
 YOUR SKILLS & EXPERIENCES 
 Master's Degree in: Materials Science and Engineering
 Metallurgical Engineering
 Mechanical Engineering
 Chemical Engineering
 Physics or related disciplines
 Candidates should demonstrate knowledge in several of the following areas:
 Physical metallurgy and materials science fundamentals.
 Metal processing technologies and manufacturing principles.
 Materials characterization techniques.
 Statistical data analysis and experimental methodology.
 Thermodynamics, kinetics, and phase transformations.
 Mechanical properties and microstructure characterization.
 Basic data analysis tools (Excel, MATLAB, JMP, Python, or equivalent).
 Hands-on experience acquired through academic research or laboratory activities.
 Knowledge of: Metallography
 SEM/EDS
 XRD
 Mechanical testing
 Surface characterization techniques
 Experience with Design of Experiments (DOE) during research projects.
 Exposure to scientific writing and technical presentations.
 Basic understanding of semiconductor, electronics, automotive, aerospace, or advanced manufacturing applications.
 Key Competencies
 Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
 Curiosity and passion for research and innovation.
 Ability to learn quickly and adapt to new technologies.
 Effective teamwork and communication skills.
 Initiative and willingness to work in a multidisciplinary environment.
 Strong attention to detail and scientific rigor.

 Übersicht 
 Research and Teaching Assistant
 100%, Zurich, fixed-term 
 print 
 Drucken 
 The newly established Chair of Global Security, held by Prof. Annette Idler, is part of the Department of Humanities, Social and Political Sciences (D-GESS) at ETH Zurich. The Chair examines global security, especially in relation to armed conflicts, the global illicit economy, transitions from war to peace, and the interconnections between local conflict dynamics and global shifts in order and power. Its mixed-methods research programme integrates macro-level theory with detailed, contextualised fieldwork across world regions, combines qualitative, quantitative, and computational approaches, and bridges the social sciences with complexity science and other disciplines. The Chair’s international research group engages closely with international organisations, governments, and civil society. From 2029, Prof. Idler will additionally assume the Directorship of the Center for Security Studies (CSS) at ETH Zurich.
 The Chair holder, Prof. Annette Idler, is seeking to appoint, as soon as possible or by agreement, a research and teaching assistant (100%).
 Job description
 You will prepare the Chair’s courses each semester, manage the online learning environment for the Chair’s courses and help with grading. You may be asked to represent the Chair on the departmental Teaching Committee. You will also support Prof. Idler with research for teaching and research projects – including literature and background research, data collection and management, editorial support and preparing presentations – and maintain the Chair’s teaching records.
 Profile
 You hold a Master’s degree in Political Science, International Relations or a related discipline, with specialist knowledge of international politics and global security, and are familiar with the relevant research institutes and publication outlets. You have an excellent command of written and spoken English; knowledge of German is an advantage. Experience with qualitative and/or quantitative research methods, a high degree of independence and very good IT skills round off your profile.
 This position is an ideal entry point after completing a university degree and is fixed-term for about two years. You can look forward to varied and challenging work in a stimulating and motivating environment at a world-leading university. You will work closely with Prof. Idler, gain insight into teaching and research at a newly established chair at ETH Zurich and engage with a wide range of global security issues. There is also scope to develop a small independent research project of your own, for example towards a PhD proposal.

items.desc: A 2.5-year Postdoctoral Research Associate position is available for an outstanding and ambitious scientist to study transition metal molecular spin qubits using pulse EPR spectroscopy and related methods. This position, funded by an UKRI grant managed by Dr Floriana Tuna (https://research.manchester.ac.uk/en/persons/floriana.tuna/), involves close collaboration with the University of Rhode Island (Huh group) and Brown University (Robinson group) under an UK-US research partnership to explore quantum information science concepts in metal organic systems. As part of the project, the successful applicant will interact closely with experts at the UK National EPR Facility at Manchester (Prof David Collison, Prof Eric McInnes) and access state-of-the-art instrumentation for cw and pulse EPR (1-34 GHz), rapid scan, light-induced EPR, and SQUID magnetometry (https://www.chemistry.manchester.ac.uk/epr/). Recent publications relevant to the project: J. Am .Chem. Soc. 2024, 146, 15000; Nat. Commun. 2019, 10, 3330; Chem. Sci. 2024, 15, 3003, Chem.Eur.J. 2026, e71619, Inorg. Chem. 2026, 65, 6544. Purpose of the Job The role holder is expected to characterise the electronic structure and coherence properties of a series of d-block metal complexes to a standard suitable for publication, using pulse EPR and magnetometry, and to supervise junior researchers in the research group. Candidates should have or expect to obtain a PhD qualification in chemistry, physics, or a closely related field. They should have experience in performing advanced spectroscopic and/or magnetic measurements. Experience of EPR spectroscopy and handling and measuring highly air-sensitive samples, using glove boxes, d/f block chemistry, and being adept at a variety of characterisation techniques and calculations, are all highly desirable. The successful candidate will be a highly capable, motivated and independent researcher who is able to manage a group of PhD and undergraduate students working on a variety of spectroscopy and magnetism projects. You will be part of a larger research team working across synthesis, measurements and calculations to characterise qubits and establish the electronic structures of paramagnetic complexes. You will be expected to take a leading role in the research group, including coordination with the Huh group at Rhode Island University involved in chemical syntheses, organising group meetings, and presenting findings at international conferences. The start date is 1 February 2027, or soon after, and the position is available for up to 2.5 years. The Department of Chemistry is strongly committed to promoting equality and diversity, including the Athena SWAN Charter for gender equality in higher education. The School of Natural Sciences holds a Silver Award, which recognises their good practice in relation to gender; including flexible working arrangements, family-friendly policies, and support to allow staff to achieve a good work-life balance. We particularly welcome applications from women for this post, who are currently under-represented at this grade. Appointment will always be made on merit. For further information, please visit: https://www.manchester.ac.uk/connect/jobs/equality-diversity-inclusion/awards/athena-swan/ The University will actively foster a culture of inclusion and diversity and will seek to achieve true equality of opportunity for all members of its community. You can also find information on our Flexible and Hybrid working here. We are an open place of enquiry and challenge. We embrace and celebrate difference, diversity and debate, and we pride ourselves on being a place of education, learning and community where we are able, within the law, to question and test received wisdom, express new ideas and explore controversial or unpopular topics and opinions. Find out more from our Freedom of Speech Policy. items.desc: About the role We already run two kinds of agent alongside our teams. AI agents diagnose performance problems and tell people the root cause. Rule-based agents recommend marketing actions to our advertising teams. The quality of their decisions shows up directly in our revenue. Next, both take a greater role in the day-to-day running of our lead generation business, moving from recommending, to acting with a person's approval, to acting on their own where it is safe. We need an engineer to build agents that are dependable in production, measurable, and safe to trust with more. This is a hands-on engineering role. You'll own agents end to end, from understanding the workflow to running them in production, alongside our existing AI engineer, data scientists, product managers and the people who use the agents every day. Today we use Claude and open-weight models such as GLM, chosen per task on quality and cost, on an agent framework we build ourselves. What you'll do Build agents Start from the workflow. Sit with the operators, map how the work is actually done, and build for that, not for the process as documented. Build on shared rules. Rule-based and LLM agents that call shared, versioned rules and tools, not logic hard-coded inside each agent. Connect them to the business. Using our data warehouse, internal services, and the APIs into the systems agents act in. Turn outputs into results people trust. Structured outputs, validation and clear application logic. Make them safe to trust Log every decision. Each action records its context, what was chosen, and whether a person accepted or overrode it, so agents can be evaluated and improved. Build the path to autonomy. Per decision, agents move from recommend, to act with approval, to act alone. Our data scientists propose the bar from agreement and override data and point people in the business sign it off; you build the mechanism that enforces it on our shared agent framework, with permissions and guardrails in the code, not the prompt. Evaluate behaviour, not just code. Test sets, agreement with expert operators, and evaluation before and after every change. Run what you ship. Tracing, failure handling, and tracking quality, latency and cost. There's no on-call rota. What we're offering you: Summer Fridays Competitive holiday benefits - 25 days a year paid holiday, plus 8 bank holidays (increases 1 day a year up to 30 days) Hybrid working - 3 days a week in the office Closed for Christmas holidays - Extra days not taken from your annual holiday allowance. Work from anywhere for 2 weeks a year Life Assurance and Income Protection to protect your loved ones Benefits allowance for health, dental, and vision coverage Six months paid maternity leave, and one month paid paternity leave (subject to qualifying conditions) inclusive of same-sex and adoptive parents Defined Contribution Pension and Salary Sacrifice Scheme Be Well: Our award-winning wellbeing and mental health programme to support all MVFers and their families Family Forward support for our MVF parents and their mini-mes 2 charity days a year What we're looking for 3+ years of engineering, including at least one LLM application or agent shipped to real users. Python and TypeScript: production-grade in one and productive in the other, with typed, tested code and clear interfaces. You'll work in both here. items.desc: About us The Curie Institute Research Center France’s leading cancer research and treatment centre, Institut Curie unites a renowned research centre and a specialist hospital, fostering close collaboration between scientists, clinicians and healthcare professionals. It offers an environment of excellence where expertise comes together around shared values: care, humanity, openness, collaboration, efficiency, innovation, solidarity and commitment. Mission Laboratory The ATOMIC team “Advanced Therapy in radiation Oncology and Molecular Imaging Characterization” (CNRS UMR9029/Inserm U1353/Université Versailles Saint-Quentin) develops new strategies to increase the therapeutic index of radiotherapy. The team brings together biologists, medical physicists and radiation oncologists. FLASH radiotherapy, discovered at Institut Curie ( Favaudon et al., Science Translational Medicine, 2014 ), delivers the dose in a fraction of a second. It reduces toxicity to healthy tissue while maintaining anti-tumour efficacy comparable to that of conventional radiotherapy: this is known as the “FLASH effect”. As part of the FRATHEA institutional project , Institut Curie is developing a new FLASH irradiator using very high-energy electrons (VHEE), designed to reach deep-seated tumours. You will conduct the preclinical studies needed to validate this equipment, working closely with the team’s physicists and radiation oncologists: a rare opportunity to take part, from the very beginning, in the development of an innovative radiotherapy technology. The position is based at Institut Curie’s Orsay site, at the heart of the Université Paris-Saclay campus, which brings together research teams in radiobiology and medical physics as well as the Institut Curie Proton Therapy Centre. Main responsibilities Design and implementation of in vivo experiments : plan and carry out irradiation protocols in mouse models to assess the effects of FLASH radiotherapy, in compliance with regulations and animal welfare standards (3Rs principle); contribute to drafting project authorisation applications (APAFiS, the French ethics approval system). Animal care and monitoring :), weighing, substance administration, anaesthesia, monitoring of clinical parameters. Irradiation sessions : prepare, anaesthetise and position animals on the FLASH irradiator, in coordination with the physicists (dosimetry, scheduling of beam time). Biological analyses : collect organs and samples; take part in analyses (histology, immunofluorescence, genotyping, flow cytometry) with other team members. Data analysis and reporting : collect, organise and statistically analyse data; keep the electronic laboratory notebook; present results at team meetings and contribute to publications. Profile Education and skills Master’s degree (MSc) or engineering degree in biology, biotechnology, physiology or life sciences. Significant initial experience in vivo required (final-year internship, work-study programme or previous position); 2 or more years of professional experience is an advantage. Regulatory training in animal experimentation required: French “Applicator” certificate or equivalent (EU Function B); training in “Conceptor (EU Function C, project design) is an advantage and may be funded as part of the position. Proficiency in rodent handling techniques Knowledge of histology, immunofluorescence and molecular biology (PCR, genotyping); experience in flow cytometry is a plus. Basic skills in statistical analysis (GraphPad Prism, R or equivalent). Experience in radiobiology or in an irradiation environment is appreciated. Personal qualities Scientific rigour, observational skills and critical thinking Strong organisational skills and autonomy Ability to work in a multidisciplinary team (researchers, physicists, PhD students, clinicians) Good writing and communication skills; scientific English (reading articles, discussions in meetings). What we offer A pioneering project: the preclinical validation of a new FLASH radiotherapy technology. A multidisciplinary biology – physics – clinical environment, on one of Europe’s leading research campuses. Funded training (flow cytometry, statistical analysis, etc.). Recognition of your work, with co-authorship of publications according to your contribution. items.desc: Date de publication : Oct 16, 2026, 12:00AM Orange Cyberdefense est l’entité stratégique du Groupe Orange dédiée à la sécurité numérique. Nous accompagnons les entreprises de toutes tailles, organismes critiques, administrations et collectivités locales dans la conception de leurs stratégies de cybersécurité, leur mise en œuvre et leur gestion opérationnelle. Nous leur apportons notre expertise afin d’assurer le meilleur niveau de protection de leurs données, de leurs équipements et des services qu’ils offrent à leurs clients ou leurs administrés. Avec un CA de 1,3 Md€ en 2025,et plus de 3.300 experts dédiés à la cybersécurité, nous nous positionnons aujourd'hui comme le Leader européen sur le marché de la cyberdéfense. Notre vocation est de construire une société numérique plus sûre. En qualité d’Ingénieur spécialisé en forensic, vous rejoignez une équipe d’Experts Techniques spécialisés en réponse à incidents, threat intelligence, reverse engineering… Vous développez votre expertise technique en prenant part aux différentes missions d’investigation et de réponse à incidents du CSIRT Orange Cyberdenfense : Intervention sur les systèmes d’information clients en cas de compromission en menant des investigations de bout en bout (qualification initiale de l’incident, collecte de preuves, analyse forensic afin de reconstituer la chronologie de l’incident) ; Détermination des causes racines d’un incident; Estimation de l’impact technique et métier; Analyse la plus exhaustive possible des actions de l’attaquant sur le périmètre compromis; Restitution et rédaction de livrables ; Conception et développement d’outils d’aide à l’analyse à la pointe de la technologie; Participation à des projets de développement interne; Contribution au retour d’expériences Post-incidents Votre mission principale : Investigation numérique sur tout type de système d’exploitation; Établissement d'une chronologie forensic ; Analyse de la mémoire vive; Analyse de malware (serveurs contactés, mécanismes de persistance, artefacts permettant de le détecter sur l'ensemble d'un parc, propagation, etc…); Reverse engineering et déchiffrement de tout élément lié à un malware (communications réseau, fichier de configuration, fichier stockant les données volées, etc…). Vous pouvez être amené(e) à intervenir en astreintes sur des incidents critiques Vous exercez votre passion pour le domaine de la sécurité informatique depuis au moins 3 ans. Vous disposez d’une expérience solide en pentest ou en SOC L2/L3, et idéalement de quelques expériences en analyse forensique, analyse réseau, levée de doutes,… Vous aimez partager vos connaissances, développer vos idées, travailler de manière autonome ou en équipe et vous tenir informé sur l'évolution de la sécurité informatique. Consciencieux et disposant de bonnes qualités rédactionnelles, vous êtes capable de parler, de lire et de rédiger des textes techniques en français comme en anglais. Vous disposez d’une forte curiosité et d’une volonté d’aller au fond des choses. Compétences et Technologies : Maitrise des environnements GNU/Linux, Windows (artefacts système, journaux d’évènements, structure de fichiers), également sur les environnements Cloud (M365/EntraID, AWS) capacité à automatiser les tâches récurrentes dans un langage de scripting (Python, Powershell) Notre état d’esprit : une culture collaborative et responsabilisante, avec des équipes engagées, des initiatives d’intrapreneuriat et un onboarding structuré pour vous permettre d’être rapidement opérationnel. Votre carrière : vous intervenez sur des missions variées, auprès de nombreux clients, technologies et éditeurs. Vous développez votre expertise grâce à des formations, certifications et des opportunités de mobilité interne et internationale. ️ Votre bien-être & équilibre de vie : télétravail, accompagnement des pratiques sportives et culturelles, et actions concrètes autour de la santé mentale. Nos engagements RSE : nous développons des solutions de cybersécurité responsables, agissons avec notre écosystème pour réduire notre impact environnemental et soutenons les initiatives à impact portées par nos collaborateurs. Nos autres avantages : tickets restaurant, remboursement des transports à 75 %, mutuelle, participation (Groupe Orange), intéressement, épargne salariale, compte épargne temps, chèques cadeaux, prime vacances, etc. Challenge, bienveillance et expertise seront au cœur de votre quotidien. Rejoignez-nous ! Chez Orange, seules vos compétences comptent. Quel que soit votre âge, genre, origine, parcours, religion, orientation sexuelle, handicap, neuroatypie, ou apparence, nous encourageons activement la diversité au sein de nos équipes, car elle constitue une force pour le collectif et un vecteur d’innovation. Orange est une entreprise handi-accueillante : n’hésitez pas à nous faire part de vos besoins spécifiques.

Research Salary: Research Officer with a Salary Scale of €42,921 to €81,218 Closing Date: 06/11/2026 12:00 PM Permanent Full Time Job Summary Duration: Permanent . A panel may be formed from which future similar vacancies may be filled; such a panel will remain active for a maximum period of 12 months. Basic Function: To develop, lead and implement a state of the art research programme in the production of suckler beef cattle with particular focus on the following: Genetic and nutritional factors influencing the productivity of suckler beef cows and their progeny Key maternal, reproductive and health related traits Increasing animal performance and efficiency from both grazed and conserved forages Impact of both genetics and nutrition on environmental sustainability of suckler beef production systems Background: The beef industry is a major contributor to the value of Ireland’s agri-food sector. For example, the output value of the Irish cattle sector is typically in excess of €3 billion annually. Additionally, beef cattle production is a significant enterprise on over 94,000 farms, which are widely dispersed throughout the country. In particular the suckler beef sector, built around a national herd of ca. 800,000 beef cows, is central to the production of premium quality beef destined for high value international markets. Teagasc plays a key role in developing and supporting competitive, profitable and sustainable systems of Irish beef production. These production systems must maximise the use of grazed grass to capitalize on Ireland’s natural competitive advantage in grass production, and to contribute to the high quality, grass-fed reputation of Irish beef worldwide. Teagasc are seeking to appoint a highly qualified and enthusiastic researcher to develop and lead a cutting edge research programme to underpin the continued development and sustainability of the Irish suckler beef production sector. The successful candidate’s research programme will have particular emphasis on, but will not be limited to, investigating the impact of animal genetics and nutrition on the biological performance of suckler beef cows and their progeny, and how these management interventions influence both economic and environmental sustainability. The programme will also investigate how to further increase animal performance from grazed and conserved forage. This will be a key appointment for Teagasc with national significance in further developing our beef industry over the coming years. The Grange campus is part of the Animal & Grassland Research and Innovation Centre in Teagasc and has extensive facilities for field and laboratory research. These include pasture and overwintering facilities for in excess of 1100 cattle including in excess of 200 beef cows and their progeny to finish. Field and laboratory resources include state of the art electronic individual feed intake and methane emissions measurement equipment; a feed digestibility research unit and a suite of animal nutrition, animal health and molecular biology based laboratories to support a world-class beef cattle research programme. Indeed, Teagasc has an international reputation for research and development in grass-based systems of livestock production and the successful candidate will work with a dynamic and multidisciplinary team of researchers and knowledge transfer specialists across Teagasc’s Animal & Grassland Research and Innovation Programme at Moorepark, Grange and Athenry. Job Objectives Develop, lead and implement a cutting edge research programme on aspects of the breeding and nutrition of suckler beef cattle Design and manage experiments; statistically analyse and publish the resulting data. Manage staff and resources assigned to the research programme. Identify opportunities for cutting-edge research to address key knowledge gaps. Lead successful submissions for external funding, that are consistent with the Teagasc research programme, with the objective of developing critical mass in the area by building and supervising a dynamic team of post-doctoral researchers(s) and post-graduate student(s). Develop and maintain active collaboration with relevant national and international research organisations. Work closely with Teagasc Knowledge Transfer Specialists to ensure effective dissemination of research findings to advisors and stakeholders. Supervise, in conjunction with academic collaborator postgraduate students to Masters and PhD level. Interpret and publish research results in the scientific and popular press, at conferences (nationally and internationally) and to stakeholders Contribute to the teamwork and team spirit in the Animal & Bioscience Department, and foster and add to further collaboration and integration To assist Teagasc in meeting the commitments of the Quality Customer Service Charter and Action Plan. items.desc: Andersen is hiring a DevOps Engineer with Italian for a project supporting web and mobile applications and enhancing CI/CD processes, security, and operational reliability. Our customer is an established automotive business operating in a European market and providing a range of distribution, commercial, and customer-focused services. It supports various aspects of vehicle sales and after-sales operations while working with a broad network of business partners. The organization continues to invest in digital transformation, cloud technologies, data-driven solutions, and cybersecurity to modernize its operations, improve customer experience, and increase overall business efficiency. The project is focused on providing managed maintenance and application support services for a large portfolio of mobile and web applications. It covers software enhancements, technical support, continuous updates, CI/CD-based lifecycle management, and documentation while ensuring reliable operations, security, and alignment with established IT service management standards. Responsibilities: Monitoring and managing software versions, dependencies, vulnerabilities, and End-of-Life (EOL) components using Aikido, Renovate, and related tools, including manual updates where required. Ensuring critical, high-risk, and standard components are updated within defined timelines, prioritizing high and critical vulnerabilities. Managing EOL components, including preparing upgrade plans within required timelines and ensuring no unsupported components remain in production. Performing impact analysis for major updates and defining upgrade plans in collaboration with Developers. Maintaining and supporting GitLab CI/CD pipelines based on the Universal Pipeline, including linting, SAST, builds, automated tests, SonarQube quality gates, Docker/Kaniko builds, and Trivy scanning. Maintaining security and quality gates, container and base image lifecycles, artifact versioning and publication, and SBOMs for delivered artifacts. Troubleshooting build and deployment issues and supporting releases and deployments across on-premises and AWS environments. Adapting CI/CD pipelines to application and technology stack changes and resolving recurring DevOps issues. Maintaining pipeline and operational documentation in Confluence and contributing to monthly reporting on update status and timeline exceptions. Must-haves: Experience in DevOps / build and release engineering for production web applications for 3+ years. Strong hands-on experience with GitLab CI/CD, including pipeline design, maintenance, and troubleshooting, as well as Git and Merge Request workflows. Experience with Docker, container image management, Kaniko or similar rootless build tools, and container registries. Experience with dependency and vulnerability management, including Renovate/Dependabot, Aikido/Snyk, Trivy, and SonarQube or equivalent tools. Experience with Java build tools (Maven/Gradle). Working knowledge of AWS, Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL), and Docker Compose environments. Experience with secrets management using Vault or similar solutions, least-privilege access, and secure CI/CD practices. Experience with Splunk or similar centralized logging and monitoring tools. Level of English – from Upper-Intermediate and above. Level of Italian – from Intermediate and above. Nice-to-haves: Experience with .NET build tooling (MSBuild, dotnet CLI, NuGet). Experience deploying and supporting applications on Windows Server / IIS. Andersen cooperates with such businesses as Samsung, Siemens, Johnson & Johnson, BNP Paribas, Ryanair, Mercedes, TUI, Verivox, Allianz, T-Systems, etc. The opportunity to change the project and/or develop expertise in an interesting business domain. items.desc: Join the research project Past to Future (P2F), an ambitious Horizon Europe research consortium. The project’s overarching goal is to radically advance our capacity to anticipate future climate changes and tipping points by utilizing Earth's deep climate history. As Impact & Stakeholder Coordinator, you will play a key role in connecting our groundbreaking research with the right audiences. Additionally, you will help ensure the project runs smoothly by supporting the management team with project-related tasks. Your job As Impact & Stakeholder Coordinator, you will be the link between P2F’s scientific advancements and their application in policy and society. Your role is essential for translating complex research into actionable insights for diverse audiences. You will join the Management Team of the P2F project. The research consortium consists of 22 European partners and 3 international associated partners. You will be based at Utrecht University (UU), working alongside two dedicated Project Managers. A core component of this role is to serve as a bridge to Cardiff University, working in close daily collaboration with P2F’s Senior Public Engagement and Impact Manager who coordinates the overall Dissemination, Exploitation and Communication (DEC) of P2F. This partnership is vital for aligning our management and outreach teams in Utrecht and Cardiff. The position therefore includes one or two work visits to Cardiff to strengthen these operational links and co-develop project-wide strategies. Key Responsibilities Stakeholder engagement: Monitor and coordinate the overall stakeholder engagement strategy to non-scientific target groups, including stakeholder mapping, in close collaboration with the Cardiff team. Support the dissemination of project results to relevant scientific stakeholders and maintain active communication with the project’s Scientific Advisory Board (SAB), particularly to promote the uptake and long-term impact of the project’s core outcomes. Communication and Outreach: Collaborate with the communications officer from the related EMBRACER project to reach diverse target groups within the Netherlands, and potential role-out of activities to European partners. Set up and supervise student projects to produce visual communication materials, interviews, and other creative outputs regarding P2F research. Further develop the P2F website, manage and track the project’s social media presence and translate complex scientific papers into engaging and accessible content for the website and social media channels. Join relevant working groups, e.g. joint-policy initiatives from the Climate Research Communication Network. Project Support & Reporting: Maintain the continuous EU reporting of DEC project activities in the EC Funding & Tenders Portal, ensuring all outreach events and publications are accurately logged. Provide general consortium management support to the UU leadership team, particularly during reporting peaks and the organization of General Assembly Meetings. Your qualities Academic background (Master’s degree at a minimum) in climate/environmental science, climate policy, climate communication, or a closely related field; Experience in building networks and facilitating collaboration across different organizational cultures and with diverse external stakeholders. Strong communication skills, with a proven ability to translate complex scientific jargon into accessible narratives for the general public and policymakers. Familiarity with the Dutch and/or European climate research and policy landscape, and experience engaging relevant stakeholders. An established network in these fields is an advantage, as the role requires building connections and developing effective engagement activities within a relatively short project timeframe. Digital proficiency, including experience managing website content and utilizing social media tracking/amplification tools. Fluency in English (the project’s working language) is required. While not mandatory, proficiency in Dutch is a strong asset for engaging with local stakeholders and aligning with national projects. Nice to have: Project coordination experience, specifically in supervising student groups or managing small-to-medium scale events. Experience with EU project management or reporting (Horizon Europe/H2020), specifically regarding DEC plans and impact tracking. Our offer a position for one year (0.4 – 0.6 FTE), with the possibility of an extension until the end of the project on 1 March 2029, after a positive evaluation; a gross monthly salary, depending on qualifications and experience, between €3.706 and €5.760 (salary scale 10 under the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities (CAO NU)). The salary is based on a 38-hour working week; 8% holiday pay and 8.3% year-end bonus; a pension scheme, partially paid parental leave and flexible terms of employment based on the CAO NU. items.desc: Surfact AS Kjelsåsveien 141, 0491 Oslo Om jobben Lagre favoritt Stillingstittel Platform Engineer Type ansettelse Fast, heltid 100% Antall stillinger 1 Arbeidsspråk Engelsk eller norsk Vis flere detaljer We make cargo talk. Why? Because a third of all food and pharma produce is wasted on the way to consumers, and we're out to change that. Our smart tracker Emma - made from recycled ocean plastic - travels with temperature-sensitive shipments for enterprise customers in food, pharma and seafood across 20+ countries. We're looking for a seasoned engineer to own the platform behind it, and to build it for ten times the fleet we run today. What you'll do Own our Azure cloud platform end to end: architecture, ingestion, data, cost, and the calls about what we run and why. Push AI-assisted development further than most dare. Claude writes most of our code and a human owns every merge - you'll define how far that goes for production infrastructure, and build the guardrails. Scale ingestion and the data tier for a fast-growing fleet - without per-device cloud cost rising with it. Make reliability unremarkable: no reading silently lost, late and backfilled data handled gracefully, and monitoring that spots trouble before a customer does. Grow the data platform so questions about the fleet or a single shipment are answered in seconds, not filed as tickets. Our stack A cloud-native platform on Azure: event-driven IoT ingestion, serverless services, and both operational and analytical data stores. CI/CD carries much of what we ship, a human reviews every change, and turning more of our infrastructure into code is a job we want you to own. AI runs through development, operations and analysis, and we are leaning into what is now just possible. We're ISO 27001 certified and our customers are audited, so security shapes real engineering decisions. We'll go through the details with you in the interview. What you bring Deep experience in building and operating production cloud infrastructure - Azure, or another major cloud and the appetite to go Azure-deep. Real conviction about AI-assisted development, with the judgement to know when to slow down and verify. A curious, fast-learning mind - being a jack-of-all-trades is a real plus here. Fluency with infrastructure as code, CI/CD and observability. Strong Postgres and SQL, and sound instincts for modelling time-series data at volume. Nice to have: IoT or telemetry at fleet scale, cellular (LTE-M, NB-IoT), ISO 27001/SOC 2 environments, Python, and cloud cost engineering. What we offer Competitive salary, good pension, and share options - own a piece of what you build. Flexible hours and location; a welcoming office at Kjelsås Stasjon with parking and good transit. Our team tends to spend about half their time at the HQ. Your choice of tools, plus best-in-class AI tools with generous quotas. This job is based in Oslo, Norway. Norwegian/EEA work permit required. Relocation support is not provided. Om bedriften Born in Norway. Built for the world. Surfact transforms temperature-sensitive logistics with sensor technology built for the cold chain. We are backed by strong partners and we cut waste and safeguard vital cargo, shipment after shipment. We build our own electronics, our own firmware, our own software. It is all engineered, built and assembled in Norway to survive the harshest environments on earth. We hire generalists with depth, give them real ownership, and trust them to make decisions. The work is serious, with pharma, food, lives and livelihoods at stake, but the way we do it is grounded, honest and unmistakably Norwegian. items.desc: Position Details Department of Applied Health Sciences, School of Health Sciences, College of Medicine and Health Location: University of Birmingham, Edgbaston, Birmingham UK Full time starting salary is normally in the range £47,389 to £56,535 with potential progression once in post to £63,606 Grade: 8 Part time (22.5 hours per week) Fixed Term contract up to July 2030 Closing date: 8th November 2026 UK travel may be required for this role Background The National Institute for Health and Care Research (NIHR) Inequalities Challenge: Maternity Disparities Consortium is a £50million national programme which brings together a diverse range of organisations with expertise in research, capacity building and working with people and communities to deliver a step change in maternity and neonatal outcomes. The research carried out by the consortium focuses on inequalities before, during and after pregnancy. The programme is underpinned by an innovative and transformative capacity building programme of career development awards and opportunities, linked and embedded within the consortium’s research areas to support the next generation of researchers working to address maternity inequalities. We are seeking a mixed-methods researcher who thrives in multidisciplinary environments to play a pivotal role in improving health outcomes and reducing maternal inequalities. The Evaluation & Impact Fellow at the University of Birmingham will lead the design, coordination and delivery of the programme-level evaluation of the NIHR-funded Maternity Disparities Consortium (MDC), assessing implementation, research outputs, outcomes, equity, influence, environmental sustainability and wider real-world impact. The fellow will work in close collaboration with the Evaluation & Impact Fellow at Newcastle University. In Newcastle, the fellow will evaluate the capacity development programme, and the impact of our work in PPIE and co-production, research inclusion and engagement with and impact on policy makers. In Birmingham, the fellow will evaluate scientific and programme impact, implementation and integration across themes, intervention progression, methodological innovation, adoption and scale-up, NHS and service influence, environmental sustainability, external leverage and the Consortium’s contribution to reducing maternity inequalities. You will co-design evaluation frameworks and apply a full range of mixed-methods approaches, including realist and other theory-driven evaluation methods, rapid evidence reviews, qualitative and quantitative data collection and analysis, and synthesis of findings into clear, actionable insights. You will lead the development of the Consortium-wide Evaluation and Impact Framework, including programme theory, logic models, theory of change processes, common programme-level indicators and approaches to assessing the added value of the Consortium model. You will synthesise evidence across themes, workstreams and core functions to identify what works, for whom, in which contexts and why, and support evidence-informed decisions about what should continue, change, stop or scale. You will also contribute to drafting high-quality reports, peer-reviewed publications, horizon-scanning and developing competitive research and evaluation proposals. The Fellow will contribute to the MDC Innovation strategy and engagement with industry partners, including identifying opportunities for responsible adoption, scale-up and wider impact. You will bring substantial experience of mixed-methods, theory-driven and/or implementation-focused evaluation, with the ability to integrate quantitative and qualitative evidence from multiple sources. Experience of realist evaluation, programme evaluation, impact evaluation, sustainable healthcare or environmental impact assessment, and engagement with industry or other external partners would be advantageous. items.desc: R&D: Analog Designer & Data Scientist – Spaceman Divisione Move Silicon – Move S.p.A. Chi siamo Move Silicon è la business unit di Move S.p.A. dedicata allo sviluppo di chip integrati per il mercato dei semi-conduttori. Parallelamente alla progettazione micro-elettronica classica stiamo sviluppando Spaceman, una piattaforma di Electronic Design Automation basata su tecniche di machine-learning per supportare i progettisti analogici nella generazione, ottimizzazione e verifica automatica di circuiti integrati. Spaceman si integra nei principali ambienti EDA, tra cui Cadence, Synopsys e Siemens, e ha l’obiettivo di trasformare specifiche circuitali in blocchi analogici ottimizzati e verificati, riducendo drasticamente il tempo necessario per progettare IP analogiche. Tutte le sezioni del software, compresa quella algoritmica sono state progettate in-house ad hoc per la specifica applicazione. La nostra visione è ambiziosa: contribuire a portare AI, automazione e generative design nel cuore del processo di progettazione analogica dei semiconduttori, un campo rimasto praticamente incontaminato da questi sviluppi a causa di peculiari difficoltà dell’ambito. La posizione A seguito di PoC con esiti positivi con importanti player del mercato dei semiconduttori, Spaceman sta entrando in una fase di evoluzione da piattaforma R&D a prodotto vendibile. Allo stesso tempo, la piattaforma presenta ancora numerosi temi di ricerca da approfondire ed estendere: architetture di reti neurali per modellare dataset elettrici, strategie di campionamento in spazi di variabili ad alta dimensionalità, tecniche per migliorare la convergenza delle simulazioni, metodi di ottimizzazione più efficienti e approcci per sfruttare in modo strutturato gli insight circuitali sulle topologie in esame. Cerchiamo una figura con background in microelettronica e forte interesse per data science, machine learning, statistica, AI e ottimizzazione applicate a problemi CAD/EDA. Il ruolo è pensato per un ingegnere elettronico con attitudine multidisciplinare, capace di comprendere il problema applicativo in profondità e contribuire allo sviluppo di soluzioni algoritmiche ad hoc. La figura lavorerà all’interno del team R&D, composto da profili con background eterogenei, contribuendo alla prototipazione di nuove tecniche, algoritmi e strategie. Le soluzioni più promettenti potranno poi essere trasferite nel prodotto. Tra i temi futuri di interesse rientrano anche l’estensione dell’approccio a IP di maggiore complessità, l’uso di agentic AI per la composizione di blocchi generati da Spaceman e, in prospettiva, attività legate al layout, come la stima di reti parassite per simulazioni post-layout e il layout automatico. Per questo ruolo sono fondamentali curiosità scientifica, capacità di studio autonomo, pensiero critico, problem solving e propositività. Cerchiamo una persona che voglia pensare, studiare, capire e progettare soluzioni nuove per problemi complessi, collaborando in modo profondo con gli altri membri del team. Responsabilità principali Contribuire alla ricerca e allo sviluppo di nuove tecniche per l’automazione del design analogico. Proporre idee, modelli e strategie per affrontare i problemi R&D legati a Spaceman. Realizzare PoC e prototipi per validare nuove soluzioni algoritmiche. Lavorare su temi di modellazione, ottimizzazione, campionamento, convergenza delle simulazioni e sfruttamento degli insight circuitali. Valutare robustezza, generalità e scalabilità delle soluzioni proposte. Studiare e approfondire autonomamente nuove metodologie utili alla risoluzione dei problemi affrontati. Collaborare con membri del team R&D con background eterogenei per giungere ad una soluzione soddisfacente. Interfacciarsi con il team software per valutare la mantenibilità e l’implementabilità delle soluzioni sviluppate. Contribuire al trasferimento delle tecniche R&D più promettenti verso il prodotto. items.desc: About Aptura We build the evaluation datasets and RL environments that make AI reliable in domains where mistakes are expensive: finance, healthcare, and legal. Our team designs expert-curated training data, calibrated rubrics, and verifiable task environments for AI labs and startups pushing the frontier of what models can do in regulated industries. We're a small, lean, London based team that moves fast and takes the work seriously. Everyone contributes directly. Initiative is rewarded, and ownership is the default. If you want to shape how frontier AI learns to operate in the real world, we'd like to hear from you. About The Role As a Member of Technical Staff on our Applied AI team, you will build the tasks and environments that AI labs use to train and evaluate their agents in finance, healthcare, and legal. Day to day, that looks like: constructing RL environments around spreadsheets, documents, and professional workflows. Writing verification logic and reward functions. Working with domain experts to scope what a correct answer actually looks like in an LBO model or a clinical note. Some days it's engineering, some days it's closer to research. The common thread is that you're producing the ground truth that frontier models get measured against. What You'll Do Build RL environments across finance, healthcare, and legal domains Assist in designing tasks with golden answers, calibrated rubrics, and programmatic reward signals Write verification logic and reward functions that can distinguish good model outputs from bad ones Work directly with domain experts (investment analysts, physicians, attorneys) to translate complex professional workflows into structured tasks Prototype new approaches to evaluation, verification, and synthetic data generation Who We're Looking For Practical experience building with LLMs: prompting, evaluation, and agentic harnesses. You've built things that actually run, not just notebooks. High agency and technically sharp. You don't wait for permission, specs, or a roadmap. You see what needs doing, figure out how, and get it done. Comfortable working across very different contexts. The job moves between engineering, evaluation design, and deep collaboration with domain experts often in the same day. You ship and iterate. Small team, no room for work that sits in review. Bias toward getting something working, learning from it, and improving it. You own problems end to end, from scoping with a domain expert through to a working environment. If you prefer clearly partitioned tickets, this probably isn't the right fit. Already using LLMs as part of how you build, not just as the thing you're building for. Nice to Have Domain knowledge in finance, healthcare, or legal Familiarity with RL concepts, model training, and post-training workflows Cloud infrastructure experience (AWS or GCP) Previous startup experience, especially as an early engineer

items.desc: When the quantum engineering technology meets the real word impact. Based in the heart of the French Alps, Quobly is the result of more than 15 years of research into quantum computing. At Quobly we made the choice of practical and scalable quantum technology. Quobly offers you the opportunity to participate in the future of quantum computing; become a member of our science and innovation team as a Cryo-CMOS Design Research Engineer to turn scientific breakthroughs into products that matter. Your main mission will be to generate new ideas, open up new avenues for the control, the addressing and the readout of large-scale quantum processors. Your tasks: • Imagine and develop original concepts of circuit architectures fabricated with industrial CMOS technologies for the readout of large arrays of silicon spin QuBits at low temperature (figures of merit: speed, noise, overall consumption and local dissipation) • Design these architectures with behavioral modeling first (Matlab, Python or Cadence), then with time, frequency and noise simulations with Cadence • Implement the designs in mask layouts in an industrial framework (eg Calibre), running LVS, DRC and parasitics extraction analyses • Interact with physicists of the quantum team, process integration engineers and the circuit design team • Actively contribute to the testing of fabricated circuits at low temperatures by interacting with the testing team • Actively participate in internal scientific discussions by contributing ideas to the scientific and innovation roadmap Collaboration Collaborate with talented people, in a culture of transparency and autonomy. Work hand in hand with members of our technical teams. Your profile: • PhD in circuit design • A minimum of 5 to 10 years’ experience in analog and mixed-signal IC design • Knowledge of pixelized devices such as CMOS imaging sensors or RAM • Ideally, knowledge of RF design Above all, you are a creative thinker, capable of challenging conventional approaches and coming up with new solutions. Your curiosity and intellectual independence will make all the difference. Nice to have: You have an industrial mind set Your curiosity and intellectual independence will make all the difference. Working at Quobly also means: Working in Grenoble, home to some of the fastest-moving tech and industrial companies around, and a great base camp for a wide range of activities from outdoor and mountain sports to arts and culture. Grenoble offers an affordable lifestyle, ensuring you can plan for a comfortable future while advancing your career with us. The opportunity to develop in-demand skills alongside the best researchers in their fields. A collaborative work environment and a company culture where trust is paramount and where individual contributions are recognized. Presenting at international conferences to share our latest results. items.desc: About the Role We have an exciting opportunity for a permanent position as a Power Systems Research Engineer/Scientist to join the Power Networks Team within NPL’s Electromagnetic Technologies Group. This role is suitable for an early-career engineer, physicist, applied scientist or post-doctoral researcher who is looking to apply and develop their expertise in power systems, measurement science, instrumentation, data analysis and grid monitoring within a collaborative research environment. The Power Networks Team conducts research and development in advanced measurement methods and instrumentation to enable intelligent monitoring of electricity grids. The UK electricity grid is undergoing a major transformation as it prepares to operate with zero carbon emissions by 2030. While new technologies such as wind and solar generation, batteries, electric vehicle charging stations and heat pumps bring major environmental benefits, they also introduce new technical challenges for maintaining grid stability and power quality. Power grid operators therefore need new and improved monitoring tools to gain a deeper insight and run the grid reliably and efficiently. The Power Networks Team at NPL works with UK industry partners, as well as national and international research organisations to ensure that next-generation grid measurement solutions are fit-for-purpose. You will be closely collaborating with the team to support activities including: Setting up and safely operating laboratory testbeds for electrical measurements related to various power grid phenomena (e.g. harmonics, frequency deviations) Developing software for automatic hardware configuration and data analysis Designing, developing and testing new measurement methods and instrumentation for power quality and grid stability monitoring Preparing and deploying instrumentation for field measurement campaigns at locations across the UK and Europe Collaborating with international research organisations and universities within R&D projects Communicating research outcomes through publications, reports, posters and oral presentations at events such as symposia and international conferences This role is an opportunity to work with a team of researchers to address cutting-edge measurement challenges in electricity networks. The work combines applied physics, metrology, instrumentation, data analysis and power systems, and is project-based and varied. This means that we continually adapt our skills and capabilities to solve new problems. The successful candidate will be highly self‑motivated, comfortable working both independently and collaboratively, and able to adapt quickly to new and evolving technical challenges. Please note, this role is known internally as Higher Scientist/Engineer. items.desc: The University of Law is looking for an AI Developer in Education to join our Technology Enhanced Learning and Teaching team and play a hands-on role in shaping how AI is used across the University. We’re looking for someone who can look at a problem, understand what we are trying to achieve, and then work out whether AI is the right solution and, if it is, build it, test it, improve it and make it work at scale. You’ll sit at the intersection of AI development, software engineering and education , working closely with our academic and learning design teams to turn ideas into practical AI-powered tools and experiences. You’ll also work directly with our key AI technology partners, helping to shape development priorities, troubleshoot issues and make sure we are getting real value from the technology we invest in. This is an opportunity to join a University that is actively exploring what AI can do for education, while having the technical expertise and influence to help determine what should actually be built and how it should work. What will you be doing? Education You’ll take technical ownership of the development, configuration and optimisation of AI tools used across our educational provision. This will include: Designing, developing and maintaining Topics, Agents and Workflows within our generative AI platform, turning educational and business requirements into functional solutions. Building, testing and refining AI-powered learning experiences, using user feedback and evidence to continually improve them. Exploring emerging AI technologies and leading technical pilots and proof-of-concept projects — assessing not just whether something can be done, but whether it delivers meaningful value. Integrating AI platforms with University systems, including Blackboard Ultra, student information systems and other digital learning technologies. Working with APIs, LLMs and data integrations to create solutions that are secure, reliable and fit for purpose. Acting as a technical expert for our key AI platforms and technology partners, understanding their capabilities, limitations and development roadmaps. Troubleshooting technical issues and identifying practical ways to improve the performance, usability and reliability of our AI tools. Helping successful ideas move beyond experimentation and into sustainable solutions that can be used across the University. Producing clear technical documentation and guidance that can be understood by both technical and non-technical colleagues. Working closely with academic, learning design and professional services teams to understand their needs and translate them into effective technical solutions. Ensuring our AI development meets the University's requirements around security, accessibility, data protection and academic integrity. What are we looking for? We’re looking for someone with a strong technical foundation who is genuinely curious about what AI can do and equally interested in whether it should be used and what difference it will make. Strong programming skills in one or more relevant languages, such as Python or JavaScript, alongside experience working with AI/ML technologies. Strong technical problem-solving skills and the ability to investigate, test and resolve complex issues. Experience communicating technical concepts clearly to non-technical audiences and working effectively with a wide range of stakeholders.
