items.desc: About Teamwill Consulting Putting domain expertise and artificial intelligence at the heart of the decisions that finance millions of projects, vehicles, and equipment around the world is the core of what we do. For more than 20 years, Teamwill Consulting has been supporting leading players in banking, consumer finance, and mobility through their strategic and technological transformations. Operating in 11 countries and bringing together more than 800 professionals, the Group combines deep industry expertise, close client relationships, and the ability to deliver on a global scale. Artificial intelligence is a cornerstone of our growth strategy. To carry that ambition, we are strengthening our technology, engineering, and data teams. Role Summary Teamwill Consulting’s CTAIO function builds and operates the firm’s reusable artificial intelligence (AI) engineering assets, then deploys them into some of the firm’s most demanding engagements. As an Applied AI Engineer, you design, build, and operate production AI systems that combine managed large language models (LLM) with managed or self-hosted, proprietary or open-weight models, under real infrastructure constraints. You turn an AI capability from a working prototype into something an engineering organization can trust in production: tested, observable, and safe to change. Key Responsibilities Design, build, test, and operate agentic systems and pipelines that call one or more LLMs to complete multi-step tasks. Contribute to clarifying requirements with Product Owners, Product Managers, Business Analysts, and Subject Matter Experts, and to formalizing non-functional requirements (e.g., application reliability, security, performance…). Start with the simplest composition that works (typically applying the KISS (keep it simple and stupid) software craftsmanship principle): a direct model call or a short chain, moving to a more autonomous, tool-using agent design once a simpler one is shown to fall short. Favor a lightweight, provider-agnostic integration approach over a heavyweight orchestration framework whenever possible. Integrate managed, application programming interface (API)-based models and self-hosted, proprietary and open-weight models into the same application, including the operational work specific to self-hosting: inference optimization and request scheduling under constrained graphics processing unit (GPU) capacity. Build and maintain the retrieval pipelines that ground models via retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) in the client’s or firm’s knowledge bases: turning source documents into a well-structured, versioned, and access-controlled form a model can retrieve from reliably. Build and maintain evaluation (“eval”) suites that gate every change before it reaches production (capability, safety, regression, and cost/latency thresholds). Implement guardrails (secret redaction, content-safety filtering, and fallback behavior), and instrument every AI-powered service for observability (token usage, latency, tool-call errors, and output quality) so a production issue can be diagnosed from data. Package AI components as containerized, deployable services with documented interfaces (API, command-line interface (CLI), Model Context Protocol (MCP)), so they can be integrated into a client’s systems. Use AI coding agents (for example Claude Code, Cursor, or OpenCode) as part of your own engineering workflow: maintain the standing context documentation a project keeps for its agents, and review agent-produced code with the same combination of automated checks and human review as code anyone else on the team writes Work closely with clients, Data Engineers, Platform Engineers, and Forward Deployed Engineers to move an asset from prototype to a client-ready, secure, and monitored deployment, and contribute field learnings back into Teamwill’s shared asset portfolio, so a solution built for one engagement strengthens every future one. What You’ll Work On Your primary engagement sits inside a large, regulated financial-services environment where AI adoption is real and accelerating. Some workloads run against managed, proprietary models under a strict data-governance agreement; others run entirely on infrastructure the client controls, using open-weight models, to meet data-residency and regulatory requirements. Both paths are rich engineering challenges: the managed path calls for rigorous prompt, cost, and safety engineering, and the self-hosted path for model serving and capacity planning in a market where GPU capacity is scarce. You will have the opportunity to build expertise in both. The work is international: you will collaborate with teams and clients across Teamwill Consulting’s geographies. items.desc: Fospha is the measurement system enterprise retail and ecommerce brands run their business on. We give marketing teams one clear, daily view of what's actually working — across every channel and everywhere they sell, from their website to Amazon and TikTok Shop — down to the level of a single ad or piece of creative. It replaces guesswork and gut feel with a number marketing, finance and agencies can all trust and act on. Brands including Dyson, Gymshark, Adanola and Huel use Fospha up to 25 times a day to decide where budget should move next. We've spent over a decade building this, with more than $40 billion in marketing spend now optimised through the platform — and we're scaling fast across London, Mumbai and Austin. About The Role We're looking for a Data Scientist to join Fospha's Data Science team in London. Fospha builds marketing measurement products for ecommerce brands — attribution, marketing mix modelling, incrementality testing, and brand impact measurement. Our Data Science team owns the models behind all of it, from methodology through to production code. You will work across our technical stacks and own maintaining and growing the codebases that power our product and solutions. This role suits an established data scientist who wants to own things properly. You'll lead larger production projects, choose the modelling approach rather than being handed it, and talk to clients as the modelling expert in the room — supported by a team that reviews each other's work seriously, and a company that rewards high agency with ownership. Team: Data Science Level: Career (Data Science Career Development Framework) Location: London What you'll do Lead larger production projects end to end — scoping, building, and shipping production-level code, rather than working through tickets someone else has specified Choose the modelling approach — independently selecting and applying the right method within our suite, across attribution, marketing mix modelling, incrementality testing, and brand impact. You will be given time to keep up-to-date on the latest methodologies in the industry Resolve bugs and queries independently — including in parts of the codebase you didn't write, without needing to route them upwards Use AI as leverage, not as a crutch — solving coding tickets quickly, unblocking yourself on product and engineering dependencies, and building automation workflows that save the team time Work with QA properly — using our automated tooling efficiently and flagging the gaps in it rather than working around them Communicate as a modelling expert — confidently and independently, with clients and with colleagues, including when the message is that a number they like is wrong Help develop the people around you — code review, methodology critique, and hands-on support for less experienced colleagues. Breaking down tickets and helping those more junior is essential What we're looking for Essential Solid commercial data science experience — typically 3–5 years, with a track record of shipping models into production Strong ML knowledge across multiple algorithm families, and the judgement to pick the right approach for the problem rather than the one you know best Strong Python and SQL, with the ability to lead on production-level code and set the standard others work to Able to debug and resolve issues independently across unfamiliar repositories, using AI tooling to accelerate rather than to guess, while still understanding the problem fully Strong AI fluency — you solve tickets quickly with it, you unblock cross-department dependencies with it, you build automation workflows with it, and you never send AI-assisted output without checking it Confident, independent communication with clients and stakeholders as the technical authority on the work Emerging mentorship — you're ready to develop junior colleagues, and you want to Initiative in accepting and planning your own work, rather than waiting to be allocated it Genuine attention to detail — much of this work involves noticing when a number is wrong Nice to have Bayesian modelling experience, particularly hierarchical models Experience with AWS or comparable cloud tooling Familiarity with automated QA tooling and test coverage practices Experience with marketing, ecommerce, or advertising data Not required Experience with attribution methodology, MMM, incrementality testing, or Bayesian modelling is genuinely an advantage at this level — but it isn't a filter. Our stack takes time to learn regardless of what you arrive with, and we'd rather hire strong modelling judgement and teach the domain. How You'll Grow We run a published Data Science Career Development Framework with six levels. You'd join at Career, where the expectations are: AI Fluency & Tooling: Leverages AI to solve coding tickets quickly; consistently unblocks themselves on cross-department dependencies, especially product and engineering; never sends AI-assisted communication without …

items.desc: Deine Aufgaben Du willst KI nicht nur ausprobieren, sondern damit unser gesamtes Company Setup smarter machen? Als Junior AI Engineer (m/w/d) entwickelst du AI-Automationen für unsere internen Prozesse, von Customer Service über Supply Chain bis Reporting, und bringst sie vom Prototyp bis in den produktiven Betrieb. Du verbindest unsere Systeme über APIs mit unserem Data Warehouse, machst Daten nutzbar und verbesserst deine Use Cases messbar. Dabei denkst du nicht in Einzelprojekten, sondern betrachtest Prozesse ganzheitlich, erkennst selbst, wo es Potenzial gibt, und arbeitest eng mit unseren Business-Teams zusammen. Wenn du ein gutes Verständnis für Python, SQL und Cloud-Architekturen mitbringst, schon selbst etwas mit LLMs gebaut hast und dich schnelle Veränderungen eher anspornen als abschrecken, dann suchen wir genau dich! Deine Aufgaben AI-Automationen: Du entwickelst und betreibst AI-Automationen für interne Prozesse wie Customer Service, Supply Chain und Reporting und begleitest sie vom ersten Prototyp bis in den produktiven Betrieb. System-Integration: Du verbindest interne und externe Systeme über APIs (z. B. Shopify, Zendesk/Resolvia, Sage/Anvyl, Klaviyo), bindest sie an unser Data Warehouse an und stellst die Daten unseren AI Agents zur Verfügung. Prompt & Agent Engineering: Du setzt Use Cases um, testest die Ergebnisse systematisch und verbesserst sie messbar in Qualität, Kosten und Latenz. Prozessoptimierung: Du verstehst unsere Prozesse im Detail, verbesserst sie und entwickelst neue interdisziplinäre Abläufe. Dein Ziel ist dabei immer, unser Company Setup als Ganzes weiterzuentwickeln. Projektverantwortung: Du identifizierst eigenständig neue Projekte und Verbesserungspotenziale, nimmst aber auch Anfragen aus den Teams auf. Im Schnitt steuerst du drei Projekte parallel und behältst sie über ein klares Meilenstein-Setup im Griff. Enablement: Du unterstützt unsere Business-Teams, baust interne Tools, dokumentierst Ergebnisse und hilfst deinen Kolleg:innen dabei, die Automationen selbstständig zu nutzen. Dein Profil Studium & Ausbildung: Du hast ein Bachelor- oder Masterstudium in Informatik, Data Science, Wirtschaftsinformatik, Mathematik oder einem vergleichbaren Bereich abgeschlossen. Ein starkes Portfolio (eigene Projekte, GitHub, Open Source) oder ein Quereinstieg mit nachweisbarer Praxiserfahrung zählt für uns genauso viel, der Abschluss ist also kein Muss. Python & SQL: Du hast fundierte Kenntnisse in Python (APIs/REST, Git, methodisches Debugging) und SQL und idealerweise erste Erfahrungen mit BigQuery oder einem vergleichbaren Cloud Data Warehouse. LLMs & AI Tooling: Du hast praktische Erfahrung mit LLMs und AI Tools (Claude/OpenAI APIs, Agents, MCP, Cursor/Claude Code) und hast damit nicht nur gearbeitet, sondern schon eigene Lösungen entwickelt. Cloud & Tools: Du kennst dich mit Enterprise Cloud (z. B. Google Cloud oder AWS) und Deployment aus, inklusive Container und CI/CD. Erfahrung mit Shopify ist ein Plus. Systemverständnis: Du erfasst schnell, wie Datenflüsse laufen und Systeme zusammenhängen. Eigeninitiative: Du bringst eine Hands-on-Mentalität mit, nimmst offen formulierte Probleme selbst in die Hand und lieferst eine erste funktionierende Lösung. Lernbereitschaft: Du hast eine schnelle Auffassungsgabe und bringst dir neue Themen gerne selbst bei, technisch genauso wie in den Business-Bereichen. In diesem Feld ändert sich jeden Monat etwas, deshalb zählt deine Lernfähigkeit für uns mehr als das, was du heute schon weißt. Kommunikation & Stakeholder Management: Du verstehst, was unsere Business-Teams wirklich brauchen, und erklärst technische Ergebnisse klar und ehrlich, auch dort, wo KI an ihre Grenzen stößt. Sprache: Du fühlst dich sicher in der englischen Kommunikation mit deinem Team (mind. C1 Level), bringst aber auch Deutsch-Kenntnisse (mind. B1 Level) mit. Warum wir? Dich erwartet ein modernes und dynamisches Arbeitsumfeld mit einer Du-Kultur von Tag eins. Wir glauben an flache Hierarchien und agile Arbeitsmethoden. Unsere Teams bestehen aus motivierten Menschen, die etwas bewegen wollen. Goodies für dich: Von Jobrad-Leasing über Zuschuss zum Deutschlandticket bis hin zu betrieblicher Altersvorsorge (Arbeitgeberzuschuss 50%) - bei uns profitierst du von vielen Extras. On top gibt’s Mitarbeitenden-Rabatt in unserem Snocks Coffee und einen steuerfreien Sachbezug (50€ / Monat), den du flexibel für deinen Wocheneinkauf oder z.B. eine Mitgliedschaft bei Urban Sports Club einsetzen kannst. Arbeiten, wie’s zu dir passt: Du arbeitest, wo du am produktivsten bist. Remote ist Standard, aber wenn du doch mal Lust hast, ins Büro nach Mannheim, Hamburg oder Berlin zu kommen, gibt’s dafür ein Monatsbudget. Echte Flexibilität: Ob Workation mit Freund:innen oder Kolleg:innen, morgendliches Yoga oder eine Sport-Session mittags – bei uns kannst du Arbeit und Privatleben easy miteinander verbinden. Onboarding: Du startest nicht mit leeren Händen, sondern bekommst top Hardware, alles was …

You will work across team boundaries and help ideas become reliable practices. You are motivated by building the systems and procedures that help an entire development organization work effectively. You follow new developments in deep learning and agentic AI, with a focus on what they can enable in practice. You combine curiosity with sound judgement and can recognise which emerging ideas have the potential to create real value. You are comfortable discussing ideas and trade-offs with stakeholders and working together to find practical ways forward. Essential Experience A master’s degree in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, or a related technical field. items.desc: About Edra Edra is solving one of the hardest problems in enterprise AI: AI models are generic but company processes are specific. We build AI agents that learn how processes actually run, and then run their operations. We're a Series A startup, backed by Sequoia and other leading VC firms, led by Co-Founders who created and led Forward Deployed AI Engineering at Palantir, and we're growing our team in New York and London. We're a deeply technical team of engineers, AI researchers, and strategists with a high bar for talent and a shared belief that exceptional people are the foundation of everything great we'll build. The Role We're building a learning system that teaches AI agents how enterprises actually work. Our system ingests knowledge bases, conversations, tickets, and system logs, then produces written instructions that agents can execute–with confidence scoring to know when to automate and when to seek human input. We're looking for Forward Deployed AI Engineers who have built complex, production LLM-based systems, and want to work directly with our enterprise customers. Whether you've scaled LLM workflows handling millions of requests, built multi-agent systems in production, or designed evaluation frameworks for enterprise deployments, we want people who bring intensity and self-direction to their craft. You’ll own the full technical journey: understanding how an operation works, identifying the right problem, designing and building the solution, shipping it to production, driving adoption, and expanding its impact. This is an engineering role: you’ll write production code, make architectural decisions, build agentic systems, and take responsibility for the outcome. What You'll Do Work directly with enterprise customers to identify new problems, prototype solutions, and ship them to production Own customer engagements from discovery and solution design through production, adoption, and expansion. Design and implement LLM-powered systems and agentic workflows from concept to production Use and extend our core context-learning library to solve customer problems, contributing reusable capabilities and lessons back into the platform. Build agentic features for knowledge management–think agents that can edit, update, and maintain large knowledge bases autonomously Build reliability and confidence systems–evaluation frameworks, confidence scoring, and logic for when to automate vs. when to escalate to a human Architect async, scalable systems that handle complex AI orchestration What We’re Looking For You've built complex, production LLM-based systems with real depth–something with multiple layers of engineering decisions you can walk through in detail You've shipped something meaningful to production and can explain how it evolved You're excited by open-ended problems where the solution might not exist yet You have experience with (or strong interest in) how systems learn and improve over time: human-in-the-loop feedback, prompt optimization and context engineering You have experience building agents and autonomous systems You can navigate between research papers and production code with equal comfort You bring customer empathy and commercial judgment, and remain effective when requirements, data, or expectations are unclear. You're a strong communicator who can clearly explain your work to teammates and customers You have 3+ years of professional experience Don’t meet all of the above traits? We’d still love to hear from you. We’re looking for exceptional people with unique skills and interests, and we know that great people have different backgrounds and skillsets. Learn More About Edra Watch our Series A announcement video Read our blog post from our launch Learn more about what we're building Our founders point of view on the market Compensation & Benefits Edra offers generous compensation and benefits in both New York & London: Competitive base salary & meaningful equity Top tier health, dental, & vision plans: Top plans with 100% premium coverage in the US (and a One Medical membership) Private medical & dental coverage in the UK Flexible paid time off Lunch provided in office most days, snacks & drinks too A stipend to set up your workspace A Few Details We work together in person five days a week from our offices in the West Village (New York) and Holborn (London). items.desc: Apify is a marketplace of ready-to-run tools for AI that automate work on the web. Apify can find missing children, protect consumers from fake discounts across the EU, and feed data to AI chatbots. Working on our mission to build the largest marketplace of tools for AI, we're becoming one of the pioneers in MCP dynamic tool discovery and agentic payments via Coinbase's x402 standard, letting autonomous agents discover the right tools and pay for them on their own. Because we serve both humans and machines, we're also making natural language a first-class interface to the platform. We stay close to where this is happening: we show our work at conferences like the AI Engineer World's Fair, where we spoke on the emerging agentic economy, and the MCP Dev Summit; we host our own Prague Crawl, where Jan Curn made the case that "MCP doesn't suck, your agent does"; and we regularly rotate people through San Francisco. We're looking for an AI Engineer to help build all of this. It's a small team with a lot of surface area, so you'll own real problems end-to-end. What You'll Be Working On Build and maintain the Apify MCP Server, turning tens of thousands of Actors into tools that agents can reliably call. Keep the server ahead of a protocol that changes fast and often breaks: stateless transports, authorization hardening, and tool discovery. Shape the agent behind Apify AI, from the runtime it runs on to the tools it reaches and the rough edges that surface when it runs a full task end-to-end. Help autonomous agents discover and pay for Apify tools. Build evals that turn real production traces into tests, catch regressions in CI, and tell us whether a change made the product better or worse. Who We're Looking For 3+ years building real software, with backend experience in Node.js/TypeScript or Python. You've built something on top of LLMs and know the pain firsthand: tools the model calls wrong, context that balloons, agents that confidently do the wrong thing. You use the Apify platform, or want to, and care about building tools other people enjoy using. Good communication skills in English. items.dept: Artificial Intelligence, Enterprise Engineering, Facebook, Generative AI
items.desc:
Meta is seeking Security Engineers with Privacy and Data protection expertise to join our Applied Artificial Intelligence (AAI) organization. You will apply deep privacy engineering expertise to hard, real-world problems in how systems collect, use, retain, expose, and delete data. Your work is AI-augmented from day one: you leverage AI tools and agents to accelerate your impact, and where the models fall short, your expertise directly drives their improvement.
The problems that matter here are the ones a capable engineer cannot solve by reading the code in front of them: which jurisdiction's deadline applies to a deletion request, whether a derived dataset clears an anonymity threshold, where a deletion has to cascade. Models already handle the privacy obligations that are stated as ordinary good engineering practice, so the work is the obligation they cannot derive.
This role is for privacy engineers who want to operate at the intersection of deep privacy expertise and frontier AI, not just applying AI to privacy work but shaping what it is capable of.

security engineering Deep expertise in at least one privacy subdomain with demonstrated ability to advance the state of the art: purpose limitation, retention and deletion, data access control, jurisdictional obligations, de-identification, consent, or ML and model privacy Experience implementing privacy obligations in production systems, in addition to reviewing or advising on them Software engineering proficiency, including code review and maintenance, with experience coding in Python, PHP, Java, C/C++, or an equivalent language Track record of architecting privacy systems, controls or programs that operate at scale and influence how others build Demonstrated ability to define and drive complex, ambiguous problem spaces with group-level impact Experience adhering to and implementing responsible, ethical AI practices (e.g., risk assessment, bias mitigation, quality and accuracy reviews) Experience improving AI model performance through expert feedback, red teaming, or evaluation design Experience with pseudonymization lifecycle, including deletion of the user-to-pseudonym mapping Demonstrated ability to integrate AI tools to optimize/redesign workflows and drive measurable impact (e.g., efficiency gains, quality improvements) Demonstrated ongoing AI skill development (e.g., prompt/context engineering, agent orchestration) and staying current with emerging AI technologies Experience implementing obligations conditioned on jurisdiction, age band, or cohort: regional carve-outs, regulatory deadlines, minor and parent-initiated request handling Contributions to the privacy or security community (original research, tools, conference presentations, publications) Experience applying differential privacy, k-anonymity, or other formal de-identification techniques in production rather than in research only Experience with privacy review or privacy incident response at scale Background in ML and model privacy: memorization, membership inference,  Why Join Us? 
 Our team is a global talent powerhouse, working remotely from every corner of the world. If you’re passionate about making a mark in the fintech space, this is your opportunity to collaborate with some of the brightest minds, pushing boundaries and setting new standards.  If you have excellent English communication skills and are ready to contribute to the most innovative platform on the planet, Tether is the place for you.
 Are you ready to be part of the future? 
 About the job 
 We are looking for Fullstack Engineer to help QVAC application teams develop, review, test, and deliver reliable software with less friction. Your focus will be our desktop and mobile applications and their shared runtime, AI harness, and skills packages. You will build and maintain developer tools, integrate AI agents into engineering workflows, and improve code quality and delivery automation. 
 This is a hands-on engineering role with room to shape the tooling roadmap. You will work with engineers to identify useful improvements and own them from implementation through adoption and ongoing support. Success means shorter feedback loops, dependable automation, and tools that developers trust and use. 
 Responsibilities 
 Evaluate, integrate, and maintain developer tools and AI agents, including the repository guidance and integrations they need to work effectively. 
 Build and operate agents in CI and scheduled workflows that investigate failures, propose fixes, and give engineers evidence they can act on. 
 Improve automated pull request reviews, evaluating finding accuracy and reducing noise for reviewers. 
 Develop code quality scripts and checks for complexity, function and file size, dependency cycles, and performance regressions. Work with package owners on practical thresholds and targeted refactoring. 
 Improve development environments, testing, and build and release workflows so engineers and agents can verify changes reliably. 
 Prioritize improvements with engineering teams, support adoption through documentation and onboarding, and measure effectiveness, reliability, and operating costs. 
 Example projects include agents that investigate CI failures, diagnose compatibility and performance regressions, and flag changes that affect package interfaces or architecture. You will choose and refine these workflows with the engineers who use them. 
 Experience building and maintaining developer tools or engineering automation used by others, with strong JavaScript/TypeScript and Node.js skills. 
 Hands-on experience using and integrating AI coding tools or agents, with sound judgment about their limitations, output validation, and human review. 
 Experience with Git, CI/CD, automated testing, and systematic debugging of build, test, or integration failures. 
 A strong approach to code quality: maintainable code, useful automated checks, and refactoring that preserves behavior. 
 Ability to work independently, collaborate with engineers, and communicate clearly in English within a remote, globally distributed team.

items.desc:
About kaiko 
 Picture Laura, 58, with a cough that will not clear. It takes four specialists and a year to find her lung cancer, though the signs were in her file from the start, spread across scans, lab results and reports. No doctor had the whole picture, or the time to weigh it.
 kaiko is named after a deep-sea vessel that went 10,911 metres down, to the bottom of the ocean, and came back with what was there. Our clinical AI does the same with a patient’s record and the medical evidence, so doctors have the whole picture when they decide. It is built on our own foundation models and used daily at leading European hospitals.
 We are a well-funded team of more than a hundred people in Amsterdam and Zurich. Join us so the next patient like Laura is diagnosed months sooner, with a better chance of a long and healthy life.
 About the role 
 As kaiko brings its clinical AI to clinicians, the decisions on where we invest depend on data we can trust. That data has to follow each user from a first visit to our website, through sign-up and first use, to the colleagues they bring in.
 There is no marketing technology stack for this yet, so you design and build it from the ground up: tracking and consent, the connection between product and marketing data, event-triggered email next to our CRM, and the data layer the team reports from. Working closely with product, engineering, data and security, you keep clinical data out of every marketing tool by design. You document what you build and hand it over to the growth team in working order, ready for new European markets.
 We’re looking for someone who has built a measurement and messaging stack from nothing for a product-led company, and who is as comfortable writing an event specification with engineers as setting up a CRM integration or modelling data in a warehouse.
 This is a freelance engagement until mid-2027, starting as soon as possible. 
 Some areas of responsibility 
 Design and build our marketing measurement from the ground up: the tracking plan, consent and server-side tracking, attribution, and the definitions the team reports on.
 Connect product and marketing data with product engineers: event specifications, one event pipeline, and one view of each user across website, product and CRM.
 Set up event-triggered lifecycle email next to our CRM, with reliable deliverability and clear rules for which tool reaches whom.
 Build the data layer and dashboards the growth team decides from, then document the stack and hand it over in working order.
 About you 
 4 to 8 years in marketing operations, growth engineering, analytics engineering, or martech consulting, including building a stack from scratch for a self-serve or product-led company.
 You have set up an event-triggered messaging tool such as Customer.io , Braze, or Iterable next to a CRM such as HubSpot, and connected both to a product.
 You set up and model a data warehouse with SQL and a tool such as dbt.
 Privacy by design: you build tracking under GDPR and ePrivacy and keep sensitive data out of marketing tools.
 A hands-on builder who works as one team with product and engineering. You document your work so others can run it.
 Nice to have: 
 Experience in healthcare, life sciences, or another regulated sector.
 Experience measuring referral loops, or setting up tracking across countries and languages.
 Working knowledge of Dutch.
 Why kaiko 
 At kaiko, we believe the best ideas come from collaboration, ownership and ambition. We’ve built a team of international experts where your work has a direct impact. Here’s what we value:
 Ownership: You’ll have the autonomy to set your own goals, make critical decisions, and see the direct impact of your work.
 Collaboration: You’ll have to approach disagreement with curiosity, build on common ground, and create solutions together.
 Ambition: You’ll be surrounded by people who set high standards for themselves and others, who see obstacles as opportunities, and who are relentless in their work to create better outcomes for patients.
 Our interview process 
 Our interview process is designed to assess mutual fit across skills, motivation, and values. It typically includes the following steps:
 Screening call: A short conversation to align on your motivation, professional goals, and initial fit for the role.
 Technical interview: A deep dive into your problem-solving approach through a technical challenge, case study, or role-specific scenario.
 Onsite meeting (optional): You’ll meet team members across functions to explore collaboration dynamics, team fit, and day-to-day context.

Scientific Assistant in Industrial Robotics and Manufacturing 
 chevron_left 
 Übersicht 
 Scientific Assistant in Industrial Robotics and Manufacturing
 100%, Zurich, fixed-term 
 print 
 Drucken 
 The Advanced Manufacturing Lab (am|z) at ETH Zurich, led by Prof. Markus Bambach, is seeking a highly motivated Scientific Assistant to contribute to research and development in industrial robotics, automated manufacturing, and metrology.
 We are looking for a candidate who combines strong programming skills with hands-on experience in robotic hardware, enjoys solving challenging technical problems, and can independently develop and implement robotic solutions.
 The position offers the opportunity to take ownership of experimental robotic systems, develop innovative automation solutions, and contribute to scientific research in advanced manufacturing.
 Project background
 The Advanced Manufacturing Lab at ETH Zurich investigates innovative manufacturing technologies by combining robotics, automation, process engineering, and data-driven methods.
 Our research aims to make industrial robotic systems more flexible, accurate, autonomous, and reliable. Applications include robotic manipulation, pick-and-place operations, and manufacturing processes such as welding, adhesive bonding, and drilling.
 Beyond conventional robot programming, we investigate methods for improving robotic capabilities through sensing, metrology, calibration, process monitoring, and data-driven approaches. Our work combines the development of practical robotic systems with experimental validation and scientific investigation.
 Job description
 Your main responsibilities will include:
 Independently develop, program, and operate industrial robotic systems for automated manufacturing and manipulation tasks
 Design and implement robotic applications, including pick-and-place operations, welding, adhesive bonding, drilling, and related manufacturing processes
 Integrate robotic hardware, including end-effectors, sensors, measurement equipment, tooling, and peripheral systems
 Develop and maintain software for robot control, motion planning, and automation, using version control, automated testing, and deployment workflows
 Design and implement automated data acquisition and processing workflows to collect, synchronize, visualize, and analyze robotic and manufacturing process data
 Integrate metrology and sensing technologies to evaluate and improve robot positioning accuracy, calibration, repeatability, and process quality
 Independently plan and conduct experiments, troubleshoot technical challenges, and evaluate system performance
 Contribute to scientific research by developing and validating novel methods, analyzing experimental results, and preparing scientific publications
 Collaborate with researchers, students, and industrial partners on robotics and manufacturing projects
 Profile
 We are looking for an independent, technically skilled, and research-oriented engineer who enjoys working with real robotic systems and transforming ideas into functioning experimental solutions.
 You should have:
 A Master's degree in Robotics, Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, Automation, or a closely related field
 Hands-on experience in programming, operating, or integrating robotic systems, gained through research, academic projects, or industry
 Strong programming skills, particularly in Python, C++, or comparable languages, with experience in developing and maintaining software for robotics and automation
 A solid understanding of robotic kinematics, coordinate transformations, motion planning, and control principles
 Practical experience with robotic hardware, including the integration, configuration, or troubleshooting of sensors, actuators, end-effectors, or mechanical components
 Proficiency with Git and version control, along with familiarity with software testing and continuous integration and continuous deployment (CI/CD) workflows
 Experience with experimental work, data acquisition, and analysis of measurement data
 The ability to independently solve technical problems, combined with creativity, initiative, and a systematic approach to engineering challenges
 A strong interest in scientific research and the development of innovative robotic technologies
 Fluent English, both written and spoken
 Knowledge of German is an advantage
 The following qualifications would be an advantage:
 Experience with industrial robots, such as ABB, KUKA, FANUC, or similar platforms
 Familiarity with the Robot Operating System (ROS/ROS 2) or other robotics frameworks
 Experience with robotic manufacturing applications, including manipulation, assembly, welding, adhesive bonding, machining, or drilling
 Knowledge of robotic metrology, calibration, coordinate measurement systems, or robot accuracy assessment
 Experience with machine vision, force/torque sensors, laser measurement systems, industrial communication interfaces, or real-time data acquisition

ESTEC, Noordwijk, Netherlands 
 Description 
 Photonic EEEE Engineer in the Components Section, Avionics and EEE Division, Electrical Department, Directorate of Technology, Engineering and Quality.
 The Components Section provides functional support to ESA projects and carries out technological research and development (R&D) in the field of electrical, electronic, electromechanical and electro-optical (EEEE) components with a strong focus on technologies and processes, development and reliability as well as on ground qualification activities. In addition, the Section is responsible for ESCC (European Space Component Coordination).
 You will provide support in the areas of:
 photonic EEEE components (laser diodes, photo diodes, LEDs, optical fibre, passive optical components, etc.);
 detectors (CCDs, CMOS sensors, IR detectors, etc.).
 Duties 
 Your tasks and responsibilities will include:
 providing expert technical support and consultancy to ESA projects, programmes and general studies in the field of photonic and detector EEEE throughout all project phases;
 contributing to the definition of technology development requirements and work plans for the Agency’s technology programmes;
 defining, initiating and managing R&D activities covering both long- and short-term needs;
 fostering new application areas for multidisciplinary activities, with an emphasis on innovative concepts and cutting-edge technologies;
 supporting technology domain-related standardisation activities (e.g. ESCC, ECSS);
 contributing to the dissemination of the results of the activities performed and the transfer of knowledge across the Agency;
 participating in feasibility studies, project reviews and evaluation of procurement proposals;
 identifying critical development problems and assisting in their resolution;
 initiating and monitoring laboratory activities including preparation of test plans and review of test reports;
 monitoring applicable scientific and technological trends and maintaining state-of-the-art expertise.
 Technical competencies 
 General background and experience in the technical domains covered by the position
 Understanding of related technologies, R&D trends and the industrial landscape
 Hands-on hardware experience
 Project support experience in a relevant domain
 Experience with laboratory or field testing of relevant technical equipment
 Experience in the preparation of procurement activities for technology development and innovation (statements of work, proposal evaluation, etc.)
 Experience in the management and monitoring of industrial activities, including participation in reviews
 Behavioural competencies 
 Result Orientation
Operational Efficiency
Fostering Cooperation
Relationship Management
Continuous Improvement
Forward Thinking

 Education and professional experience 
 A master's degree in physics, electronics engineering, photonics, optoelectronics, microelectronics or a related discipline is required for this post together with, in principle, 4 years of relevant professional experience.

 Professional experience with space projects and products would be an asset.

items.desc: The AI Teams at Agile Robots are looking for a Robotics Software Engineer (m/f/d) AI Tools & Integration , who will integrate AI models with robot hardware and build the applications and tooling around them. Customers and partners reuse this stack through open-source releases, so it has to keep working with messy data, limited compute, and real hardware. Responsibilities Robot Integration: Integrate trained AI models with single-arm and dual-arm robots through ROS 2, and maintain the runtime that runs them on hardware. Application Development: Build robot applications on top of the AI stack, including agentic workflows that chain AI models and robot skills into multi-step tasks. Tool Interfaces: Build UI, API, and CLI tools such as dataset viewers, training dashboards, and benchmark viewers. End-to-End Testing: Build test suites that run real user workflows from data through training to inference, including stress tests with messy data and limited compute. Release Readiness: Maintain nightly regression runs on the reference workflows and run reliability checks before demos and open-source releases. Documentation: Write and maintain the documentation customers and partners use to adopt the tooling. Essential Skills Engineering Background: Degree in Computer Science, Robotics, or a related field, or equivalent qualification plus professional experience building comparable software systems. Python Engineering: Professional experience building and maintaining Python software that other engineers depend on. ROS 2 Integration: Hands-on experience integrating and debugging software on physical robots through ROS 2. Containers & CI: Hands-on experience with Docker and CI pipelines such as GitHub Actions for reproducible builds and releases. Testing: Hands-on experience designing integration and end-to-end test suites and debugging failures across the full stack. Backend Services: Experience building backend services and APIs, for example with FastAPI or gRPC. Beneficial Skills C++ Development: Experience writing C++ for robot-side or performance-critical code. Agentic Systems: Experience building applications that combine language or vision-language models with robot skill execution. Frontend Development: Working experience with React or Next.js for building data-heavy interfaces. ML Workflows: Working understanding of how training and inference pipelines for robot learning models fit together. What we offer A dynamic high-tech company, combined with financial soundness and world-class investors. Join an interdisciplinary, international team with 60+ different nationalities in a collaborative work environment. Lots of development opportunities as we continue to grow. Challenging tasks and impactful projects alongside experts that enable professional and personal growth. Corporate Benefits Program covering health, mobility, and learning for 100€ net per month. Modern office facilities with a rooftop terrace overlooking Munich, free drinks & fruits, and regular company events contribute to a good working environment About us Agile Robots SE is an international high-tech company based in Munich, Germany with a production site in Kaufbeuren and more than 3500 employees worldwide. Our mission is to bridge the gap between artificial intelligence and robotics by developing systems that combine state-of-the-art force-moment-sensing and world-leading image-processing technology. This unique combination of technologies allows us to provide user-friendly and affordable robotic solutions that enable intelligent precision assembly. This is made possible by our employees, who bring out the best in each and every day with creativity and enthusiasm. Become part of this team and shape the future of robotics with us! We are proud of our diversity and welcome your application regardless of gender and sexual identity, nationality, ethnicity, religion, age, or disability.

items.desc: Il Gruppo Over, fondato nel 2020, è uno tra i primi operatori in Italia a creare soluzioni e servizi abitativi per i Senior. L'obiettivo di Over è quello di garantire luoghi dove i residenti possano mantenere le proprie abitudini, la propria socialità, la propria indipendenza ma con una protezione costante ma discreta, supportata dalle moderne tecnologie alla portata di tutti. Posizione: Operiamo nel settore socio sanitario e stiamo investendo con decisione sull'innovazione digitale, siamo certificati ISO/IEC 27001 e abbiamo inoltre avviato un percorso di conformità all'AI Act europeo. Non ci limitiamo ad adottare la tecnologia, ma la sviluppiamo internamente con un team dedicato alla progettazione di soluzioni AI-native, che vogliamo far crescere con giovani talenti. I nostri team lavorano a stretto contatto con gli operatori sanitari per progettare e fornire strumenti che semplifichino la presa in carico del paziente e la relativa cura. Siamo alla ricerca di un/a Junior Web Developer & AI Integration per le seguenti attività: Supporto alla manutenzione e all'evoluzione dei siti web aziendali (front-end e back-end), imparando a curare performance, sicurezza e accessibilità. Partecipazione all'integrazione di siti e flussi digitali con il centralino basato su AI (instradamento chiamate, automazioni conversazionali) e con il CRM (contatti, lead, appuntamenti, flussi paziente). Sviluppo di integrazioni API/webhook tra siti, CRM, centralino, marketing automation, gestionali e sistemi sanitari interni, affiancato da colleghi senior. Collaborazione con il team AI su automazioni, agenti e integrazioni che vanno oltre il "semplice sito", imparando sul campo. Attenzione alla qualità tecnica: codice pulito e manutenibile, documentazione essenziale, rispetto delle regole su sicurezza dei dati e GDPR. Requisiti: Competenze tecniche Laurea o diploma in informatica o ITS; prima esperienza anche breve (stage o progetti) nello sviluppo web. Buone basi di HTML/CSS/JavaScript e di un linguaggio back-end (PHP, Node.js, Python); gradito React o Vue. Concetti base di API REST e webhook. Attitudine AI (il nostro requisito distintivo) Utilizzo già abituale di AI coding assistant (Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, Cursor o simili) nei tuoi progetti o nello studio. Spirito critico nell'uso dell'AI: capire il codice che l'AI propone, verificarlo e non accettarlo a scatola chiusa. Interesse a conoscere API di LLM, prompt e automazioni agentiche (non serve essere già esperti). Curiosità reale, voglia di imparare e di sperimentare con strumenti in continua evoluzione. Approccio: voglia di crescere, attitudine al lavoro in team, disponibilità ad ascoltare e a chiedere, capacità di dialogare con referenti clinici e amministrativi, precisione e attenzione alla qualità. Titoli preferenziali: tirocini o progetti in ambito sanitario o in contesti regolamentati; interesse per le normative sul trattamento dei dati sanitari; progetti personali o di studio basati su AI. Altre informazioni: COSA OFFRIAMO Un percorso di crescita strutturato, con affiancamento costante da parte di colleghi senior e formazione continua. Lavoro su progetti reali di AI applicata in un'azienda in forte crescita innovativa, per sviluppare competenze che vanno oltre il web development tradizionale. Un ambiente in cui le idee vengono ascoltate e la tecnologia ha un impatto concreto sulla cura delle persone. RAL 35.000€-45.000€ SEDE DI LAVORO: GENOVA. Lavoro in sede

Contribuire all'evoluzione del framework di AI Governance del Gruppo, supportando la definizione di ruoli, processi, controlli, policy e strumenti necessari per un'adozione responsabile e scalabile dell'AI. Collaborare
items.desc: Trento, IT, 38122 Società: Gruppo Cassa Centrale Cassa Centrale Banca è Capogruppo dell’omonimo gruppo bancario cui fanno capo altre società attive in ambito finanziario ed in grado di completare l’offerta rivolta alla soddisfazione di molteplici esigenze delle banche clienti. Cassa Centrale Banca è una “Banca per le banche” che si impegna a lavorare per la rete delle banche affiliate e clienti condividendone valori, cultura, strategie e sistema organizzativo per rendere sempre più efficiente e competitivo il sistema sul mercato. La missione del Gruppo Cassa Centrale è contribuire allo sviluppo della vita economica e sociale dei territori delle banche di credito cooperativo. Il Gruppo Cassa Centrale ha il proprio headquarter presso la storica sede di Trento, e filiali territoriali nelle maggiori città italiane. Scopri di più sul sito della corporate http://gruppo.cassacentrale.it/ L'Intelligenza Artificiale sta trasformando il settore bancario e finanziario, creando nuove opportunità di innovazione, efficienza e servizio ai clienti. Entrando nel team AI Promotion & Governance, contribuirai alla definizione e all'evoluzione del modello di adozione dell'AI del Gruppo, collaborando con funzioni business, tecnologiche e di controllo per favorire uno sviluppo responsabile, sicuro e orientato al valore delle soluzioni di Intelligenza Artificiale. Chi stiamo cercando Cerchiamo una persona curiosa, analitica e motivata, con una buona preparazione sui temi dell'Intelligenza Artificiale e un interesse genuino per il settore bancario e finanziario. Valutiamo sia neolaureati con una solida preparazione accademica sia professionisti alle prime esperienze che desiderano crescere in un contesto in forte evoluzione, lavorando all'intersezione tra tecnologia, innovazione, business e governance. Cosa farai Supportare l'identificazione, la valutazione e la prioritizzazione di iniziative di Artificial Intelligence, Generative AI e Agentic AI, analizzandone benefici, impatti operativi e rischi. Contribuire all'evoluzione del framework di AI Governance del Gruppo, supportando la definizione di ruoli, processi, controlli, policy e strumenti necessari per un'adozione responsabile e scalabile dell'AI. Collaborare alla valutazione dei casi d'uso AI, anche in relazione agli aspetti di rischio e sostenibilità operativa. Monitorare l'evoluzione tecnologica, normativa e di mercato in ambito AI, predisponendo analisi e sintesi a supporto delle decisioni aziendali. Supportare attività di AI Literacy, formazione e comunicazione interna, contribuendo a diffondere conoscenza e consapevolezza sull'uso dell'AI all'interno del Gruppo. Partecipare a workshop, gruppi di lavoro e momenti di confronto con stakeholder interni ed esterni sui temi di innovazione e AI adoption. Requisiti Laurea in Informatica, Ingegneria, Matematica, Statistica, Economia o discipline affini. Conoscenza dei concetti fondamentali di Machine Learning, Generative AI, Large Language Models (LLM) e AI Agents Interesse per i temi di AI Adoption, Responsible AI, AI Governance e innovazione tecnologica Interesse o prima esposizione al settore bancario e finanziario, maturata attraverso studi, tesi, progetti o esperienze professionali Esperienza professionale compresa tra 0 e 2 anni Buona conoscenza della lingua inglese Competenze che apprezziamo Pensiero critico e capacità di analizzare problemi complessi Capacità di tradurre concetti tecnici in messaggi chiari per interlocutori non specialistici Attitudine alla collaborazione e al lavoro in team multidisciplinari Proattività, autonomia e orientamento al risultato Interesse per la trasformazione organizzativa e l'innovazione nei servizi finanziari. Per questa posizione è previsto un trattamento economico non inferiore ai minimi tabellari stabiliti dal CCNL applicabile per l’inquadramento indicato. Indicazione economica minima (base): a partire da €35.650 RAL (minimo contrattuale per Terza Area Professionale Primo Livello). Sede di lavoro: Trento La suddetta ricerca è aperta a candidature di qualsiasi orientamento o espressione di genere, orientamento sessuale, età, etnia e credo religioso, in ottemperanza e nel rispetto del d.lgs. 198/2006. Per i valori a cui ci ispiriamo, prestiamo particolare attenzione alla diversità, all’inclusività e alla tutela dell’equilibrio fra vita privata e vita professionale.

About the job We are looking for Fullstack Engineer to help QVAC application teams develop, review, test, and deliver reliable software with less friction. Your focus will be our desktop and mobile applications and their shared runtime, AI harness, and skills packages. You will build and maintain developer tools, integrate AI agents into engineering workflows, and improve code quality and delivery automation. This is a hands-on engineering role with room to shape the tooling roadmap. You will work with engineers to identify useful improvements and own them from implementation through adoption and ongoing support. Success means shorter feedback loops, dependable automation, and tools that developers trust and use. Responsibilities Evaluate, integrate, and maintain developer tools and AI agents, including the repository guidance and integrations they need to work effectively. Build and operate agents in CI and scheduled workflows that investigate failures, propose fixes, and give engineers evidence they can act on. Improve automated pull request reviews, evaluating finding accuracy and reducing noise for reviewers. Develop code quality scripts and checks for complexity, function and file size, dependency cycles, and performance regressions. Work with package owners on practical thresholds and targeted refactoring. Improve development environments, testing, and build and release workflows so engineers and agents can verify changes reliably. Prioritize improvements with engineering teams, support adoption through documentation and onboarding, and measure effectiveness, reliability, and operating costs. Example projects include agents that investigate CI failures, diagnose compatibility and performance regressions, and flag changes that affect package interfaces or architecture. You will choose and refine these workflows with the engineers who use them. Experience building and maintaining developer tools or engineering automation used by others, with strong JavaScript/TypeScript and Node.js skills. Hands-on experience using and integrating AI coding tools or agents, with sound judgment about their limitations, output validation, and human review. Experience with Git, CI/CD, automated testing, and systematic debugging of build, test, or integration failures. A strong approach to code quality: maintainable code, useful automated checks, and refactoring that preserves behavior. Ability to work independently, collaborate with engineers, and communicate clearly in English within a remote, globally distributed team. Important information for candidates Recruitment scams have become increasingly common. The role interprets emerging AI research, methods, frameworks, models and evaluation approaches, and turns the most relevant developments into practical validation questions. It performs hands-on prototypes, benchmarks and comparisons to produce evidence before architecture, platform,
items.desc: Location: Krakow, Lesser Poland, Poland Job ID: R0147165 Date Posted: 2026-10-15 Company Name: HITACHI ENERGY SERVICES SP. Z O.O. Profession (Job Category): General Management Job Schedule: Full time Remote: No Job Description: The AI Research Engineer brings research discipline to practical technology validation at Hitachi Energy. The role interprets emerging AI research, methods, frameworks, models and evaluation approaches, and turns the most relevant developments into practical validation questions. It performs hands-on prototypes, benchmarks and comparisons to produce evidence before architecture, platform, acceleration or delivery commitments are made. How you will make an impact Review AI research, publications, benchmarks and model documentation, and identify developments that merit practical testing. Translate research insight into validation questions, fair experimental designs and baselines, together with the Experimentation Engineer and Opportunity Lead. Run research-led prototypes, benchmarks and comparisons, and interpret the results with clear limitations and proportionate recommendations. Exchange methods and learnings with Hitachi Group, DAAI peers, vendors and external research communities. Publication is not a standing expectation. Keep reusable methods, benchmarks and test assets where they prevent repeated work. Turn one finding into a concrete question, for example whether a new technique beats what we use today on our kind of data. Design the experiment: baseline, tasks, how success is judged, and what would invalidate the result. Run benchmarks and research-led prototypes in Python (LLMs, retrieval-augmented generation, agents, fine-tuning, responsible-AI checks). Your Background 3+ years in applied AI research, AI engineering or ML research, in a company, consultancy or research institution. Strong Python, with hands-on AI/ML experimentation, benchmarking and evaluation. Familiar with LLMs, generative AI, fine-tuning, RAG, agentic AI and responsible-AI evaluation. MSc or PhD in AI, machine learning or computer science, valued when combined with practical work. items.desc: Intro px dynamics is a small quantitative trading firm in Berlin and Cologne. We are four people. We trade European short-term power markets systematically, on our own account, and we sell trading signals to a few trading desks. We build and run everything ourselves: the data, the models, the execution and the servers. We are looking for one more person to research and run trading strategies with us. The problem What we try to understand is price formation in a physical system. The European power market is a stack of many technologies, from nuclear and gas to wind, solar and batteries, each with its own economics, interconnected across borders so that the price in one zone depends on the weather in another. The mix shifts continuously as the energy system transforms, and the market trades it down to the last minutes before delivery. It's a fantastically complex problem and nobody has run out of things to learn. A well-traded short-term market helps a system with a lot of wind and sun run efficiently, and we like that our work has that effect. What you would work on Price models for the intraday market, built from weather model output, fundamentals and our own order-book history. Trading strategies for the continuous intraday market, together with the sizing and the risk limits that go with them. Running what you build in production, and comparing what it did with what the backtest said it would do. You take each of these from the first idea to live trading, so we don't split the work much along the value chain. How we work The team has backgrounds in machine learning, particle physics, information systems and economics, and together over two decades of experience in energy markets. Everyone works across research, trading systems, data and infrastructure. We think people do their best work when it is truly theirs. Everyone also does the ordinary work, from scheduling to the occasional invoice, because we want to stay small, and a small team only works if everyone chips in. Live systems need looking after, so monitoring on weekends and holidays rotates through the team. Our stack is open source and our own code from top to bottom, and we run it ourselves, so anyone here can read and change every part of it. We write most of that code with AI coding assistants, and the repository, the documentation and the data are organised so that both people and models can work with them. Who you are You have a strong academic background in physics, statistics or another quantitative field, typically a PhD, but a master's degree and real work with real data count just as much. We care more about how you think than about the title. You want to understand the energy system itself, not only the methods you apply to it. The domain matters to us as much as the modelling. While you'll find plenty of support and knowledge in the team, you are comfortable taking ownership for your learning journey. You have a very strong understanding of statistics and genuinely view the world probabilistically. We value that more than familiarity with any particular class of models. You know what clean code and a clean architecture look like, and you hold the code to that standard whether you or an assistant wrote it. Writing Python by hand matters less than it used to; knowing when to do it anyway, for example when you are iterating on a statistical model, matters more. You do not need to be a software engineer. You would rather be corrected than be wrong, and you can take an idea all the way to production yourself. If you are unsure whether you meet all of this, apply anyway. We would rather see your application than not. Nice to have Experience in power markets or as a quant trader. Time series modelling. R, where it is the better tool. You are at home on Linux. Some familiarity with Rust or C. What we offer Hybrid work from our Berlin office 30 days vacation VSOP (virtual shares) Core hours roughly 9 to 5, and flexibility when life happens A small team where your models trade Practicalities English is our working language; German is helpful but not required. We welcome applications regardless of gender, background or where you studied, and we particularly welcome applications from women.

items.desc: The Leibniz Institute for Astrophysics Potsdam (AIP) is dedicated to astrophysical questions ranging from the study of our Sun to the evolution of the cosmos. The research focuses on the area of stars, the Sun and exoplanets, galactic and extragalactic astrophysics, and cosmology. A significant share of the work involves research and development in the area of astrophysical spectroscopy, astrophotonics and the research data infrastructure. The AIP fulfils its research mission through numerous national, European, and international collaborations. The institute is the successor to the Berlin Observatory, founded in 1700, and the Astrophysical Observatory Potsdam, founded in 1874, which was the first institute in the world to devote itself expressly to astrophysics. Since 1992, the AIP has been a member of the Leibniz Association. Around 200 people work at our institute, set in a beautiful park landscape in Potsdam, not far from Berlin. At the department of Galactic and Extragalactic Astrophysics, we are looking for a Tenure-track scientist (m/f/d) in the field of Dwarf galaxies with particular attention to the Magellanic Clouds. The successful applicant is expected to develop an independent research programme that well fits the scope of the Research group “Dwarf Galaxies and the Galactic Halo” led by Prof. Maria-Rosa Cioni. This includes the exploitation of data from space-based imaging (e.g. Euclid, Roman, HST/JWST) and large-scale spectroscopic (e.g. 4MOST, (Blue)MUSE, MOSAIC) facilities to study the assembly history and dynamical evolution of Dwarf galaxies. In particular, using resolved stellar populations of field and star clusters, in the Magellanic Clouds and their analogs. The appointment will be for an initial period of five years, with a tenure review to be carried out in the 4th year of the appointment. The successful candidate must have a Doctoral degree or equivalent in Physics, Astronomy, or a related field as well as Post-doctoral research experience and a proven trackrecord in astronomy research, preferably on the subject of dwarf galaxies or the Magellanic Clouds. The candidate is expected to attract external funding to support junior members and act as supervisor of undergraduate and graduate research projects. The AIP offers a modern working environment, spacious and well-equipped offices, travel support, an open collegial working atmosphere and good opportunities for internal and external training. Salary is based on professional experience and expertise following the German public service collective agreement (TV-L) with a pay grade of E14. Social benefits include health insurance, contributions to the German Pension Insurance and the company pension VBL, disability and survivors’ benefits as well as a subsidy for the public transport ticket. The position is suitable for part-time employment and the start date is foreseen for the summer or fall of 2027. To apply for this position, please submit a cover letter, a curriculum vitae including a list of publications, a research statement including future research directions (max. 3 pages), plus the names and contact details of three potential reference letter writers. Letter writers will be requested to upload their recommendation only for candidates that advance to the second stage of the selection process. Equal opportunities are an integral part of staff and organisational development at the AIP; therefore, applications from all genders are equally welcome. People with disabilities will be given preferential consideration where they have the same professional qualifications and skills. Your application documents will be made available to a selection committee, relevant bodies and officials. The position covers the full knowledge-development workflow: retrieving and packaging information, framing questions, identifying evidence, collecting and structuring data, quantitative analysis, visualization, and actionable insights. You will work closely with the Knowledge Hub Team and support analytical needs across the KCC Program Lines. ensure quality and traceability Conduct quantitative and statistical analysis and modelling, and run scenario analyses as required Build dashboards, visualizations, and practical analytical tools Use AI-assisted tools for research, coding, analysis, and evidence synthesis Automate recurring research and analytical workflows where useful Support KCC’s database infrastructure and emerging intelligence platform Contribute to methodologies, models, and analytical toolkits Translate findings into reports, presentations, data stories, and recommendations Collaborate with Program Lines, research institutions, technology partners, and other stakeholders in generating new information and insights You‘re good at Conducting applied research independently and systematically Structuring complex questions into solvable analytical problems Applying quantitative, logical, and problem-solving skills Working with complex, incomplete, and multi-source data Learning new analytical, digital, and AI tools quickly Working reliably, diligently, and with attention to detail Translating evidence into clear insights and visual narratives Dealing with ambiguity Collaborating proactively in an international team You bring 2-5 years of relevant experience in applied research, either in consulting, the logistics industry, or in a relevant analytics role related to supply chains and logistics Master’s degree in Logistics, Supply Chain Management, Economics, Engineering, Mathematics, Data Science, Statistics, or a related field Good understanding of logistics, freight transport, and supply chains Strong quantitative reasoning and hands-on experience working with data, analytical methods, and models Advanced proficiency in Excel and Power BI / Tableau; experience with Python or R is highly desirable Familiarity with standard research methods and tools in the industrial context Confident use of modern AI tools for research, analysis, coding, and automation; SQL, Git/GitHub, APIs, Power Automate, SharePoint, GIS, Azure, MCP, or similar tools are an asset Strong data storytelling and communication abilities; fluency in English and German You will work with The Research Analyst reports to the Head of Knowledge & Analytics and works closely with the Senior Data Analyst, the Data Analyst, the Communications Department, the Management & Operations Team, and the Program Line leaders to deliver applied research, analytical outputs, data products, and knowledge products supporting KCC’s programs and strategic initiatives. What you can expect Work in an enthusiastic and highly motivated international team committed to making a real positive impact on climate action A high degree of creative freedom High agility and speed of implementation A stimulating and diverse range of work within a strong Foundation network Personal and professional growth driven by your own initiative and engagement Additional information The Kuehne Climate Center (KCC) is a subsidiary of the Kuehne Foundation in Schindellegi, Switzerland. Established in 1976 by the Kuehne family, it is one of the largest foundations in the German-speaking world. As an operational foundation, it is involved in the areas of logistics, medicine, culture, and, since the beginning of 2023, climate action. The Foundation is independent, operational, and international. The KCC implements the Foundation’s climate action mandate. Its mission is to accelerate climate-compatible development within and through logistics systems. KCC works through applied research and thought leadership, project and advisory work, training and capacity building, with a particular focus on countries of the Global South. KCC is a globally operating think-and-do tank headquartered in Hamburg’s vibrant HafenCity. From here, we manage and support all our global projects, actively partnering with our regional teams and with institutions from around the world. items.desc: The Department of Biomedical Engineering offers top-level education and research in one of the most relevant and exciting scientific disciplines of the 21st century: engineering health. In combining engineering and life sciences, through challenge-based learning and a multidisciplinary approach in collaboration with hospitals, industry and others, the department addresses the great challenges of the future, striving to improve healthcare and society as a whole. Introduction Do you enjoy bringing structure to complex projects and working with researchers in an innovative academic environment? Are you organized, communicative and curious about research and new technologies? Would you like to contribute to innovative research projects while developing your knowledge of research funding and project development? If so, we are looking for you. Within the Project Development Office (PDO), you will help researchers navigate the different stages of a research project, from identifying funding opportunities and preparing grant proposals to facilitating a smooth transition towards project implementation. The PDO supports researchers throughout this process, ensuring that funding opportunities are identified, proposals are well prepared and projects can move smoothly from development to implementation. We are looking for a proactive and organized Junior Project Development Officer to strengthen our research support team. In this role, you will support researchers, project coordinators and experienced Project Development Officers with grant preparation, project administration, consortium coordination and project management activities. You will help ensure that funding applications and research projects run smoothly by keeping track of deadlines, documentation, communication and administrative processes. Job Description As a Junior Advisor Research Funding, you support researchers and experienced Project Development Officers in the preparation and coordination of research proposals and projects. You help ensure that the practical, administrative and organizational aspects of funding applications are handled accurately and efficiently, keeping track of deadlines, documentation and communication. A key part of your role is keeping track of the many moving parts involved in grant applications. You coordinate input from researchers and consortium partners, organize meetings, follow up on action points, monitor deadlines, perform compliance and completeness checks, and help set up applications in funding portals such as the European Commission Funding & Tenders Portal. You also maintain application records, project documentation and internal systems, and support communication activities where needed. Once a project is awarded, you help ensure a smooth transition from proposal development to project implementation. You will support the administration and coordination of running research projects, for example by monitoring deadlines and deliverables, organizing meetings, supporting reporting and maintaining collaborative project environments such as SharePoint. Within the Project Development Office of the Department of Biomedical Engineering, you will work closely with researchers, project coordinators and colleague Project Development Officer. You will be part of a team that supports innovative research throughout the project lifecycle. This role offers an opportunity to learn about research funding, project development and the research conducted within Biomedical Engineering, while contributing to the continuous improvement of research support processes. Job Requirements We are looking for a proactive and organized colleague who is eager to learn and interested in supporting innovative research. You bring: A Bachelor's or Master's degree, preferably in Biomedical Engineering, a related field, or another relevant discipline. Strong organizational and administrative skills, with an eye for detail and the ability to keep an overview of multiple tasks and deadlines. Excellent communication skills in English, both written and verbal. A proactive and hands-on approach: you take initiative, follow up on actions and make sure things keep moving. The ability to work effectively with different stakeholders, including researchers, colleagues and external partners. An interest in research, innovation and research funding, and the curiosity to learn how research projects are developed and funded. Affinity with digital tools and new technologies, and an interest in exploring how AI and other tools can improve the way we work. Experience with academic research, project management, research funding, or tools such as Microsoft Teams, SharePoint and online grant submission systems is a plus, but not required. If you are concerned that you don’t meet all the requirements sufficiently, but the job does excite you, then be sure to respond, we would love to look at your profile. The selected candidate will contribute to the development and implementation of legal, ethical and governance frameworks for the responsible sharing and reuse of human
items.desc: The Institute The Centre for Genomic Regulation (CRG) is an international biomedical research institute of excellence, based in Barcelona, Spain, with more than 400 scientists from 44 countries. The CRG is composed of an interdisciplinary, motivated and creative scientific team which is supported both by flexible and efficient administration and by high-end and innovative technologies. In September 2026, the Centre for Genomic Regulation (CRG) has received the renewal of the 'HR Excellence in Research' Award from the European Commission. This is a recognition of the Institute's commitment to developing an HR Strategy for Researchers, designed to bring the practices and procedures in line with the principles of the European Charter for Researchers and the Code of Conduct for the Recruitment of Researchers (Charter and Code). Please, check out our Recruitment Policy The role We are seeking a Health Data Sharing and Governance Specialist, AI and Research to support the European Genome-phenome Archive (EGA) at the intersection of law, biomedical research, data governance, open science and emerging technologies. The selected candidate will contribute to the development and implementation of legal, ethical and governance frameworks for the responsible sharing and reuse of human genomic, phenotypic and other sensitive biomedical data. The role will focus on translating complex legal and regulatory requirements into practical policies, agreements, procedures and guidance for researchers, data access committees and research infrastructures. Key areas will include data access and secondary use of biomedical data, data-sharing agreements, consent, data-use conditions, data protection, AI governance and emerging regulatory frameworks. The candidate will work closely with multidisciplinary EGA teams, EMBL-EBI and international partners, and contribute to European-funded projects related to biomedical data sharing, federated access, FAIR data and responsible AI. About the EGA The European Genome-Phenome Archive (EGA, www.ega-archive.org) is a secure service for the permanent archiving and sharing of sensitive genetic, phenotypic, and clinical data resulting from biomedical research projects. It currently hosts more than 16 petabytes of data, including over 3,700 studies and 8,600 datasets. Jointly managed by the Centre for Genomic Regulation (www.crg.eu)) in Barcelona and the European Bioinformatics Institute (EMBL-EBI, www.ebi.ac.uk) in Cambridge, the EGA is an active partner in numerous international and national projects and contributes to establishing global standards in genomics and health research. It plays a central role as a core data resource for ELIXIR (www.elixir-europe.org), a driver project of the Global Alliance for Genomics and Health (GA4GH,www.ga4gh.org), and a major contributor to precision medicine initiatives. The EGA team at the CRG is a diverse group of around 25 professionals, including bioinformaticians, developers, helpdesk officers, and project managers, working across disciplines to advance biomedical data sharing. Based at the Barcelona Biomedical Research Park (PRBB, www.prbb.org), and supported by the Barcelona Supercomputing Center (BSC, www.bsc.es) and Universitat Pompeu Fabra (UPF,www.upf.edu), the EGA provides advanced services to the international research community and continues to grow steadily in both scale and impact. Whom would we like to hire? Professional experience Must Have A degree in Law, with an advanced postgraduate degree in a relevant area such as health law, data protection, technology law, artificial intelligence governance, bioethics or biomedical data governance Research experience at the intersection of law, artificial intelligence, and data governance, including legal and ethical analysis of biomedical data sharing, AI regulation, and emerging governance frameworks Experience developing data access policies, data-sharing agreements, consent templates, and governance best practices, with a focus on translating complex legal and regulatory requirements into practical frameworks for health-sector and research stakeholders.
