items.desc: Exeter, South West England, EX1 3PB Job Summary We’re looking for an exceptional Scientific Software Engineer to help us make a difference to our planet. As our Scientific Software Engineer, the job may be suitable for hybrid working, which is where an employee works part of the week in the office and part of the week from home. This is a voluntary, non-contractual arrangement and the location advertised will be your contractual place of work. Our opportunity is full time, 37 hours per week. Our people are at the heart of what we do and we'll do our best to agree a working pattern that works for everyone. World changing work From science to technology, from meteorology to management, and from planning to communication, our expertise helps us stand out as the authority on weather accuracy and climate prediction. We help individuals, industries and government to make better decisions to stay safe and thrive. This is the Met Office. This is who we are. We’re a force for good - focusing on our environmental and social impact We’re experts by nature - always learning and developing to do things better We live and breathe it - putting our purpose at the heart of decision-making We’re better together - understanding partnerships and inclusivity make us greater We keep evolving - pushing boundaries to make tomorrow better for our customers Your world of expertise This role as a Scientific Software Engineer sits within the data-driven climate modelling project in the AI4Climate initiative at the Met Office Hadley Centre, where we are combining machine learning, deep learning data science, climate science, and high-performance computing to develop faster, more flexible approaches to climate predictions for downstream applications. We are looking for an exceptional SSE with strong data science and software engineering skills. You will work at the intersection of AI and climate science, developing and explainable novel machine learning approaches for climate prediction and understanding how data-driven models (DDCMs) represent the Earth system. You will help advance scientific understanding of DDCMs and their role within future climate modelling systems. You will join a multidisciplinary group of climate scientists, data scientists and software engineers, working closely with partners across the Met Office and internationally. You will help to join our pioneering work in DDCM as part of the Met Office AI4Climate initiative. Work collaboratively with climate scientists, software engineers and internal and external research partners. items.desc: Quant Researcher, HFT Futures Firm: Leading global proprietary trading firm About the firm Our client is a highly successful proprietary trading firm. It trades only its own capital, with no clients and no outside investors. It’s a leader in high-frequency and low-latency trading across global futures markets. The culture is collaborative and driven by technology, with small, flat teams where researchers own their ideas from first hypothesis through to live trading and PnL. The role You’ll join a small, high-impact team researching and building fully automated high-frequency strategies on major futures exchanges, including CME, Eurex, ICE and SGX. The role is hands-on and end to end: you’ll find alpha in tick-level and order book data, build signals and execution logic, and work closely with traders and engineers to take strategies live and improve them. What you’ll do Research and develop short-horizon alpha signals from tick-level market data and full-depth order book data. Build, backtest and validate HFT strategies with rigorous statistics, accounting for latency, queue position, fees and market impact. Model market microstructure: order flow, liquidity, price formation and cross-asset or cross-venue relationships. Optimise execution, fill probability and risk management for live strategies. Monitor live performance, diagnose PnL drivers and keep improving strategies as market conditions change. Work with software engineers on research infrastructure, simulators and low-latency production code. What we’re looking for 2+ years in quantitative research at an HFT or market-making firm, ideally in futures. A track record of strategies that made live PnL is strongly preferred. An advanced degree (PhD or MSc) in a quantitative field such as mathematics, statistics, physics, computer science or engineering, from a top university. Strong grounding in statistics, time-series analysis and machine learning, applied to noisy, high-frequency data. Excellent programming skills in Python, plus C++ for performance-critical research or production code. A deep understanding of futures market microstructure, matching engines and order book dynamics. Comfort working with large datasets (billions of rows) and a strong engineering mindset around research tooling. An entrepreneurial, PnL-focused approach. You’re intellectually honest about what works and what doesn’t. Nice to have Experience across several futures asset classes (rates, equity indices, commodities, FX). Experience with kdb+/q or similar time-series databases. Knowledge of FPGA or ultra-low-latency trading systems. What’s on offer Highly competitive compensation: market-leading base plus a significant discretionary or PnL-linked bonus. Direct ownership of strategies, with clear visibility of your impact on PnL. Best-in-class infrastructure, data and computing resources. A collaborative, non-hierarchical environment alongside some of the strongest researchers in the industry. [Benefits: relocation support, visa sponsorship, health cover, meals, etc.]

items.desc: À propos de l’entreprise Depuis 1967, SEBIA est un acteur mondial spécialisé dans le diagnostic in vitro qui fournit des équipements et des réactifs pour le dépistage et le suivi de diverses maladies, principalement dans les domaines de l’oncologie (myélome multiple), du diabète, de l’hémoglobinopathie, des maladies auto-immunes et infectieuses et d’autres pathologies rares. La mission de Sebia est de fournir des outils puissants qui traduisent ce qui se passe dans le corps d’un patient dans un langage lisible et interprétable. Nous l’appelons notre nouveau langage de vie. À propos du poste Dans le cadre du développement de nouveaux biomarqueurs, le/la biostatisticien(ne) contribuera à la conception et à l’analyse des études visant à démontrer leur pertinence scientifique et clinique et à évaluer leur potentiel dans les différents cas d’usage identifiés. Intégré(e) à une équipe multidisciplinaire associant scientifiques, R&D, experts cliniques et chefs de projet, il/elle apportera son expertise statistique depuis la conception des études jusqu’à l’interprétation des résultats. Le poste constitue une fonction de support scientifique et clinique permettant de transformer les données générées par le programme en éléments de preuve robustes et interprétables. Vos missions Conception des études Contribuer à la définition des objectifs et des critères d’évaluation des études. Participer à la définition des populations d’étude, variables d’intérêt et stratégies d’analyse. Proposer les approches statistiques adaptées aux questions scientifiques et cliniques. Identifier les principaux biais, facteurs de confusion et limites susceptibles d’affecter l’interprétation des résultats. Contribuer, lorsque nécessaire, à la justification des tailles d’échantillon. Analyse et interprétation des données Réaliser les analyses statistiques des études scientifiques et cliniques du programme. Étudier les relations entre les biomarqueurs et les données cliniques ou biologiques disponibles. Évaluer la pertinence des biomarqueurs pour les différents cas d’usage étudiés. Contribuer à l’identification des populations ou sous-populations pour lesquelles les biomarqueurs pourraient présenter un intérêt particulier. Contribution à la démonstration de la valeur des biomarqueurs Contribuer à définir les données nécessaires pour présenter et démontrer la pertinence des biomarqueurs. Participer à l’évaluation de leur potentiel diagnostique, pronostique, prédictif ou de stratification, selon les cas d’usage. Identifier les éventuels besoins en données complémentaires. Apporter une analyse statistique objective aux décisions de poursuite, d’orientation ou de révision des travaux. Contribution aux publications et à la communication scientifique Participer à la préparation des résultats pour les présentations scientifiques, publications et congrès. Contribuer à la préparation des données et analyses destinées aux échanges avec les KOLs et experts externes. Participer à la rédaction et à la revue des parties statistiques des rapports et publications. Il/elle devra être capable de traduire une question scientifique ou clinique en une approche statistique adaptée et d’expliquer simplement les résultats à des interlocuteurs non spécialistes de la statistique. Qualifications Formation supérieure (Ingénieur, PhD) en biostatistiques, statistiques, épidémiologie, mathématiques appliquées ou domaine équivalent. Une formation en sciences biomédicales ou en recherche clinique constitue un atout. Compétences requises Une première expérience en biostatistiques appliquées aux sciences de la vie, à la recherche clinique, aux biomarqueurs ou à un domaine comparable est souhaitée. Une expérience en analyse de données biomédicales ou cliniques serait particulièrement appréciée. Bonne maîtrise des méthodes statistiques appliquées aux données biomédicales. Maîtrise de R, SAS, Python ou d’un environnement statistique équivalent. Capacité à concevoir et interpréter des analyses statistiques adaptées aux questions posées. Bonne compréhension des problématiques liées aux études cliniques et/ou aux biomarqueurs. Capacité à communiquer clairement des résultats statistiques à des interlocuteurs scientifiques et médicaux. Compétences souhaitées On vous reconnait les qualités et aptitudes professionnelles suivantes : Rigueur scientifique et esprit critique. Capacité d’analyse et de synthèse. Curiosité scientifique. Autonomie et pragmatisme. Goût du travail en équipe multidisciplinaire. Capacité à évoluer dans un environnement de recherche en développement, où les questions et les hypothèses peuvent encore évoluer. Vous vous reconnaissez dans cette description ? Rejoignez un projet qui fait sens, rejoignez nos équipes, rejoignez SEBIA ! items.desc: The Scientific Computing Center (SCC) is a central scientific institution at KIT that supports research, teaching, and innovation, and provides cross-functional services within KIT and to external parties. Curious about an exciting and versatile role in an agile team? Discover more about SCC as your professional place to be: https://www.scc.kit.edu/en/aboutus/working-at-scc.php We look forward to receiving your application, including a cover letter, resume, and transcripts. Your Tasks You will be involved in research software engineering (RSE) in the context of high-performance computing in the field of materials research. An important focus of your work is the development of domain-specific languages and supporting tools as interfaces to improve the usability of the codes, models, and data, as well as the productivity of end users, the reusability of code and data, and thus to avoid unnecessary calculations. You will conduct methodological research and actively participate in the planning, implementation, and testing of new features, as well as in bug fixes. Another task is the continuous maintenance of software repositories and databases. You will publish the results of your methodological research at conferences and in seminars. Furthermore, you will support users in the use of the newly developed tools in their projects and occasionally organize tutorials for them. Interest in working on an interdisciplinary project with scientific and technical challenges, as well as solving the tasks in the project independently or together with an interdisciplinary team in a short period of time Experience in dealing with cooperation partners and customers is an advantage. items.desc: About Quandela: Quandela is a global leader in quantum computing, designing, building, and delivering cutting-edge quantum solutions for research and industry. Its offerings include the most energy-efficient quantum computers for data centers, full-stack quantum computing solutions accessible via the cloud, and algorithm access services for academic and industrial customers. Following a pragmatic, step-by-step roadmap, Quandela has been deploying industrial-grade systems since 2023 while developing future generations of fault-tolerant quantum computers capable of scaling through the integration of thousands of photonic components. Quandela is committed to making quantum computing accessible to all in order to address the most complex industrial and societal challenges. Learn more at: Quandela | Leading Photonic Quantum Computing Solutions Our ambition is to build large-scale fault-tolerant quantum computers. Before reaching full fault tolerance, intermediate architectures will continue to operate under significant hardware and noise constraints, making error mitigation an important part of understanding and improving their performance. About this position: You will join Quandela's Quantum Information team within Architecture , working at the interface between quantum information theory, architecture performance and fault-tolerant quantum computing. The team develops methods to benchmark, characterise and evaluate the computational performance of Quandela's current and future architectures, helping guide hardware and architecture decisions. We are now looking to build dedicated expertise in Quantum Error Mitigation (QEM) . You will develop and assess mitigation methods adapted to our photonic and spin-photonic systems, working closely with Quantum Information, Device Physics and FTQC researchers. Your goal will be to understand how QEM can improve computation fidelity and extend the useful depth of quantum circuits, while assessing its cost, limitations and interaction with error correction on realistic architectures. Requirements What you'll do: As a Quantum Information Scientist working on Quantum Error Mitigation, you will: Develop and adapt QEM methods for photonic and spin-photonic architectures. Evaluate their performance, feasibility and implementation cost. Study how mitigation and Quantum Error Correction can complement each other across different operating regimes. Use realistic noise models and hardware constraints to assess their impact on computational fidelity and achievable circuit depth. Build scientific prototypes and numerical tools to test and compare different approaches. Work closely with FTQC and Device Physics researchers on noise, errors and architecture-level trade-offs. Contribute to benchmarking and broader performance-analysis activities within the team. As methods mature, collaborate with Q.Algorithms and Software teams on application-level studies and implementation. How you'll grow: During your first 3 months: become familiar with Quandela's architectures, noise models and FTQC roadmap, and identify relevant mitigation approaches. Within 6-12 months: develop and test QEM methods adapted to our systems and take increasing ownership of QEM / QEC and performance studies. Longer term: help shape how mitigation is used across future architectures and explore applications of mature methods at algorithm and software level. - What we're looking for: We are looking for a researcher with hands-on experience in Quantum Error Mitigation and an interest in applying quantum-information theory to real quantum-computing systems. Your background may also include noisy quantum systems, QEC, benchmarking or hardware-aware quantum computing. What matters is that you have already worked directly with mitigation methods and can adapt them to new physical constraints. - Must-have: PhD in Quantum Information, Quantum Computing, Theoretical Physics or a closely related field. Research experience in Quantum Error Mitigation , through the development, analysis or application of mitigation methods. Good understanding of noisy quantum systems and how errors affect quantum computations. Ability to critically assess scientific literature and adapt existing methods to new systems or architectures. Experience with scientific programming and numerical simulation, typically in Python. Scientific autonomy Collaborative and personable, with the ability to communicate ideas clearly to people from other fields of expertise. Professional English. Important, but you can grow here: Quantum Error Correction and early fault-tolerant quantum computing. Understanding of QEM / QEC trade-offs, including overhead and computational performance Hardware-specific noise models and architecture constraints. Quantum benchmarking and performance evaluation Experience working with experimental or hardware-oriented quantum-computing teams. Scientific communication through publications, conferences or technical presentations. Bonus: …

items.card: You will work closely with our multidisciplinary team to develop, optimise, and scale up a new class of organic electrolytes for redox flow batteries, aligning with our mission and business goals. Key Responsibilities: · Conduct experimental work to benchmark our proprietary electrolytes against existing alternatives. · Perform battery testing, including galvanostatic charge-discharge cycling, capacity retention
items.desc: Kodiaq Technologies Ltd is a spin-out from the University of Cambridge focusing on the commercialisation of high-energy-density electrolytes for redox flow batteries. We aim to transform the energy storage landscape through providing innovative solutions to real-world energy applications. As a dynamic start-up, Kodiaq encourages innovation, agility and a collaborative culture where every team member plays a crucial role in our success. This is an exciting opportunity to join the company at a pivotal stage in its development as expand our laboratory and R&D programmes. Position Overview: We are seeking a highly motivated, enthusiastic, and skilled Battery Researcher to join and strengthen our growing team. The ideal candidate will have a strong passion for research and development, with a focus on battery testing and benchmarking. You will work closely with our multidisciplinary team to develop, optimise, and scale up a new class of organic electrolytes for redox flow batteries, aligning with our mission and business goals. Key Responsibilities: · Conduct experimental work to benchmark our proprietary electrolytes against existing alternatives. · Perform battery testing, including galvanostatic charge-discharge cycling, capacity retention analysis, Coulombic efficiency and round-trip efficiency monitoring, and post-mortem analysis of electrolyte chemistry. · Perform electrochemical characterisation using techniques such as cyclic voltammetry (CV), rotating disk electrode (RDE) analysis, and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS). · Analyse and interpret data to guide electrolyte formulation and optimisation. · Collaborate with chemists and other scientists to integrate electrochemical insights into product development. · Maintain detailed records of experiments, protocols, and results. · Ensure all laboratory practices comply with safety regulations and company standards. · Stay informed about recent advances in the field and apply relevant knowledge to ongoing projects. Requirements: · PhD in Chemistry, Chemical engineering, or a relevant field. · Minimum of 4 years of experience in research; your PhD experience counts. · Strong hands-on experience in battery research and electrochemistry. Experimental work with redox flow batteries and a variety of organic electrolyte chemistries is an advantage. · Proficiency with chemistry lab software for data analysis. · Programming experience (Python/Matlab) for data analysis is an advantage. · Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to design and execute complex experiments. · Strong communication and collaboration skills, especially in multidisciplinary environment. · Highly self-motivated, organised, and able to manage multiple priorities effectively. What We Offer: A dynamic start-up culture where innovation and initiative are encouraged and valued. The opportunity to play a key role in a growing company with a purpose-driven mission. Meaningful responsibility from day one - we value ownership and accountability. A supportive and inclusive team that values your ideas and contributions. Laboratories in Cambridge, with access to well-equipped research facilities in one of the world's leading research hubs; putting you close to world-class academic institutions, a thriving deep-tech and biotech scene, and rich opportunities to network and connect with the wider scientific community Opportunities for training and progression as the company and lab scale up. The chance to contribute to cutting-edge projects with real-world applications in energy storage. Join us at Kodiaq Technologies Ltd and be part of a team that is shaping the future of energy storage! How to Apply: If you are excited about this opportunity and believe you have the right skills and mindset, we would love to hear from you! Please send your CV, a cover letter outlining your relevant experience, and any supporting materials (e.g., references, list of publications, or patent portfolio) to kodiaq@kodiaqtech.com with the subject line: “Battery Researcher Application – [Your Name]”. Kodiaq Technologies Ltd is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

items.card: Responsibilities And Duties Are developing global emissions inventories for current and next-generation aircraft under scenarios to 2050, including landing and take-off modelling; developing, evaluating and applying near-airport air quality modelling capabilities; collaborating with consortium partners and contributing to project deliverables; publishing and presenting research results. The skills, qualifications
items.desc: Hydrogen and electric aircraft could transform aviation's climate and air quality footprint, but their environmental impacts remain poorly quantified. A position exists, for a Research Assistant/Associate in the Department of Engineering, to work on the Environmental Impacts of Next-Generation Aircraft, developing aircraft emissions and air quality models as part of the EU-funded SESAR project ZENITIA. The post holder will join Dr Irene Dedoussi's group at the Whittle Laboratory and work with project partners including UC3M, Imperial, TU Delft and Boeing. The research will inform airport and air traffic management and European aviation policy. The Key Responsibilities And Duties Are developing global emissions inventories for current and next-generation aircraft under scenarios to 2050, including landing and take-off modelling; developing, evaluating and applying near-airport air quality modelling capabilities; collaborating with consortium partners and contributing to project deliverables; publishing and presenting research results. The skills, qualifications and experience required to perform the role are: has obtained or is close to obtaining a PhD in aerospace, mechanical or chemical engineering, atmospheric or environmental science, physics, applied mathematics or a related field; experience in modelling physical systems (e.g. atmospheric modelling, aircraft performance, propulsion, combustion or fluid dynamics); strong scientific programming skills; a publication record appropriate to career stage and excellent communication skills. Experience in aviation emissions, chemistry transport, dispersion or air quality modelling is desirable. Appointment at Research Associate level is dependent on having a PhD. Those who have submitted but not yet received their PhD will be appointed at Research Assistant level, which will be amended to Research Associate once the PhD has been awarded. Salary Ranges Research Assistant: £33,002 - £35,608 Research Associate: £37,694 - £46,049 Fixed-term: The funding is for 24 months or until 28 February 2029, whichever of these comes soonest. Click the 'Apply' button below to register an account with our recruitment system (if you have not already) and apply online. Please ensure that you upload your Curriculum Vitae (CV), including a list of publications, a covering letter, and your most representative research publication in the Upload section of the online application. If you upload any additional documents which have not been requested, we will not be able to consider these as part of your application. Please submit your application by midnight on the closing date, although early applications are strongly encouraged. If you have any questions about this vacancy, please contact Dr Irene Dedoussi at icd23@cam.ac.uk for queries of a technical nature related to the role, and Juliet Teather at jet63@eng.cam.ac.uk for queries related to the application process. Please quote reference NM51382 on your application and in any correspondence about this vacancy. The University actively supports equality, diversity and inclusion and encourages applications from all sections of society. The University has a responsibility to ensure that all employees are eligible to live and work in the UK.

items.desc:
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is looking for a Solutions Architect to join our Telco, Media, Entertainment, Games and Sports (TMEGS) team in the UK and Ireland, focusing on customers in Advertising, Publishing and Information Services. As a trusted technical advisor, you will help advertisers, ad tech platforms, publishers and information providers innovate and transform their business using AWS technologies, including generative AI and machine learning.
Solutions Architects work hand in hand with AWS customers to help them make the most of the Cloud. They own the overall technical relationship between customers and AWS and make recommendations on security, cost, performance, reliability and operational efficiency. They work to understand the customer's business needs and give prescriptive guidance on how to create business value with technology. To do this they collaborate with other teams such as account management, professional services, support, product teams and the AWS partner ecosystem.
AI is transforming Advertising, Publishing and Information Services. Publishers are rethinking how content is created, personalised and licensed. Advertisers and ad tech companies are reshaping targeting, measurement and creative production in a privacy-first world. Information services providers are turning large proprietary datasets into intelligent products. In this role you will get to practice your creativity, linking technology to tangible solutions and educating customers about the art of the possible. You will work closely with Account Managers to help customers achieve their outcomes using AWS technology.
We're looking for someone passionate and self-driven, who is curious about how technology shapes media and information, and who enjoys taking ownership of customer outcomes with limited guidance.
The Solutions Architecture team is a diverse group of technologists from a variety of backgrounds. Practical knowledge of the AWS platform is desired but not required, provided you have a sound technical foundation and a desire to learn.
Key job responsibilities
• Own the technical relationship with your customers and operate as their trusted advisor. The best interests of the customer will shape the guidance you provide
• Work backwards from customer needs to define the right solution path, then design and deliver secure, scalable and cost-effective solutions using AWS services, with a focus on generative AI, machine learning and data analytics
• Run technical discussions, architecture design sessions and workshops across use cases such as content creation and management, audience and data platforms, ad tech, clean rooms and measurement, content discovery and personalisation, and data and knowledge products
• Help customers move AI/ML workloads from experimentation into production, making sound trade-offs between time, quality and cost
• Contribute to account plans and customer engagement strategies alongside your Account Manager, and collaborate with specialist, partner and service teams to meet customer goals
• Identify risks early in customer engagements and decide when to resolve them yourself and when to escalate
• Write clear technical documentation and create content, demos and reference architectures for Advertising, Publishing and Information Services use cases
• Capture and share customer feedback with AWS service teams to help shape future services and features
• Share knowledge with your team, take part in peer reviews and support newer team members
About the team
The UKI Advertising, Publishing and Information Services team is part of the wider AWS TMEGS organisation. We work with well-known media, marketing and data brands in the UK and Ireland, from national news and book publishers to ad tech platforms and specialist information providers. We're a close-knit, collaborative team that values ownership, curiosity and learning from each other.
About AWS
Diverse Experiences
AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn't followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don't let it stop you from applying.
Why AWS?
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world's most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that's why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.
Inclusive Team Culture
AWS values curiosity and connection. Our employee-led and company-sponsored affinity groups promote inclusion and empower our people to take pride in what makes us unique. Our inclusion events foster stronger, more collaborative teams. Our continual innovation is fueled by the bold ideas, fresh perspectives, and passionate voices our teams bring to everything we do.

Together, we foster an environment where innovation and collaboration thrive.
 Every day, we face exciting new challenges and opportunities to contribute to cutting-edge research that shapes our understanding of the universe. items.desc:
Fellow position 
 Location: Center for Advanced Biomaterials for Health Care (CABHC), Naples 
 Step into a world of endless possibilities, together let’s leave something for the future! 
 At IIT, we are committed to advancing human-centered Science and Technology to address the most urgent societal challenges of our era. We foster excellence in both fundamental and applied research, spanning fields such as neuroscience and cognition, humanoid technologies and robotics, artificial intelligence, nanotechnology, and material sciences, offering a truly interdisciplinary scientific experience. Our approach integrates cutting-edge tools and technology, empowering researchers to push the limits of knowledge and innovation. With us, your curiosity will know no bounds.
 We are dedicated to providing equal employment opportunities and fostering diversity in all its forms, creating an inclusive environment. We value the unique experiences, knowledge, backgrounds, cultures, and perspectives of our people. By embracing diversity, we believe science can achieve its fullest potential.
 THE ROLE 
 You will be working in a multicultural and multi-disciplinary group, where junior and senior scientists collaborate, each with their expertise, to carry out a scientific activity with a shared research goal.
 The Bio-logic Research unit is coordinated by Prof. Paolo Netti . The research focuses on the engineering and characterization of advanced in vitro systems reproducing key features of physiological and pathological tissue microenvironments. The activity will combine fabrication approaches, advanced cell culture and quantitative imaging to investigate how cellular morphology, organization, and behavior are modulated by biochemical, physical, and mechanical stimuli.
 Within the research team, your main responsibilities will be:
 Fabrication and optimization of 3D in vitro and microphysiological systems for the generation of controlled cellular microenvironments
 Culture and characterization of cells within engineered systems under different experimental conditions
 Immunofluorescence and advanced cell imaging for morphological and functional characterization
 Quantitative investigation of cell morphology, deformation, organization, and phenotypic changes in response to external stimuli
 ESSENTIAL REQUIREMENTS 
 A MSc degree in Biomedical Engineering, Bioengineering, Biotechnology , or related disciplines
 Documented experience with mammalian cell culture and advanced 3D in vitro models 
 Experience or academic training in microfabrication, microfluidics, biomaterials, or fabrication of engineered cell culture platforms 
 Experience with fluorescence microscopy, immunofluorescence, and cell imaging 
 Familiarity with the quantitative characterization of cellular morphology and behavior in response to controlled stimuli 
 Good command of spoken and written English
 ADDITIONAL SKILLS 
 Experience with 3D cell culture, dynamic culture systems, or microfluidic devices is considered a plus
 Familiarity with image-analysis tools for quantitative assessment of cell morphology, deformation, migration, or organization
 Ability to work in a challenging and international environment
 Capacity to work autonomously and collaboratively in a highly interdisciplinary environment
 Possess Analytical Reasoning skills and a growth mindset
 COMPENSATION PACKAGE 
 A yearly gross salary of 30.000,00
 Private health care coverage depending on your role and contract

items.card: You will not meet all six in one assignment, and the exact tools depend on where you land. But across your assignments, your training and your mentor, you get hands-on with several and learn about all six . Problem definition. items.desc: Value doesn't come from building more. It comes from building the right thing: something the business truly needs, people actually use, technology can support, and where AI and data are used responsibly. That takes understanding what the business is truly struggling with, separating hype from impact, and deciding which problem is worth solving first. That bridge between technology, business and people is where the value sits now, and no agent is taking it over . Belgian companies are investing in AI and data, but many are still working out what to do with it. That's where you come in. Here's how. THE TRAINEESHIP IN SHORT By doing the work, with the right people around you. 26 months. One contract with Ormit Talent. Two to three AI and data assignments at different client companies. You don't just sharpen your AI and data skills. You build the business sense and people skills that make them count, with training, coaching, expert mentoring and a group of peers behind you. Why does that matter? Most data jobs make you better at the tech and leave the rest to chance. Here, you build all three. That's why our clients hand you work they'd normally save for someone years further along. WHAT YOU'LL ACTUALLY WORK ON Which assignments will you get? We can't tell you yet. Each one comes with its own context, questions and level of AI and data maturity, and asks a bit more of you than the last. What stays the same is the mix: hard skills in AI and data, the business sense to know what's really needed, and the people skills to get others on board. In practice, that mix comes down to six areas. We saw them come back assignment after assignment at our clients. You will not meet all six in one assignment, and the exact tools depend on where you land. But across your assignments, your training and your mentor, you get hands-on with several and learn about all six . Problem definition. Where every good project starts: turning vague requests into clear data questions. Which decision does it support? What does success look like, and is the data even there? Data analysis. The hands-on part. You clean and test datasets, find the quality issues and the anomalies, and challenge the data someone else hands you. Often in SQL and Excel, sometimes Python where the question calls for it. Insights creation. Where data turns into decisions. You build dashboards in Power BI or Tableau that someone actually decides with, not reports that describe what already happened. Plus the storytelling that gets them read. Smart automation. Where the manual work disappears. You spot the tasks that keep coming back and get rid of them, with Power Automate, an API integration or an AI agent where it earns its place. And you judge a tool on what it delivers, not on how new it is. Responsible AI and data use. Where trust gets built. You check for bias and data quality, explain what a model does and doesn't do, know which rules you're working under, and build together on clear data governance. Translation to business and IT. Where it all lands. You explain the constraint to the business and the priority to the data engineers. And you set expectations before the work starts, not when the deadline moves. TRAINING Your training runs on two tracks, and both count. On the technical side , you get room to go deeper: certifications, a platform subscription or dedicated time to master the tools your assignments ask for, with your technical mentor to challenge your approach. On the business and people side , the core trainings are the same for everyone. It starts with discovering who you are. From there, you build towards working better with others, getting to the core of what a business needs, and bringing people along. Then you put it to the test. In a hackathon and a real client case , you sit in the decision maker's seat and weigh opportunities, risks and competing priorities, not just the data question. Experts watch and give you feedback on your approach. "Let's be honest: I signed for the hard skills. If the programme hadn't been technical enough, I wouldn't have signed at all. The training and coaching on human skills? A nice bonus, I thought. Looking back, that's exactly what took me to the next level. I just didn't know what I didn't know." Louis – Alumnus Data traineeship COACHING & MENTORING Most people only get a coach once they're managing a team. You get one from day one. Every month , you sit down with your Ormit Talent coach to talk about how it's really going. They'll challenge you, give you sharp feedback and practical advice , and ask the occasional question you'd rather not answer. That's the point. Together you work on how you show up: in a tough meeting, with a sceptical stakeholder, when a project shifts under your feet. Step by step, you widen your range, until the situations that used to feel uncomfortable become the ones you handle best . Your coach helps you grow as a person. Develop and improve time-series forecasting models for industrial electricity consumption, PV generation, and other energy-relevant
items.desc: Looking for an opportunity to shape our future sustainably? Then, adjusted flow is your place to be! We are developing a software platform for energy-intensive manufacturers to optimize the use of on-site flexibility in terms of generation and consumption... Our goal: to drive the energy transition where it has the greatest impact—in industry. We are just getting started and are currently laying the groundwork for a scalable product. To this end, we are looking for an Energy Forecasting & Optimization Engineer (m/f/d) to support us in building and further developing our platform. Aufgaben You will work on the forecasting and optimization core of EOIS for industrial energy optimization. The role combines deterministic and probabilistic forecasting, uncertainty modeling, mathematical optimization, simulation, and production integration for live industrial systems. Develop and improve time-series forecasting models for industrial electricity consumption, PV generation, and other energy-relevant signals Extend and improve forecast services with probabilistic outputs Develop and improve optimization models for industrial energy flexibility, production-related decisions, storage systems, and other controllable assets Evaluate forecasting and optimization quality on noisy, incomplete, and non-stationary industrial data, including their actual operational and economic impact Design how forecasts, uncertainty measures, physical constraints, and system states are used in downstream optimization workflows Build and improve simulation, replay, benchmarking, and validation workflows to test model behavior before and alongside deployment in live systems Improve robustness through plausibility checks, fallback behavior, re-forecasting, and handling of low-confidence or missing data Support validation and technical interpretation of model behavior in real customer environments Qualifikation Your Personality Profile We’re not looking for a perfect checklist—we’re looking for people who think for themselves, ask questions, and are eager to really build something. You don’t wait for someone to tell you what to do; you contribute your own ideas You question things that aren’t working well and bring your own ideas to the table You have no problem disagreeing with us if you’re convinced there are better solutions You’re eager to take on responsibility—even if everything isn’t perfectly defined yet... In terms of technical skills, you should have experience in several of these areas: Should have skills strong applied experience in time-series and probabilistic forecasting forecast calibration, uncertainty evaluation, backtesting, and model validation strong understanding of mathematical optimization, especially LP/MILP ability to model real-world systems through objectives, constraints, and operational rules experience combining forecasts, uncertainty, optimization, and LLM-based orchestration of time-series pipelines experience working with noisy and incomplete real-world data ability to turn models into reliable production services Helpful skills industrial energy systems, electricity markets, PV, BESS, or flexible loads simulation, replay testing, or benchmarking frameworks industrial hardware and control systems basic thermodynamics model deployment, monitoring, or explainability You don’t have to be an expert in all of these areas. What matters most is that you’re willing to dive deep, understand the underlying problem, and implement robust solutions. Entrando nel team AI Promotion & Governance , contribuirai alla definizione e all'evoluzione del modello di adozione dell'AI del Gruppo, collaborando con funzioni business, tecnologiche e di controllo per favorire uno sviluppo responsabile, sicuro e orientato al valore delle soluzioni di Intelligenza Artificiale. items.desc: Your role & How we work We are hiring an AI Engineer (m/f/d) to holistically develop BIT Capital's LLM and agentic Artifical Intelligence capabilities: from the data science that turns data into investment signals, to the engineering that powers our financial intelligence agents. A strong initial focus is the build-out of “Aion” - our agentic research platform - that has first-class access to our data, models, and tools and is already in mainstream production, used by the investment team every day. Beyond, your mandate covers everything LLM- and agent-related across BIT, from research products for the investment team to internal tools in Sales, Marketing, Operations, and client-facing experiences. You work autonomously, from first scoping to shipping, and you self-select the use cases and projects where you can have the most impact. You report to our Carlos Bielsa (Chief AI Officer & Managing Partner) and work side by side with Vlad Gheorghe, our second AI Engineer, acting as our internal expert as the frontier of AI moves. Our stack is Python, SQL, AWS, and Databricks, with models and agentic frameworks from the leading AI labs (Anthropic Managed Agents, Codex). Your priorities in this role will thus include: Investment signal pipelines. Design and ship LLM-based extraction pipelines (prompts, retrieval, model selection, evaluations) that turn text and data into investment scores, alerts, signals, and insights reliable enough to drive decisions. Agentic systems behind “Aion”. Build and evolve the agentic systems that power Aion, along with the research skills and Python sidecars that agents execute. Data and tool integrations. Build the integrations that give agents performant, safe access to BIT's data and capabilities. Evaluations and model selection. Build automated and human-in-the-loop evaluations, regression tests, and monitoring that track accuracy, hallucination rates, latency, cost, and model uncertainty. Benchmark and select the right model per task, including open-source options. LLMOps at scale. Establish the LLMOps practices that keep these systems reliable at scale: versioning of prompts, configs, and models; CI/CD; error handling; fallbacks; and cost control. Frontier into production. Stay at the frontier of LLM and agentic AI techniques and bring new ideas into production rather than leaving them as experiments. The experience you bring You have a solid data science and engineering background, with at least 2 years building software, data systems, or ML in production. You adopt the mindset of a product-minded software engineer. You have shipped your own apps and agents and can point us to a public project, repo, or product. You are fluent with the current LLM and agentic frontier, with hands-on experience using leading agentic systems (Claude Code, Anthropic Managed Agents, Codex, open-source agentic loops). You have strong Python and SQL skills with clean engineering practices, plus cloud infrastructure experience (AWS strongly preferred). You bring production discipline for probabilistic systems: evaluations, regression tests, monitoring, reproducibility, and cost awareness. A scientific approach to turning LLMs into signals and scores (ground-truth datasets, train/test/iterate) is a plus; a data science or ML background helps but is not required. You have a genuine interest in investing, or at minimum a strong drive to learn about our domain quickly and deeply, paired with sharp general intelligence and clear systems thinking. 2 reasons why you should not apply You mainly use AI tools for your own productivity and have not yet taken systems into production. This role is about building and shipping AI that the whole firm relies on, so prior production experience matters here. You are looking for a finished, stable AI stack to operate and maintain. Our systems evolve quickly as the frontier moves, so you will spend much of your time building and reshaping them rather than keeping a fixed setup running. Your mindset You're an "AI Native": you use agentic AI as core infrastructure in how you work, not as a novelty. You're a "Builder": you ship working systems and improve them continuously rather than leaving ideas as experiments. You blend data science rigor with engineering pragmatism, with care for correctness, reliability, and cost. You're passionate about AI, emerging technology, and investing, and you pair technical depth with strong product judgment. You manage for outcomes, own problems end-to-end, and communicate clearly on progress, tradeoffs, and risk. What we offer Work at the frontier of applied AI in asset management, with petabytes of data and the most cutting-edge tools. Real technical direction and ownership from day one, as the internal expert while the frontier moves. Contribute to a unique success story in European asset management, surrounded by the most knowledgeable experts in the industry. A motivated, highly international team (15 nationalities) that enjoys getting …

items.desc: V Péči o klienty budujeme malý tým, který zjednodušuje fungování banky . Bereme ruční a opakující se práci - čtení dokumentů, přepisování údajů, třídění e-mailů, kontroly - a měníme ji na automatizace , které běží v reálném provozu. Většinu řešení stavíme v Power Automate a n8n a čím dál častěji do nich zapojujeme AI . Co vás u nás čeká? Automatizace od A do Z - projdete si proces s kolegy, navrhnete řešení, postavíte ho, otestujete a dostanete do provozu. Automatizace a robotizace v Power Automate a n8n - cloudové toky pro práci s e-maily, SharePointem a daty, desktopoví roboti v Power Automate Desktop pro webové aplikace banky bez API, a n8n tam, kde potřebujeme pružnější propojení systémů nebo AI. AI v praxi, ne na papíře - třídění příchozích e-mailů, vytěžování údajů z dokumentů, návrhy odpovědí podle interních postupů, a AI agent, který odpovídá kolegům na dotazy nad našimi daty. Práce s byznysem - budete chodit za lidmi z hypoték, provozu a dalších týmů, ptát se a ověřovat, že řešení dává smysl. Data a měření - SQL nad datovým skladem, reporting v Power BI a čísla, která ukážou, kolik vaše řešení reálně ušetřilo. Malý tým, velký dopad - budeme zatím tři, takže budete u všeho od začátku a vaše práce bude vidět. Zpočátku se budete věnovat hlavně automatizaci a robotizaci procesů, přibližně třetinu práce pak tvoří AI. Její podíl ale chceme postupně navyšovat a dáme vám prostor se na tom aktivně podílet. Jak si vás představujeme? / Jste student vyššího ročníku nebo čerstvý absolvent a máte za sebou alespoň první praxi - stáž, částečný úvazek nebo projekt pro reálného zadavatele / Už jste postavil/a nějakou automatizaci - v Power Automate, n8n, jiném RPA nástroji nebo vlastním skriptem - a ta opravdu běžela a někomu šetřila práci / AI jste zapojil/a do něčeho, co funguje - v práci nebo na vlastním projektu, který někdo používá. / SQL, případně Python, zvládáte tak, že si napíšete a opravíte vlastní dotaz nebo skript / Když dostanete zadání, nejdřív se doptáte, jak proces opravdu funguje / Umíte vysvětlit technické řešení lidem, kteří technici nejsou / Počítáte s tím, že věci nejen navrhnete, ale i sami postavíte a odladíte Co vám za to nabídneme? Fajn partu lidí , která se ráda pravidelně setkává v kanceláři – ale zároveň chápeme, že někdy je potřeba pracovat z domova, stačí se domluvit se svým šéfem. Možnost být součástí Air Bank, která si zakládá na otevřenosti, odvahy, jednoduchosti a přátelství. Krásných 5 týdnů dovolené + 5 dní volna za rok na cokoliv. Kvalitní zdravotní péče v síti prémiových klinik Canadian Medical / EUC Premium zdarma. Příspěvek na penzijní připojištění či doplňkové penzijní spoření ve výši 2 000 Kč měsíčně. A mnohem více – stačí se zeptat. Jak bude probíhat nábor Na začátku se vám ozve Dáša z náboru a pobavíte se spolu o vašich zkušenostech, motivaci i o tom, co od role čekáte vy i my. Pokud si to sedne, potkáme se na prvním kole online. A když bude dávat smysl pokračovat dál, uvidíme se osobně - součástí druhého kola bude i krátký test. Těšíme se na vás!

items.desc:
Job Description: 
 Your impact 
 Are you ready to lead the design of end‑to‑end services that support some of the UK’s most critical missions? At Leonardo UK, our Service Designers bring human‑centred, evidence‑based design leadership to multi‑disciplinary delivery teams, shaping services across the full lifecycle — from Discovery through to Live. You will provide expert professional advice, influence decision‑making, and lead complex design work that transforms how users interact with our services and how those services operate behind the scenes. 
 Your work at Leonardo UK will see you take the lead in solving customer problems in an agile, innovative and team-centric manner. The role may involve a blended hybrid working model, with a mixture of working from home and working on site at our Bristol office to ensure close collaboration with the wider team and with our customers. 
 What you will do as a Service Designer 
 Lead service design activities across Discovery, Alpha, Beta and Live. 
 Produce service maps, journeys, blueprints, and end‑to‑end service models. 
 Work collaboratively across multi‑disciplinary teams to align user needs, business goals and technology constraints. 
 Provide professional advice on service design approaches, risks and opportunities. 
 Coordinate service design work to time, quality and business expectations. 
 Facilitate workshops, co‑design and decision‑making forums. 
 Support the development of service design practice and mentor junior team members. 
 What you’ll bring 
 Strong expertise across the DDaT service design lifecycle. 
 Ability to influence decisions with evidence, research and clear rationale. 
 Experience delivering complex service design in multi‑disciplinary teams. 
 Strong communication skills and confidence in simplifying complexity. 
 Ability to contribute to planning, strategy and roadmap discussions. 
 Experience coaching or supporting others in service design. 
 Core areas (must have): 
 Proven experience in end‑to‑end service design (DDaT). 
 Ability to produce service artefacts at multiple levels (journeys → blueprints → ecosystems). 
 Skilled in evidence‑based design: insight synthesis, problem framing, prioritisation. 
 Ability to influence stakeholders across engineering, product and policy domains. 
 Experience coordinating service design delivery across phases and teams 
 Desirable: 
 Exposure to operational service management (ITIL, SLAs, support models). 
 Experience in defence, government or regulated environments. 
 Working knowledge of adjacent roles (UR, BA, Product, Interaction Design). 
 Experience in agile or SAFe delivery environments. 
 Professional training/accreditation in service design or human‑centred design. 
 Contribution to communities of practice or internal capability uplift. 
 This is not an exhaustive list, and we are keen to hear from you even if you might not have experience in all the above. The most important skill is a good attitude and willingness to learn. 
 Security Clearance 
 This role is subject to pre-employment screening in line with the UK Government’s Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS). An additional range of Personnel Security Controls referred to as National Security Vetting (NSV) may apply, this could include meeting the eligibility requirements for The Security Check (SC) or Developed Vetting (DV). For more information and guidance please visit: https://careers.uk.leonardo.com/gb/en/security-and-vetting 
 Why join us 
 At Leonardo, our people are at the heart of everything we do. We offer a comprehensive, company-funded benefits package that supports your wellbeing, career development, and work–life balance. Whether you're looking to grow professionally, care for your health, or plan for the future, we’re here to help you thrive. 
 Time to Recharge: Enjoy generous leave with the opportunity to accrue up to 12 additional flexi-days each year. 
 Secure your Future: Benefit from our award-winning pension scheme with up to 15% employer contribution. 
 Your Wellbeing Matters: Free access to mental health support, financial advice, and employee-led networks championing inclusion and diversity (Enable, Pride, Equalise, Armed Forces, Carers, Wellbeing and Ethnicity). 
 Rewarding Performance : All employees at management level and below are eligible for our bonus scheme. 
 Never Stop Learning : Free access to 4,000+ online courses via Coursera and LinkedIn Learning. 
 Refer a friend: Receive a financial reward through our referral programme. 
 Tailored Perks : Spend up to £500 annually on flexible benefits including private healthcare, dental, family cover, tech & lifestyle discounts, gym memberships and more. 
 Flexible working: Flexible hours with hybrid working options. For part time opportunities, please talk to us about what might be possible for this role. 
 For a full list of our company benefits please visit our website.

Overview 
 Are you passionate about AI and eager to transform the IT landscape? As a Cloud & AI Specialist, you will help leading Austrian enterprise customers accelerate their AI and cloud transformation, connecting Microsoft Azure, Data, Security, and AI capabilities to their most critical business priorities. You will act as a trusted advisor to business and technology leaders, helping customers modernize their estates, unlock data-driven insights, deploy Generative AI solutions, and build scalable digital platforms that drive revenue, growth, and innovation. 
 In this role you are the solution sales lead for your assigned accounts. You lead a virtual team of technical, partner, and consulting resources to advance the sales process and to achieve and exceed quarterly Cloud & AI revenue and consumption targets, translating Microsoft's platform into measurable business outcomes – from migrating and modernizing estates to be AI-ready, through to accelerating innovation with AI agents and platforms. 
 This opportunity will allow you to deepen your expertise across Azure, Data, Security, and AI, sharpen your solution-selling and executive-engagement skills, and shape the AI and cloud transformation of some of Austria's most significant enterprise customers. 
 Microsoft's mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
 Responsibilities 
 Customer engagement: assess and qualify sales opportunities following sales frameworks, participate in strategy development for driving and closing moderately complex, significant-value opportunities, drive sales strategies tailored to each customer's priorities, and collaborate across organizations (ATU, GPS, CSU, ISD, Partner) to orchestrate deals, earn customer buy-in, secure deals, and mitigate risk. 
 Lead a virtual team of technical, partner, and consulting resources to advance the sales process; activate partners and relationships to drive co-selling and partner attach at every stage of the sales lifecycle; and develop relationships with key customer and partner stakeholders, translating their feedback into recovery action plans. 
 Sales and pipeline management: maintain sales and consumption pipeline hygiene, engage in pipeline reviews to drive forecasting accuracy using AI-powered analytics, monitor adoption trends to help customers realize value and drive expansion and predictable renewals, and analyze propensity, renewal, consumption, and usage data to prioritize sales strategy. 
 Sales strategy: evaluate the solution area and market to align sales plays with customer priorities, using AI-driven predictive analytics and whitespace analysis to identify opportunities and market gaps, and lead discussions with customer stakeholders and decision makers to identify, qualify, prioritize, and accelerate sales opportunities. 
 Serve as a trusted advisor guiding the adoption of technologies that drive digital transformation, distinguish Microsoft's offerings in the landscape, and incorporate and reinforce security principles in customer interactions, opportunities, and pursuits to maintain trust and compliance standards. 
 Industry leadership: develop a deep understanding of industry trends across the assigned segment, engage C-level, technology, data, and business leaders on their strategic priorities and transformation initiatives, and bring thought leadership around AI-powered operations, data estate modernization, and digital monetization, representing Microsoft at key industry events and executive engagements. 
 Leverage technology (for example, AI sales agents, automation, and Power Platform) to drive growth within the assigned domain, and embody our culture and values in every engagement.
 Qualifications 
 Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Business Administration, Information Security, or related field AND few years of technology-related sales or account management experience or equivalent experience. 
 Business proficiency in both spoken and written communication in English and German (C1 or above).

 OR Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Business Administration, Information Security, or related field AND several years of technology-related sales or account management experience;
 OR equivalent experience. 
 Solution or services sales experience, including experience delivering solutions for customer personalization, inventory optimization, and workforce enablement.

items.desc: The Department of Medical Biochemistry and Microbiology (IMBIM) at Uppsala University provides a broad international environment for research and teaching. IMBIM conducts basic research in biochemistry, cell and molecular biology, tumor biology, comparative genetics, functional genomics, immunology, bacteriology, and virology. The department's research is primarily basic in nature, but its applications have a clear connection to, and significance for, health and disease in both animals and humans. A more detailed description is available at Research – Department of Medical Biochemistry and Microbiology – Uppsala University. The Medical Inflammation Research (MIR) Group led by Prof. Rikard Holmdahl at the department of Medical Biochemistry and Microbiology (IMBIM), Uppsala University, aims to improve human health by identifying the regulatory pathways of autoimmune diseases. A basis of this research some of the major genetic polymorphic alleles associated with autoimmune diseases in experimental animals have been identified and unique mouse strains developed. We are looking for an experienced researcher to lead and coordinate projects with a focus in driving the research, development, and validation of the humanized mouse model. You will have the opportunity to collaborate with leading experts, access cutting-edge resources, and contribute to transformative discoveries that can shape the future of autoimmune disease treatment. Your mission You will be involved in collecting and synthesizing existing scientific evidence and generating new data to characterize the asset for key stakeholders in rheumatology research, as well as exploring broader applicability across other research areas, as well as in overseeing and manage the animal model platform for other scientists and researchers. You will lead the design, execution, and reporting of in vivo and in vitro experiments to characeterise and validate the humanized mouse strains as a model to evaluate the efficacy and generate mechanistic insights of candidate immunotherapies targeting autoimmune diseases and other conditions, and to address key questions that shape the future of autoimmune disease treatment. You will be working with immunology-oriented research including in vivo experiment, immune assays and flow cytometry, and expression analysis. In addition, the role includes developing experimental proposals for other users, with the aim of attracting new scientific interest, collaborators, and funding opportunities. You are also expected to contribute to scientific publications and participate in the supervision of master students and teaching. Required Qualifications Doctoral degree, or a foreign degree deemed to be equivalent to a doctoral degree, in Biochemistry, Biotechnology, Immunology or a related field. This eligibility requirement must be fulfilled at the latest at the time of the employment decision. It is considered an advantage if you have and a long experience with animal models. Relevant advanced research experience in mouse handling, mouse breeding and genotyping, animal experimentation (including surgical procedures), disease models, as well as experience with laboratory cellular biology work. Strong background in genetics, immunology, biochemistry, biostatistical analysis, flow cytometry, antibody based immune assays as well as in vivo autoimmune disease models will be considered valuable. Proficient knowledge of English We place great importance on personal suitability and are looking for highly creative and motivated employees who appreciate working in a team. We expect the applicants to show good collaboration skills and at the same time great independence. About the position Fixed-term employment for one year, full-time. Starting date by agreement. Place of work: Uppsala. For further information about the position , please contact Professor Rikard Holmdahl, e-mail: rikard.holmdahl@imbim.uu.se We welcome your application no later than 9 November 2026. UFV-PA 2026/2771 Uppsala University is a broad research university with a strong international position. The ultimate goal is to conduct education and research of the highest quality and relevance to make a difference in society. Our most important asset is all of our 7,500 employees and 53,000 students who, with curiosity and commitment, make Uppsala University one of Sweden’s most exciting workplaces. The programme provides funding for three and a half years. It offers excellent working conditions and a unique research infrastructure. You will be employed full-time and receive monthly salaries based on a standard rate. Please find the detailed information about the doctorate at ETH Zurich in the AVETH survival guide. Project background About the Programme The A&T Doctoral Programme is ETH Zurich’s interdisciplinary educational platform committed to training scholars in research and teaching of technology in architecture. The programme is offered and managed collaboratively by the chairs of the Institute of Technology in Architecture (ITA) . The work of the ITA chairs assimilates many diverse aspects of employing science, technology and engineering in architecture, including computational design of buildings and structures, building processes and systems, digital and robotic construction and fabrication, and many others. For more information about our institute, please consult the ITA website. The following professorships are currently involved in the A&T doctoral programme: Architecture and Digital Fabrication (Gramazio Kohler Research) Architecture and Structures (Block Research Group) Structural Design Digital Building Technologies (DBT) Architecture and Building Systems (A/S) Construction Heritage and Preservation Architecture and Human Augmentation You will join one of the above professorships under the respective professor/mentor. Although the selected applicant will be primarily associated with the chosen professorship, the interdisciplinary character of the programme ensures the involvement of other parties during the studies. For example, one of the milestones of this doctoral programme is the Aptitude Colloquium, in which doctoral students defend their research plan before all ITA professors and researchers. Our work takes place in the Arch_Tec_Lab, a high-tech zero-emissions building designed and developed by ITA. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. MDP designs and delivers the Institute’s core diplomacy training (CDT), consisting primarily of orientation briefings and short, intensive skills development workshops which benefit cumulatively some 2,500 diplomats yearly at the United Nations Headquarters and other venues where the Organization maintains a significant presence. Parallel to CDT, MDP develops and delivers training activities at country and regional levels in close partnership with governments, universities and selected international organizations. MDP’s activities also include e-Learning courses; special projects, advisory services related to the curriculum development of diplomatic academies; and the development of other training tools and publications. MDP welcomes qualified candidates interested to work for a period of six months, at UNITAR headquarters in Geneva. The placement is on an unpaid basis, but a monthly lump-sum of 900 CHF will be provided towards transportation and miscellaneous costs. Background In line with the Institute’s efforts to enhance its training activities, the Multilateral Diplomacy Programme is developing an unprecedented amount of online and face-to-face activities offered to the diplomatic community based in Geneva, New York and elsewhere. The Programme also routinely organizes tailor-made activities upon request of donors and partners. These activities target government officials involved in bilateral and multilateral negotiations, staff of non-governmental organizations, as well as students and younger generations. Responsibilities Under the supervision of the Senior Programme Specialist of UNITAR’s Multilateral Diplomacy Programme, the trainee will assist in the coordination and implementation of face-to-face and online training activities. The trainee would assist in, inter alia, designing and managing courses and adapting training content to assessed training needs. The trainee would also be responsible for assisting in communications and outreach activities. items.desc: Developer Experience / DevEx Location: Bristol / London About Fractile Fractile was founded in 2022 on the bet that, eventually, the world's most capable AI systems would be limited in their impact by the time taken to produce useful outputs. We bet everything on the logical conclusion: that the only way to truly unlock this latent value, to make speed viable at scale, was to radically re-invent the hardware that we run our frontier AI models on. Ever since, we have been building chips and systems that tackle this problem: how to efficiently generate output at thousands of tokens per second, while handling the complexity and capacity challenges of operating large models at very long contexts. The workloads that push to the limits of the current frontier are already transformational; it is the technical and economic limits on inference speed that are constraining progress. The defining work of the 21st century will be marked by the engine of inference delivering immense and diffuse chains of intellectual inquiry, in drug discovery, in software engineering, in materials discovery, in any field where progress is driven by deep reasoning and intelligence to resolve complex problems. The Role About the Software organisation at Fractile Developer Experience sits within the Software organisation at Fractile, which is responsible for developing a full software stack for our groundbreaking AI inference systems. That's everything from ML compilers, device drivers and systems firmware, application level runtime and ecosystem integrations, ML and compute libraries, great developer tooling and a full portfolio of simulators, through to datacenter scale workload deployment solutions. At Fractile, we know that a fantastic software stack is a critical and central part of any AI inference solution and it sits at the heart of everything we're doing. About the team and role The Developer Experience team at Fractile helps shape how our customers interact with the Fractile inference accelerator. We work across the company to identify, create, and present information on how the system is being used, as well as providing the tooling to help optimise our customers' usage of the system, while keeping a shallow learning curve. As a member of the Developer Experience team you will need to understand the current state of development for inference hardware. You will need to be able to identify what will work well for engineers wanting to identify potential opportunities for performance improvements, while knowing what tooling will fit into an existing LLM engineer's workflow with the minimal amount of disruption and effort. About you We're looking for someone who is self-driven and capable of identifying tooling opportunities, designing those tools, and delivering them in a way which will fit in with an LLM engineer's existing toolset. You will have worked in this area before, possibly as an FDE or at a company that provides inference services using their own models, and have the ability to develop new tools that are designed to be functional and easy to learn and use. Key Requirements Experience with inference frameworks such as JAX and/or PyTorch Experience of software development in Python, Rust, C/C++, or a similar language Experience monitoring and optimising code written in CUDA, ROCm, OpenCL, or similar Experience monitoring and optimising LLM deployments with 50+ billion parameters Experience working with stakeholders across multiple teams What We Offer Competitive salary: A competitive salary reflective of your experience and the specialist nature of the role Equity & Ownership: meaningful equity so everyone shares in the value creation Benefits: Private Medical, Dental and Vision, Contributory Pension, 25 Days holiday plus bank holidays and Life/Critical Illness Insurance Diverse & fun office: we believe the hardest problems get solved by the broadest range of minds. We are committed to Equal Employment Opportunity through attracting and retaining a diverse team and building an inclusive environment Fractile is seeking to increase the clock speed of global progress, one chip at a time. We've recently raised $220M from investors including Founders Fund and Accel and our most important work lies ahead. Join us! items.desc: AI Engineer, Agentic Systems and Multi-Agent Orchestration Location : London (HQ), Hong Kong, Shanghai, UAE, New York About the Role A private investment firm with offices across the globe (London, Hong Kong, Shanghai, Abu Dhabi, and New York) is expanding its elite technical team to build and own state-of-the-art agentic AI infrastructure. The role can be based in any of these locations. You will architect the core systems that let autonomous AI agents plan, execute tool calls, retry on failure, and reliably hand off complex workflows in production. At the centre of this is agent harness engineering: the scaffolding around the model, covering tools, memory, guardrails, and feedback loops, that turns a raw LLM into an agent you can trust in production. You will be working on exciting projects within the quantitative finance world, such as research agents that help generate and test trading ideas, AI tools that process market data, news, and alternative data, and agentic systems that support portfolio and risk monitoring. Your work will feed directly into real trading and investment decisions. Key Responsibilities Design and build scalable multi-agent orchestration systems, covering task decomposition, inter-agent communication, and state management Own agent harness engineering, including sandboxed execution, guardrails, automated retries, fallback logic, and real-time observability Build agent memory and context engineering layers that keep long-running agents coherent across sessions and tool calls Build rigorous LLM evaluation pipelines, including LLM-as-judge and trajectory-level testing, to catch regressions before production deployment Architect reliable RAG and tool-use infrastructure across structured and unstructured data, using hybrid search and reranking, with MCP and agent-to-agent protocols for integration Fine-tune and adapt models for domain-specific tasks, and contribute to model pretraining and post-training work where it adds an edge Own ML deployment end to end, taking models and agents from experiment to production-grade serving, including monitoring, versioning, and cost and latency management Work across frontier commercial models and open-source models, routing between them based on cost, latency, and task type What You Bring Deep expertise building with advanced LLM architectures, agentic AI, agentic reasoning, and multi-agent workflows Hands-on experience with agent harnesses and orchestration, using LangGraph, AutoGen, or custom-built frameworks, alongside Model Context Protocol Practical experience with model fine-tuning, and ideally exposure to pretraining at meaningful scale Experience deploying ML models and LLM-based systems into production, with strong MLOps fundamentals Strong grounding in LLM evaluation, including designing benchmarks and metrics that reflect real-world performance Experience with RAG and vector databases such as Pinecone, Qdrant, or Chroma, and hybrid retrieval pipelines Strong Python, including AsyncIO and FastAPI, with PyTorch or TensorFlow for model-level work A clear grasp of where standard agent approaches such as ReAct loops break down, and how to engineer resilient workarounds Background in financial services, investment management, fintech, or high-throughput engineering environments is advantageous Open-source contributions, published AI research, or relevant patents are highly valued Compensation and Benefits Highly competitive compensation package Discretionary performance-based annual bonus Full visa sponsorship and premium relocation package where applicable Comprehensive private health insurance and dependent schooling allowances How to Apply If you want to build cutting-edge agentic infrastructure in a high-performance environment, apply now or reach out directly to Syed at syed@durlstonpartners.com.

With teams growing across the US, UK, and India, we’re building an elite force of innovators ready to redefine what’s possible with AI and machine learning. About the role This role sits at the intersection of systems architecture, agentic AI workflows, and customer-facing problem solving. You’ll design multi-agent systems, build reusable primitives, and convert complex financial workflows into scalable automated products. You’ll work directly with leading investment firms and own the lifecycle of every agent you build—from design to reliability, deployment, and scale. Team & Culture High-agency, high-velocity, no-politics. We move fast, unblock ourselves, work directly with customers, give clear feedback, and minimise process.
