items.desc: Build something monumental for Healthcare! At Tandem Health we’re reimagining healthcare by putting clinicians first. Our platform - designed by clinicians, for clinicians - is built on deep insight into real-world pain points, with intuitive medical notes and workflows that truly support patient care. We’re a fast-scaling health-tech company backed by top investors and expanding globally. We move fast, stay curious, and believe building something that matters starts with an extraordinary team. If you're passionate about impact and innovation, we'd love to meet you! About the Role We’re looking for a Talent Acquisition Partner to join our growing team in Stockholm and help us build the engineering, product and design teams behind Tandem. You’ll be at the heart of our mission - connecting brilliant people with meaningful work that’s reshaping how healthcare works. This role is all about people and impact. You’ll partner closely with our CTO and Engineering, Product and Design leaders to attract and hire exceptional builders - from software, security, data and AI engineers to product managers and designers. You’ll craft creative sourcing strategies, champion a high-touch hiring experience, and act as a true partner to the business as we scale our product and technology organisation. This is a demanding role with real substance. Our hiring bar is very high, the talent we go after is some of the most sought-after in Europe, and you’ll be trusted with real ownership from day one. You don’t need a decade in recruitment to thrive here - what matters most is your drive, how fast you learn and how much you want to push yourself. We’re growing fast - new products, new teams, new opportunities to make an impact. That means you’ll play a key role in building the foundations of how we hire tech talent at scale while keeping the heart of Tandem’s culture alive. If you love connecting people to purpose, thrive in high-growth, fast-paced environments, and want to help shape the team that’s transforming healthcare across Europe - this role is for you. What You Will Do Partner with Tech, Product and Design leaders to understand their needs, define what great looks like, and bring the right people into every conversation. Own end-to-end hiring across tech, product and design roles - from first outreach to signed offer. Take real ownership of your searches: run them yourself, make the judgement calls, and be accountable for outcomes, not just activity. Craft and experiment with creative sourcing strategies to reach world-class engineers, product people and designers beyond the obvious channels, including passive and highly sought-after talent. Build a thoughtful, inclusive, and seamless candidate experience from first touch to offer, including technical interviews, case work and on-site visits. Help shape and scale our recruitment processes as Tandem grows - balancing speed with quality, and keeping the bar very high, and holding an uncompromising bar, even when that means saying no to a good candidate while we wait for a great one. Use data to keep our funnels healthy, share market insights with hiring managers, and continuously improve how we hire. Strengthen our employer brand among technical talent by telling authentic stories about our people, our product and our mission. Be a culture carrier: bring energy, curiosity, and passion into every interaction. What You Bring Proven experience as a Talent Partner or Technical Recruiter, ideally in a high-growth, international environment. Years matter less than results: we care about what you’ve achieved, how much responsibility you’ve already taken on and how quickly you’ve grown. A track record of hiring engineers, product managers and/or designers, including senior and specialist profiles. An appetite for hard problems and high standards: you hold yourself to a bar most people find uncomfortable, and you actively seek out more responsibility. Deep curiosity and creativity when it comes to sourcing - you find the people others overlook, and you know how to start a conversation that gets a reply. Enough technical fluency to understand what different engineering, product and design roles actually involve and to hold credible conversations with candidates and hiring managers. You’re excited by the plethora of Talent Acquisition enablement tools and embrace AI-driven tech and sourcing innovation to work smarter and uncover hidden talent. Strong stakeholder management skills - you build trust fast, push back when needed and communicate with clarity. A passion for creating a great candidate experience and championing diversity in every process. Comfort with ambiguity and change - you thrive where things are moving fast and are energised by high pace. Bonus points Experience hiring for Stockholm’s tech/AI scene or competitive talent markets Experience building or improving hiring processes in a scale-up Location We believe the best ideas happen when we’re together. items.desc: Scania is undergoing a transformation from being a leading supplier of trucks, buses, and engines to providing complete and sustainable transport solutions. Together with TRATON and our sister brands MAN, Volkswagen Truck & Bus, and International, we are working to shape the future of mobility with innovative and environmentally conscious solutions. Our values – customer first, respect, team spirit, responsibility, and elimination of waste – are at the heart of everything we do. Together, we are at the forefront of creating a sustainable future. Role Summary Join us in our mission to provide exceptional statistical support and drive the future of Scania's quality solutions. Welcome to the Quality Information team within the SCANIA Brand Identity Development Field Quality organization! We're on a mission to provide top-notch statistical support for decision making process and analysis that describe the quality situation in the field. We gather data from various sources, including vehicle production, warranty information, fault codes, workshop work orders, and operational data. We visualize this information using Power BI and SAS VIYA. With one of our analysts moving to a new position within Scania, we're on the lookout for a new team member to join our dynamic and innovative group. Job Responsibilities Build and modify Power BI reports, perform advanced analysis, and create data models related to our customer vehicles. This includes operational data, fault codes, failures, repair history, and software updates. Dive into the exciting world of machine learning to uncover new insights and benefits in our data. Work closely with a team of analysts and data engineers in Södertälje and Brazil, all striving towards the same goal – helping our customers make data-driven decisions. Actively participate in management team meetings and be responsible for yearly planning, coordination, and follow-ups. Who You Are We're looking for someone who thrives in a transforming organization. You have a degree in engineering, computer science, or a similar field, and you possess excellent analytical skills. You enjoy helping others and have a knack for SQL coding and building reports in Power BI or SAS Viya. Experience in these platforms is a plus. As an analyst/data scientist in our team, you need to be cooperative with a strong customer focus, as you'll regularly interact with both the business side and Scania IT. You're curious about new technologies,have innovative mindset, and thrive in both team and individual settings. You are good at solving complex problems and curios about the automotive industry. Skills We Value : Statistical Analysis DAX Programming SQL Server & SSAS Building Reports in Power BI Python or R Programming This Is Us Quality Information is a team within the SCANIA Brand Identity Development Field Quality organization that provides statistical support for decisions and analysis needed to describe the quality situation in the field. Our team is currently moving all our data to the cloud as part of Scania's "cloud first" strategy, using Azure and Snowflake. We collect data from various sources, including information about our produced vehicles, warranty information, fault codes, workshop work orders, and operational data. We visualize this information in Power BI or SAS VIYA. Our team consists of three analysts and three data engineers in Södertälje and two analysts in Brazil. Since one of our analysts has moved to another position within Scania, we are looking for their replacement. Join us and be part of a team that values creativity, collaboration, and a customer-centric approach. Together, we help our customers make data-driven decisions with a smile and big hearts! Scania Offers We offer a dynamic, flexible workplace with hybrid work options, including Scania Sergel and Midway hubs. With a structured development plan and courses, Scania supports your career growth both locally and internationally. Benefits include training at our health center Gröndal or wellness allowance, result bonus, flexible hours, and company car leasing. Scania also hosts events for employees and their families, and Stockholm residents enjoy direct access to Södertälje via Scania Job express buses for an easy commute to Södertälje. Application We look forward to receiving your application, consisting of your CV and kindly ask you not to share a cover letter to ensure an efficient and unbiased recruitment process for all parties. Apply as soon as possible, no later than 2026-11-01. Screening will take place on an ongoing basis during the application period. Logical and personality tests may be used as part of the selection process, and a background check may be required for this role. If you have questions or would like more information, please contact: Ivana Jankovic, Head of Quality Information, +46 855354165, ivana.jankovic@scania.com, or Jan Lindeborg, Senior Analyst, jan.lindeborg@scania.com or Malina Grunt, Talent Acquistion …

items.desc: Do you want to build the data-driven engine taking Avanza into Denmark? At Avanza, we are driven by making savings cheaper, better, and simpler. To succeed, we need data that is not only accessible, but accurate, smart, and actionable. We are currently operating as an internal startup at Avanza, building a brand-new platform to expand our business into Denmark. We combine startup speed with corporate strength, taking an AI-first approach to everything we do. We are now looking for a Data Engineer who is ready to step outside their comfort zone, interface seamlessly with software engineering teams, and help build the foundation for our next big journey. Working at Avanza As a Data Engineer in our expansion team, you will help transform raw data into business value through robust pipelines and sustainable data models. We work according to data mesh principles, meaning you will both provide and consume data in a decentralised landscape. Our tech stack rests on BigQuery, Kafka for real-time streaming, and dbt for transformation logic. You will become part of an autonomous team with a strong mandate to shape both architecture and ways of working. We value the craft of data engineering and apply core software development principles such as traceability and scalability—often through pair programming and close cross-functional collaboration. Who You Are You are a curious and proactive team player who loves solving complex problems together with others. You turn ideas into action and see learning from mistakes as a natural part of growth. You actively contribute to maintaining a safe, inclusive, and supportive environment within the team, where asking for help is just as natural as offering it. We Believe You Have (Note: You don't need to check every single box to apply!) Solid experience with SQL, data modeling, and modern data tools such as BigQuery and dbt. Experience with streaming data and message queues (e.g., Kafka). Strong background in software engineering (e.g., Java) and API design in distributed environments—you have your primary focus in data, but can code application logic when needed. An interest in systems monitoring, observability, and analytics support. A humble, solution-oriented mindset where you prioritise team success and knowledge sharing. Professional working proficiency in English, Swedish is a bonus but not a must. Bonus Points If You Have Previous experience working with both user behavior data (e.g., clickstream, event tracking, product analytics) and core platform/financial data, with a track record of combining them to build holistic insights. Experience working with Python for advanced data automation or AI/ML integrations. A curiosity and passion for taking an AI-first approach to problem-solving and software/data development. Prior experience working in a regulated environment such as banking or fintech . What Success Looks Like at Avanza & in this Role We have many customers and they love the product! Success means building reliable, high-impact data pipelines that power our Danish expansion, collaborating seamlessly across tech domains, and fostering an environment where innovation and knowledge-sharing thrive. Ready to Build the Future of Banking with Us? We apply a hybrid workplace model and love seeing each other at our renovated office at Regeringsgatan 103 about 2–3 days a week. If you're excited to help bring Avanza to Denmark with an AI-first mindset, we’d love to hear from you! We review applications continuously, so feel free to apply today. Ready to get started? items.desc: Klarna, briefly At Klarna, we’re building an everyday finance network, helping over 120 million consumers across 26 countries save time and money, and worry less about their finances. Working here means taking on problems most companies never get to solve, and being hands-on enough that the interesting part of the work lands with you, not someone else — you’ll build with AI, not watch it happen. This is the stretch zone. Come find out what you’re capable of. About the role Klarna Bank AB is authorised in Sweden and operates in other EU markets through branches. That means Klarna answers to Finansinspektionen (FI), our home regulator, and to the host regulators in each of those markets, and what we tell one of them has to match what we tell the others. You’ll join the Regulatory Interactions team in Stockholm, work alongside a senior colleague who leads these supervisor relationships, and take on part of that portfolio. You’ll report to the Global Lead, Regulatory Interactions. The position also has a build side: you’ll design tools with AI and upgrade the processes the team already runs. Within your first year, those tools and processes should be in everyday use across the team, and you should be the person maintaining them. The brief moves with the team’s priorities rather than following a fixed task list. What you’ll do You’ll handle regulator correspondence for your part of the portfolio, answering each request accurately and on time. You’ll log every interaction, so Klarna holds a complete record of what we have said and when. You’ll prepare material for submissions and supervisory meetings, in Swedish where the matter calls for it. You’ll keep the team’s registers current: the rules that apply to us, the positions we have taken with regulators, and the periodic reports we owe, to whom and by when. You’ll design new tools with AI and upgrade existing processes, for example a workflow that logs and summarises inbound correspondence, or a check that compares a draft response with the positions we have already taken with that regulator. You’ll build every tool within Klarna’s data and security controls from the start, because much of the material is confidential and some of it is legally privileged. You’ll find out what the colleagues using your tools need, check that what you deliver works for them, and keep it running after launch. You’ll work with Compliance, Risk, Legal, the market teams in the countries you cover, and the owners of our regulatory reporting data in Financial and Regulatory Reporting and Analytics. You’ll also coordinate with the colleagues covering the FCA in the UK and BaFin in Germany. Who you are You’ve worked in or close to financial services regulation, for example in a regulatory, compliance, legal or analyst position at a bank, payments firm or other regulated institution, at a supervisory authority, or at a consultancy or law firm advising them. You understand how regulated firms work with their supervisors, from answering information requests to meeting reporting deadlines and keeping positions consistent across authorities, and you pick up new EU regulation quickly enough to apply it to a live request. You’ve built something with AI or code that other people use, such as an automation, an internal tool, a tracker or a dashboard, and you can explain how it works and where it is likely to break. You work comfortably with data and spreadsheets, and you structure information so others can find and use it. You’re fluent in Swedish and English, written and spoken: English for formal correspondence with regulators across the EU, and Swedish for correspondence with FI and work with Swedish colleagues. You write precisely in both languages, keep track of detail across many open items without missing a deadline, and handle confidential material with discretion. You notice when a process could work better and fix it rather than work around it, you raise problems early, and you’re at ease working with senior people. Bonus points for A degree in law, economics, finance, business, data or a related field. A Swedish law degree (juristexamen) is welcome but not required. Experience building with LLM APIs or agent workflows, or designing prompts and tests for AI used on confidential material, using tools such as Claude, Cursor or Google Apps Script. A recognised compliance or regulatory qualification, for example from the International Compliance Association. Experience rolling out a tool you built and training colleagues to use it. Further EU languages, since several of the regulators you will cover correspond in their own language. German is especially useful given the team’s BaFin coverage. Things you should know before applying This position is based in Stockholm. We are open to someone earlier in their career who shows clear ability, as well as someone who already runs their own workstream with limited supervision. No certifications are required. Working together: we value co-located …

Knowledge of isolator technology and aseptic processing. Understanding of EU GMP Annex 1 requirements. Experience with airflow concepts, contamination control, and First Air protection. items.desc: The Newcastle Genetics Laboratory forms part of the North East and Yorkshire Genomic Laboratory Hub, (NE&Y GLH) alongside our partners in Leeds and Sheffield. There are ongoing Clinical Scientist vacancies to join our friendly laboratory teams, (see https://ney-genomics.org.uk/for-professionals/careers2/ ) and applications are invited for a band 7 Clinical Scientist post in the Newcastle Genetics Laboratory. This is an exciting time to work in genomics, and an opportunity to be at the forefront of improving outcomes for patients. Candidates should ideally be either State Registered with the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC) or should achieve State Registration within the first year. State Registration will be required for full assimilation onto Band 7 (successful candidates within one year of HCPC registration would be appointed at 75% of Band 7 until registration was achieved). All applicants should have direct experience of the work of a diagnostic genetics service. Interview Date Monday 23 November 2023 37 Hours 30 Minutes/Week You will be redirected to Trac to apply for the vacancy. Please expand the job details section and read all of the information before applying for the vacancy NO AGENCIES PLEASE We provide testing for a wide variety of inherited and acquired conditions for a local population of over three million people, as well as services provided for the North East and Yorkshire Genomic Laboratory Hub. In addition we provide specialised services to patients throughout the UK and internationally. The Newcastle Genetics laboratory is housed in purpose built accommodation at the Institute of Genetic Medicine near to Newcastle city centre, and has a close association with the high profile academic groups working in the Institute of Genetic Medicine research laboratories. The successful candidate will be a motivated and reliable individual and will join a team of around 100 Scientific and Technical staff in the Genetics laboratories in Newcastle. They will be required to deliver coordination of testing for a range of genetic conditions, in addition to preparing reports and liaising closely with clinical colleagues and Genetic Technologist staff. A broad knowledge of diagnostic genetics and good communication, team working and supervisory skills are essential. This is a new post, and a major component of the role will be in supporting the coordination and delivery of testing in acquired cancer. As a flexible working friendly organisation, we want to be sure that you can work in a way that is best for us and for our patients, and for you. Speak to us about how we might be able to accommodate a flexible working arrangement. If it works for the service, we will do our best to make it work for you. We also have offices at Regent Point in Gosforth and community sites. items.desc: The School of Chemistry at the University of St Andrews is seeking an experienced Scientific Officer with expertise in small molecule crystallography to join its single-crystal diffraction facility. Working closely with Dr David Cordes (X-ray Crystallographer) the postholder will use advanced diffraction instrumentation to tackle challenging structural problems and help deliver high-quality structural solutions across a diverse range of research projects. You will work directly with researchers across the School, providing specialist expertise and helping them make the most of the facility’s capabilities. In addition, the postholder will become familiar with the School’s powder X-ray diffraction facilities, providing essential support for their effective operation. This is an exciting opportunity for an experienced crystallographer who enjoys scientific problem-solving, advanced instrumentation and collaborative research, and who would like to play a key role in supporting an important resource for the School’s research activities. We are looking for a collaborative scientist who will contribute to the School’s research environment and share our commitment to equality, diversity and inclusion. For an informal discussion about the role, please contact Dr David Cordes at dbc21@st-andrews.ac.uk, or Professor Sharon Ashbrook, Head of the School of Chemistry, at chem-hos@st-andrews.ac.uk. St Andrews offers more than just a place to work—it is a place to belong. We value collegiality, inclusion, and wellbeing, and we are committed to creating a workplace where staff can thrive and perform at their best. In addition to the salary on offer for this position, there are a wide range of benefits for staff working at the University of St Andrews. items.desc: Department Department of Public Health, Environments & Society Salary £40,784 to £46,643 per annum pro rata inclusive Closing Date Friday 30 October 2026 Reference PHP-PHES-2026-16 The London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine (LSHTM) is one of the world’s leading public health universities. Our mission is to improve health and health equity in the UK and worldwide; working in partnership to achieve excellence in public and global health research, education and translation of knowledge into policy and practice. We seek a quantitative researcher with experience in policy evaluation, statistical analysis, healthcare data, and information governance. The candidate will join the NIHR-funded CoSine project, which evaluates health outcomes associated with energy-efficiency upgrades for low-income households in London (UK) using linked housing and healthcare data. The role offers experience in analysing large-scale administrative datasets while engaging with climate resilience and energy poverty research questions. The team develops best practices when setting up a new platform and the candidate will have responsibilities for authoring a technical handbook and organising an event for user feedback. The candidate will also be involved with writing research reports, evidence synthesis, knowledge mobilization as well as other reasonable duties in relation to teaching and administration. You should hold a relevant first degree and, ideally, Masters in the field of epidemiology or related quantitative field with grounding in statistics or data science. You should have relevant experience in policy impact evaluation and public health, relevant analytical skills in statistical programming, e.g. Stata or R and evidence of good organisational skills, including effective time management is essential. Further particulars are included in the. The post is full-time 35 hours per week, 1 FTE and fixed-term until 31 May 2028. The post is funded by the NIHR and is available from 01 November 2026. The salary will be on the LSHTM salary scale, Grade 5 in the range £40,784 - £46,643 per annum (inclusive of London Weighting). The post will be subject to the LSHTM terms and conditions of service. Annual leave entitlement is 30 working days per year, pro rata for part-time staff. In addition to this there are discretionary “Wellbeing Days”. Membership of the Pension Scheme is available. The post is based in London. Applications should be made on-line . Online applications will be accepted by the automated system until 10pm of the closing date. Any queries regarding the application process may be addressed to jobs@lshtm.ac.uk. The supporting statement section should set out how your qualifications, experience and training meet each of the selection criteria. Please provide one or more paragraphs addressing each criterion. The supporting statement is an essential part of the selection process and thus a failure to provide this information will mean that the application will not be considered. An answer to any of the criteria such as "Please see attached CV" will not be considered acceptable. Please note that if you are shortlisted and are unable to attend on the interview date it may not be possible to offer you an alternative date. The London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine is committed to being an equal opportunities employer. items.desc: Job Summary We are seeking a dynamic and detail-oriented QA Analyst to join our innovative technology team. In this role, you will be responsible for ensuring the quality and functionality of software applications through rigorous testing, automation, and analysis. Your proactive approach will help deliver seamless user experiences, optimize system performance, and uphold the highest standards of software quality assurance. This position offers an exciting opportunity to work with cutting-edge tools and methodologies in a fast-paced environment dedicated to continuous improvement and excellence. Responsibilities Develop, execute, and maintain comprehensive test cases and test plans based on detailed requirements gathering and analysis. Design and implement automated testing frameworks using tools such as Selenium, TestNG, Cucumber, and Jenkins to streamline testing processes. Perform various types of testing including functional, system, regression, load, performance, user acceptance testing (UAT), and API testing to validate software quality across platforms like Android, iOS, web, and desktop. Conduct root cause analysis to identify issues related to software bugs, system failures, or performance bottlenecks; collaborate with development teams for effective troubleshooting. Integrate testing procedures within the SDLC (Software Development Life Cycle) using DevOps practices and tools like GitHub, GitLab, TFS, Jenkins, Maven, Ant, and Waterfall methodologies. Support release management activities by verifying software builds and coordinating deployment processes across environments such as AWS or Azure. Collaborate with business analysts and developers to understand requirements thoroughly and ensure test coverage aligns with project goals. Experience Proven experience in software testing with a strong understanding of SDLC methodologies including Agile Scrum and Waterfall models. Hands-on expertise in test automation using Selenium WebDriver, TestNG, Cucumber, JUnit, or similar frameworks across various programming languages such as Java or C#. Familiarity with performance testing tools like LoadRunner or JMeter to evaluate system scalability under load conditions. Solid knowledge of APIs (RESTful & SOAP), web services (XML & JSON), and service-oriented architecture (SOA) principles for integration testing. Experience working with databases such as MySQL, Oracle, SQL Server, MongoDB or DB2; proficient in writing complex SQL queries for data validation. Strong debugging skills combined with experience in troubleshooting issues related to Windows/Linux operating systems and network configurations. Ability to analyze requirements from multiple sources including business analysis documents and technical specifications; excellent data analysis skills are essential. Join us if you’re passionate about delivering high-quality software solutions! We value innovative thinkers who thrive on continuous learning and enjoy working collaboratively within a fast-paced environment committed to excellence in quality assurance. Pay: £35,500.00-£65,100.00 per year Benefits: Casual dress Company events Company pension Free fitness classes Gym membership Private medical insurance Sick pay UK visa sponsorship Work from home Work Location: Hybrid remote in London EC1Y 8LZ

items.desc: Site Reliability Engineer About the role The Site Reliability Engineer will ensure highly reliable, secure and scalable application platforms by applying SRE practices on cloud native systems built on AWS, Kubernetes and Springboot microservices using Java. The role focuses on observability with Splunk, performance optimization and incident prevention for complex hybrid environments in day shift with a strong focus on continuous improvement and service resilience. Location: Glasgow, UK Work Arrangement: This is a fully onsite role, requiring attendance at the Glasgow office 5 days per week . Mandatory Skills Java, Springboot, Microservices, Kubernetes, Dynatrace and Splunk. Certifications Required: AWS Certified SysOps Administrator or AWS Certified DevOps Engineer and Certified Kubernetes Administrator and Splunk Core Certified Power User Additional eligibility requirements: Candidates must be available to start within 4 weeks of receiving an offer. Candidates must currently reside in the UK. In this role, you will: Design and implement highly available and resilient application infrastructure on AWS to ensure business critical services run reliably and efficiently across hybrid environments. Optimize Kubernetes based container platforms by tuning resource usage, scaling strategies and deployment pipelines to maintain consistent performance under varying workloads. Develop and enhance Springboot microservices in Java to improve reliability, modularity and fault tolerance while aligning with best practices for cloud native architectures. Create and maintain SRE focused monitoring and alerting strategies using Splunk to provide deep visibility into application health, latency, errors and capacity trends. Apply SRE principles such as error budgets, service level indicators and service level objectives to guide reliability decisions and balance innovation with stability. Conduct detailed root cause analysis for production incidents and implement robust corrective actions to prevent recurrence and improve overall system resilience. Collaborate with application engineers and platform teams to design scalable release strategies that reduce deployment risk and improve change success rates in day shift operations. Automate routine operational tasks including deployments, rollbacks, configuration updates and health checks to reduce manual effort and improve consistency. -Implement capacity planning and performance testing strategies to ensure systems meet growth expectations and maintain optimal response times for end users. Document runbooks, operational procedures and reliability patterns to support consistent incident response and knowledge sharing across global teams. Partner with stakeholders supporting asset and wealth management processes to understand domain specific reliability needs and translate them into technical solutions. Drive continuous improvement initiatives by analyzing reliability metrics, identifying bottlenecks and proposing targeted enhancements that support organizational goals. Ensure security, compliance and governance requirements are integrated into SRE workflows so platforms remain protected while delivering dependable services. Qualifications -Show proven experience working as a Site Reliability Engineer in complex environments for eight to twelve years with consistent focus on reliability and performance. Demonstrate strong hands on expertise in AWS services such as compute, storage, networking and managed application components used to host production workloads. Exhibit practical experience implementing SRE frameworks including observability, incident management, error budgets and service level definitions in large scale systems. Display advanced skills using Splunk for log management, custom dashboards, alerts and analytics to support proactive detection of issues and trends. Provide solid experience managing Kubernetes clusters including configuration, scaling, workload orchestration and troubleshooting in production contexts. Show deep proficiency building and maintaining Springboot based microservices using Java with emphasis on modular design, resilience and maintainability. Highlight any background in asset and wealth management domains where reliability and integrity of transactional systems and client facing platforms are critical.

items.desc: Join Police Digital Service as NMC Cyber Incident Responder (Cloud Security) Salary starting at £55,000 per annum As a member of the National Management Centre (NMC) Cyber Incident Response team, you will lead and support the investigation of cyber security incidents affecting UK policing. This role combines incident response, cloud security and stakeholder engagement, requiring the ability to identify, contain and investigate sophisticated cyber threats across traditional, hybrid and cloud-hosted environments. You will investigate incidents across cloud, endpoint, network and identity platforms, analysing security telemetry and attacker activity to determine scope, impact and root cause. Working alongside threat intelligence, detection engineering and force stakeholders, you will provide technical advice to support incident response, recovery and organisational decision-making. Key Responsibilities Incident Response & Investigation Lead and support investigations into cyber security incidents affecting UK policing, including ransomware, malware, unauthorised access, data compromise and insider threats. Conduct technical investigations across endpoints, servers, cloud environments and identities to determine the scope, root cause and impact of incidents. Support containment, eradication and recovery activities through evidence-based recommendations. Develop and maintain investigative methodologies, playbooks and procedures aligned to recognised incident response frameworks. Cloud Security Lead and support investigations into cyber incidents affecting Azure, AWS and GCP environments. Analyse cloud telemetry, audit logs, identity events and security alerts to identify malicious activity and support incident response activities. Investigate attacks targeting the identity control plane, including Microsoft Entra ID and other identity providers (IdPs), identifying compromised accounts, privilege escalation and unauthorised access. Support response activities across cloud infrastructure, workloads and SaaS platforms, providing technical expertise during active incidents. Work closely with threat intelligence, detection engineering and force stakeholders to improve investigative outcomes and situational awareness. Translate lessons learned into improvements to cloud security controls, detections, playbooks and response procedures. Stakeholder Engagement Act as a trusted advisor to police forces and policing organisations during cyber incidents. Deliver clear technical and strategic briefings to senior stakeholders, including Chief Officers, CIOs, Heads of IT and Heads of Cyber Security. Coordinate with internal and external stakeholders to ensure effective incident management throughout investigations. Support national coordination activities where incidents have cross-force or sector-wide implications. Threat Analysis & Continuous Improvement Apply threat intelligence, attacker TTPs and frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK to support investigations and response activities. Identify trends, lessons learned and opportunities to improve cyber resilience across UK policing. Contribute to the development of detection capabilities and incident response processes through post-incident reviews and technical findings. Support knowledge sharing, mentoring and capability development across the wider NMC function. What you need to succeed in the role Experience investigating and responding to cyber security incidents within enterprise environments. Experience investigating ransomware, malware, unauthorised access, cloud compromise and data breach incidents. Experience analysing telemetry from cloud, endpoint, network and identity platforms to determine attacker activity, scope and impact. Experience working with Azure, AWS or GCP environments. Experience investigating identity-based threats involving Microsoft Entra ID and other identity providers (IdPs). Strong understanding of attacker tactics, techniques and procedures, and the incident response lifecycle. Experience using EDR, SIEM and cloud security tooling to support investigations and response activities. Ability to communicate technical findings and recommendations to senior stakeholders. Why Join us? You can find out more here: Benefits - Police Digital Service (pds.police.uk) Diversity, equity and inclusion We are committed to equal opportunities for all and will not discriminate on any grounds. We encourage applications from people from the widest possible span of experience. All applicants will be considered without attention to age, ethnicity, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, parental status, nationality, neurodiversity or disability status. Working Arrangements At the NMC, you will benefit from hybrid working, getting the advantages of both face-to-face team engagement and home working. NMC employees have the opportunity to work in our modern office environment for in-person collaboration, alongside the opportunity to work from home 2 days a …

items.desc: Solution Architect (London) AND Introduction At AND, we accelerate the development of digital capabilities. In practice, that means helping ambitious leaders and organisations build the teams, products, processes and even operational structures they need to close the digital skills gap within their organisation today, so that they thrive tomorrow. Clients rely on our experience, agility and craft skills across tech and business strategy, software development and product management to address some of the toughest challenges facing their businesses. We bring aboard thinkers, tinkerers, passionate software craftspeople and inspiring technologists to help us solve these challenges. Together, we’re united by a sense of pragmatism, purpose and a deeply-held belief that digital products and technology alone won’t transform a business or save the world: it’s the people that count. About You As a Solution Architect Lead, you will provide solution architecture expertise, supporting our clients to deliver their digital objectives. As a result, you will need to be able to: Analyses and translates business, information and technical requirements into an architectural blueprint that outlines solutions to achieve business objectives for our client Work with our clients to provide solution architecture expertise, supporting our clients to deliver their digital objective Work with enterprise architecture, application and infrastructure teams to produce an optimal designs for the technology to support the product and identifies and designs dependencies with other systems in the enterprise Manage and lead the target design, policies and standards, working proactively to maintain a stable, viable architecture and ensure consistency of design across designated projects Provide hands-on support alongside the Dev Team for complex solutions and code migrations Coach and develop the AND Digital Product Developers across the squads To do that, it’s essential you bring the following: Broad understanding of the key layers of IT architecture including enterprise, data, application and solution, specific to enterprise level platforms A track record of delivering end to end solution architecture for large and complex multi-channel digital projects Experience in cloud technologies such as AWS and Azure, Saas and Iaas, cloud infrastructure and multiple programming languages Experience of best practices processes and frameworks such as TOGAF and architectural patterns / models Experience in a consulting role and confident in presenting /working and building relationships with all levels of seniority, from clients to dev teams. It’s helpful if you also have: Good knowledge of open source technologies (in full-stack environments) and stretching into code management, testing and deployment tools You have worked for a professional services business, in a solution architecture role for leading corporate clients Commercial awareness of implementing software i.e. cost of system, ownership, impact of new tech into established organisation Good experience and knowledge of the Agile /Scrum delivery process Understanding of IT organisations, functions, roles, activities Joining AND From the work we deliver, to the way we serve and support our people, we work hard to ensure that there’s nowhere quite like AND. But joining a company is a two-way street: the fit has to work on both sides. So before you apply, here’s three key things to understand about us: We’re built for people - like, real humans. Not ‘resources’ or ‘staff’. That means happiness and wellbeing really do matter to us, and we hate unnecessary hierarchy and bureaucracy. There’s no well-trodden path ahead: AND is growing fast and forging a new trail. That’s exciting, and gives us all the autonomy and opportunity we love - but bear in mind it also demands focus, patience and resilience. Diversity is a priority. After all, to build great products that a wide variety of different people love to use, we need a wide variety of people to help us build them. So diversity is more than a policy or a word: it’s business critical for us. Still sound good? Great! Fill out the short application form below and we’ll be in touch.

items.desc: Code Wizards Group is looking for an organised, proactive Systems and Compliance Administrator to help maintain our internal IT infrastructure and support our information security and compliance activities. You’ll work across on-premises and cloud environments, including AWS, Microsoft Azure and Microsoft 365, helping to ensure systems are secure, reliable and well maintained. You’ll also coordinate day-to-day ISO 27001 compliance activities, maintain evidence and documentation, support audits and help complete security assessments from clients and partners. The role is primarily focused on internal systems and compliance, although you may occasionally support technical or security activities across the wider Code Wizards Group. Key responsibilities Systems administration Administer and troubleshoot on-premises servers, virtual machines and supporting infrastructure. Support services across AWS, Microsoft Azure and Microsoft 365. Maintain patching, monitoring, backups, access controls and secure configurations. Support identity and access management, including onboarding and offboarding. Investigate infrastructure and security issues and escalate where appropriate. Maintain accurate system documentation, inventories and operational procedures. Support backup restoration testing, disaster recovery and infrastructure improvement activities. Information security and compliance Maintain the ISO 27001 compliance schedule and ensure recurring activities are completed on time. Maintain ISMS documentation, policies, asset records, risk records and corrective actions. Coordinate activities such as access reviews, supplier reviews, security awareness and vulnerability remediation. Gather and maintain evidence for internal and external audits. Track audit findings and remediation actions through to completion. Help ensure documented controls remain aligned with business and technical practices. Security assessments Prepare responses to security questionnaires, due diligence requests and client or partner assessments. Work with internal stakeholders to verify responses and gather evidence. Maintain a library of approved security responses and supporting documentation. Track deadlines, follow-up questions and resulting actions. Escalate gaps, unclear requirements or significant commitments for review. Essential experience and skills Experience working in systems administration or an infrastructure-focused IT role. Experience with on-premises servers and virtualised environments. Hands-on experience with AWS or Microsoft Azure, with familiarity with the other. Experience supporting Microsoft 365. Good understanding of networking, identity and access management, backups, patching and secure administration. Strong troubleshooting, organisation and documentation skills. Clear written and verbal communication. An interest in information security and ISO 27001. Ability to work independently while recognising when escalation is required. Desirable experience Proxmox, VMware, Hyper-V or similar virtualisation platforms. Administration across both AWS and Azure. Microsoft Entra ID, Intune and Defender. Windows Server and Linux. ISO 27001, audit preparation or compliance evidence gathering. Security questionnaires or supplier assessments. Vulnerability management, disaster recovery or business continuity testing. PowerShell, Bash or other scripting experience. Relevant Microsoft, AWS or information security certifications. Support and development You’ll work closely with the Head of IT and have the opportunity to develop your experience across infrastructure, cloud technologies, information security and ISO 27001 compliance. We welcome applicants with strong systems administration foundations who are still developing experience in some of the technologies or compliance areas listed above. What success looks like Internal systems are secure, reliable and well documented. Maintenance and compliance activities are completed on time. Audit evidence and compliance records are organised and up to date. Security and remediation actions are followed through to completion. Client and partner security assessments are completed accurately and consistently. Why Join Code Wizards? We're passionate about building technology that powers great games, but we're equally passionate about building an environment where talented people can do the best work of their careers. If you're an experienced engineering leader who enjoys developing people, solving difficult technical problems and working with world-class game studios, we'd love to hear from you. Life’s better in Co-op. Pay: From £35,000.00 per year Benefits: Casual dress On-site parking Private medical insurance Ability to commute/relocate: Theale, Berkshire: reliably commute or plan to relocate before starting work (required) Work authorisation: United Kingdom (required) Location: Theale, Berkshire (preferred) Work Location: Hybrid remote in Theale (Berkshire, South East Region)

items.desc: Job Description: EXL (NASDAQ: EXLS) is a global data and artificial intelligence ("AI") company that offers services and solutions to reinvent client business models, drive better outcomes and unlock growth with speed. EXL harnesses the power of data, AI, and deep industry knowledge to transform businesses, including the world’s leading corporations in industries including insurance, healthcare, banking and financial services, media and retail, among others. EXL was founded in 1999 with the core values of innovation, collaboration, excellence, integrity and respect. We are headquartered in New York and have more than 60,000 employees spanning six continents. For more information, visit www.exlservice.com . Role Title: Data Governance Consultant BU/Segment: Analytics Location: London, United Kingdom (Hybrid working 4 days a week in the office) Employment Type: Permanent Summary of the role: EXL Analytics provides data-driven, action-oriented solutions to business problems through statistical data mining, cutting edge analytics techniques and a consultative approach. Leveraging proprietary methodology and best-of-breed technology, EXL Analytics takes an industry-specific approach to transform our clients’ decision making and embed analytics more deeply into their business processes. Our global footprint of nearly 2,000 data scientists and analysts assist client organizations with complex risk minimization methods, advanced marketing, pricing and CRM strategies, internal cost analysis, and cost and resource optimization within the organization. EXL Analytics serves the insurance, healthcare, banking, capital markets, utilities, retail and e-commerce, travel, transportation and logistics industries. As part of your duties, you will be responsible for: Conduct governance reviews, assessments, and sign-offs for strategic and transformational initiatives to ensure compliance with the organization's Data Minimum Standards (DMS). Provide governance oversight across a portfolio of ongoing strategic initiatives, supporting each project through the end-to-end governance lifecycle from initial engagement and assessment to completion and sign-off. Represent Data Governance at weekly enterprise review forums, including the Architectural Review Board (ARB), Salesforce Review Board (SRB), and Change Approval Board (CAB), as well as relevant Data Governance forums. Act as the primary conduit between project delivery teams and Data Governance, ensuring governance requirements and Data Minimum Standards are considered and applied throughout the project lifecycle. Review initiatives at the ARB stage, providing governance guidance and oversight before solution design activities commence. Assess whether projects have appropriately addressed data ownership, data quality, metadata management, and governance requirements before progressing through delivery. Participate in Salesforce Review Board discussions to ensure Salesforce-related initiatives align with enterprise data governance principles and standards. Attend Change Approval Board meetings to validate that governance requirements have been met before solutions are approved for production deployment. Ensure all relevant projects complete the required governance artefacts, including the Data Readiness Checklist (DRC) and Metadata Capture Template (MCT), prior to governance approval. Provide reviews and guidance to project teams so that governance requirements are understood, appropriately addressed, and delivered in line with organizational standards. Drive consistency and quality in governance assessments, supporting improved data management, accountability, and compliance outcomes across the organization. Strengthen collaboration between Data Governance, Architecture, Technology, and Business teams to embed governance considerations from design through implementation while supporting successful delivery. Promote awareness and adoption of Data Governance principles and Data Minimum Standards across project and delivery teams, building strong relationships with project managers, business stakeholders, data owners, architects, and technology teams. Qualifications and experience we consider to be essential for the role: Bachelor's degree in Information Management, Computer Science, Business, or a related field (Required). Experience in data governance, data management, or data risk and compliance roles, ideally within financial services or insurance (Required). Hands-on experience performing governance reviews, assessments, and sign-offs for projects against defined data standards (Required). Working knowledge of data ownership, data quality, metadata management, and data governance frameworks (Required). Experience participating in enterprise governance forums such as architecture review boards, change approval boards, or platform review boards (Required). Familiarity with governance artefacts such as data readiness checklists and metadata capture templates (Preferred). Skills …

items.desc: 56 Dean Street is an award winning HIV and Sexual Health service based in Soho in the heart of London’s West End. We are looking for a skilled and dynamic Health Adviser to join our team. You must be able to offer skilled compassionate advice and care to our service users and be able to work in a busy environment. To see clients diagnosed with sexually transmitted infections including HIV, for information, health education, partner notification, health promotion and risk reduction. To undertake PEP assessments, offer sexual health screening (including venepuncture) and issue PEP and PrEP under a PSD. To see clients in a Sexual Health setting for time limited 1:1 work specifically around risk reduction and behaviour change. To provide time limited support for clients newly diagnosed with HIV. To take on specific project work as negotiated with the senior sexual health adviser. Chelsea and Westminster Hospital NHS Foundation Trust is one of England's top-performing and safest trusts. We operate two main acute hospital sites—Chelsea and Westminster Hospital and West Middlesex University Hospital—along with award-winning clinics across North West London. Our nearly 7,500 staff care for a diverse population of 1.5 million, providing full clinical services, including maternity, A&E, and children’s services, plus specialist HIV and sexual health clinics. The Care Quality Commission rates us 'Good' in safety, effectiveness, care, and responsiveness, and 'Outstanding' in leadership and resource use. We continually invest in our facilities, including a £30m expansion of critical care at Chelsea and Westminster and an £80m Ambulatory Diagnostic Centre at West Middlesex. We welcome applications for flexible working arrangements, accommodating requests where possible to support our staff and patient needs. The Trust is committed to equality and welcomes applications from all, regardless of background. Adjustments can be made for disabled candidates. Early application is advised as vacancies may close once sufficient applications are received. If you haven’t heard from us within three weeks of the closing date, your application was likely unsuccessful. Employment is subject to a six-month probationary period. Some roles may require weekend shifts at multiple sites. Clinical Practice Provide information and health education for clients diagnosed with sexually transmitted infections, including HIV, providing support and onward referral as required. To manage the process of partner notification/management for these clients in order to encourage, with the client’s consent, the attendance of all potentially infected sexual contacts to a Sexual Health clinic. To provide time limited work for clients specifically around risk reduction and behavior change, using evidenced based tools such as Motivational Interviewing and Behavioral Change models. Assessing all factors which might negatively affect a client’s sexual health and referring to appropriate specialist services e.g. Psychology/Psychiatry & Alcohol & Drug services. Ensure at all times that the client’s identity and the confidential nature of the information obtained is respected in accordance with the Sexually Transmitted Disease Regulations of 1974 and the NHS VD directive of 1991, within clinic, outreach and off site services. Facilitate the recall of clients with untreated infections or those in need of follow-up and/or test of cure by letter, telephone or visit. To exchange relevant information about clients and contacts with other Sexual Health clinics as necessary. Provide initial crisis intervention, assessment and appropriate referral for those clients attending the clinic with associated problems, e.g. termination of pregnancy, sexual identity, sexual assault, substance misuse and sexual dysfunction. Offer information and support, to deal with enquiries from, both the general public and health professionals about Sexually Transmitted Infections, including HIV and managing clients who present with health anxiety; assessing and referring as appropriate. To be competent in the management of under 16 year olds and vulnerable adults working within Fraser Guidelines and liaising with the multi-disciplinary team & Child Protection Services as appropriate. To take sexual histories from clients as appropriate and refer on to relevant individuals in the multi professional team as part of the care pathway. To undertake training as per Trust guidelines on dispensing Azithromycin for those patients with Chlamydia as part of the care pathway where appropriate and participate with Pharmacy in regularly auditing this. Provide HIV pre-test discussion for clients requesting an HIV test attending the department and where necessary for inpatients requesting the test in either the Chelsea & Westminster Hospital or Charing Cross Hospital. items.desc: An exciting opportunity to join a fast paced and dynamic team. Meadowcroft PICU is a 10 bedded male intensive psychiatric ward. The team are looking to recruit a passionate and enthusiastic activity worker. We are looking for someone who is able to support patients in engaging in activities on and off the ward. This person will need to be able to use good interpersonal and communication skills to encourage patients to engage in physical health wellness and rehabilitation style activities. Meadowcroft PICU is a ten bedded male unit that is currently looking for a driven and passionate individual who is rewarded by his/her patients turning a corner after a challenging path to recovery. Our unit is often a fast paced and fluid environment and a diverse a workplace setting. It is an exciting team to be part of. You will work within a specialist multi-disciplinary team, delivering high quality, intensive care to patients experiencing acute mental illness. Meadowcroft PICU has an experienced team of mental health professionals and support staff who support patients with a wide range of mental health issues. There is a wide remit for the Activity worker's role within PICU which requires networking and collaborating with numerous internal and external stakeholders. It's important that you have an understanding of multidisciplinary services and the challenges that face people with mental health problems. We want to hire individuals that are passionate about mental health, who believe in our recovery model and who will act as advocates for the reduction of stigma in the wider community. Welcome to Birmingham and Solihull Mental Health NHS Foundation Trust. Our 4000 clinical and support staff help us to improve mental health wellbeing and meet the needs of the 70,000 people we serve each year. We provide a range of mental healthcare services across Birmingham and Solihull, as well as specialised services nationally. We also offer medical, nursing and psychology training and are proud of our international reputation for both research and innovation. Our population is culturally diverse, characterised in places by high levels of deprivation which create an increasing demand for our services and a necessity for us to make sure everyone can access the help they need. We are a team of compassionate, inclusive and committed people working together to provide excellent care to support our community. If you are looking for a place to belong, where you can make a real difference to people’s lives, join our team where our warm welcome is waiting for you. Plan Activities: Design a flexible weekly timetable of group and one-to-one sessions based on patient choices, interests, and care plans. This includes arts, games, physical fitness, and basic life skills. Support Recovery: Use activities to help patients build confidence, reduce boredom, manage symptoms, and learn coping skills. Collaborate with Teams: Work closely with Occupational Therapists and nurses as part of a wider team to support each patient's journey to a less restrictive ward. Monitor Patients: Observe how patients react during activities, track their progress, and report any changes in their behaviour or mental state to the nursing team. We highly recommend you submit your application as soon as possible, this post may close earlier than the indicated closing date if a sufficient number of applications are received. A little about the role We are looking for an FP&A Analyst to join our Finance Team, working closely with our FP&A Manager, Head of Strategic Finance and colleagues across the hospital. You will help us understand how our services are performing, what drives our revenue and where we need to plan ahead. From building financial models to explaining changes in performance, your work will turn complex information into clear insights that colleagues can use. This opportunity would suit someone with a foundation in finance who is ready to move towards a more analytical and commercially focused role. Preparing financial reports, Power BI dashboards and presentations that make information accessible to different audiences. Supporting longer term planning, scenario analysis and business cases. Helping the Head of Strategic Finance identify revenue trends and insights to inform commercial discussions. Working with large datasets, checking accuracy and understanding how the information can be used. Identifying ways to streamline reporting and improve existing processes. What we’re looking for This role would be a natural next step for someone currently working as an Assistant Management Accountant, Assistant Accountant or in a similar finance role, who is ready to build on their experience and move into financial planning and analysis. Part qualified in ACCA or CIMA. At least one year’s relevant experience in finance, such as management accounts, financial reporting, budgeting or analysis. Excellent Excel skills and confidence working with financial data. The ability to interpret financial information and present it clearly to colleagues with different levels of financial knowledge. Strong attention to detail and a careful approach to checking your work. A collaborative approach and the ability to build effective working relationships. A clear interest in developing your analytical skills and commercial understanding through a career in FP&A. What you’ll be part of Our Finance Team works closely with clinical, operational and commercial colleagues to support the effective running of the hospital. You will have the opportunity to understand how different services operate, build relationships across departments and see how your analysis contributes to decisions. Working alongside our FP&A Manager and Head of Strategic Finance, you will broaden your experience in financial modelling, revenue analysis and planning. It is an opportunity to build on your existing knowledge, develop your commercial understanding and grow your confidence in presenting insights to others. As the UK's largest independent charitable hospital, we care for over 120,000 patients each year. What makes us different is what we do with that success. We reinvest it back into our services, our technology and, most importantly, our people. From developing innovative new ways of delivering care to supporting continuous learning and career progression, we're always looking ahead. Based in our main hospital, you'll be part of a team delivering care across 234 beds, 10 theatres and a 13-bed intensive care unit. You will work alongside more than 1,300 colleagues in specialist teams and over 700 consultant surgeons and physicians, all united by a shared commitment to high quality, compassionate care. We are incredibly proud to be the only independent healthcare provider included in the Top 10 of the Financial Times UK Best Employers Survey 2026. Who We Are Water and our natural environment are the foundation of life, society and economies. As part of Anglian Water’s ambitious capital investment programme, the @one Alliance is delivering new and upgraded water and water recycling assets that will help provide resilient water supplies, support sustainable growth and protect the environment for generations to come. At @one Alliance, we bring together industry-leading partners to deliver complex engineering projects and innovative solutions. Alongside the physical assets we build, we also ensure the delivery of high-quality digital asset information that supports effective asset management throughout the lifecycle of our infrastructure. If you're passionate about data, engineering and making a real impact through digital transformation, we'd love to hear from you. What Will You Be Doing as a Master Data Specialist? As a Master Data Specialist you will play a vital role in ensuring that accurate, high-quality asset data is delivered alongside our capital projects, enabling the safe, efficient and reliable operation of critical infrastructure assets. You'll lead asset data management activities across a portfolio of projects, working closely with engineers, project teams, suppliers and business stakeholders to ensure new, modified and decommissioned assets are correctly represented within Anglian Water’s asset register. You'll review and interpret engineering information from a variety of sources, including 3D models, process flow diagrams, P&IDs and equipment schedules, ensuring all asset data meets business standards and requirements. You will oversee the collation, validation and upload of asset information into SAP PM, coordinating delivery against project milestones and ensuring compliance with asset data and maintenance standards. Working as a key link between engineering, digital and operational teams, you'll provide insight and reporting on asset data performance, identify risks and opportunities, and help drive improvements across data management processes. You'll champion asset data quality and governance, ensuring standards are consistently applied across projects and suppliers. This role will also give you the opportunity to support innovation across the Alliance, helping to automate workflows, improve reporting capabilities and enhance the way asset information is managed. You'll contribute to the development of new tools, processes and business intelligence solutions that improve efficiency, visibility and decision-making. Through your expertise, you'll help ensure that the valuable assets delivered through our capital programmes are supported by equally valuable digital information. What Does It Take to Be a Master Data Specialist? We're looking for someone who enjoys working with data, systems and engineering information and thrives on building relationships across a wide range of teams and stakeholders. You'll ideally have: Experience managing engineering or asset data within a technical, utilities, infrastructure or capital delivery environment Experience working with SAP PM, asset management systems or enterprise asset registers The ability to interpret engineering documentation, including drawings, schedules, P&IDs and asset hierarchies Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with excellent attention to detail Experience producing reports, analysing data and identifying trends and improvement opportunities Experience in automating processes using ETL tools to streamline workflows Strong stakeholder management skills with the ability to work collaboratively across multiple teams Experience driving improvements in data quality, governance and process efficiency A proactive approach and confidence in challenging and improving existing ways of working Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal Experience with digital engineering, BIM, asset information management or business intelligence reporting would be advantageous You’ll be someone who is naturally curious, embraces innovation and enjoys finding smarter ways of working while maintaining a strong focus on accuracy and quality. Why Anglian Water? Our people are at the heart of everything we do, and we're committed to supporting and rewarding them. Some of our benefits include: Bonus scheme Private healthcare Competitive pension scheme Up to 26 days annual leave, increasing with length of service Flexible benefits to support your wellbeing Hybrid and flexible working arrangements Career development and learning opportunities Inclusion is for Everyone We are an equal opportunity employer and welcome applications from all backgrounds. The post holder will work with the existing Band 8 Lead MND Care Centre AHP coordinator. The post holder will work in collaboration with a diverse range of acute, community and third sector colleagues, including neurology, respiratory, nutrition, community therapies, pallia, community nursing and palliative care, across the Wessex Region to support and develop expert MND Care. The successful candidate will hold a caseload specialising in MND, attend specialist MND clinics, participate in the community MND MDT meetings, contribute to the MND improvement and development plan, including audit of the NICE standard and offer informal and formal teaching opportunities relating to MND. As one of the largest acute teaching Trusts in England, we offer learning and development opportunities to help you achieve the career you aspire to. UHS is rated ‘Good’ by the CQC and in the latest national NHS Staff Survey, we were in the top 10 acute trusts for staff engagement and for staff recommending the hospital as a place to work or receive care. We support flexible working and will consider requests taking into account the needs of the service. UHS employees are able to access a range of NHS discounts, are entitled to a minimum of 35 days paid holiday (pro rata), and we offer a generous pension scheme. Southampton is an attractive place to live and work situated on the south coast, with an international airport and direct trains to London. The New Forest National Park and beaches of the Jurassic coast are also right on our doorstep. The city offers living costs 30% lower than London and 17 schools rated outstanding by Ofsted. We believe that using technology wisely shows strong time management and commitment to innovation. However, personalising your recruitment application to highlight your unique skills and experiences is crucial. Relying too heavily on generic, AI-generated content instead of drawing from your own strengths and accomplishments may lead to your application being rejected if multiple candidates present identical or similar information. In this role, your key responsibilities will include Hold a clinical caseload of MND patients, working with Lead MND Coordinator and the wider regional team to provide supportive care. Act as single point of contact for patients with MND and their families within the activities of the Care Centre Undertake the established post diagnostic support visit to patients recently diagnosed with MND, offering post diagnostic advice, emotional support, clinical advice relating to NICE guidance and actioning referrals to the wider MDT for ongoing support. Attend and offer MND coordination support within the specialist regional MND clinic structure. Attend and participate in MND coordinator led MDTs across the region. Participate in the MND service objectives and clinical improvement plan, meeting the conditions of the MND Association grant, participating in management review meetings, , participating in the regular NICE audit and taking responsibility for delivery for defined service objectives. Represent the MND Coordination Team at relevant meetings. Provide MND specific training to colleagues at UHS and the wider regional team, offer advice and support regarding MND care as required. Collaborate within the service to support the MND research pathway and Senior MND Research Nurse.

items.desc: This post is based at the St. Ann’s satellite sites of Moorfields Eye Hospital which is one of the world's leading eye hospitals, providing expertise in clinical care, research and education. The post holder is responsible for assessment of care needs of patients, planning programmes of care, implementation and evaluation of these programmes with direct supervision. The post holder will be a key member in relation to the development of practice on the ward. They will be working independently autonomously and at times without direct supervision, accountable for their own professional actions. Ensuring the safety and well-being of service users, and always working in a manner that promotes dignity and human rights through the adoption of person centered care principles. Our main focus is the treatment and care of NHS patients with a wide range of eye problems, from common complaints to rare conditions which require treatments not available anywhere else in the UK. We treat people at our main hospital base in London's City Road and at 19 satellite facilities in and around the capital, which enables us to provide expert treatment closer to patient’s homes. items.desc: A twelve-month Locum Consultant Anaesthetist position is available to start as soon as possible. We are delighted at your interest in joining our Anaesthetics department at the Royal Surrey Hospital. We are a department that provides a consultant-led service to dynamic surgical teams at the cutting edge of surgical innovation. Our department prides itself in allowing individuals to develop and bring their own areas of expertise and interest to what is already a very diverse mix of special interests. These include the more conventional areas such as examinerships, deanery roles, quality improvement, editorships, fellowship leads etc; but have expanded to medical examiner roles, mortality reviews, clinical risk, project management, ethics, management roles within the trust and even Magistracy. There is increasing demand for anaesthetic support for procedures away from theatres, with endoscopy, interventional radiology and radiotherapy being at the forefront of expansion recently. These are relatively new areas of demand, and along with an expansion of elective obstetrics and obstetric clinics offers a new consultant niche areas to organise and streamline. We are also expanding our pre-assessment service including a greater provision of consultant-led high-risk anaesthetic clinics and CPET. The department has historically led the way in holding senior deanery roles and we would look to new consultants to join our group of educational supervisors. Work has started on a purpose built, modular, ambulatory care centre – the Cancer and Surgical Innovation Centre (CASIC) - in the grounds of the RSFT that will give us additional capacity of 6 new theatres and associated facilities. Expected to come online in 2026, this exciting development opens up new opportunities to appointees. This will include involvement in planning new protocols and pathways for the area. Royal Surrey is a compassionate and collaborative acute and community Trust. Recognising that our 5,000 colleagues are our greatest strength, we offer a comprehensive health and wellbeing programme alongside a strong commitment to developing your career. Our diverse and welcoming Royal Surrey family ensures you feel valued from your initial interview and throughout your time with us. We are clinically led and provide joined-up care by bridging hospital and community services, alongside delivering regional specialist cancer care. Our main acute hospital site is in Guildford, with community sites at Milford, Haslemere and Cranleigh, and services delivered in patients’ homes across Guildford and Waverley. We work in partnership with Ashford & St Peter’s Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust through a collaborative Group Model, supporting joined-up services, workforce flexibility and development opportunities. The Care Quality Commission (CQC) has rated us as Outstanding. We are proud of our achievements and continue to invest in our people and infrastructure. To learn more about life at Royal Surrey, please watch our short video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R96pMboIYdo Adverts may close early, so you are encouraged to apply as soon as possible. For further details on the role, please see attached job description and person specification attached.
